summary: Complete computational pipeline and outputs for the manuscript “Information limits of acoustic constraint on CO₂-mixture equations of state in the metering-critical window” (R. C. Aiken; prepared for Measurement Science and Technology). An earlier version of the manuscript was titled “Acoustically optimal state points for constraining CCS mixture models in the metering-critical region of CO₂ + N₂, O₂, and Ar”. Contents: candidate-grid Jacobians and input-derivative grids for CO₂ + N₂, O₂ and Ar (295–310 K, 7.4–11 MPa, 1–5 mol%); measurement designs with per-point precision requirements; projected covariances; replicate fit results; extracted literature comparison values; and the verified CO₂–Ar model implementation. The environment specification gives exact package versions and random seeds (CoolProp 8.0.0). New in version 1.2.0: Nested design sequences regenerated with a deterministic pair-search initialization. The 48-point designs are unchanged; the v1.1.0 sequences are retained as greedy_seq_v1_*.csv. Revision analyses (scripts/revision_*.py, outputs in out/revision/): dependence on composition uncertainty, comparison with conventional designs, batch structure, D/I/G criterion comparison, prediction uncertainty under parameter anchoring, density and bubble-pressure propagation, linearized out-of-family detection, and nonlinear coverage. README_REVISION.txt describes the additions and their run order.
title: Data and analysis code for: Information limits of acoustic constraint on CO₂-mixture equations of state in the metering-critical window

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

QUANTUM COMPUTING FOR INVERSE DESIGN OF 4D MATERIALS FAMILY 12 / F056-F060 / THE OTHER SIDE OF THE RESEARCH MONOGRAPH Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI / White Rainbow Era Scientific status: Prospective nonclinical proposal. All diagrams are analytical synthetic illustrations. No quantum advantage, qualified device, biomedical treatment or patient recovery has been demonstrated. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE 4D MATERIALS RESEARCH An inverse design begins with a wish: a material should bend to a specific shape after a particular sequence of heat, light, solvent or magnetic stimuli. The wish is not evidence. A specimen has a history, a printer has a feature limit, and a camera can mistake a smooth silhouette for recovered function. In this notebook the research chain is followed from physical permission to constitutive model, to competing computational designs, to damaged and rejected specimens, and finally to a negative case that another laboratory can recreate. Five independent flagships supply different scientific questions. F056 concerns a constrained inverse map from target response to material recipe. F057 studies the discrete matching of material configuration with time-dependent target shapes. F058 forces mathematical topology into a printable connected solid. Executive Portfolio Overview FAIR+D Canon™ — Five-IP Commercial Infrastructure Software Ecosystem V2.0.0 is a consolidated, rights-reserved commercial software portfolio comprising five independently identifiable infrastructure software product families. The portfolio is supported by shared integration interfaces, policy controls, deployment components, technical specifications, licensing utilities, validation resources and commercial administration materials. The ecosystem is structured to establish identifiable product boundaries and provide a documented foundation for controlled technical evaluation, enterprise integration assessment, product-specific licensing, private deployment planning, OEM integration discussions, technology-transfer negotiations and potential recurring commercial licensing arrangements. The five principal software portfolios address distinct infrastructure and technology domains: AETHERGRID™ — Infrastructure Resilience and Recovery Decision Software. SENTINEL NEXUS™ — Security Event Intelligence and Triage Software. GRIDMIND™ — Energy and Compute Optimization Software. SOVEREIGN OS™ — Sovereign Infrastructure Policy and Deployment Software. AGENTOMY™ — AI Agent Authorization and Constrained Execution Software. CLOUDGUARD™ is additionally identified as a separately identifiable and separately licensable module within the AETHERGRID™ product family. The five principal portfolios retain distinct product identities and licensing boundaries. Their inclusion in a consolidated ecosystem does not automatically authorize commercial deployment, redistribution, sublicensing or exploitation of every product or module. The V2.0.0 release consolidates implemented software components, reference services, integration interfaces, schemas, deployment scaffolds, technical documentation, validation resources, release-integrity records and commercial licensing materials into a versioned software portfolio. Its purpose is to document the delivered implementation scope, product boundaries, technical limitations and commercial licensing architecture for controlled evaluation and potential future commercial deployment under separately negotiated written authorization. 2. Five Principal Software Portfolios 2.1 AETHERGRID™ — Infrastructure Resilience and Recovery Decision Software AETHERGRID™ provides deterministic infrastructure-state evaluation, policy-based recovery planning, constraint assessment, recovery-target ranking and integrity-oriented decision records. The included implementation components cover: Infrastructure-state normalization and validation. Workload and resource-constraint evaluation. Provider, region, capacity, health and data-residency policy checks. Deterministic recovery recommendations. Simulation-oriented execution boundaries. Append-only JSONL decision records. SHA-256 hash-chain verification for supported decision records. Read-on

QUANTUM OPTIMIZATION FOR REHABILITATION CONTROL AT THE LIMIT FAMILY 11 | F051-F055 | SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK A connected argument through 82 chapters: Mechanism / Measurement / Refutation Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI | White Rainbow Era | 2026 SCIENTIFIC STATUS: Prospective, nonclinical, falsifiable research architecture. No patient trial, tested quantum supremacy, demonstrated stroke recovery, or qualified medical device is claimed. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CONTROL MONOGRAPH The technical notebook is not a glossary pasted below the research monograph. It is a second argumentative surface. The monograph states exactly what can be tested, with candidate equations, independent measurements and research gates. The notebook asks why the experiment deserves construction, which competing explanation should be taken most seriously and how an unsuccessful first generation could become a stronger foundation for someone else. This difference is a methodological commitment rather than a claim of novel experimental results. Family eleven begins from an uncomfortable contrast between optimization and authority. A method may compute a more attractive control input, but no numerical attractiveness can authorize an illegal actuator command. The physical and ethical permission envelope must be defined outside the optimizer, and a safe fallback must remain available when the proposed method is late, uncertain, energy-depleted or dependent on inaccessible backend infrastructure. The most important output of a difficult trial may be an unambiguous refusal. The five flagship mechanisms form a causal chain without becoming duplicates. F051 asks what it means to optimize permitted control gains fairly. F052 places the optimizer inside the receding-horizon control clock. F053 asks whether progressively less assistance can maintain a fixed mechanical task, while refusing to equate phantom success with human recovery. F054 requires energy and latency to be counted across acquisition, computation, communication and actuation. F055 tests whether every scientific conclusion remains subordinate to command legality, independent vetoes and serious classical rivals. This lineage comes from two distinct source studies and the author-supplied STARLI forty-family research DNA blueprint. The four-dimensional microrobotics source supplies material history, force generation, responsive structures and safety concerns. The BCI-stroke atlas supplies intention observability, minimally necessary assistance, withdrawal and the crucial distinction between assisted motion and restored independent function. These source relationships are not evidence that a fused 4D, quantum, BCI and clinical treatment platform exists. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is a public name for a disciplined research workflow. Physical origin asks what the bench is permitted to do. Mathematical evolution asks which candidate model and parameters represent it. Counterfactual branching makes the ordinary baseline and hidden confounder genuine competitors. Extreme extrapolation applies bounded adversarial inputs, where the correct output may be stop. Evidence convergence leaves both a reconstructable result and an open Research Gate. These stages are viewpoints on one research contract, not literal physical parallel worlds. A 4D actuator can return to its familiar geometry and still lose force. A quantum optimizer can return a lower cost and still arrive after the legal deadline. A minimally assisted movement can succeed while a person would remain dependent on the device. A smooth average can hide a rare illegal command. Those four asymmetries explain why this research must separate shape, computation, mechanical assistance, function and safety, and why none of these outcomes can be imported into the others without a new experiment. The wisdom of stopping is the opposite of indifference. It means ending a research round when the testable contract is complete, the strongest rival has been confronted, the permission gates have been audited and the next laboratory can reconstruct the adverse case. When further parameter search no longer distinguishes the mechanism from the rival, additional polished prose or training calls do not create new evidence. The unresolved difference becomes an explicit research door for future investigators. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F051 | Quantum-Assisted Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Control Optimization at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is control gain search under hard actuator and state constraints. Its measurable endpoint is angle tracking error and total tuning-to-command cost. The leading alternative says benefit is produced by extra search, hidden preprocessing or the classical controller. The preregistered blind competition would blind-swap candidate gain vectors on identical nonhuman control traces. A fully observed test requires encoder angle [rad], actuator command, output torque [N m], motor work [J], gain-search calls and full wall time [ms] and resource-equivalent comparison with tuned robust PID/LQR, constrained SQP, CMA-ES and mixed-integer gain search with identical runs and CPU/GPU ledger. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F052 | Quantum-Assisted Model Predictive Control for Rehabilitation Robots at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is finite-horizon constrained optimization with receding-horizon deadlines. Its measurable endpoint is closed-loop error, solver completion percentile and deadline violation. The leading alternative says a solver-only benchmark ignores compilation, upload, readout and communication. The preregistered blind competition would conceal horizon changes and impose actuator-relevant controller deadlines. A fully observed test requires state estimator [rad,rad/s], solver input/output timestamp [ms], horizon [steps], safety margin and fallback event and resource-equivalent comparison with well-tuned conventional MPC, SQP, mixed-integer solvers, warm starts and robust tube MPC on identical task clocks. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F053 | Quantum Optimization for Minimum Necessary Assistance at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is assistance-minimizing policy with a fixed task-feasibility envelope. Its measurable endpoint is minimum delivered force and unassisted phantom-task feasibility. The leading alternative says a more forceful actuator makes the task look easier without reducing dependence. The preregistered blind competition would blindly taper physical assistance and test device-off task feasibility. A fully observed test requires independent load cell [N], motion target error [rad], assisted/unassisted phantom condition and residual passive force and resource-equivalent comparison with a fixed-gain assistive policy, optimal classical assistance scheduler and a fully disengaged zero-assistance phantom control. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F054 | Energy-Latency Tradeoffs in Quantum Rehabilitation Control at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is energy-constrained compute-actuation scheduling and deadline-aware fallback. Its measurable endpoint is joules per safe episode, wall latency and feasible trajectory fraction. The leading alternative says external service electricity or device idle consumption disappears from cost. The preregistered blind competition would inject finite battery, network stalls and safe-stop events in randomized order. A fully observed test requires electrical energy [J], power [W], battery state [J], acquisition and network timestamp [ms], safe-stop trace and resource-equivalent comparison with energy-aware classical MPC, local deterministic fallback and measured on-device scheduling with the same task energy budget. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F055 | Safety-Constrained Quantum Rehabilitation Control Against Classical Baselines at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is noncompensatory command legality with paired quantum-classical evaluation. Its measurable endpoint is illegal commands, veto timing, safety margin and matched-cost task error. The leading alternative says rare forbidden states are omitted while average performance improves. The preregistered blind competition would inject hidden infeasible states and verify fail-silent refusal before actuation. A fully observed test requires command legality indicator, independent hardware veto timestamp [ms], state margin, source version and paired baseline results and resource-equivalent comparison with independently certified physical interlock, robust classical MPC, rule-based veto and cost-matched quantum candidates. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question.

summary: Many high-stakes AI failures trace to the training data rather than the model, yet teams still treat pre-training data validation as a checklist and rarely wire its signals to a go/no-go decision or to a governance framework. We study the detectability boundary of that validation: what a pre-training data-readiness gate catches, what it misses, and why a flagged source is often not blocked. We reuse a validation gate from a prior single-domain system and generalize it across three high-stakes domains (healthcare, finance, and government) on the real MIMIC-IV, SEC EDGAR, and CMS Open Payments datasets, injecting controlled defects across simulated sources. A composite readiness score detects 0.76 of degraded sources (95% CI [0.74, 0.76]) but withholds only 0.42; the 0.34 gap (95% CI [0.32, 0.35]) traces to a single averaging step, and we show it is fixable but privacy-sensitive. The grid is small by design (six sources per domain, two degraded, five seeds), so the intervals describe this controlled setting, not field variability. We map the privacy-utility curve of validating on differentially private summaries, prove a blind spot for symmetric label noise on balanced targets, and add a confident-learning label detector that runs on DP-noised summaries and keeps its recall down to epsilon = 0.1. We compare against Great Expectations and Deequ, measure how poorly thresholds port across domains, and map the gate to the NIST AI RMF MEASURE function. We report the negatives, among them a near-chance inter-rater reliability on fine-grained incident coding. What is new is the integration of production incidents, a private benchmarked gate, and a governance mapping, not any one of those parts.
title: Detection Is Not Action: The Detectability Boundary of Pre-training Data-Readiness Gating

summary: siwecal-soft v0.1.0 First release of siwecal-soft , the software of the SiW-ECAL TB2026 test-beam campaign at CERN: data conversion, simulation, reconstruction and analysis in one Key4hep/Gaudi project. Origin This repository merges two earlier repositories into a single code base with a fresh history: siwecal_k4sim @ 075dedd : simulation of the prototype. DD4hep geometry (including the H2-like upstream beam line), ddsim launchers, digitisation and the simulation campaigns. siwecal-tb2026 @ 90b2e55 : test-beam data. Raw/LCIO decoding, event building with the muon calibration, particle-ID shower variables, ACTS tracking, event viewer and analysis. An important part of the DAQ data decoding (SLB frame and raw decoders) and of the pedestal/MIP calibration is based on SiWECAL-TB-analysis , the SiW-ECAL test-beam analysis software. Both repositories are frozen at those commits (tag final-before-monorepo ); new development happens here. Every file of the two repositories is accounted for in tools/migration/ (copied, rewritten or excluded), and the merge was validated against the frozen builds (identical tracking output: 137/137 data and 144/144 simulation EDM4hep branches). What changed with the merge One CMake project (C++20, Key4hep 2026-04-08), one install, one environment script ( init_siwecalsoft.sh ). Shared code and mappings live once in common/ ; calibration tables are read from EOS only. Unified ACTS tracking for data and simulation. Processing steps formerly done in Python now run as Gaudi algorithms: ecal tree writer, occupancy-sag and trigger turn-on calibrators, and the post-PID event selection and valtree ( EcalEventSelection , EcalValTreeWriter ). Each was validated against the Python version. New: run-by-run simulation ( simulation/campaign/make_run_sim_dag.py ). One simulated sample per data run, with the gun tuned to that run's measured beam spot ( siwecal_beamspot ) and the run's statistics; used for final_v10. Control tests ( tests/control/ ) run with ./build.sh (ctest + pytest). Authors Jesus Pedro Marquez Hernandez (IJCLab), Olmo Arquero Peinazo (CIEMAT), Yukun Shi (LLR). See CITATION.cff for how to cite this software.
title: siwecal-soft: SiW-ECAL TB2026 data conversion, simulation and analysis software

summary: This record contains supplementary research materials supporting the manuscript entitled "Evaluating Out-of-Fold Weighted Soft Voting for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefits and Limitations of Classifier Fusion" (Manuscript ID: MJCSC-D-26-00018R3), submitted to the Mesopotamian Journal of Computer Science. The study evaluates training-derived optimized weighted soft voting for multiclass network intrusion detection using Decision Tree (DT-Gini), Random Forest variants (RF-Gini and RF-Entropy), and XGBoost. The primary evaluation uses a prepared CICIDS2017 development subset comprising 78,437 observations and 15 traffic classes. An additional dataset-specific evaluation uses a prepared CICIoT2023 subset comprising 99,327 observations, 34 traffic classes, and 39 numerical predictors. The experimental framework includes data preprocessing, mutual information-based feature selection, training-only minority-class oversampling, stratified outer cross-validation, and inner out-of-fold optimization of classifier fusion weights. The supplementary materials are intended to support verification of the reported experimental configurations and results. The original complete source-scanning log and sampling-run metadata for CICIoT2023 are unavailable; therefore, exact independent reconstruction of the original sampling run has not been established. These materials accompany the third-round revised manuscript submitted to the journal.
tags: Network Intrusion Detection; CICIDS2017; CICIoT2023; XGBoost; Weighted Soft Voting; Machine Learning; Reproducibility

summary: This paper studies all-to-all broadcast scheduling for underwater swarms with collision-resilient physical layers that can decode asynchronously overlapping packets. Propagation-aware collision-free schedulers coordinate packet arrivals but do not account for this reception capability. We first design a data-driven neural reception model that captures per-interferer power and timing effects. The model improves prediction accuracy over SINR baselines while admitting an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The resulting neural-network-embedded MILP (NN-MILP) optimizes transmission times while explicitly encoding schedule-dependent overlaps and the predictor's inference, enabling globally optimal scheduling for small-scale instances. For larger networks, a two-stage ant colony optimization (ACO) heuristic combines low-cost transmission-order search with neural-aware timing refinement. Simulation results show that ACO shortens broadcast rounds compared with existing schedulers. It approaches the NN-MILP optimum on small-scale instances while supporting larger networks at substantially lower computational cost.
title: Collision-Resilient All-to-All Broadcast Scheduling in Underwater Acoustic Networks

summary: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.
title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer

summary: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.
title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels

summary: The proliferation of maritime activities has spurred the emergence of numerous computation-intensive and delay-sensitive marine applications and services. Given the inherent rationality, selfish nature, and limited computational abilities of marine devices, devising effective strategies to incentivize their participation in task processing become a critical challenge. In this paper, we investigate the satellite-assisted marine multi-access edge computing (MEC) and propose a two-tier task offloading scheme through a hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining game approach to enhance offloading efficiency and maximize the utility of marine devices. Specifically, for the underwater acoustic communication, we consider the scenario where multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), managed by maritime autonomous surface ships (MASSs), upload their collected data using non-orthogonal multiple access(NOMA) to optimize channel utilization. For the data transmission above the sea surface, we consider the scenario where a low earth orbit satellite (LEOS) functions as a space edge server to provide computing services, and MASS offloads workloads to LEOS through frequency division multiple access(FDMA) to prevent co-channel interference. we define the utility of AUVs, MASSs and LEOSs, and model the offloading process between AUVs and MASSs as a Stackelberg game, while representing the offloading interaction between MASSs and LEOSs as a Bargaining game. Additionally, we propose efficient algorithms to optimize AUV offloading strategies and MASS pricing strategies, while refining the bidding strategies for both MASSs and LEOSs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly outperform benchmark schemes in achieving optimal solutions.
title: Two-Tier Task Offloading for Satellite-Assisted Marine Networks: A Hybrid Stackelberg-Bargaining Game Approach

summary: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.
title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels

MINIMUM NECESSARY ASSISTANCE IN STROKE REHABILITATION AT THE LIMIT F086-F090 | A FIVE-FLAGSHIP SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK | 33 x STARLI STATUS: prospective nonclinical research design, synthetic numerical examples, not an experiment with patients and not an established clinical effect. A LETTER FROM THE RESEARCH GENERATION A successful assisted action is an astonishingly incomplete explanation. The hand may rise because a person acts, because a robot lifts, because an elastic interface returns stored energy, or because the observer failed to record a missing contact force. When support has been removed, the original appearance of success can disappear without contradiction: the two tests were measuring different capacities. This notebook begins by giving that distinction the dignity of a research problem rather than quietly merging it into a single performance score. The integrated F086-F090 family proposes five mechanisms. First, assistance must be minimized under safety and accuracy constraints. Next, an independent force audit must distinguish who performed the work. Then withdrawal timing becomes an intervention, not an inconvenience. A fourth study asks whether observed movement is actively generated or passively imposed. Finally, a blinded device-off and unfamiliar-task probe asks what remains without the apparatus. All these studies can be falsified on an inert mechanical-hand bench or an offline synthetic replay platform. They do not constitute a clinical evaluation. Our five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is an intellectual strategy: lock the origin of the question, formalize candidate relations, allow a rival causal world, discover limits through safe bounded stress, and transfer the contradiction to a future laboratory. The phrase names branches of scientific interpretation, not physical travel between timelines. The longer this book survives, the more likely its apparatus will seem primitive. A valuable manuscript should let tomorrow's investigator explain exactly why it became obsolete. FOURTEEN RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | The decisive difference: assisted success versus retained ability A robot can move an object smoothly with an inactive motor proxy. The key question is not whether an assisted task is completed but whether a blinded, device-off and preferably untrained endpoint remains afterward. This manuscript is a prospective nonclinical research design; neither the synthetic results nor the labels demonstrate rehabilitation efficacy. A representative unresolved case is task complexity and the hidden easy-trial bias. Its candidate is to find the least robot-applied effort consistent with an explicitly bounded task error and mechanical safety envelope while isolating task complexity and the hidden easy-trial bias. Investigators should replay the same trajectory under a classical deadband controller, with independent measurement of minimal feasible external work [J] and tracking error [mm]. An ordinary comparison using fixed low-gain impedance control; conventional assist-as-needed deadband; transparent force-threshold policy is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 02 | Five flagships, five separate falsifiers F086 asks how little robot force is feasible. F087 investigates who supplied work. F088 challenges the timing of withdrawal. F089 distinguishes active effort from passive displacement. F090 defines the off-device functional witness. Each hypothesis is permitted to fail independently. A representative unresolved case is force uncertainty at the switching threshold. Its candidate is to find the least robot-applied effort consistent with an explicitly bounded task error and mechanical safety envelope while isolating force uncertainty at the switching threshold. Investigators should hold task complexity fixed during an assistance sweep, with independent measurement of minimal feasible external work [J] and tracking error [mm]. An ordinary comparison using fixed low-gain impedance control; conventional assist-as-needed deadband; transparent force-threshold policy is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 03 | A reproducible phantom, not a human experiment The minimal system is an unloaded mechanical-hand motion workbench and synthetic voluntary-effort generator. We define inert virtual commands, calibrated load-cell proxies and held-out object trajectories. No human participant is controlled or treated; clinical generalization would require a separate ethics-approved design. A representative unresolved case is who performed the work at the handle. Its candidate is to identify the independent contributions of proxy self-generated work, robotic work and passive environmental dissipation while isolating who performed the work at the handle. Investigators should reconstruct work from force-displacement samples before seeing labels, with independent measurement of attributed voluntary-proxy work [J], robot work [J], and residual energy [J]. An ordinary comparison using classical inverse dynamics; independent load-cell work balance; a constrained least-squares work observer is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 04 | When helpful assistance becomes a confound Assistance can both improve a task and contaminate what task performance seems to tell us. If the actuator supplies nearly all work, a high success rate may simply quantify the actuator. F086 fixes task demands and safety while searching for the minimal possible support. A representative unresolved case is co-contraction as a measurement confound. Its candidate is to identify the independent contributions of proxy self-generated work, robotic work and passive environmental dissipation while isolating co-contraction as a measurement confound. Investigators should compare a robot-only run against a proxy-driven run, with independent measurement of attributed voluntary-proxy work [J], robot work [J], and residual energy [J]. An ordinary comparison using classical inverse dynamics; independent load-cell work balance; a constrained least-squares work observer is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 05 | The missing energy must go somewhere F087 decomposes input work, robot work, source work and dissipation. Double counting or an uncalibrated friction term can manufacture an apparent personal contribution. Independent sensors are necessary; agreeing estimates from one shared calibration chain do not constitute two witnesses. A representative unresolved case is the counterfactual robot-only trajectory. Its candidate is to identify the independent contributions of proxy self-generated work, robotic work and passive environmental dissipation while isolating the counterfactual robot-only trajectory. Investigators should audit a discrepancy in the integrated energy ledger, with independent measurement of attributed voluntary-proxy work [J], robot work [J], and residual energy [J]. An ordinary comparison using classical inverse dynamics; independent load-cell work balance; a constrained least-squares work observer is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 06 | Withdrawal is a scientific intervention F088 turns support removal into a randomized, preregistered experiment. Fixed schedules, support history, fatigue and unobserved practice may masquerade as adaptation. A truly informative test survives the surprise of the next off stage; a failed stage is counted rather than explained away. A representative unresolved case is washout duration and persistent support memory. Its candidate is to control the timing and dose of a staged or randomized withdrawal while exposing dependency on the support signal while isolating washout duration and persistent support memory. Investigators should measure what survives on a previously unseen object, with independent measurement of withdrawal-stage task error [mm], recovery latency [s], and retained off-device score [points]. An ordinary comparison using fixed linear taper; scheduled catch trials; dose-matched continuous assistance with a standard feedback rule is entitled to overturn the preferred model. The question is not resolved by a synthetic plot or by naming a more complicated controller. 07 | Movement does not equal participation F089 considers a passive limb moved by a capable actuator. Its movement trace may be indistinguishable from a weak active contribution. An independent effort proxy, lag record and force partition can challenge the interpretation; even those remain imperfect surrogates for volitional human action. A representative unresolved case is the minimum period that reveals dependency. summary: This preprint evaluates a reversible sample mapping that embeds 8-bit RGB values in the central half of a 9-bit sRGB code space before lossy JPEG XL encoding. The stored file includes a five-byte header that identifies the inverse mapping. The evaluation covers 41 previously unused CLIC Professional and DIV2K validation images at their original resolutions. Under common RGB PSNR and MS-SSIM floors and a single-thread encoding cap of 0.82 seconds per megapixel, the centered mapping reduced aggregate file size by 6.71% relative to direct JPEG XL at effort 6 (95% bootstrap interval: 3.85% to 9.86%). The centered files were 3.94% larger in aggregate than the tested AVIF files. Same-depth and transfer-function controls, together with libjxl coding counters, examine how the input representation affects the result.
title: Centered Sample-Range Remapping at JPEG XL Effort 6

But the bridge is only useful when we know what went into the decoder. An electrode voltage is a mixture of cortical, muscle, eye, reference and environmental processes. A task label may record what was instructed rather than what was imagined. A camera can record what moved but not what a person intended. This family treats those distinctions as independent scientific objects, not inconvenient details. The five flagship questions are coupled without being identical. F081 asks whether EEG adds information about spontaneous motor intention after cue clocks and residual muscle activity are accounted for. F082 distinguishes imagery, attempted movement and overt displacement with independent electromyographic and visual witnesses. F083 measures what remains stable across recording days. F084 resists the temptation to hide weak-signal and rare-class strata in a pooled score. F085 observes the safety consequences of false intention triggers during long periods of silence. The minimal platform is an anonymous, synthetic EEG-EMG-EOG task replayer with inert video coordinates, frozen event timestamps and a virtual command queue. The test generator can provide a hidden latent state to evaluate conditional identification. The model never sees that latent state during inference; it must work from the channels and timing evidence available at the specified decision moment. This is a deliberate computational thought experiment and nonclinical engineering proposal, not a physical experiment on stroke survivors. Several rival accounts deserve equal space. Cue onset may encode movement class because the task schedule is regular. Eye motion may precede an instruction. EMG can influence scalp electrodes before obvious displacement occurs. A test-day montage can reveal which session generated a signal. A preprocessing transform can learn the distribution or labels of the held-out partition. A fair protocol separates these shortcuts from useful cortical information with interventions that are physically or informationally interpretable. The real methodological enemy is the persuasive but under-identified success. A model can predict a motor class accurately without identifying voluntary intent. A classifier can distinguish imagery from actual movement using residual muscle activity, not imagination. A transfer algorithm can report stable day-to-day performance after silently adapting on test-day labels. A strong subgroup average can hide dangerous errors among weak signals. Even a correctly predicted category cannot justify a virtual or physical action without authorization and a safety envelope. Prediction and clinical recovery are separate propositions. The current manuscript does not study human participants, deliver rehabilitative interventions or report therapeutic efficacy. Device-driven motion is not device-off recovery. A physical, clinically authorized program would need separate ethical review, independent recruitment, preregistered outcomes and direct functional observation. Our synthetic graphs, however detailed, cannot stand in for that evidence. The most useful classical competitors should not be artificially weak. Cue-only prediction tests whether the experiment provided all the information needed. CSP-LDA, regularized logistic models, Riemannian covariance methods and explicit EMG-video rules can challenge a complex learner with equal data access. Calibration, preprocessing, sensor count, trial duration and temporal alignment all form part of cost. A negative finding can reveal the true measurement limit more effectively than an elaborate but unearned claim of superiority. A scientific three-dimensional plate is a way to expose a functional relationship, not to ornament it. Each surface in the PDF is computed from a documented analytic rule on an exact numeric grid. The five-stage parallel spacetime method provides a language for organizing scientific alternatives. Origin questions define the unknown, formal models specify the proposed mechanism, counterfactual branches give rivals room to win, bounded extreme scenarios locate failure, and successor reconstruction transfers the case to a new laboratory. The third constructs unfamiliar but bounded artifact worlds. The fourth gives an independent laboratory the raw history needed to rebuild a result. summary: We formulate a finite-core vorton representation of three-dimensional incompressible Navier– Stokes flow. Smooth divergence-free vorticity fields are represented by finite-core filamentary modes and studied in the limit of decreasing core scale. The singular vorton configuration is obtained strictly as a distributional concentration limit rather than imposed a priori as a singular solution. We prove dynamical equivalence by mapping the infinite-dimensional Navier–Stokes partial differential equations exactly onto the finite-dimensional ordinary differential equations of the discrete vorton ensemble. The passage through the nonlinear convective term is established via Mosco-type energy convergence and Aubin–Lions–Simon compactness. Topological reconnection supplies a microscopic writhe-to-twist transfer to regularize the ultraviolet limit, while a Fredholm boundary reconstruction controls wall interactions via weakly singular integral operators. The resulting framework proves that the continuum flow collapses onto an irreducible, compact geometric attractor, reducing global regularity to a uniform bound on vorticity and satisfying the Beale–Kato–Majda (BKM) criterion for global continuation.
title: RIGOROUS CONVERGENCE OF 3D NAVIER–STOKES TO A VORTON ATTRACTOR

Prospective, nonclinical, reconstructable and falsifiable. No completed clinical experiment or quantum hardware advantage is asserted. 33 x STARLI | White Rainbow Era THE SECOND SCIENTIFIC VOICE: WHY THE SWARM MUST BE ALLOWED TO FAIL Perhaps the most attractive image in microrobotics is a swarm moving as a single body. What the image does not reveal is what the particles know, which fields act upon them, which unit was lost, and which commanding intelligence had authority to decide the next motion. This notebook follows the scientific difficulty that starts where the visualization ends. It asks how a candidate local rule becomes a physically identifiable mechanism rather than a label assigned to any coherent animation. A convincing answer would need an independently metered actuation field, a sealed task definition, a tracked population and a competing ordinary explanation that could win. F066 begins with the neighbor graph. It asks whether local exchange can account for coordination after controlling for a common magnetic field. F067 asks whether an optimizer has delivered the work it was assigned, or quietly reduced the roster of obligations. F068 treats contact avoidance as a physical permission boundary rather than a penalty term in a solver. F069 examines the unit that never returned after a fault, even when throughput recovered. F070 holds the entire argument in a contest with well-tuned classical algorithms, full input and output timing, energy use and a separate laboratory. These five subjects cannot be collapsed into a single optimization metric without losing their causal differences. All five topics share a strict nonclinical boundary. Inert microrobots or calibrated substitutes in sealed microchannels can be used to develop hypotheses about coordination and actuation. An ex-vivo specimen requires separate authorization and does not establish implanted-device safety. A controller can generate physically interesting robot motion without helping a person who has experienced stroke. Evidence of neural intention decoding, effective assistance and unaided recovery belongs to separate, properly governed experiments. The integration imagined here is a research roadmap; it is not a report of achieved human benefit. The phrase five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning describes a plural research method, not a physical capability. We begin with a physical origin, encode a candidate model, step into an adversarial alternative world, stress the proposed mechanism at a bounded extreme, and converge only on the evidence that another laboratory can reconstruct. Each stage prevents a preferred algorithm from becoming immune to disagreement. The most important gain may be that a scientist can close one research round with a precise unanswered question, rather than polishing an unsupported claim into apparent completeness. A quantum-inspired controller often runs on ordinary classical machinery. Binary energy functions, quantum-like annealing vocabularies and Ising encodings do not establish access to quantum processors. Nor does a shorter internal solver time prove a faster physical task. Encoding, task ingestion, movement authorization, magnetic actuation, field calibration and retrieval all consume resources. Classical consensus, auctions, mixed-integer programming and model-predictive methods can be exceptionally strong competitors when carefully tuned. The design must let them win and must say so without embarrassment. The most severe oversight in long research works is not merely verbal repetition; it is a loss of the difference between hypotheses. Here the 82 chapters therefore have specific mechanisms, measured quantities, rival explanations and hidden stressors. Their six pages move from physical identification to mathematics, independent observation, fair competition, bounded adverse worlds and successor handoff. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE MICROROBOT LOCALIZATION RESEARCH Every localization experiment starts with an apparent certainty: the sensor produces numbers and the plotted bead seems to move. Yet magnetic field is not position. The sensing surface has its own alignment, laser drift, microwave response, reference coordinates and background fields. In this notebook we follow the difficult passage from quantum magnetic measurement through physical identifiability, independent motion standards, correlated fusion and finally a valid decision not to act when uncertainty is too large. The result is a program of tests, not a claimed completed biomedical device. Five flagships examine different failure paths within the same sealed bench world. F061 targets the inverse map from magnetic response to bead location. F062 investigates whether shape-changing 4D material and its actuator corrupt the sensing channel. F063 disentangles true micromotion from colored noise, flow and vibration. F064 asks what evidence magnetic-optical fusion really adds without leaking optical ground truth. F065 makes sensing costs, deadline misses, installation footprint and rejected trials part of the conclusion. Coupling them requires interface-specific measurement, not exchanging the word quantum among chapters. The genealogy is deliberately bounded. The four-dimensional microrobot source describes physical stimulation, tracking limitations, material fatigue and bench discipline. The independent BCI stroke atlas studies motor intent, assistance and the strict distinction between device-on success and device-off function. The 200 flagship blueprint designates localization as the family interface. None is proof that a quantum-tracked 4D medical microrobot has been safely deployed in a human body or contributed to rehabilitation. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning names five complementary scientific viewpoints: physical origin, mathematical evolution, counterfactual rivalry, bounded extreme challenge and evidence convergence. Their value lies in preventing a favorite sensor diagram from being insulated against an ordinary explanation. No claim is made about traveling between physical universes, nor about a measured speed or quantum advantage in producing these texts. Published diamond nitrogen-vacancy studies (DOI: 10.1002/adsr.202400108; DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevApplied.21.064010) establish working quantum magnetometry and motivate engineering tests of sensor footprints, readout sensitivity and temperature dependence. A 2026 photonic-integrated sensor-array paper (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-73701-0) also considers microscale magnetic localization, with a microrobot tracking result in simulation. These publications provide physically real background but do not establish the assembled family-level architecture or a specific application success. A synthetic illustration in this notebook must be read as a thought experiment with explicit numbers, not as a chart of measured performance. The strongest criticism of a precise location is that the reference coordinate itself may have moved. A magnetic signal might respond to a stronger bead moment rather than shorter distance; a camera may track the same fiducial used to align the magnetic sensor; a deformed substrate can move the magnetometer head; common temperature drift may persuade both channels to agree falsely. The rival mechanisms have their own falsifiable signals, not merely verbal objections. Their role is to decide whether the claimed physical phenomenon is distinguishable at all. An honest budget includes what the instrument needs before its first useful estimate: lasers, electronics, clocks, shielding, calibration, replacement sensors and the complete physical reference setup. High magnetic sensitivity can be a real achievement without proving a superior microrobot control system. If the proposed quantum head loses a matched experiment to a Hall sensor, calibrated camera or classical filter, the result may still reveal the physical threshold below which added complexity is justified. Research Gates are not footnotes to a completed narrative. They ask how a successor could make the present interpretation fail with a concealed but safe physical perturbation. A stationary bead under a changing background can become a decisive experiment. A correctly refused command may be more valuable than a fabricated trajectory. The notebook is therefore the second argumentative face of the monograph: it preserves uncertain reasoning, contested choices and the practical possibility of turning a negative observation into the next instrument. The relevant physical endpoints are held-out three-dimensional localization error [um], magnetic sensitivity [nT/sqrt(Hz)] and complete power [W]. A blinded test should blindly add calibrated background-field noise while fixing the magnetic bead position. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a chain across inverse sensing, actuator interference, movement discrimination, fusion and resource auditing without importing one another's evidence. F062 | Quantum Sensor Integration with 4D Microrobots at the Limit This flagship examines coupling a deformable 4D actuator geometry with an independently referenced magnetic sensor without corrupting its readout. The relevant physical endpoints are actuation-to-sensing cross-talk [nT], post-deformation localization error [um] and actuator field [mT]. A blinded test should introduce concealed deformation cycles and map the induced parasitic magnetic field. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a chain across inverse sensing, actuator interference, movement discrimination, fusion and resource auditing without importing one another's evidence. F063 | Motion-Noise Separation in Quantum Microrobot Sensing at the Limit This flagship examines distinguishing real magnetic-bead displacement from vibration, platform motion, field drift and colored sensing noise. The relevant physical endpoints are motion amplitude [um], spectral density [nT/sqrt(Hz)], velocity error [um/s] and missed-motion rate [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a band-pass filter, mechanical vibration or timing cue creates false movement estimates. A blinded test should apply separately randomized known micromotion and fixed noise with independent optical reference. Independent instruments include independent motion stage [um], accelerometer [m/s2], magnetic time series [nT], synchronized timing [ms] and raw optical reference; the ordinary comparator set comprises accelerometer-supported classical filtering, reference-channel subtraction and tuned Kalman or particle filters with identical latency and training sets. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a chain across inverse sensing, actuator interference, movement discrimination, fusion and resource auditing without importing one another's evidence. F064 | Quantum Sensing and Conventional Imaging Fusion at the Limit This flagship examines performing coordinate-consistent magnetic-optical sensor fusion under partial occlusion and correlated calibration noise. The relevant physical endpoints are fused localization RMSE [um], occlusion coverage [1], calibration residual [um] and decision latency [ms]. Independent instruments include physically separate magnetic and image fiducials [um], raw asynchronous clocks [ms], occlusion log and covariance audit; the ordinary comparator set comprises independently calibrated camera-only, magnetometer-only and joint classical fusion systems with the same decision clock. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a chain across inverse sensing, actuator interference, movement discrimination, fusion and resource auditing without importing one another's evidence. F065 | Localization Accuracy and Sensing Cost in Quantum Microrobotics at the Limit This flagship examines jointly evaluating localization precision, integration time, photon and electrical budgets, lifetime cost and sensor availability. The relevant physical endpoints are position error [um], full-chain energy [J], amortized cost [currency/accepted trial] and deadline misses [1]. A blinded test should preregister acquisition, calibration, cooling, optical readout, compute and replacement costs in every completed trial. These are candidate research tasks, not completed experiments. The five contracts form a chain across inverse sensing, actuator interference, movement discrimination, fusion and resource auditing without importing one another's evidence.

summary: Routing-driven timely data collection in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) is crucial for marine environmental monitoring, disaster warning, and underwater resource exploration, etc. However, harsh underwater conditions, including high delays, limited bandwidth, and dynamic topologies, make efficient routing decisions challenging in UASNs. In this paper, we propose a smart interrupted routing scheme for UASNs to address dynamic underwater challenges. We first model underwater noise influences from real underwater routing features, e.g., turbulence and storms. We then propose a Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-based Interrupted Software-defined UASNs Reinforcement Learning (ISURL) framework, which ensures adaptive routing through dynamical failure handling (e.g., energy depletion of sensor nodes or link instability) and real-time interrupted recovery. Based on ISURL, we propose the MA-MAPPO algorithm, integrating multi-head attention mask mechanism with MAPPO to filter out infeasible actions and streamline training. Furthermore, to support interrupted data routing in UASNs, we introduce MA-MAPPO\_i, MA-MAPPO with interrupted policy, to enable smart interrupted routing decisions in UASNs. The evaluations demonstrate that our proposed routing scheme achieves exact underwater data routing decisions with faster convergence speed and lower routing delays than existing approaches.
title: Smart Interrupted Routing Based on Multi-head Attention Mask Mechanism-Driven MARL in Software-defined UASNs

TRUSTWORTHY QUANTUM AI FOR REHABILITATION RESEARCH F076-F080 | SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION Prospective | Nonclinical | Falsifiable | Reproducible | Unbuilt Research Concepts 33 x STARLI OPENING ESSAY | THE AUTHORITY A MODEL DOES NOT HAVE A predictive score is a statement about a model conditional on the data and assumptions that produced it. It is not evidence that the model has identified a causal neural mechanism. It is not permission to issue a physical command. It is not a clinical outcome. This family studies the boundaries between those three categories. The central object is a synthetic offline audit environment, designed so that the model may succeed, the ordinary rival may win, or a safety policy may correctly refuse the request. Five separate flagship questions meet at the same test bench. F076 tests the intervention fidelity of explanations; F077 asks whether unfamiliar inputs can be recognized before acceptance; F078 audits the source lineage and disparate failures that can manufacture attractive evaluation scores; F079 gives authorization a separate and explicit place in the decision path; F080 measures the usefulness of quantum-labelled computation after whole-pipeline cost. Each flagship has its own failure conditions. Their coupling is useful only if interfaces are causal, auditable and independently replaceable. Interpretability is especially vulnerable to beautiful output. Heatmaps, feature masks and counterfactual diagrams can look precise while merely expressing local correlation or an approximate post hoc surrogate. A serious explanatory claim tells the next investigator which feasible feature intervention will change the prediction and which independent witness can confirm it. A neural feature that was never intervened on cannot be declared causal from the color of a plot. Distribution shifts change the meaning of confidence. The familiar recording can be transformed by a new electrode montage, a different clock, an unknown class or missing-channel patterns. A detector that recognizes only the noise signatures on which it was trained may appear successful while failing precisely where a reliable refusal is needed. This is why F077 preserves selective risk, coverage, false acceptance and the full latency of the veto, not just aggregate classification accuracy. Leakage often survives a superficial audit. A synthetic source can be transformed into many nearly identical examples. The copied signals may receive new filenames, be presented as a different session or pass through a normalization fitted on the entire dataset. A high score on this partition does not demonstrate that the proposed quantum model has learned generalizable neural dynamics. F078 requires source ancestry, label availability at inference time, group balance and versioned data contracts before model comparison. Human authorization has a different grammar from prediction. A permission token may be valid for one task and forbidden for another; a model version may change while a previously signed policy does not. An operator may revoke consent after inference begins. These are not situations to be resolved by increasing confidence thresholds. A correct engineering design makes the action envelope an intersection of scope, role, time and safety, independently auditable after both successful and refused requests. In this book the commands remain inert simulations. Quantum performance remains an open empirical question for the present application. A systematic review of quantum machine learning in digital health, DOI 10.1038/s41746-025-01597-z, did not find a consistent empirical advantage over classical methods. That does not forbid the search for new architectures. It does require clean experiments. Encoding overhead, noisy operations, repeated runs, queueing, mitigation, hardware drift and classical tuning all belong to a practical utility comparison. A result below the preregistered benefit threshold must be allowed to stop the search. The five-stage parallel spacetime method organizes scientific uncertainty into origin questions, mathematical proposals, competing explanations, bounded stress worlds and independently reconstructable evidence. This phrase describes intellectual branches, not physical travel through alternative universes. The stages are most useful when a late counterfactual changes what we thought we knew at the beginning. No stage gives special permission to call a hypothesis established. A technical notebook does not repeat an entire research monograph line by line. It attempts to show why a researcher would care about an experiment, how instruments might mislead, and what interpretation could survive a fair adversary. Repeated concepts are welcome when their role deepens; recycled paragraphs masquerading as new research are not. This notebook uses Mechanism, Measurement and Refutation not as decorative labels but as obligations that make one another more exact. The research is deliberately nonclinical. It uses synthetic and authorized nonclinical proxies, inert test-bench decisions and invented stress scenarios. The proposal does not support diagnosis, implantation, robotic stroke rehabilitation or therapeutic claims. Clinical translation would require a separately approved, prospective, human-subject program with its own risk and endpoint design. Neither this document nor its figures can supply that evidence. The future reader may inherit much better hardware and different methods for causality, uncertainty or governance. If our circuits look primitive, the questions remain: what was actually measured, which part was guessed, where did the permission come from, what ordinary explanation could prevail, and who can reproduce the result? A living research civilization does not demand that its first equations remain sacred. It tries to leave an apparatus for self-correction. summary: DjangoDefects is an inter-release defect prediction benchmark for Python, built from the full version history of the Django web framework. It covers 24 consecutive releases (1.0 to 5.2, September 2008 to April 2025). For every release it provides defect labels at four granularities, all derived from a single SZZ run: - File level: 20,442 file-release instances, 32.0% buggy - Method level: 169,744 function and method instances with their source code, 9.8% buggy - Line level: 14,917 buggy source lines - AST-node level: 5.38 M nodes from a full DFS traversal of each affected file's AST, with typed parent edges (ready to load as a graph), 1.29% buggy A source snapshot of every release is included. All file paths, method spans, line numbers and node spans refer to the code exactly as it shipped in that release. Construction. 5,585 closed, fixed Bug tickets from Django's Trac issue tracker were linked to 4,801 fix commits through Fixed #<ticket> references. Each fix was traced back to the commits that introduced the bug using SZZ Unleashed, with whitespace-insensitive blame and whitespace and comment filters, giving 6,306 bug records. Fixes that only add code, such as a missing check, change no existing line that blame could trace. Each one is attributed instead to the nearest code line above the insertion point. This adds 1,914 bug records, which label files and methods only. Releases are assigned by git ancestry rather than by date, which accounts for Django forking each stable branch months before the release tag. Buggy lines are located in each release snapshot by blame identity. Contents. - file_level.zip, method_level.zip, line_level.zip, ast_level.zip: one CSV per release - source_code.zip: every file under django/ at each release tag - code.zip: the pipeline that generated the dataset, the cached ticket-to-commit links, and instructions for reproducing it - README.md: full documentation, including schemas, statistics and threats to validity Intended uses. - Cross-version defect prediction at file and method level - Fine-grained defect localisation at line and AST-node level - Training models that use code structure, such as graph neural networks on the ASTs or code language models on method source Known limitations. - Labels for the most recent releases (about 5.0 to 5.2) are incomplete, because many of their bugs have not been reported or fixed yet. - File and method labels cover every release in which a bug is present. Line and node labels cover only the release that introduced it. - Labels from fixes that only add code are a heuristic. The anchor line can be older than the bug itself, so these bugs may start a few releases too early. They are marked label_source = added_only and can be filtered out. - See README.md §7 for the other threats to validity. Changes in 2.0.0. Fixes that only add code now label files and methods, which adds 746 buggy file-release instances and 2,474 buggy method-release instances. A new label_source column (removed / added_only) in the file- and method-level CSVs marks where each label comes from. Keeping only rows with label_source = removed reproduces the 1.0.0 labels exactly. The line, AST-node and source-code files are unchanged. Licence. The labels, documentation and code are released under CC BY 4.0. The included Django source code is © Django Software Foundation and individual contributors, redistributed under its BSD-3-Clause licence (LICENSE-DJANGO).
title: DjangoDefects: A Multi-Granularity SZZ-Labeled Defect Dataset for Python

summary: MDPSolver 0.12.0 Faster, with less memory : the transition probabilities are now stored in compressed sparse rows (CSR) and read by direct loops, and each sum is split over four partial sums. Large models given as arrays solve 9–12× faster end to end than with 0.11.0, with 3.4–4.6× less peak memory. On one thread, value iteration is 2.4–3.6× faster on models with many next states per state and action. Against pymdptoolbox, MDPSolver is now up to 719× faster with policy iteration, 407× with modified policy iteration and 6.2× with value iteration (see the wiki page Performance experiments ). New: NumPy arrays as input : every input format of mdp() accepts NumPy arrays, and lists still work. As arrays, every state has the same number of actions, and tranMatProbs / tranMatColumns pad state-action pairs with fewer entries with the probability 0. As lists, or in the elementwise formats, states may still have different numbers of actions. New: float32 transition probabilities : transition probabilities given as float32 are kept as float32, which takes 8 instead of 12 bytes per non-zero probability. Rounded to float32, the probabilities of a state and action sum to 1 only to within about 1e-7. That can take the solver more iterations, and limits the tolerance it can reach under the average reward criterion. New: NPY files : rewardsFromFile and tranMatFromFile read NumPy .npy files, recognised by the .npy extension, straight into the solver, so the model is never held in Python. The files hold the elementwise rows ( [state, action, reward] and [from_state, action, to_state, probability] ) as float64, float32, int64 or int32. A model with 1 billion non-zero transition probabilities loads in 19 seconds, instead of 9 minutes from CSV files, with the same peak memory. CSV files work as before. See the wiki page Loading models from NPY files . New: Python threads : solve() lets other Python threads run while it computes, so models in several threads are solved at the same time. Calls on one model object still run one at a time. Bug fix : CSV files with more than 2^31 (about 2.1 billion) lines overflowed the loader's line counter, which made errors name wrong line numbers. Outputs : getPolicy() and getValueVector() now return NumPy arrays (int64 and float64) instead of lists. Dependency : NumPy is now required, and pip installs it with MDPSolver. Results : values can differ from those of 0.11.0 in the last digits (relative differences up to about 1e-14), since the sums are now added in a different order. Policies and iteration counts were unchanged in our tests. Tests : two new unit tests cover NumPy arrays and Python threads, and the import test now covers .npy files. Documentation : the README has a new performance table, with models up to 1 billion non-zero transition probabilities, and the benchmark against pymdptoolbox was rerun with the newest versions of both packages. Backward compatible with 0.11.0, except for the outputs: code that compares getPolicy() or getValueVector() with a list, passes them to json.dumps , or uses list methods on them needs .tolist() , e.g. mdl.getPolicy().tolist() . Verified across Linux, Windows, and macOS before release.
title: areenberg/MDPSolver: MDPSolver v0.12.0 Release Notes

summary: This record is the replication package for the paper "New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules" (Gustavo Pedro Ricou, Trinity College Dublin). It holds the paper and its supplement, the code that computes and checks every number they print, the hand-built evidence that no script can rebuild, and the result tables every number is computed from. Why the manuscript is archived here. The manuscript is archived with its code and data, not as a second place of publication, because the three are one object. Every number in the paper is computed from the archived result tables by the archived code, and the archived tests fail if the text and the tables disagree. So the version of record of the evidence includes the version of the text it supports, and a reader can check any sentence of the paper against the data behind it. The preprint is arXiv:2609.05584; this record is its data complement. Versions. Version v1.0.0 of this record held the first version of the preprint, a nine-sport paper on how playing time is allocated. Versions v2.0.0 and v2.0.1 hold its second version. Version v2.0.1 carries the same paper and the same numbers as v2.0.0. Its archive holds only the files the paper's builders and tests use. What the paper does. Studies of a rule change usually report one average effect. This paper asks whether a rule change reorders the leagues, in 101 leagues of seven sports. When football's substitution limit rose from three to five, the fourteen top leagues kept their order into the first season under five (rank correlation 0.89). That is about as firmly as from one ordinary season to the next. A prediction for twelve second tiers, written before their records were read, held (0.73), and they ranked like their own country's top league. Across rule changes in other sports, leagues kept their order in four of eight tests. In every sport measured, a league stayed near its place among its sport's leagues from season to season. So a rule change is best judged league by league, against each league's own seasons. What is in the files. source-v2.0.1.tar.gz : the manuscript and supplement sources with their generated tables, among them the audit of the pre-specification (paper_b/), and the files that the paper's builders and tests open, measured by a trace of their runs, as the tagged commit paper2-v2.0.1 holds them, unchanged. Those files are the pipeline's stages (src/), the tests (tests/), the builders (tools/), the hand-built evidence (data/manual/: the rule limits, the registers of pre-specified tests and an extract of the repository host's push log) and the plan of stages 361 to 368 (docs/). A README, the LICENSE, CITATION.cff and a checksum for every file (SHA256SUMS-source.txt) are added. derived-outputs-v2.0.1.tar.gz : the 156 result tables that the paper's builders and tests read, which are the minimum dataset needed to verify every claim, with a checksum for every table (SHA256SUMS-tables.txt). manuscript.pdf and supplement.pdf : the paper and its supplement, compiled from the tagged sources. SHA256SUMS.txt : the SHA-256 checksum of each of the four files above. The archives are built deterministically, with sorted entries, no owner and fixed timestamps. So a rebuild from the same tag gives the same bytes, and the checksums mean what they say. From the two archives alone, all of the paper's gate tests pass but one, which reads a third-party index of competitions that cannot be redistributed. Licence carve-out. Three different terms apply inside this record. The data compilation and the documentation are released under CC BY 4.0. The code is released under the MIT Licence, whose text is in LICENSE inside the source archive. The manuscript and supplement files (manuscript.pdf, supplement.pdf and the sources under paper_b/) are (c) the author and are expressly NOT released under CC BY, pending journal publication. The record's licence field reads CC BY 4.0 because Zenodo all
title: New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules — replication package (code, derived tables and manuscript)
