summary: Speaker representation learning is fundamental to speech processing tasks such as speaker verification and diarization. Although long-context speaker encoders can produce stable and discriminative embeddings, short-duration verification and diarization require finer-grained temporal representations. Short temporal contexts limit the available speaker evidence and make speaker identity difficult to disentangle from phonetic and acoustic variability. This creates a temporal resolution-representation reliability trade-off: speaker representations should maintain local within-speaker consistency, between-speaker discriminability and remain sensitive to speaker changes at fine temporal resolution. Accordingly, we propose a framework for reliable speaker representation learning at fine temporal resolution. FineSpeaker first constructs resolution-controllable frame-wise speaker representations through mean pooling over an adjustable n-frame window, enabling flexible control of representation granularity. It then introduces a speaker encoder with local temporal modeling that exploits short-range speaker context to improve the stability and discriminability of short-duration and frame-wise representations. Furthermore, we develop a generative disentanglement strategy for optimizing frame-level speaker representations, combining VAE-based probabilistic modeling with flow matching to characterize speaker-related variation and suppress non-speaker interference. Experiments demonstrate competitive full-utterance performance, improved fine-grained speaker verification on VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb, and strong zero-shot diarization results, highlighting the benefits of balancing temporal resolution and representation reliability.
title: FineSpeaker: Reliable Speaker Representation Learning at Fine Temporal Resolution

summary: This document describes the measurement setup, signal processing, data organization, and MATLAB file format of a database of acoustic responses measured on a Knowles Electronics Manikin for Acoustic Research (KEMAR) using the Hearpiece, a multi-microphone, multi-driver in-ear research device. The data include binaural room impulse responses (BRIRs) and Hearpiece driver responses, together with center-microphone room impulse responses and a loopback impulse response of the playback and recording system. The BRIRs cover two Hearpiece configurations, three room conditions, three independent insertions per configuration, and 24 horizontal source directions. The database supports reproducible research on binaural and hearing-device signal processing, with potential applications in speech enhancement, spatial filtering and source separation, dereverberation, active noise and occlusion control, and acoustic feedback cancellation. The database, MATLAB loading script, and technical documentation are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667308.
title: The Hearpiece Database of Binaural Room Impulse Responses and Driver Responses on KEMAR

summary: This paper studies the capability of an object-centric audio representation to support multiple downstream tasks within a unified framework. The object-centric model is trained in a self-supervised setup using slot attention by reconstructing Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) patch embeddings from a set of latent slots. It is trained on synthetic audio mixtures, which provides controlled multi-source audio scenes. These slot representations are evaluated for the classification, detection, and separation of sound events by training task specific output layers. On the classification task, the model achieves an F1-score of 0.8, comparable to clip-level AST embeddings which achieve 0.7. For sound event detection, it reaches a macro F1-score of 0.7, outperforming clip-level AST embeddings at 0.4 and matching AST patch embeddings at 0.7, which encode finer time-frequency information. In source separation, it achieves an SI-SDR improvement (SI-SDRi) of 18.4 dB. Furthermore, in a zero-shot source separation setting, the model achieves an SI-SDRi of 14.5 dB. These results demonstrate that slot-based representations capture transferable and compositional structure in audio scenes, enabling generalization across tasks and datasets.
title: Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representation for Multi-Task Audio Analysis

summary: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feature distillation with text and click conditioning, and then fine-tune the separator using the adapted visual features. We also introduce an on-screen interference setting, where both the target and interferer are visible, to evaluate target selectivity. Experiments on standard benchmarks and the on-screen interference setting demonstrate consistent improvements in separation quality and target selectivity, particularly for mixtures containing semantically similar sources.
title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation

summary: Many real-world signals are corrupted by localized, structured perturbations whose distribution is unknown: an intermittent background noise in a music recording, a watermark stamped on a photograph, a cast shadow. We study the task of recovering a clean signal $x$ from an observation $y$ containing such a localized out-of-distribution (OOD) corruption. We propose Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion, SORD, an iterative algorithm to recover $x$ using only two ingredients: a binary map of the corruption support and a single diffusion model pretrained on clean signals. SORD does not require any paired data or any statistical model of the corruption. We evaluate SORD on natural images and human faces with spatially localized corruptions including handwritten digits, other images, watermarks, and shadows, as well as audio recordings of different musical instruments with temporally localized corruptions including other instruments and human speech. SORD is competitive with, and often outperforms, posterior-sampling inpainting given the same diffusion prior and the same mask, source-separation baselines that require a separate diffusion model for each source, and, on several benchmarks, supervised networks trained on paired clean and corrupted signals. The code is released here: \href{https://github.com/voilalab/SORD}{https://github.com/voilalab/SORD}.
title: Support-guided OOD Removal with Diffusion

summary: Generative target speaker extraction (TSE) models achieve high-quality extraction, but suffer from considerably slow training convergence. Representation Alignment (REPA) accelerates diffusion transformer training by aligning hidden states with a pre-trained Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) teacher. However, existing alignment in the speech and audio domain operates at a single granularity. For TSE, frame-level alignment leaves the global, time-invariant characteristics of the target speech implicit, whereas utterance-level alignment leaves the time-varying content implicit, even though extracting the target requires both. We propose Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment (MG-REPA), aligning the hidden states with an SSL model at the frame level and a speaker verification model at the utterance level. We further apply temporal normalization to the frame-level target, removing its utterance-level statistics so that each branch concentrates on its granularity. On Libri2Mix, MG-REPA reaches the OVRL and PESQ of a MeanFlow-TSE baseline with $3.0\times$ and $2.1\times$ fewer epochs, respectively. Trained for 750 epochs, it is competitive with the published 2,000-epoch baseline on intrusive metrics while improving non-intrusive metrics. An ablation demonstrates that MG-REPA outperforms alignment at a single granularity.
title: MG-REPA: Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment for Generative Target Speaker Extraction

summary: Large self-supervised speech models provide powerful representations for speaker verification, but full fine-tuning is expensive. Most conventional adapters insert small trainable modules to modify the output of each layer, while keeping the original residual connections unchanged. Building on our preliminary study of manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections in speaker encoders, we explore parameter-efficient adaptation of both residual paths and feature selection across layers. We first propose a Manifold-Constrained Residual Adapter (MCRA), which splits the hidden dimensions of each Transformer residual state into N groups and uses a small Sinkhorn-normalized matrix to exchange information among them. A learnable gate controls the balance between the original and mixed residual paths. The gate adds only one scalar parameter at each residual connection and initially favors the original path, allowing gradual adaptation. We further propose Frame-Adaptive Layer Aggregation (FALA), an attention-based aggregation method that uses a single learned query shared across all utterances to compute layer weights separately for each speech frame. Because the layer representations depend on the input, the resulting weights vary across both utterances and frames, unlike the fixed weights of a conventional layer-weighted sum. Compared with a frozen WavLM baseline using a fixed layer-weighted sum, our method achieves relative EER reductions of 22.4% on VoxCeleb1-O and 2.9% on CN-Celeb, with trainable adaptation parameters equivalent to only 0.0009% and 0.0016% of the WavLM-Large parameters, respectively.
title: Manifold-Constrained Residual Adaptation with Frame-Adaptive Layer Aggregation for Speaker Verification

summary: End-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) is a strong framework for long-form conversational diarization, where speaker embeddings are used to link local speaker decisions across windows. Conventional EEND-VC systems extract these embeddings by cutting out regions assigned to each local speaker, preferably using only non-overlapped speech. This works well when enough clean target-speaker speech is available, but it discards useful speaker evidence in overlapped regions and becomes unreliable when a local speaker appears mostly in overlap. We propose a speaker-activity-conditioned embedding extractor that adapts a pretrained WavLM-MHFA speaker verification model to extract target-speaker embeddings directly from full conversational windows. Inspired by the recently proposed diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW) model for target-speaker ASR, frame-level diarization-dependent transformations inject local speaker-activity information into intermediate WavLM representations while preserving the pretrained initialization. Experiments on multiple conversational diarization benchmarks show that fine-tuning with limited real meeting data reduces speaker-confusion errors and improves EEND-VC diarization performance. The results further indicate that real conversational data provides an effective alternative to large-scale simulated-mixture training for diarization-aware speaker embedding extraction.
title: Learning Speaker-Activity-Conditioned WavLM Speaker Embeddings with Real Conversational Data

summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) isolates a desired speaker from a multi-speaker mixture using cues that identify the target. Prior work has explored acoustic and textual cues, such as enrollment audio and different types of speaker descriptors, but typically relies on a single cue family. Yet no single cue is both broadly available and reliably discriminative. Moreover, most TSE systems adopt mask-prediction models, which are prone to audible artifacts and generalize poorly across acoustic conditions. To address these limitations, we propose PromptSep-Speaker, a generative TSE model based on latent diffusion that unifies four interchangeable cues: speaker temporal order, transcript, enrollment audio, and speaker caption. The generative formulation delivers higher separation quality and multi-modal prompting improves applicability across scenarios. To fully exploit each cue, we further introduce a frozen WavLM representation with an auxiliary alignment loss that supervises query-mixture cross-attention without extra labeling. Across four evaluation sets and a listening study, PromptSep-Speaker achieves state-of-the-art performance over TSE and universal source separation baselines, improving separation accuracy and quality across cue modalities.
title: PromptSep-Speaker: Generative Target Speaker Extraction via Multimodal Prompting and Semantic Alignment

summary: Drum beats are often conceptualized and produced as arrangements of repeated single-drum sound events or one-shots. Drum Analysis-by-Synthesis (AbS) models combine this structural assumption with reconstruction-based training to perform MIR tasks such as drum transcription, drum source separation, and one-shot extraction, offering a flexible alternative to more traditional task-specific supervision. However, leading AbS approaches struggle to generalize to a broad range of drum timbres (e.g., electronic drum kits), rely on high-quality paired audio-transcription training data, and do not model intra-class timbral variation within a single arrangement (e.g., multiple kick sounds). To overcome these limitations, we propose D-Composer, an autoregressive language modeling framework that decomposes drum recordings into labeled sound events and their onset times. In drum transcription and one-shot extraction tasks, D-Composer performs comparably to or better than a state-of-the-art AbS system and task-specific baselines while generalizing to a broader range of drum timbres. Our results demonstrate that when equipped with abundant synthetic data and compact acoustic token representations, language modeling provides a simple recipe for unifying transcription and sound event decomposition.
title: D-Composer: Language Modeling for Simultaneous Drum Transcription and Sound Event Decomposition

summary: Understanding how residue variations affect protein stability is crucial for designing functional proteins and deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying disease-related mutations. Recent advances in protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized computational protein analysis, enabling, among other things, more accurate predictions of mutational effects. In this work, we introduce JanusDDG, a deep learning framework that leverages PLM-derived embeddings and a bidirectional cross-attention transformer architecture to predict $ΔΔG$ of single and multiple-residue mutations while simultaneously being constrained to respect fundamental thermodynamic properties, such as antisymmetry and transitivity. Unlike conventional self-attention, JanusDDG computes queries (Q) and values (V) as the difference between wild-type and mutant embeddings, while keys (K) alternate between the two. This cross-interleaved attention mechanism enables the model to capture mutation-induced perturbations while preserving essential contextual information. Experimental results show that JanusDDG achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting $ΔΔG$ from sequence alone, matching or exceeding the accuracy of structure-based methods for both single and multiple mutations. Code Availability:https://github.com/compbiomed-unito/JanusDDG
title: JanusDDG: A Thermodynamics-Compliant Model for Sequence-Based Protein Stability via Two-Fronts Multi-Head Attention

summary: This record is the replication package for the paper "New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules" (Gustavo Pedro Ricou, Trinity College Dublin). It holds the paper and its supplement, the code that computes and checks every number they print, the hand-built evidence that no script can rebuild, and the result tables every number is computed from. Why the manuscript is archived here. The manuscript is archived with its code and data, not as a second place of publication, because the three are one object. Every number in the paper is computed from the archived result tables by the archived code, and the archived tests fail if the text and the tables disagree. So the version of record of the evidence includes the version of the text it supports, and a reader can check any sentence of the paper against the data behind it. The preprint is arXiv:2609.05584; this record is its data complement. Versions. Version v1.0.0 of this record held the first version of the preprint, a nine-sport paper on how playing time is allocated. Versions v2.0.0 to v2.0.2 hold its second version. Version v2.0.2 carries the same results as v2.0.0 and v2.0.1, with small changes of wording. Its archive holds only the files the paper's builders and tests use. What the paper does. Studies of a rule change usually report one average effect. This paper asks whether a rule change reorders the leagues, in 101 leagues of seven sports. When football's substitution limit rose from three to five, the fourteen top leagues kept their order into the first season under five (rank correlation 0.89). That is about as firmly as from one ordinary season to the next. A prediction for twelve second tiers, written before their records were read, held (0.73), and they ranked like their own country's top league. Across rule changes in other sports, leagues kept their order in four of eight tests. In every sport measured, a league stayed near its place among its sport's leagues from season to season. So a rule change is best judged league by league, against each league's own seasons. What is in the files. source-v2.0.2.tar.gz : the manuscript and supplement sources with their generated tables, among them the audit of the pre-specification (paper_b/), and the files that the paper's builders and tests open, measured by a trace of their runs, as the tagged commit paper2-v2.0.2 holds them, unchanged. Those files are the pipeline's stages (src/), the tests (tests/), the builders (tools/), the hand-built evidence (data/manual/: the rule limits, the registers of pre-specified tests and an extract of the repository host's push log) and the plan of stages 361 to 368 (docs/). A README, the LICENSE, CITATION.cff and a checksum for every file (SHA256SUMS-source.txt) are added. derived-outputs-v2.0.2.tar.gz : the 156 result tables that the paper's builders and tests read, which are the minimum dataset needed to verify every claim, with a checksum for every table (SHA256SUMS-tables.txt). manuscript.pdf and supplement.pdf : the paper and its supplement, compiled from the tagged sources. SHA256SUMS.txt : the SHA-256 checksum of each of the four files above. The archives are built deterministically, with sorted entries, no owner and fixed timestamps. So a rebuild from the same tag gives the same bytes, and the checksums mean what they say. From the two archives alone, all of the paper's gate tests pass but one, which reads a third-party index of competitions that cannot be redistributed. Licence carve-out. Three different terms apply inside this record. The data compilation and the documentation are released under CC BY 4.0. The code is released under the MIT Licence, whose text is in LICENSE inside the source archive. The manuscript and supplement files (manuscript.pdf, supplement.pdf and the sources under paper_b/) are (c) the author and are expressly NOT released under CC BY, pending journal publication. The record's licence field reads CC BY
title: New rules, old habits: across seven team sports, each league keeps its own way of using the rules — replication package (code, derived tables and manuscript)

summary: A georeferenced benchmark for comparing terrain-aware flood-evacuation routing methods and remotely sensed inputs in the valley below Eoeun Reservoir, Republic of Korea. The dataset combines UAV-derived land-cover predictions and a digital surface model with Sentinel-2 Level-2A predictions and Copernicus DEM GLO-30 elevations harmonized to EGM96. Two hundred fixed cases are evaluated under nine 30 m input conditions. Each case follows a start–intermediate target–shelter sequence. All 1,800 attempts are retained: 989 completed routes are provided as cell sequences and GeoJSON, and 811 input-eligibility failures carry their first reported check outcome. Thirteen GeoTIFF inputs include native UAV reference rasters at approximately 1.03 m and the derived 30 m inputs. Configurations, data dictionaries, source metadata, validation records and SHA-256 checksums support reuse on the same cases and conditions. The benchmark supports comparison of input resolution, barrier aggregation, elevation sources and route objectives. Its georeferenced outputs can be linked to subsequent field checking and evacuation-planning studies. CC BY 4.0 applies to the authors' rights; Copernicus-derived material carries the notices in NOTICE.md. The routing engine, reference and verification code, and analysis scripts may be requested from the corresponding author under separate terms. Contact: Sangik Lee (sangik@knu.ac.kr). Funding: This work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Ministry of Education (MOE) (No. RS-2026-25536642).
title: A multiresolution benchmark for terrain-aware evacuation routing

summary: This record is the replication package for the paper "Who is who: injury rates between players and within each player in professional team sports" by Gustavo Pedro Ricou and Nicholas Mahony (Trinity College Dublin). It holds the manuscript and its supplement, the pipeline that computed every number in them, the tests that fail when the text and the data disagree, and the aggregated tables the numbers are computed from. The manuscript's data availability statement cites this record. Why the manuscript is archived here. The manuscript is archived with its code and data, not as a second place of publication, because the three are one object. Every number in the paper is computed from the archived tables by the archived code. The archived tests fail if the text and the tables disagree. So the version of record of the evidence includes the version of the text it supports, and a reader can check any sentence of the paper against the data behind it. The preprint is arXiv:2608.11228 , where this paper will appear as the next version. This record is its data complement. What the paper does. Using public match records from nine team sports, with injury records for 22,573 players in six of them, the paper measures how injury rates differ between players and with recent load. Players' usual injury rates differed: between two players picked at random, the higher was typically 1.83 times the lower. Per-hour rates that compare players therefore mix recent load with who carries it. Comparing each player's heavy weeks with the same player's weeks after a longer gap needs a check by simulation first: with no effect of load at all, heavy weeks still read as riskier, because injuries lower later load. What is in the files. paperA-v1.0.0-source.tar.gz : files from the tagged commit paperA-v1.0.0. They are the manuscript, the supplement, the three checklists and the cover letter, with their numbers, tables, figures and references (paperA/); the pipeline, one numbered stage per file (src/); the tests (tests/); the builders and the scripts that collected the match records (tools/); the hand-built evidence that no script can rebuild (data/manual/); and the analysis plans, each fixed before its results were read, with the record of how each source was collected and what its terms allow (docs/). A README, the LICENSE, CITATION.cff and a checksum for every file (SHA256SUMS-source.txt) are added. paperA-v1.0.0-derived-outputs.tar.gz : the 577 derived tables and figures that the paper's numbers, tables and figures are computed from, with a checksum for every file (SHA256SUMS-derived-outputs.txt). Every number and table of the paper was rebuilt from this record alone and came out as the record holds it. paperA-v1.0.0-manuscript.pdf and paperA-v1.0.0-supplement.pdf : the paper and its online supplement, compiled from the tagged sources. SHA256SUMS.txt : the SHA-256 checksum of each of the four files above. Unpack both archives in the same folder. Each unpacks into paperA-v1.0.0/, so the derived tables land beside the code that reads them. The archives are written with sorted entries, no owner and fixed timestamps, so the same files always give the same bytes. The README in the source archive gives the steps that rebuild every number, table and figure, and then the PDFs. Personal data. The derived tables are league, season, team and model summaries, simulation results and figures. None holds a player identifier, a player's name or a row about one person. Before the archives were written, every file was checked for columns that identify a player and for players' names. What is not deposited, and why. The match records the stages read come from public providers: league and federation sites, their statistics services, Transfermarkt, Soccerdonna, FBref and others. Their terms permit the research use made here but not the redistribution of the records. The records also identify players. So they are not in this record. How each source was collected, its terms of us
title: Who is who: injury rates between players and within each player in professional team sports — replication package (code, derived tables and manuscript)

summary: all3DSignDB is a unified benchmark database for 3D online signature verification, built by merging all publicly available 3D signature databases that provide explicit (x,y,z)  coordinates: 3DIIT, captured with a Leap Motion sensor, and DeepAirSig, captured with an Intel Senz3D depth camera. The resulting database contains 120 users, 2,400 genuine signatures, and 1,266 skilled forgeries. Together with the database, a standardized evaluation protocol is provided — inspired by the SVC-OnGoing competition — including comparison files for 1vs1 and 4vs1 enrollment scenarios under both random and skilled forgery conditions. All comparison files are publicly shared to ensure reproducibility, along with a DTW-based baseline verifier, enabling fair and transparent comparison across future 3D signature verification systems. If you are using this database in your research, please cite the following paper: Moises Diaz, Cristian Rodriguez, Gabriel Ojeda-Suarez, Miguel A. Ferrer, "all3DSignDB: A Unified Database and Benchmark for 3D Signature Verification," 58th IEEE International Carnahan Conference on Security Technology (ICCST 2026), Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, 14-16 October 2025, pp. 1-6..
title: all3DSignDB: A Unified Database and Benchmark for 3D Signature Verification

summary: VERSION 0.2.0. What is new in 0.2.0. The multi-criteria decision now uses eight criteria in four dimensions (technical, economic, environmental and structural), chosen so that the same water saving is not counted twice; weights can be declared per dimension or computed from the results by the CRITIC method; and the result is reported as a choice band (the volumes whose score lies within 5% of the range from the best) rather than a single 'optimal' volume. PROMETHEE II and SMAA were corrected, and the system weight (dry mass, water load, and operating load) was added. The volume the decision points to can change: a study ranked with 0.1.0 is reproduced with 0.1.0. Release notes of each edition are in the manuals and in the repository. Novidades da 0.2.0. summary: Breaking Changes InitialConditions , BoundaryForcing , TidalForcing and SurfaceForcing now raise a ValueError where regridding left NaN at ocean points, instead of silently writing 0 there; setups that built before may now fail. ( #719 ) The error names the variable and the number of such points, and suggests a likely cause. Without dask it is raised at construction; with dask it is raised at .save() , possibly after a long compute, and the files that save started are removed, including any earlier file at an output path, which the save has already truncated. bypass_validation=True restores the old behavior and writes 0 there. A ROMS-restart (nesting) initial condition whose child grid reaches the parent's edge now raises: velocities there have no parent value. Changes to Output ESPER-derived tracers are now groomed by default, so ESPER initial conditions and boundary forcing change wherever cells are flagged; pass groom=False to InitialConditions / BoundaryForcing for the raw estimates. ( #715 ) A YAML written by roms-tools 5.0–5.3 has no groom key and loads with grooming on; add groom: false to its section to skip grooming. ESPER oxygen below 5.0 mmol/m³ now reads 5.0 (previously 2.0), matching MARBL's default parm_o2_min ; there is no setting to restore 2.0. ( #715 ) Initial conditions and boundary forcing change wherever the ROMS grid is deeper than its lat/lon source or ROMS parent: tracers below the source's bottom differ, velocities do not. ( #717 ) YAML files saved by earlier versions load with the new 25 m default; setting bottom_fill_blend_m=float("inf") restores the old output for GLORYS and CESM sources. Nested initial conditions change too: #709's fixed 100 m blend and child-grid donors are replaced by the 25 m default and the parent's own columns; no setting reproduces 5.3.0's nested output, and inf gives the copy-down from before 5.3.0. BGC fields from the WOA and GLODAP climatologies change below the source's seafloor in the same way; no setting reproduces WOA's earlier deep_fill="annual_blend" values below the seafloor. ERA5 qair values change. Specific humidity now uses ERA5's surface pressure ( sp , or msl if sp is absent) instead of a fixed 1010 hPa, which biased qair by about 1% over the open ocean (usually high) and by more over land. ( #722 ) Streamed ARCO ERA5 picks up surface_pressure automatically. A local ERA5 extract with neither sp nor msl keeps the 1010 hPa value and now logs a warning. The three ERA5 physics zarr reference fixtures are regenerated ( qair only). New Features New bgc_check and bgc_groom check or groom BGC tracers in a Dataset or NetCDF file, for analysis or one-off repair; bgc_check also accepts InitialConditions / BoundaryForcing . ( #715 ) Checks cover plausible bounds, nutrients and oxygen at their floor beside ordinary water, salinity-normalized spikes, ALK/DIC consistency, and oxygen above 1.25 times saturation, which is clipped. Results are identical for any chunking or tiling. InitialConditions and BoundaryForcing take groom (default True ) and groom_settings , optional overrides of the grooming thresholds and fill parameters; both are recorded in the YAML. ( #715 ) groom_settings is validated before any regridding; unknown keys or invalid values raise. InitialConditions and BoundaryForcing take bottom_fill_blend_m , the depth (m) below the source bottom over which tracers go from the column's own bottom value to the nearest same-depth source column's value. ( #717 ) 0 takes the neighbouring column's value right below the bottom, inf copies the bottom value down, and negative or NaN values raise. The value is forwarded to BGC sources, written to the output file's attributes and kept in YAML. SurfaceForcing(source={"name": "CONUS404"}, type="physics", correct_radiation=False, use_dask=True) . summary: Overview This repository contains the Python source codes used to generate the analytical models, structural configurations, and hydro-elastic dynamic response data presented in the study on the stability and dynamic stress resilience of Concrete-Filled Tube (CFT) floating arch bridges. To ensure absolute numerical transparency and eliminate external commercial software dependencies, the stability and modal analyses are driven by a custom-built, Pure-Python 2D Finite Element Analysis (FEA) solver . The codes also integrate Mander's triaxial concrete confinement model for composite cross-sections and utilize the Capytaine Boundary Element Method (BEM) solver for time-domain stochastic wave simulations. File Descriptions Figure_1.py (Snap-through Buckling Mechanism & CFT Effect) Generates the conceptual schematic of the snap-through instability for a hollow steel arch and demonstrates the theoretical confinement-induced buckling prevention of CFT arches under fixed-end boundary conditions. Figure_2.py (Structural Configuration & Cross-Sectional Layout) Visualizes the physical geometry of the 1,000-m span floating arch bridge system. It details the dimensions of the 11 prestressed concrete pontoons and compares the cross-sectional properties of the heavily stiffened hollow steel girder versus the proposed CFT girder under matched nominal flexural rigidity ( $EI$ ). Figure_3.py (Hollow Steel Arch: Snap-Through & Modal Analysis) Executes the Pure-Python FEA solver (using Euler-Bernoulli beam elements and consistent mass matrices) to perform generalized eigenvalue analysis and trace the non-linear static equilibrium path of the conventional hollow steel arch, identifying the initial limit-point load. Figure_4.py (CFT Arch: Stability Enhancement & Modal Analysis) Extends the FEA solver to incorporate Mander's confined concrete model, calculating the physical composite stiffness ( $EA_{eff}$ , $EI_{eff}$ ). The script outputs the enhanced non-linear static equilibrium path, demonstrating a ~310% increase in the normalized critical snap-through load ( $P_{cr}/EA_s$ ) compared to the hollow steel baseline. Figure_5.py (Hydro-Elastic Dynamic Response under Stochastic Waves) Couples the analytical structural model with the Capytaine BEM solver. It calculates the 6-DOF dynamic response (RAOs) of the pontoon foundations and simulates the time-domain hydro-elastic response under irregular JONSWAP wave spectra (45° quartering and 90° beam seas), quantifying the dynamic bending stress mitigation provided by the CFT arch ribs. Dependencies & Requirements The scripts are written in Python 3. To run the codes successfully, the following libraries are required: numpy (Numerical operations and matrix assemblies) scipy (Generalized eigenvalue problem solver via scipy.linalg.eigh ) matplotlib (High-quality academic plotting and vector graphics) capytaine (Linear potential flow BEM solver for hydrodynamics - required for Figure_5.py ) Usage All scripts are provided as standalone, single-file executables. No external CSV datasets or commercial structural analysis software (e.g., Abaqus, OpenSees) are required to reproduce the exact figures presented in the manuscript. Simply execute each script in a standard Python environment to generate the corresponding high-resolution (300 DPI) .png files.
title: Source Codes for: Hydro-Elastic Snap-Through and Dynamic Analysis of CFT Floating Arch Bridges

summary: TopoALV-TP is a regional dataset of reconstructed lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage changes across the Tibetan Plateau. It was developed using the Topography-constrained Area–Level–Volume Reconstruction (TopoALV) framework, which integrates multitemporal satellite-derived lake extents, machine-learning-based depth estimation, shoreline-distance constraints, and surrounding topography. The dataset provides 64 m resolution water-depth and lakebed-elevation rasters for 1,080 lakes, together with lake-specific composite area–water-level curves and reconstructed lake area, relative water level, and storage changes for 16 observation epochs from the 1970s to 2022, referenced to the year 2000. The time-series archive contains 17,280 lake–epoch records, with missing observations explicitly retained. Additionally, the dataset includes a nominal 8 m super-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) of the Tibetan Plateau and 1,080 three-dimensional bathymetric visualizations. The archive contains GeoTIFF rasters, CSV time series, composite area–elevation curves, metadata, quality-control diagnostics, data provenance records, and processing scripts to support reproducibility and further research. Users should note that the reconstructed bathymetry and absolute lake volumes are model-derived estimates rather than comprehensive in situ measurements. Relative water-level and storage changes should be interpreted together with the provided quality flags and supported inversion ranges. The original “1970s” observation label is preserved; the numeric year 1975 is used only for chronological sorting and does not indicate an exact observation year.
title: TopoALV-TP: Terrain-constrained lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage reconstructions across the Tibetan Plateau (1970s–2022)

summary: 摘要: 主流新古典经济学以原子化个体、线性因果与均衡收敛为基本预设,在解释内生不确定性、主体互动、预期自我实现与系统非线性演化等问题时面临解释力困境;行为、复杂与演化等修正路径又因缺乏统一本体论与可复用的分析流程而呈碎片化。本文阐释量子经济学的分析方法, 提出 “叠加态识别—主体纠缠网络刻画—观测建构效应评估—系统演化路径推演”四位一体的基准分析框架。 该框架以经济系统内生的不确定性、关系性、建构性与演化性为本体论基础,将多重可能性、主体内生关联、认知建构作用与动态演化纳入统一逻辑,并给出各环节的操作路径与技术方法。通胀预期治理的整合应用表明,该框架为复杂经济问题提供了层次清晰、可迭代复用的分析工具,也为构建中国自主的经济学知识体系提供了新的方法论路径。 关键词: 量子经济学 ; 叠加态 ; 主体纠缠 ; 观测建构 ; 经济演化

summary: This report and reproducibility package develop a conditional mathematical model connecting joint-source correlations to electromagnetic receiver records. The calculation combines full numerical evolution of a retained finite-mode scalar–gauge Hamiltonian with an explicit model of transmission and measurement. Source preparations with matching individual-mode states can retain different joint correlations. Within the specified interaction, these differences transfer to the outgoing electromagnetic mode and produce receiver-accessible contrasts. A further comparison uses preparations with matching first and second moments but different higher joint correlations. Isometric nesting preserves predictions when the state, interaction and observables are transported consistently. The receiver model includes vacuum loss, reference-phase fluctuations, calibrated gain, offset and independent additive noise. Explicit equations describe the record mean, variance and probability distribution without requiring a Gaussian source state. Under common stationary calibration, three phase-resolved variances suffice to predict another variance within the declared receiver family. Reproducible numerical verification includes 177 passing source-evolution checks and 766 passing explicit receiver checks. These establish implementation consistency within the retained model. Separate measured-data comparisons retain their observed discrepancies: the primary optical GKP receiver prediction falls outside its declared ±5% tolerance. No calibration correction is fitted, and the complete source interaction is not experimentally validated. The report specifies the independent calibration, preparation and acquisition information needed for further receiver tests, together with the physical operator and coupling correspondence required for a laboratory implementation of the source model. Contributions of suitable datasets, calibration records and controlled analogue proposals are invited. The accompanying package contains the report, consolidated equations, executable code, protocols, inputs, results, verification records and provenance archives.
title: Nested Electromagnetic Source and Receiver Model

summary: Big Bang nucleosynthesis predicts about three times more primordial lithium than old metal-poor stars show, while laboratory measurements exclude a comparable reduction of the ³He(α,γ)⁷Be capture that makes most of it. Mittermeier Attractor Theory (MAT) fixes, without lithium input, a finite-support mobility M∂ = e³ρ²/(8π^(5/2)) = 0.251864, where ρ is the plastic number. We test the hypothesis that this number multiplies both directions of ³He + ⁴He ⇄ ⁷Be + γ in the primordial plasma. A common factor on a reaction and its reverse changes how fast it runs against cosmic expansion, not where its equilibrium lies; detailed balance and all conservation laws are kept. Executed in the PRIMAT network with its standard thermal history and the MAT baryon density, the hypothesis lowers primordial mass seven from (5.44 ± 0.21) × 10⁻¹⁰ to (1.472 ± 0.053) × 10⁻¹⁰ per hydrogen nucleus, against the stellar inference (1.45 ± 0.25) × 10⁻¹⁰, while deuterium and helium-4 change by less than three parts per million. A response theorem for trace products explains the result: the surviving beryllium meets almost no reverse reaction, so its yield follows the mobility nearly in proportion, and the standard solve alone predicts the modified yield to 0.04%. The effect is decided at photon temperatures of 22–58 keV, whose Gamow energies laboratory data cover closely enough to exclude any realization as a modified cross section: the mobility must be a property of the primordial plasma. The stellar comparison is retrospective; the sharp test is the ratio to standard nucleosynthesis, 0.2704 ± 0.0012, almost free of nuclear uncertainty. The microscopic map that switches the mobility on in that plasma, and nowhere else, remains open.
title: The Primordial Lithium Problem in Mittermeier Attractor Theory: Finite-Support Scaling of Reversible Reaction Kinetics

summary: Life-cycle cost comparisons for seismic retrofit are decision-useful only when loss equations are dimensionally coherent and alternatives share a consistent cost basis. This study presents a traceable audit framework and applies it to the case of a two-storey rubble stone-masonry dwelling in Greece with five reported strengthening alternatives. We recalculate base-masonry strength estimates from stated assumptions, test the reported loss arithmetic and comparison baseline, refit displacement–exceedance relations, and examine consequence-cost scaling. Two readings of one formula differ by a factor of two; neither is validated as a physical loss. Evaluating the record’s own six-step procedure on its own stated inputs finds seventeen of the twenty-two reported loss totals consistent with those inputs; of the five exceptions, four lack an identified cause and one coincides with an internal inconsistency in the reported cost table. Correcting the comparison basis lowers reported savings, and one cost-recovery conclusion changes across arithmetic readings. A separately tested, unit-explicit loss-assessment engine provides a reusable methodological tool; it does not reproduce or validate the case building’s structural model. Version note: Author proof v2, revised 6 November 2026; accepted 2 November 2026. This is an author proof and not the publisher’s final Version of Record. The ADAPT4CE project, “Adaptive digital systems for sustainable construction and material management in the circular economy” (Grant Agreement No. 101182768), supported the cross-case synthesis, reproducibility framework, visualization, and manuscript preparation reported in this article. ADAPT4CE is funded by the European Union under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Research and Innovation Staff Exchange, Horizon Europe (HORIZON-MSCA-2023-SE). Views and opinions are those of the authors only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the European Commission.
title: Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study

summary: Introduction Scott Adams’s God’s Debris: A Thought Experiment (2001) presents a fascinating hypothesis: an omnipotent and omniscient God might have destroyed itself to experience something it could not otherwise experience—nonexistence. The universe would consequently consist of God’s debris, with existence potentially representing the gradual reconstruction of divine consciousness (Adams). I propose extending this thought experiment by identifying the Big Bang as a possible physical counterpart to God’s self-destruction and the Absolute as the ultimate destination toward which individual consciousnesses might eventually return. Furthermore, investigating the universe beyond the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) might help constrain theories about the earliest state of existence and, indirectly, inform philosophical investigations of the afterlife.
title: From God's Debris to the Absolute: The Big Bang, Cosmic Origins, and the Possibility of an Afterlife

summary: Bone resorption following tooth loss is considered an obstacle for dental implant placement in desired positions, requiring bone augmentation procedures. Many techniques have been described to reconstruct horizontal alveolar ridge  defects. But one of many, platelet concentrate fibrin is considered nowadays an efficient technique in oral surgery, which is based on concentrating platelets and growth factors that is activated in fibrin gel in order to improve the healing. The aim of this review was to discuss the use of PRF in oral surgery by exposing 3 clinical cases and discussing the properties in bone tissue engineering for PRF membranes, and wound healing with bone formation for Leucocyte platelet rich fibrin (L-PRF) used as scaffold. In the 3 clinical cases bone maturation was found excellent at 5 months as seen clinically, on X-rays and CAT scans

summary: We construct a common Fourier local-norm domain for exact alternating spatial blocking and temporal decimation of an SU(3) lattice transfer model. The state consists of the current coarse action, its source- free one-time part, its full multitime and source-dependent remainder, and its scalar normalization. A two-link spatial pushforward contracts the field-dependent norm by k = e1/20/3 < 0.350424, and temporal marginalization does not increase that norm. Consequently every finite alternating iteration remains in the ball r∗ = 0.00235, with coupling radius 2 and source radius 10−4 unchanged. A direct analytic estimate gives a one-cycle Lipschitz constant below 0.431657. We prove conditional cumulant bounds under the interacting one-time reference, recertify its spatial mixing after each rebase, and preserve the generating functional of the fixed original source family. An all-order entrance certificate places a specified transfer family inside the ball. Physical consequences include preservation of all connected source responses, a uniform comparison of finite coarse-field marginals with product Haar measure, and suppression of aligned dyadic Wilson squares. The computational supplement includes the seven precursor stages and an independent rational verification of their one-link spectral input. The result closes the local iteration problem for this action space; physical-source scaling, a compatible bare-theory trajectory, reflection-compatible continuum reconstruction, and a nontrivial four-dimensional limit remain separate obligations.
title: Certified Alternating Space-Time Coarse-Graining with Full Memory -An invariant Fourier domain for an SU(3) lattice transfer model

summary: JAPAQ is a nationwide dataset of hourly air quality observations in Japan from January 2018 to December 2025. It covers the five pollutants regulated by Japan's Environmental Quality Standards — fine particulate matter (PM2.5), sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitric oxide (NO), suspended particulate matter (SPM), and photochemical oxidants (Ox) — and three meteorological variables (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity), from the Atmospheric Environmental Regional Observation System (AEROS, "Soramame") of the Ministry of the Environment, Japan. The deposit (japaq_v1.0.0.zip) contains two products built from the same records — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched hourly table, and JAPAQ-KG, its knowledge graph — together with the raw observations, station metadata, and corrections log from which they are built, in five folders that follow the processing steps: 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_hourly_obs_v1.0.0.csv — raw hourly observations as downloaded: 114,237,726 records from 1,850 stations (station, timestamp, five pollutants, three meteorological variables). 4_JAPAQ-FE/japaq_fe_v1.0.0 (CSV and Parquet) — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched, analysis-ready table and main data record: 110,328,514 records from 1,806 stations with documented quality control (three correction stages that remove 2,235,358 non-physical pollutant values; a physical range check for meteorology; quality flags for 2,345 implausible pollutant values and 141,448 meteorological values from faulty sensors, kept and marked), station metadata including complete resolved fields, calendar and time-of-day attributes, severity labels referenced to the Environmental Quality Standards, and a Beaufort wind-speed class (48 columns). 3_quality_control/japaq_corrections_log_v1.0.0.csv — every value set to null or flagged, with its original value, stage, and rule (2,473,666 records). 2_station_metadata/japaq_station_metadata_v1.0.0.csv and 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_station_list_v1.0.0.csv — English station metadata for 1,825 stations, including 143 stations missing from the current station list whose metadata were recovered from official NIES station files and municipality codes, with the source of each station's metadata; and the original Soramame station list (Japanese). 2_station_metadata/japaq_romanisation_log_v1.0.0.csv and STATION_METADATA_METHOD.md, and sources.csv — romanised address values, full source citations, and the recovery method for station metadata. 5_JAPAQ-KG/japaq_kg_v1.0.0.dump — JAPAQ-KG, the records of JAPAQ-FE as a Neo4j 2026.02 property graph with 220,660,640 nodes (Station, Location, ObservationTime, ObservedPollutant) and 330,987,348 relationships. JAPAQ-KG is the evaluation substrate of the AirCypher text-to-Cypher benchmark (IEEE BigData 2026). The quality flags, meteorological variables, resolved station metadata, and source properties are additions that change no node, relationship, or original value; all 4,000 reference queries of the benchmark return the same rows on this graph. The complete code, which rebuilds this release end to end from 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_hourly_obs_v1.0.0.csv to the knowledge graph and reproduces the released tables byte for byte, is available on GitHub (MIT licence). Coverage gaps: no station has records for 12–31 July 2019, 29–31 March 2021, 27–30 September 2022, and 1 October – 31 December 2024 (118 days in total), because these periods are absent from the downloaded source files; annual statistics for 2024 therefore cover January to September only. Severity labels are descriptive classification aids, not determinations of regulatory compliance. The measurements are provisional values published by the Ministry of the Environment; confirmed values are released later by the National Institute for Environmental Studies. The meteorological variables come from sensors at air quality stations and are intended mainly as covariates. Terms of

summary: This repository contains the data, analysis scripts and fitted model objects for the manuscript ` Nowhere except under negation? Exceptive constructions in native and heritage grammars '. The .rds files contain the saved model objects, and the model scripts load them instead of refitting when they are present. Participant identifiers in the raw data have been replaced with random codes. The corpus folder contains fig_corpus_licensing.R , which plots the distribution of krome kak across licensing environments from the hand-coded counts of the corpus study. The experiment1_pilot folder contains the pilot comparison of baseline and heritage speakers. The ratings are in data/raw/krome_kak_pilot.xlsx , and 01_prepare_pilot.R converts them to data/pilot_ratings.csv and computes the cell means of the pilot table ( derived/pilot_cell_means.csv ). No models are fitted for the pilot. The experiment2 folder contains the main acceptability experiment. The data/raw folder holds the PCIbex result files for the native group and the two heritage groups, and the background questionnaire ( participants.csv ). 00_import_raw.R reads these files and writes the eligible ratings to data/ , and 01_prepare_data.R applies the exclusions and writes the analysis files to derived/ . 02_fit_models.R fits the graded response model of the heritage-diagnostic items, the ordinal models with the heritageness score (overall and for each grammatical role), and the models in which heritage status is a binary speaker group or the mean diagnostic-item rating. 04_fit_supplementary_models.R fits the by-item variability models for each speaker group and the model of the four attested corpus items. 03_make_figures.R produces the figures in figures/ , and 05_bimodality.R computes the bimodality diagnostics of the participant mean ratings (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test, and one- versus two-component Gaussian mixtures). These scripts are run from inside the experiment2 folder. The heritageness_model folder contains the primary analysis of Experiment 2, in which heritageness is a continuous score estimated from the seven diagnostic items and its uncertainty is carried into the experimental model. 01_prepare_background.py recodes the background questionnaire. 02_fit_measurement_model.R fits the measurement model to the diagnostic items without speaker-group information, stores the posterior draws of the participant scores, and fits the experimental model with posterior-mean scores ( main_plugin.rds ). 03_fit_joint_model.R fits the joint model, in which the diagnostic and experimental ratings inform the score together ( joint.rds ). 04_fit_primary_model.R fits the experimental model separately to 32 posterior draws of the scores ( main_draw_01.rds to main_draw_32.rds ), pools them, and writes the summaries in output/ using summarize.R , additional_summaries.R and helpers.R . The estimates reported for Experiment 2 are in output/main_modular_contrasts.csv and output/joint_contrasts.csv . These scripts are run from the top folder. The analyses use R (brms with the cmdstanr backend, tidyverse, posterior, readxl, moments, diptest, mclust) and Python 3. Package versions are listed in heritageness_model/output/session_info.txt .
title: Nowhere except under negation? Exceptive constructions in native and heritage grammars

NEUROPLASTICITY MEASUREMENT AFTER STROKE AT THE LIMIT F106-F110 | FAMILY 22 | FIVE-FLAGSHIP SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK 33 × STARLI | The companion to the 819-page nonclinical research monograph EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: all 3D surfaces and cortical-source experiments are analytic or synthetic. This notebook contains no new patient study, no observed clinical benefit, no demonstrated quantum advantage, and no treatment or stimulation instruction. A LETTER FROM THE TWENTY-SECOND RESEARCH FAMILY What would it mean to say a nervous system had changed? A beautiful map of EEG connections might reflect rereferencing; a high coherence score might reflect one oscillation leaking into several electrodes. A neural marker might improve alongside repeated task practice without causing that improvement. The hand might reach farther by moving the trunk rather than recovering distal control. A favorable follow-up might be an early maximum remembered more clearly than all missing visits. Each uncertainty opens a different laboratory door. This family therefore studies the measurement conditions under which a neural observation may remain interpretable. F106 studies network reconstruction, F107 EEG false connectivity, F108 causal separation, F109 compensation and F110 delayed transfer. The minimum common platform is a synthetic cortical source and artifact mixer with an independently generated functional score. Our experimental success is the ability to differentiate models, expose failure and stop an unjustified claim. We cannot infer human rehabilitation efficacy from these mathematical exercises. The companion PDF preserves the 819-page research architecture with 42 standalone reproducible mathematical grids, 30 candidate equations, 82 chapters of six progressive pages, 200 Research Gates and 33 unbuilt Phoenix concepts. The notebook tells the same research questions as extended scientific prose. The public five-stage parallel spacetime name refers to a reasoning workflow, not multiple real spacetimes; no confidential computation-time target is published. I. FOURTEEN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | The network can move while the person does not A cortical network plot can change strikingly while a function measure remains unchanged. The distinction is the founding problem of this family. We do not assume that a topological transition on a page is neuroplastic recovery; we design experiments that can make such a claim fail. Take cortical network reorganization as a specific case. The candidate says genuine network reorganization should survive rereferencing and independent source-level reconstruction. The rival explanation says volume conduction, electrode-reference choice or movement artifact creates a convincing but unstable cortical connectivity map. A research team should change the electrode reference and nuisance mixing in concealed replay batches, then reconstruct an independently defined network invariant and report network metric change [1], adjacency error [1], coherence [1], retest dispersion [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is graph edge false positives and rereferencing sensitivity. Compare with reference-robust channel statistics, a common-source null, and spatially constrained source-reconstruction with identical sensor budget. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if an unidentifiable cortical edge presented as direct recovery evidence. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 02 | Five hypotheses are not five names for one mechanism F106 asks whether reconstructed motor networks survive changes of reference. F107 challenges functional EEG connections with a planted common source. F108 separates neural markers from motor performance by independent causal contrasts. F109 asks whether an improved movement was executed through compensation. F110 demands retention on novel tasks after a delayed follow-up. Each has a different potential defeat. Take eeg functional connectivity as a specific case. The candidate says a connectivity measure should discriminate dynamic coupling from a shared oscillatory source under a blinded nuisance intervention. The rival explanation says common-source contamination, spectral leakage and the cue schedule produce false positive interchannel edges. A research team should inject a hidden common-source component, vary phase lag and reference choice, and quantify false-positive edges on withheld data and report magnitude-squared coherence [1], imaginary coherence [1], false-edge rate [1], phase-lag error [rad]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is known-null edge rate after common-source injection. Compare with pairwise coherence with shuffled-time controls, imaginary coherency and nuisance-regression models with equal preprocessing budget. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if shared-source EEG coupling mistaken for verified brain plasticity. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 03 | A family of synthetic witnesses The minimum platform is an offline cortical source generator, a controlled EEG-like mixture, an artifact and task-cue log, a kinematic compensation proxy, and a separate functional task score. The platform never observes or stimulates a patient. Synthetic subject indices are simulation seeds, not human data records. Take plasticity–performance causal separation as a specific case. The candidate says a neural marker and an independent behavioral endpoint can diverge under interventions that change cues, task practice or measurement quality. The rival explanation says practice familiarity, time-dependent spontaneous change or residual confounding explains both observed marker and performance improvement. A research team should hold a neural marker shift constant while changing independently simulated practice history and verify the hidden functional endpoint and report independent task-score change [points], marker shift [1], causal contrast [points], interval coverage [%]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is function change with and without a negative-control trend. Compare with preregistered no-intervention trend, matched practice, negative-control outcomes and an equal-information classical causal model. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if a neural correlation promoted into a causal rehabilitation conclusion. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 04 | What exactly is a connection? Magnitude-squared coherence is a statistic between signals at a frequency; it does not by itself demonstrate direct neural information flow. Source leakage and common reference can create dependencies. This book tests source transformations and independent negative-control graphs before it allows a connection to be spoken of as reorganization. Take adaptation versus compensation as a specific case. The candidate says independent kinematic and physiological witnesses can reveal when task completion improves through substitution instead of changed motor capacity. The rival explanation says greater trunk substitution, altered limb strategy or sensor frame drift creates an attractive functional-looking trace. A research team should preserve target completion while increasing hidden trunk contribution, then ask whether the decoder falsely reports recovered arm control and report trunk/hand motion ratio [1], joint contribution [%], new-task accuracy [%], compensation error [1]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is trunk contribution under fixed task achievement. Compare with simple trunk-displacement ratio, kinematic decomposition and matched-task no-adaptation model under the same camera budget. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if successful task completion reported as neural recovery without voluntary capacity evidence. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 05 | Rereferencing and identifiable graphs Network topology depends on source definitions, filters, frequency bands and adjacency rules. F106 uses hidden transformations to ask which graph properties survive reasonable changes of observation. A graph eigenspectrum is a property of the estimate and must not be mistaken for anatomical evidence. Take long-term retention and cross-task transfer as a specific case. The candidate says a durable candidate mechanism must preserve independently measured performance on delayed unfamiliar tasks beyond practice and assessor drift. The rival explanation says a best early session, selection of favorable tasks and time-dependent calibration drift mimic retained transfer. A research team should freeze the model before a hidden follow-up session with new task families and independently score both neural and function proxies and report delayed retention ratio [1], untrained-task score [points], retest reliability [1], attrition rate [%]. Only a blinded difference that survives a strong comparison could justify a narrower technical claim. The most important practical inheritance is delayed novel-task score with complete attrition ledger. Compare with no-training trend, equally practiced familiar task, untrained holdout tasks and calibrated longitudinal reliability control. Preserve calibration, missingness, exclusions and trial count; refuse if a short-term proxy score advertised as durable human recovery. A future study involving human motor function would require a new ethically approved protocol, independent functional endpoints and clinical safety review. 06 | Connectivity with a false edge inserted F107 explicitly plants shared oscillatory sources and changes the phase structure. Its goal is not a more colorful heatmap but a count of false edges under declared null networks. A network estimator must be allowed to abstain when it cannot distinguish source leakage from interaction. Take cortical network reorganization as a specific case. A LETTER FROM THE TWENTY-FIRST RESEARCH FAMILY The visible movement of a muscle analog can be a poor witness to the mechanism that produced it. A command may be delivered imperfectly across a changing electrical contact; a trigger may coincide with a learned task cue; a tired load can be driven harder until its output seems ordinary again. A mathematical inverse may confidently assign a unique dose to a nonunique response. Even after a controller reads OFF, a passive mechanism can move. These five ways to be misled are the joint research problem of this family. We therefore begin with independent electrical witnesses, not therapeutic claims. An isolated dummy load, a guarded stimulation-port emulator, an offline BCI cue-replay system and a synthetic force proxy form the minimum environment. By design, no patient evidence is created by this book. Each chapter proposes an explicit competing world, a blind counterfactual and a refusal condition; every result that cannot distinguish those worlds is left unresolved. The research becomes worth inheriting when another laboratory can reproduce an error and improve the question. The companion PDF preserves a fixed 819-page research architecture, 42 recomputable analytic 3D plates, diagrams of the 200 questions and 33 unbuilt Phoenix prototype schematics. The five-stage parallel spacetime label names a reasoning workflow rather than a claim about physical parallel universes. I. FOURTEEN RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | When motion is not recovery A motor proxy can contract because a circuit drives it. A person may recover motor function through mechanisms not present in any nonclinical dummy load. This monograph is built around that difference. Its central objective is not to prove rehabilitation efficacy but to design independently testable experiments that isolate electrical input, controller decisions, mechanistic response and attribution of autonomous activity. An example research hinge is closed-loop stimulation. Its proposed mechanism is that measured contact-state feedback can control a load-proxy response without obscuring electrical burden. Its strongest alternative is that a visually stable proxy motion is caused by a fixed sequence or a contact-dependent artifact rather than closed-loop regulation. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to conceal a new contact-impedance trajectory and score measured delivered charge before revealing the programmed waveform. Reporting must include delivered charge [microC], current residual [mA], command-to-load latency [ms], dissipated proxy energy [mJ]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by open-loop constant-sequence replay with equal pulse budget and an instrumented impedance controller. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is electrical overlimit, contact heating surrogate or untraceable charge balance. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 02 | Five flags, five distinct modes of failure F101 tests closed-loop measurement of delivered charge under contact change. F102 asks whether triggers align with intention-like events rather than a hidden cue. F103 refuses to purchase apparent output with escalating energy during synthetic fatigue. F104 treats the inverse map from dose to response as potentially nonidentifiable. F105 requires off-state proof and unseen task transfer without interpreting proxy performance as human recovery. An example research hinge is intention-stimulation synchrony. Its proposed mechanism is that an independently timed intention proxy can predict a useful bounded stimulation window without learning task cues. Its strongest alternative is that a cue clock, eye activity or residual EMG, rather than intended action, explains the apparent synchrony. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to hide the cue schedule, alter the decoding delay and compare onset timing against an independent event clock. Reporting must include trigger latency [ms], absolute synchronization error [ms], false trigger rate [count/h], calibration error [1]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by fixed-delay trigger; shuffled-intention trigger; simple threshold decoder with the same recording and compute budget. summary: The clinical biochemistry laboratories are vital for screening, diagnosis and selection of treatment and monitoring. These results are reliable as a result of reliable quality management carried out during pre-examination, examination and post-examination. Internal quality control (IQC) is used to track the day to day stability of analytical procedures and external quality assessment (EQA) is used to make an independent comparison of the laboratory's performance with assigned values or other laboratories. An unacceptable control result, however, does not, however, mean that the problem has been solved. The nonconformity must be investigated, the direct effects of the nonconformity must be controlled, the root cause (s) of the nonconformity must be identified, the corrective and preventive action (s) must be implemented and effectiveness verified through a structured corrective and preventive action (CAPA) framework. The principles of IQC and EQA in Clinical Biochemistry are reviewed and the contribution of the findings of the two to a CAPA system of Quality Management are assessed. It outlines typical nonconformities that will be found in an analysis, quality control statistical approaches, root cause analysis tools, corrective and preventive actions, documentation requirements and indicators of CAPA effectiveness. Special focus on quality management based on risk and the ISO 15189:2022 requirements. The review also points out that good CAPA go beyond incident reports closing and are evidenced by subsequent data on IQC, EQA, and process performance to show continued improvement. An integrated approach will decrease the chance of analytical failure, improve laboratory competence and promote patient safety.
title: Evaluation of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Framework for Internal and External Quality Control in a Clinical Biochemistry Laboratory

summary: Background: Emphysematous cystitis (EC) is a rare but potentially life-threatening urinary tract infection characterized by gas accumulation within the bladder wall and/or lumen, most commonly associated with gas-producing microorganisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, including empagliflozin, promote urinary glucose excretion, raising questions about a possible association with genitourinary infections. However, the relationship between empagliflozin use and EC remains uncertain, with evidence currently limited to published case reports. Aim: To review the reported cases of emphysematous cystitis (EC) associated with empagliflozin use and to summarize the demographics, clinical features, treatment modalities and outcomes. Methodology: A systematic review was conducted using the databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science from inception until October 2026. The review included published case reports and several patients who developed EC while taking empagliflozin. Patient characteristics, laboratory findings, radiographic findings, management strategies, and clinical outcomes were extracted and qualitatively evaluated. Results: We examined seven patient cases with ages ranging from 62 to 90 (median 76). Two patients received empagliflozin for heart failure, and five patients had type 2 diabetes. Hematuria, dysuria, frequent urination, and suprapubic discomfort were common symptoms that emerged between two weeks and eight months following treatment. Urinary retention, bladder outlet obstruction, chronic renal disease, advanced age, and recent catheterization were among the contributing variables. Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most frequently isolated microorganism, based on microbiological culture results. Computed tomography (CT) was the principal imaging modality used to confirm the diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis. Management generally included discontinuation of empagliflozin, antibiotic therapy, and bladder drainage or decompression when indicated. Five patients recovered, whereas two patients died. Conclusion: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis is a rare but serious condition mostly seen in elderly patients with multiple health issues and urinary tract abnormalities. Early detection and treatment are crucial to minimize risks. More research is needed to understand its causes and frequency.
title: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis: a systematic review of published case reports

summary: Data and result logs of the PhishVN URL-benchmark study: the three external corpora in the exact rows the study used, and (from version 1.2.0) the study's result logs. External corpora. Class-balanced 1:1 subsamples of PhiUSIIL (20,000 rows, UCI, label polarity converted so that 1 is phishing), ISCX-URL2016 (15,894 rows) and PhishStorm (20,000 rows), the last two in the phishing/legitimate form redistributed with the GramBeddings repository. Each row carries the host the study featurises, 25 lexical features in the CompPhish schema (computed with the public-suffix list of the library version used) and the label. The subsamples were not drawn by a seed, so these files define the transfer experiments. With the PhishVN corpus (Mendeley Data, DOI 10.17632/b97hxbxtpd.4) they are the inputs of the benchmark, protocol, decomposition and transfer tables, which the walkthrough notebook notebooks/url_benchmark/url_benchmark_walkthrough.ipynb in https://github.com/vuthainguyen1602/phishvn recomputes. Cite the original datasets when using the rows (see README.md). Result logs ( results.zip ). One row per model family, protocol and seed for every experiment, the summary files the paper's tables are generated from, and the logs of the analyses added in the first revision (operating points, thresholds carried across corpora, forward cut-offs, the protocol contrast within one phishing feed, label-error scenarios, corpus probe, two-class temporal check, string models, tuning, attribution, cost). results_manifest.csv inside the archive gives every file's size and SHA-256. The files are aggregates and hold no URL, hostname or e-mail address. Three files of the repository's results folder are not included because they are copies of corpus rows (the PhishVN corpus one row per URL or per host); they are regenerated from the public corpus by the scripts the repository names. Files: phiusiil_compphish.csv , iscx_compphish.csv , phishstorm_compphish.csv , results.zip , README.md , SHA256SUMS . Version 1.3.0 adds to results.zip the logs of two analyses: a threshold carried across corpora and the protocol contrast with the phishing class drawn from one feed. Version 1.2.0 added results.zip . The three data files are byte-identical in every version.
title: PhishVN URL benchmark: the external transfer corpora and the study's result logs

summary: Tributaries of the middle Rio São Francisco basin, including the Rio Verde Grande, are important nursery habitats for reproduction of migratory fishes and provide water for economic activities such as agriculture, but the characterization of the fish fauna in these areas remains understudied. We document the presence of 53 species across 43 genera within 21 families in the Rio Verde Grande, encompassing the otophysan orders Characiformes (30 species), Gymnotiformes (two species), and Siluriformes (16 species), as well as the percomorph families Cichlidae (two species) and Poeciliidae (three species). Megalamphodus eques and Poecilia reticulata are non-native species and introduced in the Rio Verde Grande and along the São Francisco basin. The sampling site near Jaíba situated at the lowest altitude of 467 m a.s.l. harbored the highest species richness among all sites with 37 species representing 62% of the overall richness and was completely dry in 2019. Analysis of ecological trait factors resulted in assemblage dominated by medium- and large-bodied fishes, prevalence of benthic feeding strategies, and habitat association with lotic environments. This survey represents a baseline for future regional initiatives that require the development of conservation plans focused on the Rio Verde Grande that can thus maintain the unique freshwater species diversity.
title: Ichthyofauna of the Rio Verde Grande, middle São Francisco basin, eastern Brazil (Actinopterygii, Teleostei)

summary: Replication package (paper, code and data) for "Hindsight or Foresight? Alternative Data, Early Warning, and the Measurement of Corporate-Group Failure". It scores eleven families of alternative data on lead time, specificity, Thai accessibility, cost, legal safety and point-in-time integrity; codes 28 failures and turnarounds of firms and business groups by the first public signal in each family; measures hindsight bias on a public panel of 146,045 U.S. firm-years with SEC enforcement labels (Bao et al., 2020), where a gradient-boosting model's ROC AUC falls from 0.833 under random cross-validation to 0.697 under point-in-time evaluation; and runs Monte Carlo simulations of forking paths, alignment artefacts, timeliness versus noise and base rates.
title: hindsight-or-foresight
