summary: Gridded density fields and cosmic-web class masks used to train and test DeepVoid , a 3D U-Net that labels each cell of a simulated volume as void, wall, filament or halo. These grids are derived from simulation data produced and released by others: the IllustrisTNG project (TNG300-3-Dark) and the Bolshoi simulation (via the CosmoSim database). We only gridded the particles and halos and computed the class masks. Please credit the simulations as listed below whenever you use these files. All grids cover the full periodic simulation box at redshift 0, with axis order (x, y, z) and lengths in h -1 Mpc. File Contents tng300-3-dark_dm_n512.npz TNG300-3-Dark, dark-matter density from all particles; 512 3 cells in a 205 h -1 Mpc box tng300-3-dark_tweb_n512.npz T-web classes from that density (0 void, 1 wall, 2 filament, 3 halo): effective smoothing 1 h -1 Mpc, eigenvalue threshold 0.65 tng300-3-dark_subhalos_L{3,5,7,10}_n512.npz Mass density of the most massive subhalos, selected so that their mean separation is 3, 5, 7 or 10 h -1 Mpc. The subhalos are from the TNG group catalogs, found by the Subfind algorithm bolshoi_dm_n640.npz Bolshoi, dark-matter density from all 2048 3 particles (mean separation 0.122 h -1 Mpc); 640 3 cells in a 250 h -1 Mpc box bolshoi_tweb_n640.npz T-web classes from that density: effective smoothing 1 h -1 Mpc, eigenvalue threshold 0.65 bolshoi_halos_L{3,5,7,10}_n640.npz Bolshoi halos at mean separations of 3, 5, 7 or 10 h -1 Mpc, found by the Bound Density Maxima (BDM) halo finder MANIFEST.txt Size and SHA-256 checksum of every file   Format. Each .npz opens with NumPy alone: np.load("tng300-3-dark_dm_n512.npz")["data"] . data holds the values (uint8 for class masks, float32 otherwise); header is a JSON string with the box size and the file's provenance; fvol_header keeps the header of the file the grid was converted from. The conversion is lossless: each original file can be rebuilt byte for byte as fvol_header followed by data as float32, and its SHA-256 checksum is stored in header under source_sha256 . Cosmologies. TNG300: Ω m = 0.3089, Ω Λ = 0.6911, Ω b = 0.0486, σ 8 = 0.8159, n s = 0.9667, h = 0.6774. Bolshoi: Ω m = 0.27, Ω Λ = 0.73, Ω b = 0.0469, σ 8 = 0.82, n s = 0.95, h = 0.70. Credit IllustrisTNG. Any use of the TNG300 data should cite the data release paper and the introductory papers: Nelson, D., et al. 2019, Computational Astrophysics and Cosmology, 6, 2 Springel, V., et al. 2018, MNRAS, 475, 676 Pillepich, A., et al. 2018, MNRAS, 475, 648 Nelson, D., et al. 2018, MNRAS, 475, 624 Naiman, J. P., et al. 2018, MNRAS, 477, 1206 Marinacci, F., et al. 2018, MNRAS, 480, 5113 The data come from https://www.tng-project.org . Bolshoi. Cite the simulation, the CosmoSim Bolshoi dataset and, for the halo grids, the halo finder: Klypin, A. A., Trujillo-Gomez, S., & Primack, J. 2011, ApJ, 740, 102 CosmoSim Bolshoi dataset, https://doi.org/10.17876/cosmosim/bolshoi Klypin, A., & Holtzman, J. 1997, arXiv:astro-ph/9712217 (Bound Density Maxima halo finder) Riebe, K., et al. 2011, arXiv:1109.0003 (the MultiDark database) The CosmoSim database asks publications to include its acknowledgment paragraph, given at https://www.cosmosim.org/cms/credits/ . DeepVoid. If these grids are useful to you, please also cite Kumagai, S., Vogeley, M. S., Aragon-Calvo, M. A., Douglass, K. summary: Modern AI assistants, agents, and decision-support systems increasingly rely on information beyond model parameters by retrieving documents, accessing memory, invoking tools, and combining external evidence. Retrieval-Augmented Generation is one prominent realization of this broader information-grounding paradigm. Yet external grounding does not by itself ensure trustworthiness. Systems can still fail under incomplete, noisy, conflicting, or misleading evidence, and these failures become harder to diagnose as retrieval, reasoning, memory, tool use, and generation interact. Existing evaluation frameworks measure important aspects of system quality, but do not necessarily ensure deliberate coverage of the conditions most likely to expose system vulnerabilities. We introduce PRISM as a methodology for systematic stress testing of retrieval-grounded AI through controlled synthetic data generation. Rather than treating evaluation data as a static benchmark, PRISM constructs and validates document and question-answer pairs designed to reproduce deployment-relevant failure conditions. Its 25 evaluation instruments are organized across ten diversity dimensions and eight thematic clusters, covering conditions such as fragmented or noisy evidence, lexical and semantic mismatch, unanswerable queries, and adversarial or epistemically unreliable content. Because these conditions are generated synthetically, they can reproduce relevant document and evidence characteristics without requiring access to proprietary or sensitive operational data. Stress conditions are also linked to concrete system choices to support targeted diagnosis. PRISM is expected to provide reproducible and traceable evaluation artifacts that help reveal vulnerabilities before deployment and distinguish failures originating from retrieval, evidence selection, generation, or abstention. Automated construction and validation are also intended to reduce the manual effort associated with human-curated evaluation sets while preserving the control, coverage, and consistency needed for systematic evaluation. More broadly, PRISM reframes evaluation as not only a measurement problem but also an experimental-design problem. By complementing existing metrics, human evaluation, observability, and post-deployment monitoring, it contributes toward more systematic pre-deployment assessment of increasingly agentic, retrieval-grounded AI systems.
title: Toward Trustworthy Retrieval-Grounded AI through Synthetic Stress Testing

summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Recent ECG foundation models offer transferable representations for automated AF detection. However, their relative effectiveness remains unclear because existing studies use different datasets, preprocessing procedures, classifiers, and validation protocols. This study presents FOUND-AF, a unified, leakage-controlled, and deployment-oriented benchmarking framework that evaluates the quality of pretrained ECG representations under identical experimental conditions. Nine publicly available foundation models from five families, including HuBERT-ECG, CLEF, ST-MEM, ECG-JEPA, and ECGFounder, were evaluated across four heterogeneous ECG datasets, namely AFDB, CinC2017, CPSC2021, and LTAFDB. All models were used as frozen feature extractors with standardized preprocessing, model-native resampling, a fixed XGBoost classifier, and recording-level grouped cross-validation. The evaluation included classification metrics, receiver operating characteristic analysis, paired recording-level bootstrap comparisons with Holm correction, embedding-space visualization, and computational efficiency profiling. The ECGFounder model consistently achieved the strongest overall performance across datasets while offering a favorable trade-off between accuracy, model size, inference time, and memory usage. FOUND-AF therefore provides a reproducible framework for selecting ECG foundation models and demonstrates that compact, clinically pretrained encoders can support robust and computationally efficient AF detection across heterogeneous acquisition settings.
title: FOUND-AF: Benchmarking ECG Foundation Models for Atrial Fibrillation Detection

summary: Large language model research agents can connect literature retrieval, analysis code, and manuscript preparation, but coherent output does not establish scientific validity. We developed Plato-Bio, a biology-routed extension of the open Plato/Denario architecture that couples explicit workflow states with provenance records, citation checks, claim-to-evidence links, scoped file writes, and publication gates. A source audit identified and repaired three defects that could distort evaluation: loss of task domain in the default factory, omission of declared method signals from scoring, and evidence sidecars that lacked the drafted-claim denominator. On the current clean revision, the full Python suite completed with 931 passes, six skips, and no failures or errors; targeted biology, genomics, evidence/citation, and adversarial-safety suites likewise completed without failure. We evaluated two narrow use cases. In a frozen historical rediscovery task, independent pre-1986 literature bridges ranked the later-studied relation between fish oil and Raynaud phenomenon first; TF-IDF ranked it second and corpus frequency third. This single curated task measures retrospective ranking, not prospective discovery. In a separate comparison of AlphaFold models with experimental structures for 15 human proteins, 11 targets had high-confidence-core C-alpha RMSD below 1 Angstrom (median 0.501 Angstrom). Four targets exceeded 2 Angstrom, and confidence masking reduced the SUMO1 discrepancy from 16.61 to 2.58 Angstrom over 74 residues. The workflow emitted 27 traceable discrepancy regions, all retained as unvalidated hypotheses. Plato-Bio therefore provides reproducible software contracts and auditable screening baselines; broader claims of agent efficacy or biological novelty require preregistered evaluation, independent review, and prospective validation.
title: Plato-Bio: verification-first biological novelty screening with temporal rediscovery and structural benchmarks

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can benefit from more sophisticated retrieval, but extra retrieval may be unnecessary for many questions and gains in evidence retrieval may not translate into faithful or correct answers. We study a cost-aware, two-action retrieval policy that chooses between a dense-retrieval-plus-reranking baseline and a hybrid lexical--dense retriever. Rather than classifying baseline retrieval as simply successful or unsuccessful, we estimate the question-specific incremental evidence-retrieval benefit of hybrid retrieval using features available before the routing decision. A regularized linear model and decision threshold are selected using document-grouped cross-validation and frozen prior to held-out evaluation. On 60 previously unseen QASPER training-split articles (188 questions, 169 evidence-evaluable), the policy triggers hybrid retrieval on 46 questions (24.5\%) and obtains the same evidence Hit@10 as always-hybrid retrieval (78.70\%, versus 76.92\% for always-keep). Paired, paper-cluster bootstrap intervals do not establish a reliable utility advantage. We further compare generated answers from a 4-bit Qwen3-4B model under the three retrieval policies. Provisional answer-level assessments show no clear correctness or faithfulness improvement after partial review, despite the evidence-retrieval result. The generation assessments remain model-assisted and lack independent human validation. These results expose an important distinction between retrieving relevant evidence efficiently and improving the reliability of the generated answer. The work is presented as a reproducible empirical study, not a claim of statistically established answer-quality superiority.
title: When Is Additional Retrieval Worthwhile? A Cost-Aware Study of Evidence Gain and Answer Reliability in RAG

summary: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43 examines the governance and evidence requirements that arise when artificial intelligence influences consequential business decisions. The paper defines a decision chain of custody as a controlled, verifiable record connecting the information used, systems involved, applicable policies, delegated authority, approvals, execution and preserved evidence behind an AI-influenced decision. Its central operating test is independent reconstruction: an authorised reviewer should be able to determine what happened, which authority permitted the action and how the resulting business state was verified without relying on the original operator's memory. The analysis distinguishes decision custody from related concepts including accuracy, explainability, data lineage, observability and content provenance. It argues that these controls answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable forms of transparency. Content provenance might identify the history of a digital asset, for example, while providing no evidence that a user held authority to approve a payment or that the resulting transaction was correctly executed. The paper proposes eight linked evidence domains for consequential AI-influenced decisions: information received, intelligence used, rules applied, tools invoked, state changed, authority held, outcome approved and evidence preserved. These domains connect through a shared decision identifier and are intended to preserve relationships between initial inputs, policy evaluation, delegated authority, approval, execution and verified outcome. Particular attention is given to the moment of commitment, when an AI-generated recommendation becomes an external or financial business action. The paper argues that approvals must remain linked to the material terms ultimately executed. Changes to amount, recipient, purpose or other material conditions require a defined re-evaluation path rather than reliance on an earlier approval. The paper also addresses delegation across multiple agents and systems, retry behaviour, transaction reconciliation, evidence integrity, retention, human oversight and supplier evidence obligations. It distinguishes reconstruction from reproduction and outcome verification, noting that exact reproduction of stochastic model output is neither always possible nor necessary for reconstructing observable system behaviour. Three cases illustrate different dimensions of the argument. IBM provides company-reported evidence of reduced data-clearance processing time within an integrated governance programme. HSBC demonstrates large-scale financial-crime detection alongside explainable and auditable investigative outputs. AstraZeneca provides published evidence concerning the organisational scope and challenges of ethics-based AI auditing. None of these cases is presented as proof of a complete decision-custody architecture. The paper proposes consequence-based evidence requirements, independent reconstruction tests, explicit stop conditions for missing authority or mandatory evidence, supplier acceptance tests and measurable indicators including reconstruction pass rate, authority coverage, approval match, outcome reconciliation and preservation verification. The chapter concludes that auditability after an AI-influenced decision is becoming as important as intelligence before the decision. Enterprises expanding autonomous authority should first demonstrate that completed consequential decisions can be independently reconstructed from preserved evidence with clear ownership, valid authority and verified outcomes. The eight-domain decision record, consequence-based evidence model, reconstruction tests and associated management controls are author-developed conceptual frameworks informed by established provenance, AI governance, legal and assurance sources. They are not externally validated standards or universal legal requirements.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43: Every AI Decision Needs a Chain of Custody

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition: The Dualverse — From Quantum Factualization and Physical Memory to Hierarchical Individuality and Spacetime

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: for 1 < p < 2 this paper finds the exact Schatten-norm constant for sums of matrix moduli when there are at least as many matrices as the matrix size, gives a new general upper bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , and certifies in exact arithmetic that rank-one matrices do not give the answer to Lee’s two-matrix problem. The question. For numbers, |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|. A matrix A has a natural absolute value |A| = (A*A) 1/2 , but for matrices the size of a sum can exceed the size of the sum of the absolute values. Measuring size by the Schatten p-norm (p = 1 is the trace norm, p = 2 the Frobenius norm), one asks for the smallest constant c with ‖A 1 +…+A m ‖ p ≤ c ‖|A 1 |+…+|A m |‖ p . What was known. summary: The Brina Gap measures the difference between the growth a company can self-finance and the growth its market price already assumes.  Its fundamental arm is the sustainable-growth ceiling,  g f  = ROIC × Reinvestment Rate; its pricing arm is the market-implied growth  g *, recovered from a reverse discounted-cash-flow on enterprise value. Both come from public filings, so the Gap makes the market's embedded growth expectation explicit — mechanically, reproducibly, and without an analyst's private valuation. Stated in growth units, it is the only kind of valuation claim that can be checked against what firms later deliver —  and it checks out. On the complete point-in-time S&P 500 (2010–2024, survivorship-free), the market-implied growth  g * genuinely tracks the growth firms subsequently realize (correlation ≈ 0.4–0.5, nearly unbiased at the 10-year horizon) and is robust across independent recovery methods (Spearman 0.73–1.00).  The Brina Gap is a detector of over-extrapolated growth expectations:  the market systematically over-extrapolates growth — the calibration slope sits below one at every horizon — and the median firm priced for high growth under-delivers what its price implies (≈ 26% priced in vs ≈ 22% realized).  Head-to-head against the classical Margin of Safety, the Gap is mechanical and falsifiable where the Margin of Safety is not, nearly orthogonal to it in cross-section, and more accurate on the one directional test both can take (+3.9 points, p ≈ .004; the Gap's expensive-side calls were correct 58.9% of the time on the full universe).  Among all pure valuation metrics tested — book-to-market, earnings yield, EPV, the Margin of Safety — the Brina Gap ranks first, and it is the only one whose central claim can be verified at all.  Its practical form is the  Brina Matrix , which crosses the Gap's pricing read with fundamental quality and yields one rule that survives every specification tested:  "cheap" is only a bargain when quality is high — cheap plus low quality is the value trap, the worst-performing cell in the sample. We are equally explicit about the limits: the fundamental arm is a conservative anchor, not a forecast; and the Gap — like every metric in the companion audit, the Margin of Safety included — is not a standalone return signal, which is exactly what efficiency logic predicts for any transparent, filings-based measure, in the most pricing-hostile decade on record. Data and code are published: a per-call outcomes file and a one-command verifier reproduce every headline number (see below). Verify the headline numbers yourself (added in v3.0.1). directional_outcomes_v3.0.csv lists all 1,504 directional calls on the complete point-in-time S&P 500, 2010–2024, delisted and acquired firms included (CRSP-style). Running python3 verify_headline_claims.py (Python standard library only) recomputes: • Stocks the Brina Gap clearly flagged as priced too high trailed the S&P 500 over the next five years in 546 of 927 cases (58.9%; a coin flip gives 50%). Exact one-sided binomial p = 3.3×10⁻⁸: if the warnings were coin flips, a record this good would come up about once in 30 million tries. • On the same 1,504 calls the classic Margin of Safety scored 50.9% (chance); the Gap 54.8%: +3.9 points, year-clustered bootstrap p = 0.0038. • Value Trap calls: 59.5% (207 of 348). The Gap's "cheap" calls were at chance (48.2%), as the paper reports. The paper claims no standalone return edge (over every stock, sign only: 52.4%). See README_VERIFY.md. Two parts:  Part I — the paper (the construct, its theory, the validity battery, the Brina Matrix); Part II — the complete empirical record (directional tests, robustness, failure modes, pre-registered refinements).  Supersedes v1.0 and v2.0; their d

summary: The Brina Gap measures the difference between the growth a company can self-finance and the growth its market price already assumes.  Its fundamental arm is the sustainable-growth ceiling,  g f  = ROIC × Reinvestment Rate; its pricing arm is the market-implied growth  g *, recovered from a reverse discounted-cash-flow on enterprise value. Both come from public filings, so the Gap makes the market's embedded growth expectation explicit — mechanically, reproducibly, and without an analyst's private valuation. Stated in growth units, it is the only kind of valuation claim that can be checked against what firms later deliver —  and it checks out. On the complete point-in-time S&P 500 (2010–2024, survivorship-free), the market-implied growth  g * genuinely tracks the growth firms subsequently realize (correlation ≈ 0.4–0.5, nearly unbiased at the 10-year horizon) and is robust across independent recovery methods (Spearman 0.73–1.00).  The Brina Gap is a detector of over-extrapolated growth expectations:  the market systematically over-extrapolates growth — the calibration slope sits below one at every horizon — and the median firm priced for high growth under-delivers what its price implies (≈ 26% priced in vs ≈ 22% realized).  Head-to-head against the classical Margin of Safety, the Gap is mechanical and falsifiable where the Margin of Safety is not, nearly orthogonal to it in cross-section, and more accurate on the one directional test both can take (+3.9 points, p ≈ .004; the Gap's expensive-side calls were correct 58.9% of the time on the full universe).  Among all pure valuation metrics tested — book-to-market, earnings yield, EPV, the Margin of Safety — the Brina Gap ranks first, and it is the only one whose central claim can be verified at all.  Its practical form is the  Brina Matrix , which crosses the Gap's pricing read with fundamental quality and yields one rule that survives every specification tested:  "cheap" is only a bargain when quality is high — cheap plus low quality is the value trap, the worst-performing cell in the sample. We are equally explicit about the limits: the fundamental arm is a conservative anchor, not a forecast; and the Gap — like every metric in the companion audit, the Margin of Safety included — is not a standalone return signal, which is exactly what efficiency logic predicts for any transparent, filings-based measure, in the most pricing-hostile decade on record. Data and code are published: a per-call outcomes file and a one-command verifier reproduce every headline number (see below). The Gap's "cheap" calls were at chance (48.2%), as the paper reports. The paper claims no standalone return edge (over every stock, sign only: 52.4%). See README_VERIFY.md. summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law. For $n=3$ the examples refine the symmetric non-mixable laws of Yin and Zhu, and the reduction explains why those laws satisfy the inequalities.

summary: Replication package for the working paper "Precision Matters: Anti-Corruption Campaigns, Targeted Crackdowns, and Sector Returns in China's Stock Market" (Xuanyuan Li, 2026). The package contains: (1) four hand-verified event libraries — 31 general anti-corruption campaign events (2012–2026), 12 sector-targeted interventions, 12 local-flagship case-study events, and 14 positive policy tools — every date anchored to an official primary source (CCDI, NDRC, MIIT, NPC, SAMR); (2) a 152-month hand-compiled CCDI eight-point-regulation enforcement series (2013-09 to 2026-09) with per-month source anchors and the December 2019 coverage-revision flag; (3) Sina hfq-adjusted daily return panels for the sector proxies and the CSI 300 benchmark; (4) all analysis scripts (Python 3.11, pandas/numpy): event-study grids, monthly enforcement-intensity regressions, exact permutation / cluster-bootstrap / sign-test inference, index-proxy robustness, and a beta-adjusted market-model replication with Newey-West lag sensitivity; (5) the manuscript (Markdown and Word), cover letter, and title page. Run the scripts from the package root; README.md gives replication steps and data-source conventions. All paper results are reproducible from the cached CSVs without network access. Inference note: policy events of this precision are scarce by construction; the paper reports exact permutation tests as primary evidence and discloses that the beta-adjusted replication weakens the headline targeted-intervention spread (p = 0.073).

The package contains: (1) four hand-verified event libraries — 31 general anti-corruption campaign events (2012–2026), 12 sector-targeted interventions, 12 local-flagship case-study events, and 14 positive policy tools — every date anchored to an official primary source (CCDI, NDRC, MIIT, NPC, SAMR); (2) a 152-month hand-compiled CCDI eight-point-regulation enforcement series (2013-09 to 2026-09) with per-month source anchors and the December 2019 coverage-revision flag; (3) Sina hfq-adjusted daily return panels for the sector proxies and the CSI 300 benchmark; (4) all analysis scripts (Python 3.11, pandas/numpy): event-study grids, monthly enforcement-intensity regressions, exact permutation / cluster-bootstrap / sign-test inference, index-proxy robustness, and a beta-adjusted market-model replication with Newey-West lag sensitivity; (5) the manuscript (Markdown and Word), cover letter, and title page. Run the scripts from the package root; README.md gives replication steps and data-source conventions. All paper results are reproducible from the cached CSVs without network access. Inference note: policy events of this precision are scarce by construction; the paper reports exact permutation tests as primary evidence and discloses that the beta-adjusted replication weakens the headline targeted-intervention spread (p = 0.073).

summary: Replication code for a study of battery storage investment prioritisation across five campuses of a merged public technical university in Taiwan, under a contract-capacity time-of-use tariff. The code recovers tariff parameters from billing records, jointly optimises storage size, contracted capacity and time-of-use dispatch for each site-year by linear programming with a genetic-algorithm benchmark, and values storage against an administratively optimised counterfactual so that contract reductions obtainable without capital expenditure are not credited to storage. The institutional billing records analysed in the paper are not included, having been obtained under a data use agreement that does not permit redistribution; a synthetic panel with the same schema is provided so the code runs out of the box.
title: Analysis code for: Visible in kilowatts, invisible in money — contract capacity, storage and investment priorities under a Taiwanese demand-charge tariff

summary: Measurement data and analysis code for maximum independent set (MIS) written as a single penalty (QUBO) objective and run on quantum annealers (D-Wave Advantage_system6 and Advantage2_system1) and gate-model processors (IBM Heron r3 and Nighthawk r2) through a QAOA circuit. The deposit contains: measurement count histograms of every executed circuit and annealer read set, with the executed angles, compiled depth, two-qubit gate counts and physical layouts; job ledgers and submission plans; the calibration snapshot each gate-model batch ran under; noiseless state-vector results for the same circuits; the instance generator (every instance is a pure function of size, fill fraction and seed) for king-lattice graphs, random 3-regular graphs, Erdős–Rényi graphs and heavy-hex induced subgraphs; the analysed tables; four hardware jobs whose predictions and criteria were written before submission, with the written designs and plan hashes; and the analysis scripts. reproduce.py recomputes derived quantities from the deposited tables offline. Not included: per-shot bitstrings (the provider returns count histograms), compiled circuit files (rebuilt from instance, angles and transpiler seed), optimizer per-evaluation traces and annealer embeddings. Account identifiers and budget statements were removed; the redactions are listed. The record is one zip archive ( zenodo_deposit.zip , directory structure preserved) with the README.md and a SHA-256 checksum list of every archived file alongside. Code: MIT ( LICENSE-code.txt in the archive). Data, tables and documents: CC BY 4.0.

summary: This record provides MATLAB code, processed inputs and Source Data supporting the manuscript “Tectonic pump closes the evolutionary loop for long-buried subseafloor microbes.” The software archive includes poroelastic fluid-flow modeling and its benchmark, fluid and cell source budgets, and analyses of Costa Rica microbial communities and seismicity, including partial Spearman correlations controlling for temperature and pH. The accompanying Source Data archive contains the numerical data underlying the main-text and supplementary figures and tables. README files provide software requirements, running instructions, expected outputs and workflows.
title: Numerical model code and datasets for "Tectonic pump closes the evolutionary loop for long-buried subseafloor microbes"

summary: Computational detection of intertextuality has so far used individual features such as word n-grams, edit distance, or word embeddings to identify text reuse or allusion, with only limited efforts to combine two such features for improved detection. This article presents Tesserae V6, a freely available platform that searches, weights, and combines into a single fused score ten distinct signals: shared headwords; a single shared headword; identical surface forms; character-trigram sound similarity; near-identical strings by edit distance; shared meaning by sentence embedding; curated cross-headword synonym pairs; matching dependency-tree patterns at shared headwords; identical dependency frames without any shared word; and shared rare words. The fused score also incorporates word-rarity weighting from corpus-wide frequencies. On the founding Lucan–Vergil benchmark, the previous V3 lexical baseline recovered about 27% of known parallels. Against five commentator-attested benchmarks comprising 862 parallel passages from Latin epic, the new fused V6 system recovered 91.5% in its full ranked output. Of the top distinct results for the Lucan–Vergil comparison, 79% (34 of 43) are meaningful instances of intertextuality. The platform was built by a classicist directing a sequence of AI coding assistants in natural language, with no traditional programming, and with each stage of development checked against the same benchmarks. The platform is available at https://tesserae.caset.buffalo.edu . This preprint has not been peer reviewed.
title: Feature Fusion for Computational Intertextuality Detection in Tesserae V6

summary: MakeCOO is a Wolfram Language command-line package that constructs a stoichiometric matrix from reaction definitions. It represents each reversible reaction as separate forward and reverse records and constructs a matrix with chemical species as rows and directed reactions as columns. It also exports the species list and directed reaction table. This archive contains MakeCOO version 0.3.0, the version used to construct the stoichiometric matrix in the anaerobic Mn(II) oxidation case study. It includes the source code, documentation, example inputs and tests, and the shared Utils/IO.wl file. The software is distributed under the MIT License. If you use MakeCOO in research, please cite the accompanying article by Mayumi Seto and Yuya Tsukamoto in Geomicrobiology Journal ( https://doi.org/10.1080/01490451.2026.2762317 ).
title: MakeCOO: Stoichiometric matrix construction from reaction definitions

summary: eglish version)This work presents a three-parameter mechanical-medium framework for the forward derivation of physical constants and characteristic scales within the Four-Forces–Quantum-Induction research program. The central objective is to determine how a minimal set of medium parameters can generate a hierarchy of microscopic and macroscopic physical quantities through a closed forward construction, rather than through post-hoc fitting to target observations. The current formulation includes an absolute-scale solution that no longer requires Newton’s gravitational constant as an external scale-setting calibration. Newton’s constant is instead used as a downstream consistency and round-trip closure test. The framework develops explicit relations among the characteristic medium density, elastic scale, viscosity-related input, characteristic radii, effective gravitational quantities, particle-scale structures, and derived observables. Strict NoAlias and NoDoubleCount rules are applied throughout to prevent numerically similar quantities or multiple readouts of the same physical inventory from being incorrectly identified or counted twice. An independent internal consistency test is provided by two routes to the model’s Hubble-equivalent scale. A global-field calculation and a local curvature or pressure-gradient calculation converge to approximately 67.33789544 km/s/Mpc. This quantity is reported as a model Hubble-equivalent scale. Its exact identification with the standard cosmological expansion rate H0 remains subject to a separate clock-identity condition and is therefore not assumed. The release also incorporates the current charge-conjugate electron-origin structure and the resulting birth-population asymmetry. The frozen current value is 6.117043204146319e-10. This result is treated as a theoretical output of the current model structure and is not presented as a new blind observational test. A strict theory-to-evidence firewall is maintained throughout the project. The workflow is: authority snapshot, declared inputs, forward operator, frozen prediction, external evidence, and statistical or qualitative score. Observational information is not permitted to modify a prediction after the prediction has been frozen. The empirical portfolio is intentionally reported with mixed outcomes. It includes compatible historical cross-checks, the Hubble-equivalent forward result with its explicit clock qualifier, cosmic-age consistency checks, an electron g-2 comparison that currently fails the frozen operator at high experimental precision, ring-laser results that remain retrospective rather than a new blind holdout, and prospective constant-drift predictions reserved for future evaluation. Compatible but non-discriminating tests are distinguished from genuinely discriminating evidence. The accompanying archive contains the English manuscript, validation and evidence status material, selected derivation records, Hubble-equivalent and asymmetry authority snapshots, provenance and reproducibility information, SHA256 manifests, and the sealed v4.43 historical authority package. This Zenodo release should therefore be interpreted as a frozen research record of the current theoretical construction, its absolute-scale closure, its derived cross-scale relations, and its explicitly classified empirical status. It is not a claim that every external observable has been successfully reproduced. Failed, conditional, prospective, and not-yet-opened evidence channels are retained explicitly as part of the scientific record.     预印本 — 未经同行评审。

summary: Large language model research agents can connect literature retrieval, analysis code, and manuscript preparation, but coherent output does not establish scientific validity. We developed Plato-Bio, a biology-routed extension of the open Plato/Denario architecture that couples explicit workflow states with provenance records, citation checks, claim-to-evidence links, scoped file writes, and publication gates. A source audit identified and repaired three defects that could distort evaluation: loss of task domain in the default factory, omission of declared method signals from scoring, and evidence sidecars that lacked the drafted-claim denominator. On the current clean revision, the full Python suite completed with 931 passes, six skips, and no failures or errors; targeted biology, genomics, evidence/citation, and adversarial-safety suites likewise completed without failure. We evaluated two narrow use cases. In a frozen historical rediscovery task, independent pre-1986 literature bridges ranked the later-studied relation between fish oil and Raynaud phenomenon first; TF-IDF ranked it second and corpus frequency third. This single curated task measures retrospective ranking, not prospective discovery. In a separate comparison of AlphaFold models with experimental structures for 15 human proteins, 11 targets had high-confidence-core C-alpha RMSD below 1 Angstrom (median 0.501 Angstrom). Four targets exceeded 2 Angstrom, and confidence masking reduced the SUMO1 discrepancy from 16.61 to 2.58 Angstrom over 74 residues. The workflow emitted 27 traceable discrepancy regions, all retained as unvalidated hypotheses. Plato-Bio therefore provides reproducible software contracts and auditable screening baselines; broader claims of agent efficacy or biological novelty require preregistered evaluation, independent review, and prospective validation.
title: Plato-Bio: verification-first biological novelty screening with temporal rediscovery and structural benchmarks

summary: Core Objective : To construct pure quantum Yang-Mills theory with compact simple gauge group $SU(N)$ in four-dimensional Euclidean space, prove the strict positivity of its mass gap, and reduce the mass-gap problem to a small set of explicit, identified inputs. Methodology : Uses lattice regularisation, renormalisation-group control of the continuum limit, and Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction of a relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski space. Expresses the clustering rate of the reflection-positive two-point function as the mass gap. Factorizes the mass-gap problem into three independent aspects: Existence (forced by reflection positivity and Fekete's lemma), Value (governed by an anomalous dimension), and Positivity (carried by the discrete centre of the gauge group and uniform control of confining flux). Key Innovations & Structure : Works in the flow-time coordinate where the dimensional-transmutation scale is an entire function and the marginal coupling region is compact. Proves the factorisation of the clustering rate and demonstrates that the mass gap equals the spectral gap of the transfer operator restricted to the centre-charged sector. Verifies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms (temperedness, reflection positivity, symmetry) conditional on identified inputs (uniform non-percolation, rotational invariance restoration, and limit uniqueness). Closes with a closure scheme, dimensional calibration against three-dimensional models, and explicit worked examples. The monograph titled "The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional $SU(N)$ Yang–Mills Theory" presents a construction of pure quantum Yang–Mills theory with a compact simple gauge group on four-dimensional Euclidean space. Its primary objective is to establish the existence of the theory and the strict positivity of its mass gap , reducing the overall problem to a small set of explicitly identified, non-analytic inputs.
title: When is 4D-Yang-Mills-Theorie possible; The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills Theory: A Construction, Its Reduction to a Single Non-Analytic Input, and a Scheme for Its Closure

summary: We develop a price-based framework for stochastic portfolio theory in which trading strategies are generated from nominal price weights and evaluated relative to a price-weighted benchmark. Stock splits and reverse splits induce jumps in the generating weights without changing the value of existing investments. In a semimartingale market with predictable adjustment events, we incorporate the corresponding share adjustments into the self-financing condition and construct additively and multiplicatively generated strategies with explicit jump-corrected wealth decompositions. For additive generation, an entropy-based example exhibits relative wealth tending to $-\infty$ almost surely under repeated splits, demonstrating why the usual argument for long-horizon relative arbitrage does not extend directly. We also show that advance adjustment information alone provides no model-free guarantee of improved performance for functionally generated portfolios. For multiplicative generation, wealth-preserving restarts retain the classical portfolio allocation evaluated at the current price weights. We also establish a correspondence with the capitalization-based framework that preserves absolute wealth and yields a strategy-independent benchmark conversion. We illustrate the framework using daily NYSE data, comparing price- and capitalization-weighted benchmarks and the corresponding diversity-weighted portfolios across price- and capitalization-selected universes.
title: A Price-Based Framework for Stochastic Portfolio Theory

summary: Many existing Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions on mobile devices rely on an extensive collection of sensitive data, raising privacy concerns and often requiring storage for both context and model improvement. Apple's Private Cloud Compute (PCC) aims to address this by emphasizing mobile device integration and a privacy-first design. The central claim of PCC is that it does not store any user data and that user input and user accounts are unlinkable. While most of the PCC system specifications are public, compiled binaries add a layer of opaqueness. There are no reproducible builds, and there are no symbols within those binaries, creating potential discrepancies between the specification and what is shipped to the user. Additionally, the underlying models and interfaces for querying PCC are not openly accessible, limiting academic evaluation of model properties, such as accuracy. This poses a challenge in assessing whether a privacy-preserving approach like PCC is actually trustworthy while also providing high-quality answers. We are the first to reverse-engineer the PCC implementation on mobile devices to evaluate privacy aspects and to open its non-public interfaces on local devices to support custom PCC queries. We demonstrate this level of access beyond Apple's intended use cases by independently benchmarking the PCC model. We enable future research by making our PCC benchmarking framework publicly available.
title: Unlocking Apple's Private Cloud Compute: An Analysis of Privacy-Preserving Artificial Intelligence

summary: This paper presents our submission to the ACMMM25 - Grand Challenge on Multimedia Verification. We developed a multi-agent verification system that combines Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with specialized verification tools to detect multimedia misinformation. Our system operates through six stages: raw data processing, planning, information extraction, deep research, evidence collection, and report generation. The core Deep Researcher Agent employs four tools: reverse image search, metadata analysis, fact-checking databases, and verified news processing that extracts spatial, temporal, attribution, and motivational context. We demonstrate our approach on a challenge dataset sample involving complex multimedia content. Our system successfully verified content authenticity, extracted precise geolocation and timing information, and traced source attribution across multiple platforms, effectively addressing real-world multimedia verification scenarios.
title: Multimedia Verification Through Multi-Agent Deep Research Multimodal Large Language Models

summary: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43 examines the governance and evidence requirements that arise when artificial intelligence influences consequential business decisions. The paper defines a decision chain of custody as a controlled, verifiable record connecting the information used, systems involved, applicable policies, delegated authority, approvals, execution and preserved evidence behind an AI-influenced decision. Its central operating test is independent reconstruction: an authorised reviewer should be able to determine what happened, which authority permitted the action and how the resulting business state was verified without relying on the original operator's memory. The analysis distinguishes decision custody from related concepts including accuracy, explainability, data lineage, observability and content provenance. It argues that these controls answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable forms of transparency. Content provenance might identify the history of a digital asset, for example, while providing no evidence that a user held authority to approve a payment or that the resulting transaction was correctly executed. The paper proposes eight linked evidence domains for consequential AI-influenced decisions: information received, intelligence used, rules applied, tools invoked, state changed, authority held, outcome approved and evidence preserved. These domains connect through a shared decision identifier and are intended to preserve relationships between initial inputs, policy evaluation, delegated authority, approval, execution and verified outcome. Particular attention is given to the moment of commitment, when an AI-generated recommendation becomes an external or financial business action. The paper argues that approvals must remain linked to the material terms ultimately executed. Changes to amount, recipient, purpose or other material conditions require a defined re-evaluation path rather than reliance on an earlier approval. The paper also addresses delegation across multiple agents and systems, retry behaviour, transaction reconciliation, evidence integrity, retention, human oversight and supplier evidence obligations. It distinguishes reconstruction from reproduction and outcome verification, noting that exact reproduction of stochastic model output is neither always possible nor necessary for reconstructing observable system behaviour. Three cases illustrate different dimensions of the argument. IBM provides company-reported evidence of reduced data-clearance processing time within an integrated governance programme. HSBC demonstrates large-scale financial-crime detection alongside explainable and auditable investigative outputs. AstraZeneca provides published evidence concerning the organisational scope and challenges of ethics-based AI auditing. None of these cases is presented as proof of a complete decision-custody architecture. The paper proposes consequence-based evidence requirements, independent reconstruction tests, explicit stop conditions for missing authority or mandatory evidence, supplier acceptance tests and measurable indicators including reconstruction pass rate, authority coverage, approval match, outcome reconciliation and preservation verification. The chapter concludes that auditability after an AI-influenced decision is becoming as important as intelligence before the decision. Enterprises expanding autonomous authority should first demonstrate that completed consequential decisions can be independently reconstructed from preserved evidence with clear ownership, valid authority and verified outcomes. The eight-domain decision record, consequence-based evidence model, reconstruction tests and associated management controls are author-developed conceptual frameworks informed by established provenance, AI governance, legal and assurance sources. They are not externally validated standards or universal legal requirements.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43: Every AI Decision Needs a Chain of Custody

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition: The Dualverse — From Quantum Factualization and Physical Memory to Hierarchical Individuality and Spacetime

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: for every preorder that contains no “crown”, the support polynomial of its preorder polytope is the h-polynomial of a flag simplicial sphere, which settles the flag form of a 2026 conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton for that class. The release also identifies the gamma-coefficients as counts of matchable pairs (found at the same time, independently, by Y. Zhong) and proves two Ehrhart conjectures from the same paper. The objects. A preorder is a way of ranking things in which ties are allowed. Athanasiadis and Chapoton (arXiv:2605.26916) attached to each preorder τ on n elements a lattice polytope Q τ : its integer points are the ways of putting nonnegative whole-number loads on the elements so that no downward-closed group carries more than its own size. Counting these points by how many loads are nonzero gives a polynomial H τ (t). For the chain 1 < 2 < 3 the counts are 1, 6, 6, 1, and 1 + 6t + 6t 2 + t 3 = (1+t) 3 + 3t(1+t); the 3 counts the three ways to pick one element and one strictly above it. The conjectures. Athanasiadis and Chapoton conjectured that H τ always looks like the h-polynomial of a sphere: palindromic, unimodal, gamma-positive (a nonnegative combination of t j (1+t) n−2j ) and realised by a simplicial, even a flag simplicial, polytope. They also conjectured several Ehrhart identities. Gal conjectured that flag spheres always have gamma-positive h-polynomials, so families that are both gamma-positive and realised by flag spheres are natural test cases. Results. (1) The gamma-coefficient γ j counts ordered pairs of disjoint j-element sets that can be matched upwards in τ; this proves gamma-positivity (their Conjecture 5.2). Y. Zhong (arXiv:2611.16858, 12 November 2026) obtained the same formula independently and concurrently, by the same route. (2) New here: if τ contains no crown (2k ≥ 6 elements joined in a closed zig-zag), then H τ is the h-polynomial of the boundary of an n-dimensional flag simplicial polytope (Conjecture 5.1(d) for this class). The class includes all arbors (Chapoton’s original setting), compositions, width-two posets, series–parallel and interval orders, and every preorder with at most five blocks. The proof builds a quadratic Gröbner basis for a root polytope, adapting Ohsugi–Hibi and Ohsugi–Tsuchiya; the new step is to pull a special simplex first. For preorders with a crown, the two polytopes used here have no flag regular unimodular triangulation, and the six-element crown is the smallest open case. (3) Matrix Ehrhart–zeta duality (Conjecture 4.2) and double Ehrhart reciprocity (Conjecture 7.2) hold for every preorder; the descent formula (Conjecture 4.4) and the zeta value Z(P τ , −1) = (−1) n #max(P τ ) follow. Also: a simplicial-polytope realisation for every preorder (Conjecture 5.1(c)), an explicit reflexive polytope with Ehrhart numerator H τ , and a table of the status of every conjecture in the originating paper (Conjecture 5.4 was proved by Dai et al., Conjecture 6.3 by Luo, and Conjecture 5.3 is false by Patel’s example). Limits. The flag result covers crown-free preorders only. Several of the Ehrhart proofs are short applications of standard tools (Postnikov’s lattice-point formula, Ehrhart–Macdonald reciprocity, Athanasiadis’s special-simplex theorem). Magic positivity, Conjectures 6.2, 8.1 and 8.2 and the q-form of Conjecture 4.9 remain open. Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); exact Python checks with a runner that compares every output byte for byte in normal and python -O mode (all 355 labelled four-element preorders and smaller ones, 24 seeded preorders at each size 5–8, 689 small bipartite graphs, 560 matrix-duality cases, 390 preorders for the corollaries); flag-sphere checks on 570 crown-free preorders and Macaulay2 Gröbner-basis certificates for 461

summary: This record contains two complementary reproducibility packages supporting the manuscript "Mean Squared Error of 3 x 3 Median Filtering for Two-Dimensional Ising Images: Local Determinant Representation and Denoising Improvement Boundaries" by Jun Tsuzurugi. The filtering-examples package contains one reproducibly generated 256 x 256 free-boundary Ising image at K = 0.40, independent pixel-flip noise at p = 0.10 and 0.30, a single simultaneous 3 x 3 median-filtering pass, saved arrays, measured sample mean squared errors, thermalization diagnostics, and plotting code. These images are illustrative single-sample results, not estimates of infinite-lattice expected risk. The near-critical finite-size package contains deterministic central-pixel mean squared errors for free-boundary square lattices of side length 15, 31, and 63 at K = Kc +/- 0.005 and flip probabilities 0.10 and 0.20, compared with infinite-lattice references. It includes code, numerical tables, figures, convergence checks, validation records, and provenance. summary: Gridded density fields and cosmic-web class masks used to train and test DeepVoid , a 3D U-Net that labels each cell of a simulated volume as void, wall, filament or halo. These grids are derived from simulation data produced and released by others: the IllustrisTNG project (TNG300-3-Dark) and the Bolshoi simulation (via the CosmoSim database). summary: The Brina Gap measures the difference between the growth a company can self-finance and the growth its market price already assumes.  Its fundamental arm is the sustainable-growth ceiling,  g f  = ROIC × Reinvestment Rate; its pricing arm is the market-implied growth  g *, recovered from a reverse discounted-cash-flow on enterprise value. Both come from public filings, so the Gap makes the market's embedded growth expectation explicit — mechanically, reproducibly, and without an analyst's private valuation. Stated in growth units, it is the only kind of valuation claim that can be checked against what firms later deliver —  and it checks out. On the complete point-in-time S&P 500 (2010–2024, survivorship-free), the market-implied growth  g * genuinely tracks the growth firms subsequently realize (correlation ≈ 0.4–0.5, nearly unbiased at the 10-year horizon) and is robust across independent recovery methods (Spearman 0.73–1.00).  The Brina Gap is a detector of over-extrapolated growth expectations:  the market systematically over-extrapolates growth — the calibration slope sits below one at every horizon — and the median firm priced for high growth under-delivers what its price implies (≈ 26% priced in vs ≈ 22% realized).  Head-to-head against the classical Margin of Safety, the Gap is mechanical and falsifiable where the Margin of Safety is not, nearly orthogonal to it in cross-section, and more accurate on the one directional test both can take (+3.9 points, p ≈ .004; the Gap's expensive-side calls were correct 58.9% of the time on the full universe).  Among all pure valuation metrics tested — book-to-market, earnings yield, EPV, the Margin of Safety — the Brina Gap ranks first, and it is the only one whose central claim can be verified at all.  Its practical form is the  Brina Matrix , which crosses the Gap's pricing read with fundamental quality and yields one rule that survives every specification tested:  "cheap" is only a bargain when quality is high — cheap plus low quality is the value trap, the worst-performing cell in the sample. We are equally explicit about the limits: the fundamental arm is a conservative anchor, not a forecast; and the Gap — like every metric in the companion audit, the Margin of Safety included — is not a standalone return signal, which is exactly what efficiency logic predicts for any transparent, filings-based measure, in the most pricing-hostile decade on record. Data and code are published: a per-call outcomes file and a one-command verifier reproduce every headline number (see below). Verify the headline numbers yourself (added in v3.0.1). directional_outcomes_v3.0.csv lists all 1,504 directional calls on the complete point-in-time S&P 500, 2010–2024, delisted and acquired firms included (CRSP-style). Running python3 verify_headline_claims.py (Python standard library only) recomputes: • Stocks the Brina Gap clearly flagged as priced too high trailed the S&P 500 over the next five years in 546 of 927 cases (58.9%; a coin flip gives 50%). Exact one-sided binomial p = 3.3×10⁻⁸: if the warnings were coin flips, a record this good would come up about once in 30 million tries. • On the same 1,504 calls the classic Margin of Safety scored 50.9% (chance); the Gap 54.8%: +3.9 points, year-clustered bootstrap p = 0.0038. • Value Trap calls: 59.5% (207 of 348). The Gap's "cheap" calls were at chance (48.2%), as the paper reports. The paper claims no standalone return edge (over every stock, sign only: 52.4%). See README_VERIFY.md. Two parts:  Part I — the paper (the construct, its theory, the validity battery, the Brina Matrix); Part II — the complete empirical record (directional tests, robustness, failure modes, pre-registered refinements).  Supersedes v1.0 and v2.0; their d
title: The Brina Gap: A Framework for Identifying Growth Mispricing in Equity Markets

summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law. For $n=3$ the examples refine the symmetric non-mixable laws of Yin and Zhu, and the reduction explains why those laws satisfy the inequalities.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

summary: MakeCOO is a Wolfram Language command-line package that constructs a stoichiometric matrix from reaction definitions. It represents each reversible reaction as separate forward and reverse records and constructs a matrix with chemical species as rows and directed reactions as columns. It also exports the species list and directed reaction table. This archive contains MakeCOO version 0.3.0, the version used to construct the stoichiometric matrix in the anaerobic Mn(II) oxidation case study. It includes the source code, documentation, example inputs and tests, and the shared Utils/IO.wl file. The software is distributed under the MIT License. If you use MakeCOO in research, please cite the accompanying article by Mayumi Seto and Yuya Tsukamoto in Geomicrobiology Journal ( https://doi.org/10.1080/01490451.2026.2762317 ).
title: MakeCOO: Stoichiometric matrix construction from reaction definitions

summary: Supplementary materials (v5.3.0) for: Design-based null audits: what two decades of pronoun-production experiments could and could not detect This package supports a design-based statistical audit of the predictability literature on pronoun production (story-continuation paradigm, 1994–2023). The audit asks whether the designs that produced this literature's null results were capable of detecting the effects they tested, via (i) a re-extraction of all eligible effect sizes on the log-odds-ratio scale with quasi-separation screening, (ii) design-by-design minimum-detectable-effect (MDE₈₀) simulation under each study's own published parameters, and (iii) power-contour guidance for future designs. Package structure: Online Resource 1 (search & PRISMA screening), Online Resource 2 (effect-size extraction workbook with provenance and separation flags), Online Resource 3 (publication-bias diagnostics: Egger regression and contour-enhanced funnel plots), audit data and figures (MDE table, power grid, Figures 1–3), seeded simulation code (Python authoritative + R re-implementation, plus separation-screening and power-grid tools), and the superseded original OSF materials of the companion meta-analysis. Relation to other materials: The correlation-based meta-analytic dataset audited and superseded by this re-extraction is archived in the OSF project osf.io/gx5ad ("Referential Predictability in Pronoun Production: Evidence from Meta-Analysis and Simulation for a Generalized Bayesian Model"). Version note (v5.3.0): BRM submission-readiness revision of v5.2.1 — data unchanged; adds separation flag column, contour-enhanced funnel plots with generation script, bit-exact power-grid code (verified against the shipped grid), separation-screening tool, requirements.txt and sessionInfo() records. Egger-test p-values in the manuscript should read .020 (subjecthood) and .312 (thematic role); see Online Resource 3 README. All simulations are seeded (20260825 / 20260827).

summary: Receive → Give-Forward as the Substrate-Invariant Atom of a Reciprocity Economy This paper discloses a design criterion for peer-to-peer gift, reciprocity and gratitude systems (pay-it-forward schemes, time banks, complementary currencies, peer-recognition ledgers): classify each transfer by where the recipient's next transfer goes — onward to a third party (generalized reciprocity: a gift that circulates) or back to its source in a return that settles the account (balanced reciprocity: an exchange). With it come a six-way taxonomy of gift flows by relational scope, a bounded relay subclass that preserves provenance, and a three-tier classification of transferable value by hoardability that predicts how much lifecycle machinery each kind requires. The criterion is applied to HeartBank, which is, on its surface, many mechanisms: a family-scale money economy, an adult-scale time economy, a line of physical gratitude artifacts, a matchmaking instrument, an autonomous AI successor, a planetary balancing game. This paper makes a reductive claim about all of them. There is exactly one atomic operation underneath the entire institution: give as a gift, not as exchange — whose circulation form, and the form every network product implements, is receive a gift, then give it forward — never back. The claim has three dimensions of invariance. The operation is invariant across currency : the thing received-and-forwarded can be money (a re-tip), time (funded presence), a physical object (a passed artifact), or a gene (a trait selected and propagated), and the operation is structurally identical in each. It is invariant across scale : it runs at the level of a person (one self-thank forwarded), a family (a circulating object), a civilization (a synchronized annual disbursement), and a species (kindness propagated by mate choice). And it is invariant across substrate : it is the same operation whether it executes in software, in the hand, or in biology. The biological cases (the gene, the species, the biological substrate) are resemblances rather than instances by the sameness criterion of §9.8; the invariance claimed is across money, time and object, from person to civilization, in the digital and physical substrates. summary: The internet's prevailing identity-and-authentication systems were designed for account ownership, not for proving authentic human presence at the moment of digital interaction. As generative AI makes synthesized content indistinguishable from human-produced content, every platform that depends on a distinction between human and machine participation faces a sybil-resistance problem the existing identity stack cannot solve. Proof of Humanity ℠ (PoH℠) is an open protocol for proving authentic human presence at the moment of action, structured as four optional layered proofs (passkey-per-action, witness-and-document-attested kinship graph, continuous breath-signature liveness, DNA-verified kinship lineage) surfaced as depth on a user profile, paired with recipient-side filters that route the spam-cost decision to the parties who bear it. B-PoH℠ is HeartBank's reference deployment of the PoH protocol — brand-family-prefixed by the project's B-prefix convention, the way Let's Encrypt is a specific certificate authority implementing the SSL/TLS protocol. This paper specifies the protocol architecture, the recipient-filter mechanism, the BLE-Nearby proximity verification path that preserves location privacy, the bilateral-uncacheable-anonymity property, and the placement of B-PoH℠ beside Proof of Work and Proof of Stake as a proof bounded by humanness, in the line of earlier proof-of-personhood work (§12) — the proof-of-X primitive that fits the era when compute and capital have both become AI-commodified, leaving humanness as a scarce resource AI cannot readily manufacture. The protocol is offered defensively to the commons under CC0; the authors and HeartBank® will not seek patent on the protocol specification or any portion thereof. Trademark rights on specific marks ( Proof of Humanity ℠ , PoH℠ , B-PoH℠ , Aquarius℠ , HeartBank® , the B-heart logo) are separately and explicitly reserved. summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. summary: For every integer p>=4, a previously constructed symmetric numerical semigroup ring R_p and rigid two-generated monomial ideal determine a conductor ideal T_p whose special fiber C_p = F(T_p) is one-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay, generated in degree one by 10p monomials, with multiplicity 24p. Taking the imported offset bases as input, we prove that C_p ≅ k[xy^a : a ∈ G_p] ⊆ k[x,y]/(y^24p), that its defining ideal J_p is primary to the ideal of positive offsets, with nilpotency index 24p, and that Proj(C_p) is a saturated length-24p curvilinear fat point, locally Gorenstein although the coordinate ring has Cohen-Macaulay type 10p+1. The Kähler differentials split by characteristic. We then determine the reduced Gröbner basis for graded reverse lexicographic order with X_0 last. Its degree profile is (50p^2-17p, 5p-1, p-2) and no minimal leading monomial contains X_0, which gives a flat Cohen-Macaulay monomial degeneration. The quadratic part, the stabilization of the staircase, the absence of elements in degree five and higher, the absence of X_0 from the leading monomials and the flatness are derived from derived imported input; the imported relation type three is machine-verified. The cubic and quartic classification, for all p, is machine-verified and not derived: 16 Presburger obligations are decided unsatisfiable by Z3 and by cvc5 on identical queries, with no checked proof object. Exact sweeps at every p=4,...,300, an independent clique recomputation and negative controls validate the formulas. The results concern the conductor fiber cones of this explicit family; they do not assert that arbitrary monomial fiber cones are primary, curvilinear, Cohen-Macaulay or locally Gorenstein. Source code, compact artifacts, premise hashes and proofs: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH .

summary: The widespread application of inductive loads in today ‘s power distribution systems where power factor (PF) correction has become an integral requirement, has led to power factor degradation as a serious problem and requires correction for more efficient power distribution. In this paper, an innovative AI based Adaptive PF correction scheme is proposed to integrate conventional PF correction capacitor bank compensation with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based predictor-controller for dynamic reactive power compensation. A detailed MATLAB/Simulink 3–phase distribution system-based model has been evolved which yields operational data sets for ANN training and testing with different loading conditions. Proposed ANN predictor-controllers are trained with back-propagation algorithm applying MSE (Mean Squared Error) function as a network performance measure. The network prediction accuracy 96.9 to 97.8% and the generalization capability has been established through comprehensive results analysis. The proposed architecture significantly decreases the reactive power demand by approximately 77%, apparent power consumption by 28.1% and the dynamic response by 3 times compared to fixed capacitor compensation method. Moreover, the (PF) is maintained between 0.95–0.96, confirming its effectiveness for real-time adaptive power factor correction in modern distribution systems.
title: AI-Based Adaptive Power Factor Correction for Reactive Power Reduction in Distribution Systems

summary: Microbiome Repo — data package v1.34.0 (2026-11-14) One catalog, two tiers, all ages. The catalog tables ( catalog_* ) are the curated tier: human-associated microbial communities sequenced by shotgun DNA or RNA sequencing, from every body site and at every age — 5,086 projects, 813,356 samples, 4,814,518 sample × field values — with body site, age at collection, sex, BMI, country, health condition (controlled vocabulary), antibiotic exposure, subject and timepoint recovered from archive attributes (R1), supplementary tables (R2), paper full text (R3) and abstracts (R4); every value carries a verbatim evidence quote (≤ 12 words), a labelled source, a route and a confidence. Each run is labelled DNA or RNA ( catalog_runs.nucleic_acid ), each sample says which data sets it has ( has_dna , has_rna ), and each project carries the nucleic acid of its data sets ( catalog_studies.nucleic_acid ). Coverage over all catalog samples: age 24%, sex 31%, country 89%, health condition 45%, antibiotic exposure 14%. The registry tables ( registry_* ) list every screened public study in ENA/SRA/DDBJ with a human-associated metagenome signal — 64,369 studies — with archive-only classification (host, UBERON-anchored body sites, life stages, assay, access) and the harvested BioSample tier (637,397 BioSamples with normalised site / age / sex / country). Start here. catalog_studies.parquet (one row per project: body sites, DNA / RNA, papers, methods and setting read from the paper, per-field coverage, age-category and health-condition mix, curated depth) → catalog_sample_metadata_wide.parquet (one row per sample: every field with __route / __confidence , body_site_code , age_category + basis, has_dna / has_rna ) → catalog_sample_determinations.parquet (the evidence behind every value) and catalog_runs.parquet (every run). registry_studies.parquet is the registry; registry_runs_v1.34.0.parquet (every screened run) ships as a GitHub Release asset.
