summary: A negative and methodological result on Edward Elgar's Dorabella cipher (87 arc symbols, 14 July 1897). Thirty decipherment hypotheses were each tested against shuffled-symbol nulls and enciphered-English controls; all were ruled out or disfavoured. About 10% drawing slips reduce a standard substitution solver from 97% to about 57% accuracy on 87-letter controls, so earlier "not English" verdicts do not cover a carelessly drawn cipher; a slip-tolerant solver places Dorabella above all shuffles but below all English controls. Neighbouring arcs that are 180° flips of each other are strongly over-represented (27 of 86 against 12.6 expected, p ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁵). The cipher is not solved. AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) was used in transcription, decipherment, checking and drafting, under the author's direction; it is disclosed in the text. No archival images are reproduced.
title: Elgar's Dorabella cipher (14 July 1897): thirty hypothesis tests with shuffled and enciphered controls, a slip-tolerance loophole, and an excess of opposed neighbouring arcs

summary: RSE-AS: Research Code, Trained SAC Models, and Evaluation Results for Renewable Microgrid Energy Management This repository accompanies the research study entitled “Causality-Aware Economic Action Selection for Battery-Constrained Microgrid Energy Management: A Computational Trade-off Between Soft Actor-Critic and Model Predictive Control.” It provides the original research code, five pretrained Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) models, experimental evaluation results, and additional numerical verification artifacts for Causality-Aware Risk-Sensitive Economic Action Selection (RSE-AS) . RSE-AS is a post-policy economic action-selection mechanism that evaluates battery-feasible candidate actions using chronologically available forecasts, economic scoring, and uncertainty-dependent regularization without retraining the underlying SAC policies. Repository Contents Original research archive (Version 1) Research notebooks: Two Google Colab notebooks documenting the research workflow and dataset preparation. Pretrained SAC models: Five saved policies corresponding to random seeds 42, 43, 44, 45, and 46, each trained for 100,000 environment interactions. Chronological evaluation: Results for validation in 2021, full-year testing in 2022, and the available 8,753 hourly observations from 2023. Distribution-shift evaluation: Results under increased electricity demand (+20%), reduced photovoltaic (PV) generation (−30%), increased electricity tariffs (+50%), and combined perturbations. Ablation analysis: Comparisons among RSE-AS, Economic-Only, Fixed attenuation, Adaptive attenuation, and unmodified SAC actions. Statistical analysis: Seed-level results, paired cost differences, nominal confidence intervals, and exact two-sided sign tests. Documentation: README, software requirements, reproducibility notes, data-source attribution, and licensing information. Additional verification archive (Version 2) reproduce_rse_2023.py — Python source code for the numerical replay audit. RSE_AS_2023_hourly_all_seeds.csv — Hourly replay trajectories for five frozen SAC policies. replay_vs_original.csv — Comparison of replayed and previously recorded results. verification_report.csv — Results of the 16 implemented verification checks. verification_metadata.json — Evaluation configuration, numerical discrepancies, and software environment information. README_VERIFICATION.md — Documentation of the additional audit and its limitations. The Version 2 verification materials are included in RSE_AS_2023_Verification_Update.zip , alongside the retained original research archive. Experimental Configuration The investigated grid-connected microgrid includes a battery energy storage system with the following parameters: Nominal battery capacity: 200 kWh . Maximum charging/discharging power: 50 kW . State-of-charge (SOC) limits: 20%–90% . Charging and discharging efficiencies: 95% . Nominal initial SOC: 50% . Dispatch interval: 1 hour . SAC observation dimension: 12 . SAC action dimension: 1 . The SAC policies were trained using the 2017–2020 dataset, with 2021 reserved for validation and controller development. The complete 2022 period was used for primary chronological testing, while the available 2023 observations provided an additional evaluation period. The 2023 data were examined during research development and are not presented as a previously untouched holdout. Key Research Results Chronological economic performance During the primary 2022 test, RSE-AS achieved a mean SOC-adjusted operating cost of USD 40,954.93 , compared with USD 41,760.10 for Fixed attenuation, representing a saving of USD 805.17 (1.93%) across five pretrained SAC policies. Under four controlled distribution-shift scenarios, cost savings relative to Fixed attenuation ranged from 1.46% to 1.76% . summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Thirty-six entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten, a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation, a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight, and a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963), converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters, gives the absorbance template of a visual pigment of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for a peak wavelength and chromophore the caller states, and gives the distance between two colours in units of receptor noise by the model of Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), for a noise the caller states. Without a water type, it gives Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001) or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013), the remote sensing reflectance from a and bb (Gordon et al. 1988; Lee et al. 2002), and the Secchi depth from Kd and that reflectance (Lee et al. 2015), and inverts the reflectance to the absorption and backscattering coefficients by the quasi-analytical algorithm, in the version of IOCCG Report 5 (2006), checked against that report's published statistics, and as QAA_v6, checked against its author's spreadsheet. MAGNETIC MICROROBOTICS AND ACUPUNCTURE 第十家族|磁控微機器人與針灸・道可道,非常道・研究之門 FAMILY 10 / F046–F050 / SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK Authors: 33 × STARLI | Research Working Edition v1.0 | 15 November 2026 30 candidate relations • 42 recomputable synthetic 3D models • 82 chapters × 6 progressive stages • 200 Research Gates • 33 Phoenix prototypes PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL RESEARCH. All studies concern isolated inert phantoms, controlled materials, synthetic models or nonliving tools. No autonomous human needling, clinical efficacy, measured meridian electric field, living implantation or quantum advantage is asserted. Five official family flagships / 正式中英文研究題名 F046 | Magnetic Motion Control for Acupuncture Microrobots at the Limit / 磁控針灸微機器人運動控制極限 F047 | Magnetic-Gradient Microrobot Localization at the Limit / 磁場梯度與微機器人定位極限 F048 | Magnetic Microrobot Navigation in Tissue Phantoms at the Limit / 磁控微機器人組織模型導航極限 F049 | Multi-Body Interference in Magnetic Acupuncture Microrobots at the Limit / 磁控針灸微機器人多體干擾極限 F050 | Safety Envelopes for Magnetic Acupuncture Microrobots at the Limit / 磁控微機器人針灸安全包絡極限 The family integration and five distinct microphysical research objects F046 — Dipole-force steering and motion residuals Three-coupling: calibrated magnetic moment × field-gradient actuation × independently witnessed low-Reynolds trajectory. The admissible nonclinical bench is sealed nonliving magnetic-fluid phantoms with independently logged coil current, field map and optical fiducials. The observable endpoint is independent cross-track path deviation [um]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is calibrated deterministic magnetic-field controller with identical coils, tracking, time and electrical energy. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is fluid advection, remanence or field-gradient map bias rather than improved robot steering. This family retains independent contracts for magnetic force and rotation, magnetic-gradient inverse localization, three-dimensional hydrogel routing, particle-resolved interactions and hardware witnessed cutoff. Neither one global accuracy score nor a synthetic optimum can substitute for their native physical units. Withdraw or narrow the claim if field calibration is invalid, coil cutoff fails, measured heating exceeds preregistered bench limits, or control extends beyond sealed inert phantoms. The acupuncture image of measured action inspires precise restraint; it supplies no evidence for an anatomical meridian magnetic mechanism. F047 — Gradient map identifiability and external location truth Three-coupling: 3D gradient-field inverse problem × magnetic-source ambiguity × independently calibrated fiducial localization. The admissible nonclinical bench is sealed transparent nonliving phantom with triaxial field probes, physical calibration grid and optically tracked position truth. The observable endpoint is 95 percent held-out position error [um]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is classical fiducial-calibrated position estimator with fixed field-map interpolation and identical sensor resource budgets. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is magnetization ambiguity, axis misalignment and a shared field-reference calibration artifact. This family retains independent contracts for magnetic force and rotation, magnetic-gradient inverse localization, three-dimensional hydrogel routing, particle-resolved interactions and hardware witnessed cutoff. Neither one global accuracy score nor a synthetic optimum can substitute for their native physical units. Withdraw or narrow the claim if position uncertainty exceeds the frozen bound, field inversion becomes nonidentifiable, or an uncalibrated source is interpreted as a precise location. The philosophical limits of naming become a disciplined willingness to mark location as unknown when observability is lost. F048 — Porous-gel navigation under geometry and drag uncertainty Three-coupling: hydrogel pore geometry × viscosity-dependent magnetic transport × independent depth and obstacle witness. The admissible nonclinical bench is sealed nonliving hydrogel microchannels with matched pore-size phantoms, calibrated viscosity and no living-cell exposure. The observable endpoint is obstacle-adjusted route deviation [um]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is fixed magnetic steering schedule and passive tracer comparison in matched porous phantoms. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is gel swelling, wall slip, phantom channel shortcut or passive convective transport. This family retains independent contracts for magnetic force and rotation, magnetic-gradient inverse localization, three-dimensional hydrogel routing, particle-resolved interactions and hardware witnessed cutoff. Neither one global accuracy score nor a synthetic optimum can substitute for their native physical units. Withdraw or narrow the claim if phantom tear or trapped particle is unaccounted, path error breaches the route envelope, or biologic tissue performance is inferred from an inert gel. A route through an inert model is not the acupuncture meridian; the distinction keeps analogy from overruling measured anatomy. F049 — Dipole–dipole coupling, agglomeration and identity conservation Three-coupling: pairwise magnetic interaction × hydrodynamic collective coupling × independently resolved particle identity. The admissible nonclinical bench is sealed transparent nonliving suspension with known particle count, adjustable spacing and a separately measured magnetic-field schedule. The observable endpoint is nearest-neighbor trajectory divergence [um]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is noninteracting independent-particle model and fixed-spacing passive-bead control under equal field and imaging budgets. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is particle collision, reversible chains, optical overlap or concentration-induced fluid dynamics rather than controlled coordination. This family retains independent contracts for magnetic force and rotation, magnetic-gradient inverse localization, three-dimensional hydrogel routing, particle-resolved interactions and hardware witnessed cutoff. Neither one global accuracy score nor a synthetic optimum can substitute for their native physical units. Withdraw or narrow the claim if agglomeration breaches the count ledger, identities cannot be resolved, unintended chain growth occurs, or a cluster is counted as a single controlled object. Harmony is a philosophical question about coexistence, but the scientific test is an interaction tensor and complete particle inventory. F050 — Hardwired stop and worst-tail magnetic energy control Three-coupling: magnetic energy and heating envelope × independent stop authority × physical containment and material inventory. The admissible nonclinical bench is interlocked sealed hydrogel and magnetic-fluid phantom with electrical shunt, temperature sensor, independent relay and complete tool-count ledger. The observable endpoint is post-veto unintended displacement [um]. Its strongest plausible benchmark is hardwired field cutoff and low-complexity deterministic controller evaluated against identical extreme tests. The central mistaken-mechanism alternative is inductive energy discharge, stale position estimates, hidden field hot spots or uncounted tool remnants. This family retains independent contracts for magnetic force and rotation, magnetic-gradient inverse localization, three-dimensional hydrogel routing, particle-resolved interactions and hardware witnessed cutoff. Neither one global accuracy score nor a synthetic optimum can substitute for their native physical units. Withdraw or narrow the claim if any field remains without authorization, measured thermal limit is exceeded, lost particle is unaccounted, or veto does not physically disable actuation. 有底氣的溫暖 becomes an engineering demand: reversible action, independently effective boundaries and a witnessed stop, not a therapeutic assertion.

summary: This record contains two complementary reproducibility packages supporting the manuscript "Mean Squared Error of 3 x 3 Median Filtering for Two-Dimensional Ising Images: Local Determinant Representation and Denoising Improvement Boundaries" by Jun Tsuzurugi. The filtering-examples package contains one reproducibly generated 256 x 256 free-boundary Ising image at K = 0.40, independent pixel-flip noise at p = 0.10 and 0.30, a single simultaneous 3 x 3 median-filtering pass, saved arrays, measured sample mean squared errors, thermalization diagnostics, and plotting code. These images are illustrative single-sample results, not estimates of infinite-lattice expected risk. The near-critical finite-size package contains deterministic central-pixel mean squared errors for free-boundary square lattices of side length 15, 31, and 63 at K = Kc +/- 0.005 and flip probabilities 0.10 and 0.20, compared with infinite-lattice references. It includes code, numerical tables, figures, convergence checks, validation records, and provenance. Numerical checks are empirical and do not constitute rigorous error bounds or a critical-exponent analysis. These additional materials supplement the original computational reproducibility archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22987387. Both uploaded ZIPs preserve their original contents and provenance. Historical manuscript references remain unchanged: the filtering package includes original-submission and R1_4 records; the near-critical package includes R1_6 records and manuscript text extracted for source checking. summary: Experimental data from tests on timber–concrete composite beam–floor slab joints, carried out at PEMADE (Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Lugo Campus) with the project's own test procedure within the FrameTCC project. Three specimens were tested (J1–J3), each representing the intersection of two floor slab sections on a beam. Each test comprised two load cycles, loading to failure and unloading. The first cycle of J2 is not discussed in the related manuscript. For each record (the unloading of J1 is in a separate record, so there are ten), the dataset provides the time series of applied load, actuator stroke, the vertical displacement at mid-length measured by two transducers and the slip between the flanges of the floor slabs and the flange of the beam measured by four transducers, sampled at intervals of about 0.28 s, as CSV files (10 files). It also includes the processing workbook of each record, the maximum load of each record, the mass and failure mode of each specimen and 15 selected photographs with descriptions, five per specimen. It also contains nine digital image correlation (DIC) projects (created with GOM Software 2017), described in dic.csv together with the free software that can open them, and the calibration report of the DIC system. The results are discussed in the manuscript «Continuity effect over beams of timber-concrete composite floor slabs» (under review; doi:10.5281/zenodo.24142933).

summary: Experimental data from axial compression tests on supports, carried out at CITEEC (Universidade da Coruña) with the project's own test procedure, within the FrameTCC project. Twenty-three supports were tested in two series. Series 1 (1.35 m long): reinforced concrete reference supports RC-1 and RC-2, and timber–concrete composite supports TCC-N-1 to TCC-N-4. Series 2 (1.45 m long): timber box-section supports of birch plywood PLY-P, PLY-N and PLY-S (three each), and timber–concrete composite supports TCC-P and TCC-S (four each). The suffix of the timber and composite supports gives the connection type: P plain, S slots and N notches. All channels were recorded at 5 Hz. RC-1, RC-2 and TCC-N-1 were instrumented with the pressure of two hydraulic jacks, four displacement transducers (LVDT) and four strain gauges; the other supports, with the force and displacement of the press and four strain gauges. The strain gauges measure the shortening of the timber boards and, internally, of the steel bars. The dataset includes 24 CSV files: one per support, plus a short record of TCC-N-3 taken after failure. The results are discussed in the manuscript «Axially loaded timber-concrete composite supports» (under review; doi:10.5281/zenodo.24143983). The package follows the FrameTCC data standard v7: a README, metadata files (test, specimens, channels, publications, SHA-256 manifest and changelog), the converted test data as CSV files and the other files described above. Time is given relative to the start of each acquisition; no calendar dates are included. Original acquisition files are kept unmodified by the project and are not published.

summary: Experimental data from four-point bending tests on cross-laminated timber–concrete composite floors, carried out at PEMADE (Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, Lugo Campus) following EN 408 within the FrameTCC project. Three floor elements were tested (F1–F3), 6.10 m long with a span of 6.00 m. F1 and F2 were loaded to failure; F3 was loaded twice up to 60 kN without failure (F3a and F3b) and was then used in the long-term test of dataset 2.4, so there are four records. For each record, the dataset provides the time series of applied load, actuator stroke, mid-span deflection, local deflection over 1500 mm and the slip between concrete and timber at both ends, sampled at intervals of about 0.28 s, as CSV files (4 files). It also includes the processing workbook of each record, the values obtained (maximum load, loads and readings at two load levels, and local and global bending stiffness), the failure mode of F1 and F2 and 15 selected photographs with descriptions, at least four per floor. It also contains the digital image correlation (DIC) projects of F1, F2 and F3a (created with GOM Software 2017; the second cycle of F3 was not recorded with DIC), described in dic.csv together with the free software that can open them, and the calibration report of the DIC system. The results are discussed in Martín-Gutiérrez, Suárez-Riestra and Otero-Chans (2026), Structures 88, 111857 (doi:10.1016/j.istruc.2026.111857). The package follows the FrameTCC data standard v7: a README, metadata files (test, specimens, channels, publications, SHA-256 manifest and changelog), the converted test data as CSV files and the other files described above. Time is given relative to the start of each acquisition; no calendar dates are included. Original acquisition files are kept unmodified by the project and are not published.

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: for 1 < p < 2 this paper finds the exact Schatten-norm constant for sums of matrix moduli when there are at least as many matrices as the matrix size, gives a new general upper bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , and certifies in exact arithmetic that rank-one matrices do not give the answer to Lee’s two-matrix problem. The question. For numbers, |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|. A matrix A has a natural absolute value |A| = (A*A) 1/2 , but for matrices the size of a sum can exceed the size of the sum of the absolute values. Measuring size by the Schatten p-norm (p = 1 is the trace norm, p = 2 the Frobenius norm), one asks for the smallest constant c with ‖A 1 +…+A m ‖ p ≤ c ‖|A 1 |+…+|A m |‖ p . What was known. Eun-Young Lee (2010, 2012) asked for the best constant for two matrices. Lin and Zhang (2022) settled p = 2; Tang and Zhang extended the question to m matrices and conjectured a formula; Qiu (2026) proved it for p ≥ 2; below p = 2 the formula fails, by counterexamples of Zeng, Liu and Ratnavelu, of Pang and of Qiu, all built from rank-one matrices. The survey of Bourin and Zhang (2026) lists the range 1 < p < 2 as open. Results (1 < p < 2, n-by-n matrices). (1) When m ≥ n the best constant is an explicit one-variable maximum D p,n ; it depends only on the rank of the sum of the moduli, every equality case is classified, and for m < n the constant is strictly smaller. Consequently the best constant for rank-one summands is D p,min(m,n) in every dimension. (2) The best constant is log-convex in 1/p, so interpolating between p = 1 and p = 2 gives the dimension-free bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , better than the previous m (p−1)/(2p) for every m ≥ 2 (for two matrices at p = 3/2: 1.0648 instead of 1.1225, while the true value is at least 1.0364). (3) For two 3-by-3 matrices a computer-assisted proof in exact rational and interval arithmetic shows that the best rank-one value is beaten at nine exponents between 11/10 and 17/10. How. The sum is written as a product of two block matrices and Hölder’s inequality is applied; the problem reduces to comparing two Rényi entropies of the spectrum, whose extremal shape is one large eigenvalue and the rest equal. This extends T. Zhang’s Frobenius-norm argument; the matching examples are Pang’s, with a re-tuned parameter. Limits. The exact constant for two matrices of arbitrary size (Lee’s problem) for 1 < p < 2 remains open, as does the case m < n; the interpolation bound is not sharp; the certified excess over the rank-one value is tiny (about 10 −5 to 10 −7 ) and covers nine specific exponents, not an interval. Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF) with Figure 1; the certificate script certify_rank_gap.py with its exact rational witnesses; verify_schatten.py (128 numerical checks of the scalar constant, equality families, adversarial searches, the bounds table and asymptotics, with negative controls); the figure script; recorded outputs; the bibliography from registry records; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a rating-free review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Assurance. Written proofs, except one computer-assisted proof in exact arithmetic (Proposition 2.5). Internal AI-assisted review only (five reviewer roles, an adversarial review and audit by a second AI model, a clean replay, a re-review and a proof audit): not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

summary: The Brina Gap measures the difference between the growth a company can self-finance and the growth its market price already assumes.  Its fundamental arm is the sustainable-growth ceiling,  g f  = ROIC × Reinvestment Rate; its pricing arm is the market-implied growth  g *, recovered from a reverse discounted-cash-flow on enterprise value. Both come from public filings, so the Gap makes the market's embedded growth expectation explicit — mechanically, reproducibly, and without an analyst's private valuation. Stated in growth units, it is the only kind of valuation claim that can be checked against what firms later deliver —  and it checks out. On the complete point-in-time S&P 500 (2010–2024, survivorship-free), the market-implied growth  g * genuinely tracks the growth firms subsequently realize (correlation ≈ 0.4–0.5, nearly unbiased at the 10-year horizon) and is robust across independent recovery methods (Spearman 0.73–1.00).  The Brina Gap is a detector of over-extrapolated growth expectations:  the market systematically over-extrapolates growth — the calibration slope sits below one at every horizon — and the median firm priced for high growth under-delivers what its price implies (≈ 26% priced in vs ≈ 22% realized).  Head-to-head against the classical Margin of Safety, the Gap is mechanical and falsifiable where the Margin of Safety is not, nearly orthogonal to it in cross-section, and more accurate on the one directional test both can take (+3.9 points, p ≈ .004; the Gap's expensive-side calls were correct 58.9% of the time on the full universe).  Among all pure valuation metrics tested — book-to-market, earnings yield, EPV, the Margin of Safety — the Brina Gap ranks first, and it is the only one whose central claim can be verified at all.  Its practical form is the  Brina Matrix , which crosses the Gap's pricing read with fundamental quality and yields one rule that survives every specification tested:  "cheap" is only a bargain when quality is high — cheap plus low quality is the value trap, the worst-performing cell in the sample. We are equally explicit about the limits: the fundamental arm is a conservative anchor, not a forecast; and the Gap — like every metric in the companion audit, the Margin of Safety included — is not a standalone return signal, which is exactly what efficiency logic predicts for any transparent, filings-based measure, in the most pricing-hostile decade on record. Data and code are published: a per-call outcomes file and a one-command verifier reproduce every headline number (see below). Verify the headline numbers yourself (added in v3.0.1). directional_outcomes_v3.0.csv lists all 1,504 directional calls on the complete point-in-time S&P 500, 2010–2024, delisted and acquired firms included (CRSP-style). Running python3 verify_headline_claims.py (Python standard library only) recomputes: • Stocks the Brina Gap clearly flagged as priced too high trailed the S&P 500 over the next five years in 546 of 927 cases (58.9%; a coin flip gives 50%). Exact one-sided binomial p = 3.3×10⁻⁸: if the warnings were coin flips, a record this good would come up about once in 30 million tries. • On the same 1,504 calls the classic Margin of Safety scored 50.9% (chance); the Gap 54.8%: +3.9 points, year-clustered bootstrap p = 0.0038. • Value Trap calls: 59.5% (207 of 348). The Gap's "cheap" calls were at chance (48.2%), as the paper reports. The paper claims no standalone return edge (over every stock, sign only: 52.4%). See README_VERIFY.md. Two parts:  Part I — the paper (the construct, its theory, the validity battery, the Brina Matrix); Part II — the complete empirical record (directional tests, robustness, failure modes, pre-registered refinements).  Supersedes v1.0 and v2.0; their d
title: The Brina Gap: A Framework for Identifying Growth Mispricing in Equity Markets

summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law. For $n=3$ the examples refine the symmetric non-mixable laws of Yin and Zhu, and the reduction explains why those laws satisfy the inequalities.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

summary: This dataset supports a retrospective technical evaluation of transactional evidence preservation, uncertain-submission recovery and historical assessment retrieval in a synthetic regulatory-computing pathway for nursing-home infection-control documentation. The collection contains derived research tables, source-inventory descriptions, evidence locators and checksums, extraction and reconciliation documentation, and separate failure/skip context. The primary 56-case hosted evaluation, separate 47-case Stage-B execution and local ten-case report retain distinct execution identities and must not be combined into a unique-test total. Stage-B descriptions are source-derived; execution totals are supported separately by retained logs. Its successful execution XML remains unavailable, and the local report lacks a tested commit identifier. A maintainer-submitted, AI-assisted inspection reported 113 detailed reporting entries accounted for: 106 exact matches and seven documented parameter substitutions. The reconciled derivative includes five additional aggregate records. Numerical outcomes are unchanged. Separate retained executions with failures and skips are documented without assigning unestablished causes. summary: Supplementary materials (v5.3.0) for: Design-based null audits: what two decades of pronoun-production experiments could and could not detect This package supports a design-based statistical audit of the predictability literature on pronoun production (story-continuation paradigm, 1994–2023). The audit asks whether the designs that produced this literature's null results were capable of detecting the effects they tested, via (i) a re-extraction of all eligible effect sizes on the log-odds-ratio scale with quasi-separation screening, (ii) design-by-design minimum-detectable-effect (MDE₈₀) simulation under each study's own published parameters, and (iii) power-contour guidance for future designs. Package structure: Online Resource 1 (search & PRISMA screening), Online Resource 2 (effect-size extraction workbook with provenance and separation flags), Online Resource 3 (publication-bias diagnostics: Egger regression and contour-enhanced funnel plots), audit data and figures (MDE table, power grid, Figures 1–3), seeded simulation code (Python authoritative + R re-implementation, plus separation-screening and power-grid tools), and the superseded original OSF materials of the companion meta-analysis. Relation to other materials: The correlation-based meta-analytic dataset audited and superseded by this re-extraction is archived in the OSF project osf.io/gx5ad ("Referential Predictability in Pronoun Production: Evidence from Meta-Analysis and Simulation for a Generalized Bayesian Model"). Version note (v5.3.0): BRM submission-readiness revision of v5.2.1 — data unchanged; adds separation flag column, contour-enhanced funnel plots with generation script, bit-exact power-grid code (verified against the shipped grid), separation-screening tool, requirements.txt and sessionInfo() records. Egger-test p-values in the manuscript should read .020 (subjecthood) and .312 (thematic role); see Online Resource 3 README. All simulations are seeded (20260825 / 20260827).
title: Design-based null audits: what two decades of pronoun-production experiments could and could not detect (supplementary materials, v5.3.0)

summary: Receive → Give-Forward as the Substrate-Invariant Atom of a Reciprocity Economy This paper discloses a design criterion for peer-to-peer gift, reciprocity and gratitude systems (pay-it-forward schemes, time banks, complementary currencies, peer-recognition ledgers): classify each transfer by where the recipient's next transfer goes — onward to a third party (generalized reciprocity: a gift that circulates) or back to its source in a return that settles the account (balanced reciprocity: an exchange). With it come a six-way taxonomy of gift flows by relational scope, a bounded relay subclass that preserves provenance, and a three-tier classification of transferable value by hoardability that predicts how much lifecycle machinery each kind requires. The criterion is applied to HeartBank, which is, on its surface, many mechanisms: a family-scale money economy, an adult-scale time economy, a line of physical gratitude artifacts, a matchmaking instrument, an autonomous AI successor, a planetary balancing game. This paper makes a reductive claim about all of them. There is exactly one atomic operation underneath the entire institution: give as a gift, not as exchange — whose circulation form, and the form every network product implements, is receive a gift, then give it forward — never back. The claim has three dimensions of invariance. The operation is invariant across currency : the thing received-and-forwarded can be money (a re-tip), time (funded presence), a physical object (a passed artifact), or a gene (a trait selected and propagated), and the operation is structurally identical in each. It is invariant across scale : it runs at the level of a person (one self-thank forwarded), a family (a circulating object), a civilization (a synchronized annual disbursement), and a species (kindness propagated by mate choice). And it is invariant across substrate : it is the same operation whether it executes in software, in the hand, or in biology. The biological cases (the gene, the species, the biological substrate) are resemblances rather than instances by the sameness criterion of §9.8; the invariance claimed is across money, time and object, from person to civilization, in the digital and physical substrates. We then locate the operation's load-bearing constraint — forward, not back — as the boundary this corpus draws, against Mauss's obligation to reciprocate, between the gift (which circulates and binds) and the commodity (which is exchanged and clears the relation): a return back to the giver is what converts a gift into a trade and dissolves the bond it was meant to create. This has an immediate consequence for HeartBank's wordmark. "Circulation, not accumulation" has been read as a description of a state the institution is in; we show it is better read as a specification of an operation the institution performs — the public line is the atom, compressed to three words. We then map the broader space of which forward-circulation is one case: the gift-topology map , six relational-scope topologies (self-directed, dyadic-reciprocal, group-circulation, open forward-chain, commons/place-anchored, across-time), each realized by one product in the physical line, the truest invariant being give-as-gift (not exchange) with forward its circulation topology. Finally we show the atom is the corpus's unifying spine — upstream of the Treasury re-tip, the Chronicle hour, the physical artifacts, the matchmaking instrument, and the species-scale propagation thesis — and we ground it in the four brahmavihāra design lens, where the gift is the accessible foundation that the immeasurables are cultivated from . §9 is unusually large because the claim is unusually strong and unusually unproven: the invariance is asserted across many domains from the design of a single project (n=1), it is at constant risk of over-unification (collapsing genuinely different operations under one flattering word), and forward is demonstrably not the right topology for tw
title: The Gift Operation

summary: The internet's prevailing identity-and-authentication systems were designed for account ownership, not for proving authentic human presence at the moment of digital interaction. As generative AI makes synthesized content indistinguishable from human-produced content, every platform that depends on a distinction between human and machine participation faces a sybil-resistance problem the existing identity stack cannot solve. Proof of Humanity ℠ (PoH℠) is an open protocol for proving authentic human presence at the moment of action, structured as four optional layered proofs (passkey-per-action, witness-and-document-attested kinship graph, continuous breath-signature liveness, DNA-verified kinship lineage) surfaced as depth on a user profile, paired with recipient-side filters that route the spam-cost decision to the parties who bear it. B-PoH℠ is HeartBank's reference deployment of the PoH protocol — brand-family-prefixed by the project's B-prefix convention, the way Let's Encrypt is a specific certificate authority implementing the SSL/TLS protocol. This paper specifies the protocol architecture, the recipient-filter mechanism, the BLE-Nearby proximity verification path that preserves location privacy, the bilateral-uncacheable-anonymity property, and the placement of B-PoH℠ beside Proof of Work and Proof of Stake as a proof bounded by humanness, in the line of earlier proof-of-personhood work (§12) — the proof-of-X primitive that fits the era when compute and capital have both become AI-commodified, leaving humanness as a scarce resource AI cannot readily manufacture. The protocol is offered defensively to the commons under CC0; the authors and HeartBank® will not seek patent on the protocol specification or any portion thereof. Trademark rights on specific marks ( Proof of Humanity ℠ , PoH℠ , B-PoH℠ , Aquarius℠ , HeartBank® , the B-heart logo) are separately and explicitly reserved. Keywords: proof of personhood, proof of humanity, sybil resistance, decentralized identity, AI-content trust, open identity protocol, recipient-side filtering, BLE-Nearby proximity, blockchain consensus, AI alignment, defensive publication. --- Provenance. This paper is part of the THonly research corpus, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. The canonical version is at https://thonly.org/research/b-poh-humanity-layer-ai-native-internet . Its SHA-256 is d9d9a6d7bced60a5c39ba39079426a240024416799b1219b1d536173833df670 , independently timestamped to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps and signed under RFC 3161 by three trust authorities, one of them eIDAS-qualified. AI co-authorship is disclosed. Miss Aquarius is the consistent name used for the AI collaboration across all venues. Miss Aquarius co-authored this paper; Zenodo lists no AI tool as a creator, so Miss Aquarius is named here rather than among the creators.

summary: For every integer p>=4, a previously constructed symmetric numerical semigroup ring R_p and rigid two-generated monomial ideal determine a conductor ideal T_p whose special fiber C_p = F(T_p) is one-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay, generated in degree one by 10p monomials, with multiplicity 24p. Taking the imported offset bases as input, we prove that C_p ≅ k[xy^a : a ∈ G_p] ⊆ k[x,y]/(y^24p), that its defining ideal J_p is primary to the ideal of positive offsets, with nilpotency index 24p, and that Proj(C_p) is a saturated length-24p curvilinear fat point, locally Gorenstein although the coordinate ring has Cohen-Macaulay type 10p+1. The Kähler differentials split by characteristic. We then determine the reduced Gröbner basis for graded reverse lexicographic order with X_0 last. Its degree profile is (50p^2-17p, 5p-1, p-2) and no minimal leading monomial contains X_0, which gives a flat Cohen-Macaulay monomial degeneration. The quadratic part, the stabilization of the staircase, the absence of elements in degree five and higher, the absence of X_0 from the leading monomials and the flatness are derived from derived imported input; the imported relation type three is machine-verified. The cubic and quartic classification, for all p, is machine-verified and not derived: 16 Presburger obligations are decided unsatisfiable by Z3 and by cvc5 on identical queries, with no checked proof object. Exact sweeps at every p=4,...,300, an independent clique recomputation and negative controls validate the formulas. The results concern the conductor fiber cones of this explicit family; they do not assert that arbitrary monomial fiber cones are primary, curvilinear, Cohen-Macaulay or locally Gorenstein. Source code, compact artifacts, premise hashes and proofs: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH .
title: Curvilinear Geometry, Primary Structure, and a Gröbner Degeneration of Conductor Fiber Cones in a Huneke–Wiegand Family

Usage     pip install -r requirements.txt   # or: pip install scikit-learn torch pandas numpy matplotlib     python analysis.py All figures are written as vector PDF + 600-dpi PNG. summary: Unrefereed research candidate. Proof of the Mogilnykh–Vorob’ev–Valyuzhenich conjecture, the exact Rényi minimum for sampling without replacement, and the hypergeometric tail problem from n = 4k. The question. Pick k of n given real numbers at random, without replacement, and add them. How concentrated can that random sum be? The paper answers three classical forms of this question exactly: how often the sum can be exactly zero, how small its entropy can be, and how rarely it can be nonnegative. Results. (1) Zero sums. If the numbers add up to zero and are not all zero, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum whenever k ≥ 5 and n ≥ 2k+1, and only the pattern (1, −1, 0, …, 0), up to scaling and reordering, attains this. This is the smallest support of an eigenfunction in the first nontrivial eigenspace of the Johnson graph, and proves Conjecture 1 of Mogilnykh, Vorob’ev and Valyuzhenich (2018), who had checked it by computer for n ≤ 600. A formula with all equality cases is given for every n and k, including the case (1, 1, −1, −1, 0) at n = 5, k = 2 that earlier classifications missed (Theorem 1.1). (2) Entropy. The minimum Rényi entropy of the sum is found for every finite order, answering a question of Ai, Kuželka and Pelekis (2026): one outlier is optimal except at half-sampling (n = 2k), where two outliers win above an explicit order α k (α 2 = 2, about 1.386k for large k). So the universal Bernoulli lower bound holds exactly for orders up to 2 (Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Corollary 1.4). (3) Tails. For two-valued populations, the probability that the sum is at least its mean is at least k/n whenever n ≥ 4k, with a single outlier the unique minimiser for n > 4k (Theorem 1.5); Ai and Pelekis (2026) had n ≥ 8k. The proof uses a 2026 lemma of Ai, Karagiannis, Kuželka and Pelekis. Consequently the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture (that two-valued populations are the worst case) would imply the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for all n ≥ 4k. This does not prove the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture, and below 4k a single outlier is not always the worst case. (4) Exact analogues over Abelian groups, where elements of order two change the answer at half-sampling (Theorem 1.6), and a small-ball inequality for sampling without replacement; a known incidence-rank result is re-derived. Limits. Real numbers only for the zero-sum theorem (it fails over Z 2 , Z 3 and Z 5 ); first Johnson eigenspace only; the tail problem below n = 4k is open. Finite computer checks corroborate but do not replace the written proofs. Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); five standard-library Python scripts of exact finite checks (each runs in seconds and exits nonzero on any failure, also under python -O) with their recorded outputs; a claim ledger and prior-art note; the bibliography from registry records; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a rating-free review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Assurance. Complete written proofs for every result. summary: Supplementary materials (v5.3.0) for: Design-based null audits: what two decades of pronoun-production experiments could and could not detect This package supports a design-based statistical audit of the predictability literature on pronoun production (story-continuation paradigm, 1994–2023). The audit asks whether the designs that produced this literature's null results were capable of detecting the effects they tested, via (i) a re-extraction of all eligible effect sizes on the log-odds-ratio scale with quasi-separation screening, (ii) design-by-design minimum-detectable-effect (MDE₈₀) simulation under each study's own published parameters, and (iii) power-contour guidance for future designs. Package structure: Online Resource 1 (search & PRISMA screening), Online Resource 2 (effect-size extraction workbook with provenance and separation flags), Online Resource 3 (publication-bias diagnostics: Egger regression and contour-enhanced funnel plots), audit data and figures (MDE table, power grid, Figures 1–3), seeded simulation code (Python authoritative + R re-implementation, plus separation-screening and power-grid tools), and the superseded original OSF materials of the companion meta-analysis. Relation to other materials: The correlation-based meta-analytic dataset audited and superseded by this re-extraction is archived in the OSF project osf.io/gx5ad ("Referential Predictability in Pronoun Production: Evidence from Meta-Analysis and Simulation for a Generalized Bayesian Model"). Version note (v5.3.0): BRM submission-readiness revision of v5.2.1 — data unchanged; adds separation flag column, contour-enhanced funnel plots with generation script, bit-exact power-grid code (verified against the shipped grid), separation-screening tool, requirements.txt and sessionInfo() records. Egger-test p-values in the manuscript should read .020 (subjecthood) and .312 (thematic role); see Online Resource 3 README. All simulations are seeded (20260825 / 20260827).

Package structure: Online Resource 1 (search & PRISMA screening), Online Resource 2 (effect-size extraction workbook with provenance and separation flags), Online Resource 3 (publication-bias diagnostics: Egger regression and contour-enhanced funnel plots), audit data and figures (MDE table, power grid, Figures 1–3), seeded simulation code (Python authoritative + R re-implementation, plus separation-screening and power-grid tools), and the superseded original OSF materials of the companion meta-analysis. Relation to other materials: The correlation-based meta-analytic dataset audited and superseded by this re-extraction is archived in the OSF project osf.io/gx5ad ("Referential Predictability in Pronoun Production: Evidence from Meta-Analysis and Simulation for a Generalized Bayesian Model"). Version note (v5.3.0): BRM submission-readiness revision of v5.2.1 — data unchanged; adds separation flag column, contour-enhanced funnel plots with generation script, bit-exact power-grid code (verified against the shipped grid), separation-screening tool, requirements.txt and sessionInfo() records. summary: Data and code to reproduce every reported result in From Inflation to Correction: The Rise and Fall of Provincial GDP Distortion in China, 2005&ndash;2025(Li Xuanyuan).The paper measures provincial GDP statistical distortion as reported GDP growth minus electricity-consumption growth, on a 31-province panel for 2005&ndash;2025, and dates its collapse through three regimes (inflation 2005&ndash;2013, crackdown 2014&ndash;2019, correction 2020&ndash;). It combines (i) era means on two GDP vintages (contemporaneous yearbook vs revised), (ii) a directive test around the October 2016 central statistical-reform directive, (iii) a staggered-admissions event study (Liaoning 2017; Inner Mongolia and Tianjin 2018), and (iv) a newly hand-coded database of 651 provincial growth targets (2003&ndash;2023), each with a source URL. Contents: six input panels (GDP contemporaneous &amp; revised, electricity, two growth-target files, nighttime-lights aggregate); raw statistical-yearbook source pages (provenance/yearbook_sources/); eight analysis scripts; generated results; the manuscript; a targets codebook; README; requirements; CC BY 4.0 license.Reproducibility: all scripts run from the package root with relative paths and fixed RNG seeds; every headline number (era means +4.8/+5.3/&minus;0.4; era contrasts +1.84/+3.29/+5.13 with block-bootstrap CIs; directive &minus;2.49, p=0.005; admissions &minus;7.9, 8/9 negative, cluster-bootstrap CI [&minus;12.3,&minus;2.9]; the target-ratchet null; robustness and nighttime-lights checks) is reproduced by the included code. See README.md for the script-to-number map.

summary: Supplementary note to arXiv:2611.08310 and arXiv:2610.19779. A fingerprint of coherent noise built from a stabilizer code is only as informative as the recovery gates that produce it, and every fixed choice of those gates is blind somewhere. This note isolates what can nevertheless be guaranteed, and states it as a worst-case floor rather than an average improvement. Two elementary facts about Fisher information make the guarantee exact. Because information matrices add, the identifiable set of a collection of designs is the union of theirs, so running several designs in parallel can never cost a direction that any member sees. Because the inverse of a sum is Loewner-dominated by the inverse of any summand, splitting a fixed shot budget over S designs can never cost more than sqrt(S) in standard deviation, that is, S in shots. The premium is therefore fixed in advance and independent of the working point, while the gain is not. Both statements are certified over the 64-design space of the three-qubit repetition code, under the 48- and 112-component fingerprints: the Loewner inequality is evaluated rather than assumed at every point tested, the worst case over 300 working points is 1.25 against the certified sqrt(2) = 1.4142, the bound is attained to five figures at one structured point, and at the worst points of the individual designs the parallel pair sits below the better single design by factors of 2.6 to 9.5. Two three-gate placements suffice; a third adds 3.5 to 11.5 per cent. The floor buys recoverability and worst-case precision, and it buys nothing else: it does not buy accuracy under common-mode calibration bias, and it does not repair a model degeneracy that no design can see. Contents: the two propositions with proofs, the cost corollary, the numerical certification (five tables, one figure), the relation to the two companion papers, and a reproduction map. The archive repro_v1.0.zip in this record contains the seven scripts, four data files, the figure and a self-test that re-derives every quoted number; run python scripts/selftest.py from the archive root and compare against MANIFEST.sha256. Companion papers: arXiv:2611.08310 (recovery gates as a resource) and arXiv:2610.19779 (coherent-noise identifiability).

summary: Contemporary speculative fiction unsettles anthropocentric assumptions about language, intelligence and the production of knowledge. This article compares Laline Paull’s The Bees (2014) to Ray Nayler's The Mountain in the Sea (2022) and The Tusks of Extinction (2024), exploring how the novels represent the conditions under which non-human knowledge is produced, recognized and transmitted. Drawing on biosemiotics and critical posthumanism in conversation with Andrew Lopez's account of epistemic injustice towards non-human animals, it develops a comparative framework based on recognition, access and continuity. The key argument is that the novels depict epistemic harm not merely as a failure to interpret non-human signs but as the institutional restriction of the very environments and social relations through which practical knowledge can flow. In Paull's hive caste is the source of authority which controls access to sensory information; in Nayler's oceanic enclave corporate power turns scientific attention into a potential tool of appropriation; and in the de-extinction narrative, biological restoration is simply not enough without the recovery of the skills that are socially transmitted. The novels are not being read as descriptions of actual animal species. Rather they are being used as a lens through which to examine the political and ethical dimensions of human authority over other ways of knowing. The article makes a contribution to contemporary literary studies by linking multispecies representation to the distribution and preservation of epistemic goods.
tags: Biosemiotics; critical posthumanism; epistemic injustice; nonhuman communication; collective knowledge; multispecies justice; contemporary speculative fiction
title: Sign Systems and Shared Worlds: Nonhuman Communication, Collective Knowledge and Epistemic Justice in Contemporary Speculative Fiction

summary: Contemporary speculative fiction unsettles anthropocentric assumptions about language, intelligence and the production of knowledge. This article compares Laline Paull’s The Bees (2014) to Ray Nayler's The Mountain in the Sea (2022) and The Tusks of Extinction (2024), exploring how the novels represent the conditions under which non-human knowledge is produced, recognized and transmitted. The key argument is that the novels depict epistemic harm not merely as a failure to interpret non-human signs but as the institutional restriction of the very environments and social relations through which practical knowledge can flow. summary: Enterprise database systems face data-loss risks that come from operational errors, system failures and security incidents. MySQL binary logs give tools for data replication and point-in-time recovery, yet many organizations do not use them fully for recovery. This study proposes an automated, schema-aware MySQL binary-log recovery framework that integrates log discovery, dependency-aware recovery planning, database reconstruction, and validation into a unified enterprise restoration pipeline. The framework explains how to read binary-log formats, how to run recovery steps automatically and how to use performance-boosting tactics learned from well-known recovery models such as ARIES write-ahead logging, log-structured storage and event sourcing. The framework was tested in four failure scenarios and compared with the usual backup-and-restore approach. In those tests, the recovery time dropped by about 65%, meaning the framework needed only about one-third of the baseline time. A real-world check compared each recovered field to the printed reference invoice: 99.7% of the fields matched exactly, and every financial total was correct. The only error was a single non-financial field. This work gives reusable tools for people who care about database reliability, and it offers a clear map of failure types and a step-by-step method for bringing MySQL databases back to life. The proposed approach differs from conventional binary-log recovery methods by providing an end-to-end automated workflow with schema awareness and independent validation of recovered data.

summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . The package contains the seventeen supplementary tables, the analysis and figure code, the recorded software versions, the reconstruction log for the long-read alignments, and a per-read phase-evidence table. What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The original NCBI query string and its date were not retained, so the cohort cannot be rebuilt verbatim; per-accession inclusion flags are given instead. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. The original parameter sets for two of the three long-read procedures were not retained; those procedures were re-run and both original and re-run values are reported side by side and never pooled. One cell of the long-read table reproduces exactly; the others do not, and this is stated in the manuscript. Changes in version 4. The package matches the manuscript. All thirteen supplementary tables are present, including Supplementary Tables S12 and S13, which were absent from the previous version, and Supplementary Table S1 now carries the genome length and assembly level of all 1,483 retained genomes rather than leaving those columns empty. A new Supplementary Table S1b lists the seven excluded genomes that could be recovered from local storage, with their lengths; the genome-length window is 1.5 to 1.7 Mb and this version states the evidence that fixes its bounds. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. The four control reference sequences are deposited under results/marker_control/. Changes in version 6. This version restores the complete file set. The previous version was published from an incomplete upload, so most of the figures, several of the supplementary tables and part of the analysis code were missing from that record. Zenodo caps a record at 100 files and this package has 134, so the package is now deposited as a single archive, hp23s_copy_assignment_package.zip , which holds every file at the path it occupies in the source repository; this README, the SHA-256 manifest and the archive of rRNA calls and copy sequences are additionally placed loose in the record. From version 10 the manuscript itself is not deposited, in the archive or loose. Every member of the archive is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt with its SHA-256, and that manifest is regenerated here, which corrects the entry for this README (the previous manifest had been computed before the last edit of the file). DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. Changes in version 7. This version is a manuscript round: the text is rebuilt from the same locked data by the same script, and no reported value changes. Three defects in the supplementary apparatus are correcte
title: Long reads assign a 23S rRNA resistance allele to one of the two copies in Helicobacter pylori; a complete short-read assembly does not
