summary: Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN): mathematical revisions, corrected datasets, and reproducible computational resources This repository provides an integrated historical, empirical, and computational resource for the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN) framework. It brings together the foundational development of the model, original and corrected crown-network records, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, principal component analyses (PCAs), editable network drawings, and computational tools for reconstructing and analyzing woody crown networks. The deposit is an independent scientific resource, not tied to any particular journal or manuscript. HISTORICAL FOUNDATION Four publications document the development of the WCHN framework: Souza et al. (2011): initial network analyses of Cerrado tree crowns. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11258-010-9797-7 Prado et al. (2020): formalization of network decomposition, topology, and the four original properties. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtbi.2020.110318 Prado and Trovão (2023): expansion to eight properties and comparative analyses of Caatinga and Cerrado networks. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2023.110345 Prado (2024): stochastic node-addition networks and size-matched comparisons. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40626-024-00340-5 These references enable users to trace the original definitions, subsequent revisions, and development of the framework. INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REFERENCE The definitions, revised equations, algebraic identities, mathematical properties, conditions of definition, and theoretical implications of the WCHN framework are now documented in a separate, independently published and versioned Zenodo record: Prado (2026). Algebraic Relationships and Mathematical Properties of the Woody Crown Hydraulic Network (WCHN). Version 1.0.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24181915 This mathematical reference includes the revised definitions of symmetry (SYM), complexity (COM), and topological vulnerability (VUL); exact algebraic relationships among WCHN properties; network-size dependence; and mathematical and numerical checks. In particular, revised VUL is equivalent to normalized mean node depth in a rooted tree. The near-reciprocity observed between navigability (NAV) and VUL is an empirical relationship, not an additional algebraic identity or evidence of physiological equivalence. The mathematical document was included in an earlier version of the present dataset deposit. Beginning with the current version, it is maintained exclusively in its independent Zenodo record. Earlier published versions retain their original archived files for historical traceability. EMPIRICAL DATASETS AND ECOLOGICAL REANALYSES The deposit contains the original Cerrado and Caatinga source spreadsheets, recalculated WCHN properties, ecological comparisons, reduced PCAs, and exploratory network-size-adjusted analyses. The complete field collection comprises 99 WCHNs: 75 from Cerrado and 24 from Caatinga. Recalculated tables incorporate the revised SYM, COM, and VUL definitions. The reduced PCAs use NAV, VUL, LAT, BAS, and PTP, with 24 Caatinga networks and 74 complete Cerrado networks. Previously deposited PCA and partial-correlation results are preserved without numerical recalculation in this update. Their interpretation should account for network-size dependence, shared topological information, and the revised mathematical meaning of VUL. The accompanying README_Size_Adjusted_PCA_v2.md documents the methods, results, assumptions, and limitations of the size-adjusted analyses. summary: Data belonging to the work "An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua" Using Lunaria annua , I manipulated resource availability via branch removal to test whether reduced competition induces compensatory funiculus thickening. I measured funiculus thickness and seed area in basal and apical fruits, analyzing seed fate and trait scaling relationships. Branch removal induced global funiculus hypertrophy, which was disproportionately higher in basal positions. Funiculus expansion was positively associated with seed survival and growth, though plants converted transport capacity into biomass more effectively in apical positions. Results also showed a decoupling of the within-fruit size–number trade-off, challenging classical inverse correlations.
tags: competition, plasticity, resource allocation, seed abortion, sub-individual variation.
title: An architectural upgrade? Funiculus hypertrophy under altered source–sink balance in Lunaria annua

summary: The rapid growth of digital payments has increased the importance of reliable credit card fraud detection systems. Traditional rule-based approaches can struggle to identify com plex and evolving fraud patterns, particularly when fraudulent transactions represent only a small proportion of transaction data. This paper presents a machine learning-based framework that combines data preprocessing, class-imbalance handling, autoencoder-based feature representation, and XGBoost clas sification. The study uses the publicly available credit card transaction dataset containing 284,807 transactions, including 492 fraudulent transactions. Robust scaling is used to reduce the influence of extreme values, while the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied only to the training data. An autoencoder learns a compact representation of trans action features and calculates reconstruction error; these outputs are combined with the prepared features for downstream clas sification. XGBoost is used to distinguish legitimate transactions from potentially fraudulent ones. The framework is evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, area under the precision recall curve (PR-AUC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). The paper also describes an API-oriented deployment workflow. Numerical results should be reported from the final reproducible experiment; illustrative or previously obtained values must not be treated as independently verified without rerunning the implementation.
title: Securing Digital Transactions: Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: Equipment-embodied growth theory predicts that reallocating fixed-capital formation from civil structures toward machinery and plant modernization accelerates industrial output, yet high-investment transition regions routinely channel over half of capital outlays into construction-installation works. Assembling regional fixed-capital simplex panels across all 14 regions of Uzbekistan (2000–2025 for technological shares, N = 364; 2007–2025 for reproduction modes, N = 266; 2016–2025 for constant-price industrial value-added growth, N = 140) alongside boundary-harmonized regional benchmarks from Kazakhstan (2003–2026Q3), we evaluate compositional reallocation hypotheses using full-simplex two-way fixed-effects regressions and 9,999 null-imposed wild cluster bootstrap replications. Across all six primary specifications conditioning on real investment scale, real investment growth, employment growth, and residual simplex shares, shifting 10 percentage points from construction-installation works into machinery and equipment yields statistically unresolved contemporaneous (+0.74 percentage points; bootstrap p = 0.7025; 95% bootstrap interval [-1.66, 3.66]) and lagged (+0.56; bootstrap p = 0.3828) industrial growth associations that remain null under predetermined scale controls (+0.63; bootstrap p = 0.3710); a one-year-ahead dynamic association (+1.52; bootstrap p = 0.0319) does not survive six-horizon Holm correction (p = 0.1914), and omitting either Karakalpakstan's 10 region-years (-0.60; bootstrap p = 0.0812) or its single 2016 observation (-0.35; bootstrap p = 0.4017) reverses contemporaneous point estimates negative. On the capital-input margin, reallocating 10 percentage points from greenfield expansion to reconstruction and modernization is associated with a 4.35 percentage-point higher regional machinery share (bootstrap p = 0.0003; 5.75 percentage points with real-scale controls, bootstrap p = 0.0003), while Uzbek-Kazakh subnational comparisons show persistent civil-works dominance whose cross-sectional financing gradients depend on regional consolidation and own-funds scope. Archive contents and offline reproduction: Version 1.0.0 ( central-asia-capital-composition-industrial-growth-v1.0.0.zip ; 99 files; SHA-256: 480f9ee676afa63aaa7eefe0848d162ceadc63d7c1f7292264b5406ef6404572 ) contains frozen official primary statistical and statutory inputs publicly available on or before 13 November 2026 ( raw_data/ ), harmonized estimation panels and variable dictionaries ( analysis_data/ ), numerical regression and diagnostic tables ( output/ and results/ ), publication-scale 300 DPI PNG and vector SVG multi-panel figures ( figures/ ), pinned Python dependencies ( requirements.txt ), and self-contained offline reproduction scripts ( python code/run_all.py and python code/render_figures.py ).
title: Dataset and Replication Code for: Bricks Over Machines: Capital Technological Composition, Reconstruction Versus Greenfield Expansion, and Regional Industrial Growth in Uzbekistan with Subnational Benchmarks from Kazakhstan

summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score

summary: Oltre il Quadrato: La griglia 4:3 e la precisione architettonica nell’Adorazione dei Magi Il saggio propone un ribaltamento metodologico nell’analisi del disegno preparatorio per l’Adorazione dei Magi di Leonardo da Vinci conservato agli Uffizi. Superando la tesi tradizionale di una maglia prospettica a base quadrata, l’autore dimostra, attraverso l’uso di software CAD e tecniche di retro-ingegneria, come Leonardo abbia adottato una griglia di rettangoli in rapporto armonico 4:3. Questa scoperta non solo risolve storiche incongruenze visive — restituendo alle arcate delle scale la loro perfetta forma a tutto sesto coerente con la misura del “braccio fiorentino” — ma svela un’applicazione consapevole di geometrie legate al pentagono e alla sezione aurea. Il lavoro sottolinea il notevole rigore logico e matematico di Leonardo, trasformando quello che era ritenuto un errore prospettico in una sofisticata architettura della visione. L’analisi si sviluppa attraverso una sequenza di osservazioni visive direttamente leggibili sul foglio 436E, verifiche CAD e procedimenti di geometria inversa, concepiti come linee di evidenza indipendenti ma convergenti. Beyond the Square: The 4:3 Grid and Architectural Perfection in the Adoration of the Magi This study presents a methodological shift in the analysis of Leonardo da Vinci’s preparatory drawing for the Adoration of the Magi. Moving beyond the traditional assumption of a square based perspective grid, the author utilizes CAD software and reverse-engineering techniques to demonstrate Leonardo’s use of a rectangular grid with a 4:3 harmonic ratio. This discovery resolves long-standing visual inconsistencies, showing that the arches in the background regain their perfect semicircular form when aligned with this modularity, consistent with the Florentine braccio unit of measurement. Furthermore, the analysis reveals the deliberate application of pentagonal geometry and the Golden Ratio.   This research highlights Leonardo’s mathematical rigour, showing that what was previously perceived as a perspectival error is, in fact, a sophisticated architecture of vision.  The analysis unfolds through a sequence of direct visual observations readable on the Uffizi sheet, CAD-based verifications, and inverse procedures, conceived as independent yet convergent lines of evidence.  This study integrates direct visual evidence from Leonardo’s drawing with CAD-based verification and inverse geometric reasoning.   Keywords: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration of the Magi, Perspective, 4:3 Grid, CAD Analysis, Florentine Braccio, Golden Ratio.
title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / The Revealed Geometry (it/en)

QUANTUM COMPUTING FOR INVERSE DESIGN OF 4D MATERIALS FAMILY 12 / F056-F060 / THE OTHER SIDE OF THE RESEARCH MONOGRAPH Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI / White Rainbow Era Scientific status: Prospective nonclinical proposal. All diagrams are analytical synthetic illustrations. No quantum advantage, qualified device, biomedical treatment or patient recovery has been demonstrated. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE 4D MATERIALS RESEARCH An inverse design begins with a wish: a material should bend to a specific shape after a particular sequence of heat, light, solvent or magnetic stimuli. The wish is not evidence. A specimen has a history, a printer has a feature limit, and a camera can mistake a smooth silhouette for recovered function. In this notebook the research chain is followed from physical permission to constitutive model, to competing computational designs, to damaged and rejected specimens, and finally to a negative case that another laboratory can recreate. Five independent flagships supply different scientific questions. F056 concerns a constrained inverse map from target response to material recipe. F057 studies the discrete matching of material configuration with time-dependent target shapes. F058 forces mathematical topology into a printable connected solid. F059 asks whether prediction intervals survive new lots and measurement chains. F060 refuses to consider a design validated until printed output, failures, material loss and costs have been measured. Coupling them yields a useful research system only when their evidence contracts remain distinct. The source genealogy matters. The author-provided four-dimensional microrobotics research book gives a physical vocabulary for responsive structures, fatigue and fabrication. The independent BCI-stroke study gives a separate rationale for minimizing assistance and distinguishing device function from recovery after a device is removed. The forty-family blueprint identifies the F056-F060 lineage and emphasizes the hazard of an optimum that cannot be manufactured. No source proves that a quantum-designed microbot has restored human motor function. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is the public name of the present research method. The first stage asks what material and laboratory can legitimately do. The second asks which mathematical program is meaningful. The third proposes a strong ordinary rival. The fourth tries hard, bounded counterexamples. The fifth freezes the evidence that can survive independent reconstruction. This is a set of epistemic viewpoints, not a claim about physical parallel universes. A strong scientific notebook should be able to disagree with the monograph. Where the monograph records an observable and a pre-registered test, the notebook should ask why the observable was chosen, what the test would miss, and which apparently trivial rival might explain its result. Repetition can be a conceptual return to a difficult distinction rather than duplicated filler. But no return should be mistaken for new measurement. The most important distinction is between speed of design and quality of evidence. More candidate samples, more attractive plots or more pages cannot establish physical printability. Nor can a verified specimen establish quantum computational advantage if the full pipeline costs and carefully tuned classical methods were never compared. A scientific stop is legitimate when the boundary and next decisive experiment are clear. Research Doors should remain the most alive part of this system. The question left at the end of each chapter is not an invitation to endorse the current model. It is an instruction to try to defeat it with a better observation. If the next laboratory discovers that a classical algorithm, a clamp motion or a material batch artifact explains the beautiful result, the research family has still preserved useful knowledge. That is what makes it a handoff rather than a claim of perfection. The relevant physical endpoints are held-out curvature error [1/m], tip displacement [um] and batch yield [1]. Its strongest immediate rival is the proposition that a rich surrogate or uncounted classical preprocessing explains the optimization gain. A blinded test should blindly swap material lots and stimulus order after designs are frozen. Independent instruments include independent optical displacement [um], curvature [1/m], locally mapped temperature [K], material lot ID and complete query ledger; the ordinary comparator set comprises tuned Bayesian optimization, adjoint or surrogate inverse search, classical mixed-integer programming and matched evaluation budgets. QUANTUM OPTIMIZATION FOR REHABILITATION CONTROL AT THE LIMIT FAMILY 11 | F051-F055 | SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK A connected argument through 82 chapters: Mechanism / Measurement / Refutation Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI | White Rainbow Era | 2026 SCIENTIFIC STATUS: Prospective, nonclinical, falsifiable research architecture. No patient trial, tested quantum supremacy, demonstrated stroke recovery, or qualified medical device is claimed. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CONTROL MONOGRAPH The technical notebook is not a glossary pasted below the research monograph. It is a second argumentative surface. The monograph states exactly what can be tested, with candidate equations, independent measurements and research gates. The notebook asks why the experiment deserves construction, which competing explanation should be taken most seriously and how an unsuccessful first generation could become a stronger foundation for someone else. This difference is a methodological commitment rather than a claim of novel experimental results. Family eleven begins from an uncomfortable contrast between optimization and authority. A method may compute a more attractive control input, but no numerical attractiveness can authorize an illegal actuator command. The physical and ethical permission envelope must be defined outside the optimizer, and a safe fallback must remain available when the proposed method is late, uncertain, energy-depleted or dependent on inaccessible backend infrastructure. The most important output of a difficult trial may be an unambiguous refusal. The five flagship mechanisms form a causal chain without becoming duplicates. F051 asks what it means to optimize permitted control gains fairly. F052 places the optimizer inside the receding-horizon control clock. F053 asks whether progressively less assistance can maintain a fixed mechanical task, while refusing to equate phantom success with human recovery. F054 requires energy and latency to be counted across acquisition, computation, communication and actuation. F055 tests whether every scientific conclusion remains subordinate to command legality, independent vetoes and serious classical rivals. This lineage comes from two distinct source studies and the author-supplied STARLI forty-family research DNA blueprint. The four-dimensional microrobotics source supplies material history, force generation, responsive structures and safety concerns. The BCI-stroke atlas supplies intention observability, minimally necessary assistance, withdrawal and the crucial distinction between assisted motion and restored independent function. These source relationships are not evidence that a fused 4D, quantum, BCI and clinical treatment platform exists. Five-stage parallel spacetime reasoning is a public name for a disciplined research workflow. Physical origin asks what the bench is permitted to do. Mathematical evolution asks which candidate model and parameters represent it. Counterfactual branching makes the ordinary baseline and hidden confounder genuine competitors. Extreme extrapolation applies bounded adversarial inputs, where the correct output may be stop. Evidence convergence leaves both a reconstructable result and an open Research Gate. These stages are viewpoints on one research contract, not literal physical parallel worlds. A 4D actuator can return to its familiar geometry and still lose force. A quantum optimizer can return a lower cost and still arrive after the legal deadline. A minimally assisted movement can succeed while a person would remain dependent on the device. A smooth average can hide a rare illegal command. Those four asymmetries explain why this research must separate shape, computation, mechanical assistance, function and safety, and why none of these outcomes can be imported into the others without a new experiment. The wisdom of stopping is the opposite of indifference. It means ending a research round when the testable contract is complete, the strongest rival has been confronted, the permission gates have been audited and the next laboratory can reconstruct the adverse case. When further parameter search no longer distinguishes the mechanism from the rival, additional polished prose or training calls do not create new evidence. The unresolved difference becomes an explicit research door for future investigators. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F051 | Quantum-Assisted Post-Stroke Rehabilitation Control Optimization at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is control gain search under hard actuator and state constraints. Its measurable endpoint is angle tracking error and total tuning-to-command cost. The leading alternative says benefit is produced by extra search, hidden preprocessing or the classical controller. The preregistered blind competition would blind-swap candidate gain vectors on identical nonhuman control traces. A fully observed test requires encoder angle [rad], actuator command, output torque [N m], motor work [J], gain-search calls and full wall time [ms] and resource-equivalent comparison with tuned robust PID/LQR, constrained SQP, CMA-ES and mixed-integer gain search with identical runs and CPU/GPU ledger. Each result must be classified as tested observation, source-derived background, synthetic mathematical illustration or unverified hypothesis. No single flagship may import a clinical efficacy conclusion from its neighboring research question. F052 | Quantum-Assisted Model Predictive Control for Rehabilitation Robots at the Limit The core candidate mechanism is finite-horizon constrained optimization with receding-horizon deadlines. Its measurable endpoint is closed-loop error, solver completion percentile and deadline violation. summary: siwecal-soft v0.1.0 First release of siwecal-soft , the software of the SiW-ECAL TB2026 test-beam campaign at CERN: data conversion, simulation, reconstruction and analysis in one Key4hep/Gaudi project. Origin This repository merges two earlier repositories into a single code base with a fresh history: siwecal_k4sim @ 075dedd : simulation of the prototype. DD4hep geometry (including the H2-like upstream beam line), ddsim launchers, digitisation and the simulation campaigns. siwecal-tb2026 @ 90b2e55 : test-beam data. Both repositories are frozen at those commits (tag final-before-monorepo ); new development happens here. Every file of the two repositories is accounted for in tools/migration/ (copied, rewritten or excluded), and the merge was validated against the frozen builds (identical tracking output: 137/137 data and 144/144 simulation EDM4hep branches). What changed with the merge One CMake project (C++20, Key4hep 2026-04-08), one install, one environment script ( init_siwecalsoft.sh ). Shared code and mappings live once in common/ ; calibration tables are read from EOS only. Unified ACTS tracking for data and simulation. Processing steps formerly done in Python now run as Gaudi algorithms: ecal tree writer, occupancy-sag and trigger turn-on calibrators, and the post-PID event selection and valtree ( EcalEventSelection , EcalValTreeWriter ). summary: This record contains supplementary research materials supporting the manuscript entitled "Evaluating Out-of-Fold Weighted Soft Voting for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefits and Limitations of Classifier Fusion" (Manuscript ID: MJCSC-D-26-00018R3), submitted to the Mesopotamian Journal of Computer Science. The study evaluates training-derived optimized weighted soft voting for multiclass network intrusion detection using Decision Tree (DT-Gini), Random Forest variants (RF-Gini and RF-Entropy), and XGBoost. The primary evaluation uses a prepared CICIDS2017 development subset comprising 78,437 observations and 15 traffic classes. An additional dataset-specific evaluation uses a prepared CICIoT2023 subset comprising 99,327 observations, 34 traffic classes, and 39 numerical predictors. The experimental framework includes data preprocessing, mutual information-based feature selection, training-only minority-class oversampling, stratified outer cross-validation, and inner out-of-fold optimization of classifier fusion weights. The supplementary materials are intended to support verification of the reported experimental configurations and results. The original complete source-scanning log and sampling-run metadata for CICIoT2023 are unavailable; therefore, exact independent reconstruction of the original sampling run has not been established. These materials accompany the third-round revised manuscript submitted to the journal.
tags: Network Intrusion Detection; CICIDS2017; CICIoT2023; XGBoost; Weighted Soft Voting; Machine Learning; Reproducibility
title: Reproducibility Materials for Evaluating Out-of-Fold Weighted Soft Voting for Network Intrusion Detection: Benefits and Limitations of Classifier Fusion

summary: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain residual redetection then revise the active path set. For linear frequency modulation (LFM) probes, an observable signal-to-residual ratio adaptively scales the model-order penalty to mitigate overestimation caused by delay-scale coupling. Theoretical analysis links off-grid parameter errors to local cancellation-residual curvature and weak-path detectability. Factorial ablations, paired comparisons against standard sparse and off-grid estimators, and measured channel replay demonstrate improved path-set recovery and waveform reconstruction while delineating the operational boundaries of the method.
title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels

summary: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.
title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels

summary: This preprint evaluates a reversible sample mapping that embeds 8-bit RGB values in the central half of a 9-bit sRGB code space before lossy JPEG XL encoding. The stored file includes a five-byte header that identifies the inverse mapping. The evaluation covers 41 previously unused CLIC Professional and DIV2K validation images at their original resolutions. Under common RGB PSNR and MS-SSIM floors and a single-thread encoding cap of 0.82 seconds per megapixel, the centered mapping reduced aggregate file size by 6.71% relative to direct JPEG XL at effort 6 (95% bootstrap interval: 3.85% to 9.86%). The centered files were 3.94% larger in aggregate than the tested AVIF files. Same-depth and transfer-function controls, together with libjxl coding counters, examine how the input representation affects the result.
title: Centered Sample-Range Remapping at JPEG XL Effort 6

STROKE MOTOR INTENTION AND BRAIN-COMPUTER RESEARCH F081-F085 | SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION Prospective | Nonclinical | Falsifiable | Reproducible | Unbuilt Research Concepts 33 x STARLI OPENING ESSAY | THE AUTHORITY A MODEL DOES NOT HAVE A brain-computer interface is tempting to describe as a bridge between thought and action. But the bridge is only useful when we know what went into the decoder. An electrode voltage is a mixture of cortical, muscle, eye, reference and environmental processes. A task label may record what was instructed rather than what was imagined. A camera can record what moved but not what a person intended. This family treats those distinctions as independent scientific objects, not inconvenient details. The five flagship questions are coupled without being identical. F081 asks whether EEG adds information about spontaneous motor intention after cue clocks and residual muscle activity are accounted for. F082 distinguishes imagery, attempted movement and overt displacement with independent electromyographic and visual witnesses. F083 measures what remains stable across recording days. F084 resists the temptation to hide weak-signal and rare-class strata in a pooled score. F085 observes the safety consequences of false intention triggers during long periods of silence. The minimal platform is an anonymous, synthetic EEG-EMG-EOG task replayer with inert video coordinates, frozen event timestamps and a virtual command queue. The test generator can provide a hidden latent state to evaluate conditional identification. The model never sees that latent state during inference; it must work from the channels and timing evidence available at the specified decision moment. This is a deliberate computational thought experiment and nonclinical engineering proposal, not a physical experiment on stroke survivors. Several rival accounts deserve equal space. Cue onset may encode movement class because the task schedule is regular. Eye motion may precede an instruction. EMG can influence scalp electrodes before obvious displacement occurs. A test-day montage can reveal which session generated a signal. A preprocessing transform can learn the distribution or labels of the held-out partition. A fair protocol separates these shortcuts from useful cortical information with interventions that are physically or informationally interpretable. The real methodological enemy is the persuasive but under-identified success. A model can predict a motor class accurately without identifying voluntary intent. A classifier can distinguish imagery from actual movement using residual muscle activity, not imagination. A transfer algorithm can report stable day-to-day performance after silently adapting on test-day labels. A strong subgroup average can hide dangerous errors among weak signals. Even a correctly predicted category cannot justify a virtual or physical action without authorization and a safety envelope. Prediction and clinical recovery are separate propositions. The current manuscript does not study human participants, deliver rehabilitative interventions or report therapeutic efficacy. Device-driven motion is not device-off recovery. A physical, clinically authorized program would need separate ethical review, independent recruitment, preregistered outcomes and direct functional observation. Our synthetic graphs, however detailed, cannot stand in for that evidence. The most useful classical competitors should not be artificially weak. Cue-only prediction tests whether the experiment provided all the information needed. CSP-LDA, regularized logistic models, Riemannian covariance methods and explicit EMG-video rules can challenge a complex learner with equal data access. Calibration, preprocessing, sensor count, trial duration and temporal alignment all form part of cost. A negative finding can reveal the true measurement limit more effectively than an elaborate but unearned claim of superiority. A scientific three-dimensional plate is a way to expose a functional relationship, not to ornament it. Each surface in the PDF is computed from a documented analytic rule on an exact numeric grid. The outputs are synthetic normalized proxies. The embedded JSON and Python program permit independent recomputation of all forty-two plates. The table of physical units explains what a real EEG, EMG, video or queue experiment would have to measure before the candidate relation could be considered more than a hypothesis. The five-stage parallel spacetime method provides a language for organizing scientific alternatives. Origin questions define the unknown, formal models specify the proposed mechanism, counterfactual branches give rivals room to win, bounded extreme scenarios locate failure, and successor reconstruction transfers the case to a new laboratory. It is a method of intellectual branching. It does not assert that parallel universes were used to calculate a result. Research Gates are deliberately invitations rather than final proofs. In the first set, each door asks how a particular motor-intention ambiguity began. The next set gives conventional signal processing the right to defeat the proposed mechanism. The third constructs unfamiliar but bounded artifact worlds. The fourth gives an independent laboratory the raw history needed to rebuild a result. The final set asks what a technically advanced successor might overturn. Their varying tones should not be mistaken for different measured data; these are different arguments about possible experiments. The thirty-three Phoenix concepts are instruments that do not yet exist in verified form. Some would preserve cue-blind intention witnesses, some audit the cost of daily calibration, and others observe false triggers or the latency of a safety stop in an inert queue. Each prototype has a measurable target and a defined failure. None is authorized as a clinical device. The scientific ambition is to leave an implementable and criticizable question, not to make a claim about unbuilt hardware. For additional methodological context, TRIPOD+AI (DOI 10.1136/bmj-2023-078378) specifies transparent reporting for prediction-model studies. A review of cross-variability decoding of motor-imagery EEG (PubMed 42775222) identifies major challenges in subject/session variability and nonstationarity. These sources motivate reporting discipline and uncertainty; they do not certify our integrated candidate family or any claimed treatment effect. A living scientific manuscript need not be immutable. If future methods show that all five present hypotheses were based on crude modeling, that correction would be welcome. What should survive is the habit of showing independent clocks, an ordinary rival, a missing signal, a false command and an unambiguous stop. The knowledge of how to ask the question is one part of what we can leave to a future investigator. THE FIVE DISTINCT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F081 | Post-Stroke Motor Intention EEG Decoding at the Limit Falsifiable proposed mechanism: identify preparatory cortical signal beyond cue clocks and residual muscle activity in an offline intention replay. Declared primary observables: cue-controlled balanced accuracy [1], conditional information [bit], false triggers [events/h]. The ordinary or confounded world proposes that a decoder memorizes the cue time, recording day or ocular artifact instead of voluntary intention. The concealed discriminating test should blindly permute cue timing while maintaining the source EEG event structure. Instrumental evidence: source-separated synthetic EEG [microvolts], EMG [mV], EOG [microvolts], cue clocks [ms], free-choice intention events and versioned trial IDs. A strong baseline is cue-only timing predictor, regularized logistic EEG classifier, Riemannian covariance baseline and CSP-LDA trained only within sealed source folds. These are plans and measurement contracts only, not records of achieved effect or human treatment. F082 | Distinguishing Motor Imagery from Actual Movement After Stroke at the Limit Falsifiable proposed mechanism: disentangle motor imagery, attempted movement, residual EMG and camera-observed motion under masked timing. Declared primary observables: imagery-movement confusion [1], residual EMG amplitude [mV], intention lead [ms]. The ordinary or confounded world proposes that subthreshold muscle contractions or eye movements masquerade as imagery-dependent EEG features. The concealed discriminating test should withhold the EMG-video agreement channel and test synthetic no-movement imagery trials. F083 | Cross-Day Signal Stability of Stroke Brain-Computer Interfaces at the Limit Falsifiable proposed mechanism: test whether frozen motor-intention decoders remain calibrated across independently replayed electrode days. The ordinary or confounded world proposes that a short-session score hides montage shifts, fatigue and re-calibration leakage. The concealed discriminating test should swap a held-out electrode montage and sleep-fatigue profile without recalibrating on the test day. These are plans and measurement contracts only, not records of achieved effect or human treatment. F085 | Safety Against False Intention Triggers in Stroke BCIs at the Limit Falsifiable proposed mechanism: suppress mistaken intention-triggered commands using calibrated abstention, authorization and inert safe-stop simulation. summary: We formulate a finite-core vorton representation of three-dimensional incompressible Navier– Stokes flow. Smooth divergence-free vorticity fields are represented by finite-core filamentary modes and studied in the limit of decreasing core scale. The singular vorton configuration is obtained strictly as a distributional concentration limit rather than imposed a priori as a singular solution. We prove dynamical equivalence by mapping the infinite-dimensional Navier–Stokes partial differential equations exactly onto the finite-dimensional ordinary differential equations of the discrete vorton ensemble. The passage through the nonlinear convective term is established via Mosco-type energy convergence and Aubin–Lions–Simon compactness. Topological reconnection supplies a microscopic writhe-to-twist transfer to regularize the ultraviolet limit, while a Fredholm boundary reconstruction controls wall interactions via weakly singular integral operators. The resulting framework proves that the continuum flow collapses onto an irreducible, compact geometric attractor, reducing global regularity to a uniform bound on vorticity and satisfying the Beale–Kato–Majda (BKM) criterion for global continuation.
title: RIGOROUS CONVERGENCE OF 3D NAVIER–STOKES TO A VORTON ATTRACTOR

summary: Routing-driven timely data collection in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) is crucial for marine environmental monitoring, disaster warning, and underwater resource exploration, etc. However, harsh underwater conditions, including high delays, limited bandwidth, and dynamic topologies, make efficient routing decisions challenging in UASNs. In this paper, we propose a smart interrupted routing scheme for UASNs to address dynamic underwater challenges. We first model underwater noise influences from real underwater routing features, e.g., turbulence and storms. We then propose a Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-based Interrupted Software-defined UASNs Reinforcement Learning (ISURL) framework, which ensures adaptive routing through dynamical failure handling (e.g., energy depletion of sensor nodes or link instability) and real-time interrupted recovery. Based on ISURL, we propose the MA-MAPPO algorithm, integrating multi-head attention mask mechanism with MAPPO to filter out infeasible actions and streamline training. Furthermore, to support interrupted data routing in UASNs, we introduce MA-MAPPO\_i, MA-MAPPO with interrupted policy, to enable smart interrupted routing decisions in UASNs. The evaluations demonstrate that our proposed routing scheme achieves exact underwater data routing decisions with faster convergence speed and lower routing delays than existing approaches.
title: Smart Interrupted Routing Based on Multi-head Attention Mask Mechanism-Driven MARL in Software-defined UASNs

summary: Drum beats are often conceptualized and produced as arrangements of repeated single-drum sound events or one-shots. Drum Analysis-by-Synthesis (AbS) models combine this structural assumption with reconstruction-based training to perform MIR tasks such as drum transcription, drum source separation, and one-shot extraction, offering a flexible alternative to more traditional task-specific supervision. However, leading AbS approaches struggle to generalize to a broad range of drum timbres (e.g., electronic drum kits), rely on high-quality paired audio-transcription training data, and do not model intra-class timbral variation within a single arrangement (e.g., multiple kick sounds). To overcome these limitations, we propose D-Composer, an autoregressive language modeling framework that decomposes drum recordings into labeled sound events and their onset times. In drum transcription and one-shot extraction tasks, D-Composer performs comparably to or better than a state-of-the-art AbS system and task-specific baselines while generalizing to a broader range of drum timbres. Our results demonstrate that when equipped with abundant synthetic data and compact acoustic token representations, language modeling provides a simple recipe for unifying transcription and sound event decomposition.
title: D-Composer: Language Modeling for Simultaneous Drum Transcription and Sound Event Decomposition

summary: Understanding how residue variations affect protein stability is crucial for designing functional proteins and deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying disease-related mutations. Recent advances in protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized computational protein analysis, enabling, among other things, more accurate predictions of mutational effects. In this work, we introduce JanusDDG, a deep learning framework that leverages PLM-derived embeddings and a bidirectional cross-attention transformer architecture to predict $ΔΔG$ of single and multiple-residue mutations while simultaneously being constrained to respect fundamental thermodynamic properties, such as antisymmetry and transitivity. Unlike conventional self-attention, JanusDDG computes queries (Q) and values (V) as the difference between wild-type and mutant embeddings, while keys (K) alternate between the two. This cross-interleaved attention mechanism enables the model to capture mutation-induced perturbations while preserving essential contextual information. Experimental results show that JanusDDG achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting $ΔΔG$ from sequence alone, matching or exceeding the accuracy of structure-based methods for both single and multiple mutations. Code Availability:https://github.com/compbiomed-unito/JanusDDG
title: JanusDDG: A Thermodynamics-Compliant Model for Sequence-Based Protein Stability via Two-Fronts Multi-Head Attention

summary: TopoALV-TP is a regional dataset of reconstructed lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage changes across the Tibetan Plateau. It was developed using the Topography-constrained Area–Level–Volume Reconstruction (TopoALV) framework, which integrates multitemporal satellite-derived lake extents, machine-learning-based depth estimation, shoreline-distance constraints, and surrounding topography. The dataset provides 64 m resolution water-depth and lakebed-elevation rasters for 1,080 lakes, together with lake-specific composite area–water-level curves and reconstructed lake area, relative water level, and storage changes for 16 observation epochs from the 1970s to 2022, referenced to the year 2000. The time-series archive contains 17,280 lake–epoch records, with missing observations explicitly retained. Additionally, the dataset includes a nominal 8 m super-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) of the Tibetan Plateau and 1,080 three-dimensional bathymetric visualizations. The archive contains GeoTIFF rasters, CSV time series, composite area–elevation curves, metadata, quality-control diagnostics, data provenance records, and processing scripts to support reproducibility and further research. Users should note that the reconstructed bathymetry and absolute lake volumes are model-derived estimates rather than comprehensive in situ measurements. Relative water-level and storage changes should be interpreted together with the provided quality flags and supported inversion ranges. The original “1970s” observation label is preserved; the numeric year 1975 is used only for chronological sorting and does not indicate an exact observation year.
title: TopoALV-TP: Terrain-constrained lake bathymetry and multidecadal water-level and storage reconstructions across the Tibetan Plateau (1970s–2022)

summary: A validated state-by-quarter panel of the U.S. Department of Labor ETA 227 Overpayment Detection and Recovery report for the 53 unemployment insurance (UI) jurisdictions (50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands), covering the 57 quarters from 2012 Q2 to 2026 Q2 (3,013 jurisdiction quarters). summary: Big Bang nucleosynthesis predicts about three times more primordial lithium than old metal-poor stars show, while laboratory measurements exclude a comparable reduction of the ³He(α,γ)⁷Be capture that makes most of it. Mittermeier Attractor Theory (MAT) fixes, without lithium input, a finite-support mobility M∂ = e³ρ²/(8π^(5/2)) = 0.251864, where ρ is the plastic number. We test the hypothesis that this number multiplies both directions of ³He + ⁴He ⇄ ⁷Be + γ in the primordial plasma. A common factor on a reaction and its reverse changes how fast it runs against cosmic expansion, not where its equilibrium lies; detailed balance and all conservation laws are kept. Executed in the PRIMAT network with its standard thermal history and the MAT baryon density, the hypothesis lowers primordial mass seven from (5.44 ± 0.21) × 10⁻¹⁰ to (1.472 ± 0.053) × 10⁻¹⁰ per hydrogen nucleus, against the stellar inference (1.45 ± 0.25) × 10⁻¹⁰, while deuterium and helium-4 change by less than three parts per million. A response theorem for trace products explains the result: the surviving beryllium meets almost no reverse reaction, so its yield follows the mobility nearly in proportion, and the standard solve alone predicts the modified yield to 0.04%. The effect is decided at photon temperatures of 22–58 keV, whose Gamow energies laboratory data cover closely enough to exclude any realization as a modified cross section: the mobility must be a property of the primordial plasma. The stellar comparison is retrospective; the sharp test is the ratio to standard nucleosynthesis, 0.2704 ± 0.0012, almost free of nuclear uncertainty. The microscopic map that switches the mobility on in that plasma, and nowhere else, remains open.
title: The Primordial Lithium Problem in Mittermeier Attractor Theory: Finite-Support Scaling of Reversible Reaction Kinetics

summary: Life-cycle cost comparisons for seismic retrofit are decision-useful only when loss equations are dimensionally coherent and alternatives share a consistent cost basis. This study presents a traceable audit framework and applies it to the case of a two-storey rubble stone-masonry dwelling in Greece with five reported strengthening alternatives. We recalculate base-masonry strength estimates from stated assumptions, test the reported loss arithmetic and comparison baseline, refit displacement–exceedance relations, and examine consequence-cost scaling. Two readings of one formula differ by a factor of two; neither is validated as a physical loss. Evaluating the record’s own six-step procedure on its own stated inputs finds seventeen of the twenty-two reported loss totals consistent with those inputs; of the five exceptions, four lack an identified cause and one coincides with an internal inconsistency in the reported cost table. Correcting the comparison basis lowers reported savings, and one cost-recovery conclusion changes across arithmetic readings. A separately tested, unit-explicit loss-assessment engine provides a reusable methodological tool; it does not reproduce or validate the case building’s structural model. Version note: Author proof v2, revised 6 November 2026; accepted 2 November 2026. This is an author proof and not the publisher’s final Version of Record. The ADAPT4CE project, “Adaptive digital systems for sustainable construction and material management in the circular economy” (Grant Agreement No. 101182768), supported the cross-case synthesis, reproducibility framework, visualization, and manuscript preparation reported in this article. title: Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study

summary: Introduction Scott Adams’s God’s Debris: A Thought Experiment (2001) presents a fascinating hypothesis: an omnipotent and omniscient God might have destroyed itself to experience something it could not otherwise experience—nonexistence. The universe would consequently consist of God’s debris, with existence potentially representing the gradual reconstruction of divine consciousness (Adams). I propose extending this thought experiment by identifying the Big Bang as a possible physical counterpart to God’s self-destruction and the Absolute as the ultimate destination toward which individual consciousnesses might eventually return. Furthermore, investigating the universe beyond the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) might help constrain theories about the earliest state of existence and, indirectly, inform philosophical investigations of the afterlife.
title: From God's Debris to the Absolute: The Big Bang, Cosmic Origins, and the Possibility of an Afterlife

summary: Bone resorption following tooth loss is considered an obstacle for dental implant placement in desired positions, requiring bone augmentation procedures. Many techniques have been described to reconstruct horizontal alveolar ridge  defects. But one of many, platelet concentrate fibrin is considered nowadays an efficient technique in oral surgery, which is based on concentrating platelets and growth factors that is activated in fibrin gel in order to improve the healing. The aim of this review was to discuss the use of PRF in oral surgery by exposing 3 clinical cases and discussing the properties in bone tissue engineering for PRF membranes, and wound healing with bone formation for Leucocyte platelet rich fibrin (L-PRF) used as scaffold. In the 3 clinical cases bone maturation was found excellent at 5 months as seen clinically, on X-rays and CAT scans
title: Platelets Rich Fibrin (PRF)-Associated Bovine Bone for Horizontal Reconstruction of Atrophic Alveolar Ridges: Myth or Reality? A Three Clinical Case Reports

summary: We construct a common Fourier local-norm domain for exact alternating spatial blocking and temporal decimation of an SU(3) lattice transfer model. The state consists of the current coarse action, its source- free one-time part, its full multitime and source-dependent remainder, and its scalar normalization. A two-link spatial pushforward contracts the field-dependent norm by k = e1/20/3 < 0.350424, and temporal marginalization does not increase that norm. Consequently every finite alternating iteration remains in the ball r∗ = 0.00235, with coupling radius 2 and source radius 10−4 unchanged. A direct analytic estimate gives a one-cycle Lipschitz constant below 0.431657. We prove conditional cumulant bounds under the interacting one-time reference, recertify its spatial mixing after each rebase, and preserve the generating functional of the fixed original source family. An all-order entrance certificate places a specified transfer family inside the ball. Physical consequences include preservation of all connected source responses, a uniform comparison of finite coarse-field marginals with product Haar measure, and suppression of aligned dyadic Wilson squares. The computational supplement includes the seven precursor stages and an independent rational verification of their one-link spectral input. The result closes the local iteration problem for this action space; physical-source scaling, a compatible bare-theory trajectory, reflection-compatible continuum reconstruction, and a nontrivial four-dimensional limit remain separate obligations.
title: Certified Alternating Space-Time Coarse-Graining with Full Memory -An invariant Fourier domain for an SU(3) lattice transfer model

summary: JAPAQ is a nationwide dataset of hourly air quality observations in Japan from January 2018 to December 2025. It covers the five pollutants regulated by Japan's Environmental Quality Standards — fine particulate matter (PM2.5), sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitric oxide (NO), suspended particulate matter (SPM), and photochemical oxidants (Ox) — and three meteorological variables (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity), from the Atmospheric Environmental Regional Observation System (AEROS, "Soramame") of the Ministry of the Environment, Japan. The deposit (japaq_v1.0.0.zip) contains two products built from the same records — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched hourly table, and JAPAQ-KG, its knowledge graph — together with the raw observations, station metadata, and corrections log from which they are built, in five folders that follow the processing steps: 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_hourly_obs_v1.0.0.csv — raw hourly observations as downloaded: 114,237,726 records from 1,850 stations (station, timestamp, five pollutants, three meteorological variables). 4_JAPAQ-FE/japaq_fe_v1.0.0 (CSV and Parquet) — JAPAQ-FE, the feature-enriched, analysis-ready table and main data record: 110,328,514 records from 1,806 stations with documented quality control (three correction stages that remove 2,235,358 non-physical pollutant values; a physical range check for meteorology; quality flags for 2,345 implausible pollutant values and 141,448 meteorological values from faulty sensors, kept and marked), station metadata including complete resolved fields, calendar and time-of-day attributes, severity labels referenced to the Environmental Quality Standards, and a Beaufort wind-speed class (48 columns). 3_quality_control/japaq_corrections_log_v1.0.0.csv — every value set to null or flagged, with its original value, stage, and rule (2,473,666 records). 2_station_metadata/japaq_station_metadata_v1.0.0.csv and 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_station_list_v1.0.0.csv — English station metadata for 1,825 stations, including 143 stations missing from the current station list whose metadata were recovered from official NIES station files and municipality codes, with the source of each station's metadata; and the original Soramame station list (Japanese). 2_station_metadata/japaq_romanisation_log_v1.0.0.csv and STATION_METADATA_METHOD.md, and sources.csv — romanised address values, full source citations, and the recovery method for station metadata. 5_JAPAQ-KG/japaq_kg_v1.0.0.dump — JAPAQ-KG, the records of JAPAQ-FE as a Neo4j 2026.02 property graph with 220,660,640 nodes (Station, Location, ObservationTime, ObservedPollutant) and 330,987,348 relationships. JAPAQ-KG is the evaluation substrate of the AirCypher text-to-Cypher benchmark (IEEE BigData 2026). The quality flags, meteorological variables, resolved station metadata, and source properties are additions that change no node, relationship, or original value; all 4,000 reference queries of the benchmark return the same rows on this graph. The complete code, which rebuilds this release end to end from 1_raw_observations/japaq_raw_hourly_obs_v1.0.0.csv to the knowledge graph and reproduces the released tables byte for byte, is available on GitHub (MIT licence). Coverage gaps: no station has records for 12–31 July 2019, 29–31 March 2021, 27–30 September 2022, and 1 October – 31 December 2024 (118 days in total), because these periods are absent from the downloaded source files; annual statistics for 2024 therefore cover January to September only. Severity labels are descriptive classification aids, not determinations of regulatory compliance. The measurements are provisional values published by the Ministry of the Environment; confirmed values are released later by the National Institute for Environmental Studies. The meteorological variables come from sensors at air quality stations and are intended mainly as covariates. Terms of
title: JAPAQ: Hourly Air Quality Observations and Knowledge Graph for Japan, 2018–2025

A LETTER FROM THE TWENTY-FIRST RESEARCH FAMILY The visible movement of a muscle analog can be a poor witness to the mechanism that produced it. A command may be delivered imperfectly across a changing electrical contact; a trigger may coincide with a learned task cue; a tired load can be driven harder until its output seems ordinary again. A mathematical inverse may confidently assign a unique dose to a nonunique response. Even after a controller reads OFF, a passive mechanism can move. These five ways to be misled are the joint research problem of this family. We therefore begin with independent electrical witnesses, not therapeutic claims. An isolated dummy load, a guarded stimulation-port emulator, an offline BCI cue-replay system and a synthetic force proxy form the minimum environment. By design, no patient evidence is created by this book. Each chapter proposes an explicit competing world, a blind counterfactual and a refusal condition; every result that cannot distinguish those worlds is left unresolved. The research becomes worth inheriting when another laboratory can reproduce an error and improve the question. The companion PDF preserves a fixed 819-page research architecture, 42 recomputable analytic 3D plates, diagrams of the 200 questions and 33 unbuilt Phoenix prototype schematics. The notebook brings the same five distinct mechanisms into readable scientific prose. No internal computation-time target appears in the publication. The five-stage parallel spacetime label names a reasoning workflow rather than a claim about physical parallel universes. I. FOURTEEN RESEARCH PRELUDES 01 | When motion is not recovery A motor proxy can contract because a circuit drives it. A person may recover motor function through mechanisms not present in any nonclinical dummy load. This monograph is built around that difference. Its central objective is not to prove rehabilitation efficacy but to design independently testable experiments that isolate electrical input, controller decisions, mechanistic response and attribution of autonomous activity. An example research hinge is closed-loop stimulation. Its proposed mechanism is that measured contact-state feedback can control a load-proxy response without obscuring electrical burden. Its strongest alternative is that a visually stable proxy motion is caused by a fixed sequence or a contact-dependent artifact rather than closed-loop regulation. The bounded nonclinical discrimination is to conceal a new contact-impedance trajectory and score measured delivered charge before revealing the programmed waveform. Reporting must include delivered charge [microC], current residual [mA], command-to-load latency [ms], dissipated proxy energy [mJ]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The method is deliberately open to being defeated by open-loop constant-sequence replay with equal pulse budget and an instrumented impedance controller. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is electrical overlimit, contact heating surrogate or untraceable charge balance. F104 treats the inverse map from dose to response as potentially nonidentifiable. F105 requires off-state proof and unseen task transfer without interpreting proxy performance as human recovery. An example research hinge is intention-stimulation synchrony. Its proposed mechanism is that an independently timed intention proxy can predict a useful bounded stimulation window without learning task cues. Reporting must include proxy-force retention [1], output error [%], electrical energy [mJ], thermal proxy margin [1]; an apparently positive response must remain a proxy observation, never an inference that an individual recovered from stroke. The strongest scientific outcome may be a null result, a new hidden confounder or an early refusal. The safety boundary for this example is energy escalation under fatigue, unstable feedback or proxy thermal burden. The next laboratory should preserve these decisions while improving the observability of the physical ports, source timebase, material provenance and inference model. 04 | Physical quantities and where they live Current is measured at a declared load port in milliamperes; charge is its signed time integral in microcoulombs; time is measured by independent clocks in milliseconds; electrical energy is integrated from synchronized voltage and current in millijoules. Its proposed mechanism is that amplitude, temporal width, impedance and contact distribution can be distinguished by independently witnessed response features. summary: # Pulsed infrared thermography recordings and reproducibility pipeline for lightning-exposed unidirectional T700/epoxy CFRP panels at 25, 30, and 40 kV **Manuscript**: Sensitivity-Aware Temporal–Spatial Assessment of Thermal-Anomaly Candidate Persistence in Lightning-Exposed T700/Epoxy CFRP Using Pulsed Infrared Thermography. *Sensors*, 2026 (under review). ## Authors Xibin Zhang (corresponding, 202611085025@mail.scut.edu.cn), Lianfang Tian, Bo Peng, Dong Chen, Guozeng Liu. School of Automation Science and Engineering, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou 510640, China. ## Equipment - IR camera: FLIR Silver 480M, 30 Hz nominal, 640×512 sensor. Stored arrays cropped to 500×505×300 (25 kV front), 500×503×300 (30 kV front), 498×501×300 (40 kV front), 350 time samples per recording. - Excitation: two Xenon flash lamps, 5000 J pulse rating, 2–50 ms duration, optical flash thermography. - Specimens: unidirectional T700/epoxy pultruded panels, 100×100×5 mm, impulse-current exposure at nominal 25, 30, and 40 kV. ## Contents - `raw_mat/`: original infrared temperature sequences in MATLAB MAT format. The 35 kV front recording is quarantined as a provenance-duplicate of the excluded 45 kV group (see manuscript Section 3.1). - `temporal_pca_analysis/`: derived TSR residual arrays, candidate masks, sampled-grid PCA outputs, sensitivity tables, adaptive joint-score maps, and the eight-configuration robustness technical report. - `source_code/`: Python reproduction pipeline. Entry points: `reproduce_pipeline.py`, `reproduce_sensitivity.py`, `reproduce_background.py`, `make_summary_figures.py`, `verify_local.py`, `run.py`, `run_all.sh`. - `current_submission/`: V5.2 manuscript, cover letter, title page, highlights, supplementary information, graphical abstract. ## How to reproduce 1. Install Python 3.10+ and packages in `source_code/reproduction_project/requirements.txt`. 2. Place the files under `raw_mat/` with filenames as shipped here. 3. Run `python run.py` for the end-to-end pipeline; use `run_all.sh` on Linux/macOS. 4. Outputs regenerate into `temporal_pca_analysis/` and are verified against frozen references via `verify_local.py`. ## Scientific scope One front recording per nominal 25, 30, and 40 kV; the 35 kV front is quarantined and the 45 kV group excluded. No independent subsurface damage reference (CT/ultrasound/sectioning) is available. The adaptive temporal-spatial score is an algorithmic candidate-persistence index, not a calibrated physical-damage probability. ## License - Code: MIT License. - Raw data, derived data, and figures: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0). ## Integrity SHA-256 checksums for every file in this archive are in `SHA256_MANIFEST.csv`.
title: Sensitivity-Aware Temporal–Spatial Assessment of Thermal-Anomaly Candidate Persistence in Lightning-Exposed T700/Epoxy CFRP Using Pulsed Infrared Thermography

summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . The package contains the seventeen supplementary tables, the analysis and figure code, the recorded software versions, the reconstruction log for the long-read alignments, and a per-read phase-evidence table. What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The original NCBI query string and its date were not retained, so the cohort cannot be rebuilt verbatim; per-accession inclusion flags are given instead. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. The original parameter sets for two of the three long-read procedures were not retained; those procedures were re-run and both original and re-run values are reported side by side and never pooled. One cell of the long-read table reproduces exactly; the others do not, and this is stated in the manuscript. Changes in version 4. The package matches the manuscript. All thirteen supplementary tables are present, including Supplementary Tables S12 and S13, which were absent from the previous version, and Supplementary Table S1 now carries the genome length and assembly level of all 1,483 retained genomes rather than leaving those columns empty. A new Supplementary Table S1b lists the seven excluded genomes that could be recovered from local storage, with their lengths; the genome-length window is 1.5 to 1.7 Mb and this version states the evidence that fixes its bounds. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. The four control reference sequences are deposited under results/marker_control/. Changes in version 6. This version restores the complete file set. The previous version was published from an incomplete upload, so most of the figures, several of the supplementary tables and part of the analysis code were missing from that record. Zenodo caps a record at 100 files and this package has 134, so the package is now deposited as a single archive, hp23s_copy_assignment_package.zip , which holds every file at the path it occupies in the source repository; this README, the SHA-256 manifest and the archive of rRNA calls and copy sequences are additionally placed loose in the record. From version 10 the manuscript itself is not deposited, in the archive or loose. Every member of the archive is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt with its SHA-256, and that manifest is regenerated here, which corrects the entry for this README (the previous manifest had been computed before the last edit of the file). DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. Changes in version 7. This version is a manuscript round: the text is rebuilt from the same locked data by the same script, and no reported value changes. Three defects in the supplementary apparatus are correcte
title: Long reads assign a 23S rRNA resistance allele to one of the two copies in Helicobacter pylori; a complete short-read assembly does not

summary: Introduction Root system architecture (RSA) plays an important role in plant growth and development, influencing soil exploration, water and nutrient uptake, and interactions with the surrounding environment. However, characterising root systems under field conditions remains challenging due to their spatial complexity, below-ground location, and the cost and destructive nature of many root measurement techniques. DeepRootGen provides a computational framework for generating synthetic three-dimensional root system architectures using a stochastic, parameterised root simulation model. The model represents individual root organs and segments within a hierarchical graph, allowing their geometry, topology and spatial distribution to be analysed. The framework is intended to support the digital reconstruction of root systems using observational data collected from the field. By combining mechanistic assumptions about root development with statistical calibration and inference methods, DeepRootGen provides a means of investigating plausible root architectures consistent with available measurements. DeepRootGen has been developed with an emphasis on woody perennial root systems, including horticultural applications involving apple and grapevine rootstocks. The underlying simulator is parameterised to support different root system configurations and can be recalibrated for specific applications. Features and Functionality DeepRootGen provides the following functionality: Stochastic 3D root simulation: Generate synthetic root system architectures with configurable root numbers, lengths, diameters, branching behaviour and growth orientations. Hierarchical graph representation: Represent root organs and segments using explicit parent–child relationships, branching orders and segment identifiers. Root branching and development: Simulate primary and higher-order roots, including stochastic branching locations and configurable interbranch distances. Architectural analysis: Calculate summary statistics describing root length, diameter, branching patterns, orientation, spatial extent and root length density. Spatial aggregation: Aggregate simulated root segments onto three-dimensional soil voxel grids for comparison against field observations. Model calibration: Estimate root system parameters using optimisation and statistical discrepancy measures. Sensitivity analysis: Investigate the influence of model parameters on simulated architectural characteristics. Stochastic ensemble simulation: Generate multiple plausible root architectures under a common parameter configuration to investigate variability between realisations. Visualisation: Explore root architectures and summary statistics through interactive three-dimensional visualisations and statistical plots. Experiment management: Support reproducible simulation workflows, experiment tracking and model artefact management. The repository also contains infrastructure for simulation-based inference and generative modelling. The availability and configuration of individual inference workflows depend on the installed dependencies and repository revision. Model Overview DeepRootGen uses a stochastic root growth simulator to construct root system architectures from a configurable set of parameters. Root architecture generation A simulated root system consists of primary roots originating from the plant base, with lateral roots emerging from their parent organs according to the specified branching configuration. The model supports several aspects of root development: Number and arrangement of primary roots. Root organ lengths and diameters. Maximum branching order. Number and length of lateral roots. Stochastic variation in root growth. Interbranch distances and lateral-root attachment locations. Root growth orientation and gravitropism. Classification of structural and fine roots. Individual simulation runs may produce different architectures even when the input parameters are identical. R
title: DeepRootGen: Unlocking the 3D root architecture of perennial trees using deep learning

summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export.
