summary: Version 1.0 — November 2026. Initial preprint deposit. Umami-Enriched Capsicum: Glutamate Accumulation via GAD1/GAD4 Knockout and GDH1 Overexpression Achieves IFI-U ≥ 800 in Ultra-High-SHU Cultivars Priyanca Iyengar Ford, Scoville Splice LLC · ORCID 0000-0003-0395-1752 Preprint · Scoville Splice Research Series · Paper 5 of 11 · 2026-11-01 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── OVERVIEW This paper describes a dual metabolic engineering strategy to accumulate free L-glutamate in the placental tissue of ultra-high-SHU Capsicum annuum cultivars, achieving an Iyengar Flavor Index for umami (IFI-U) of ≥ 800 without disrupting capsaicinoid biosynthesis. The strategy combines (1) CRISPR knockout of two fruit-specific glutamate decarboxylase isoforms (CaGAD1, CaGAD4) to block the GABA shunt, and (2) overexpression of Arabidopsis thaliana glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (AtGDH1) to increase net glutamate synthesis from the TCA cycle intermediate 2-oxoglutarate. This paper should be read alongside Paper 4 (Iyengar Flavor Index methodology), Paper 7 (Kokumi engineering, which shares the glutamate/N-metabolism pool), and Paper 1 (foundational capsaicinoid engineering, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23743695). ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── BIOLOGICAL BACKGROUND Free L-glutamate is the primary ligand for the umami taste receptor, metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1), which was identified as a taste receptor by Chaudhari et al. (2000, Nat Neurosci 3:113). IFI-U is defined as 1,000 × EC₅₀(L-Glu reference, 1 mM at mGluR1) / EC₅₀(sample). In raw Capsicum cultivars, free glutamate levels are modest: 50–80 mg/100g in SS-CV-010 ripe placenta, corresponding to IFI-U ≈ 50–80. The GABA shunt (Glutamate → GABA, catalyzed by glutamate decarboxylase; GABA → succinate, via GABA-T + SSADH) represents the major glutamate sink in ripening fruit. Two fruit-expressed GAD isoforms were identified in C. annuum: CaGAD1 (Chr 6, constitutive + stress-inducible) and CaGAD4 (Chr 9, fruit-ripening-specific). CaGAD4 carries a calmodulin-binding domain-truncating polymorphism that renders it constitutively active (pH-insensitive) in ripe tissue — making it the primary target. Precedent: Kisaka et al. (1997, Plant Cell Physiol 38:255) demonstrated that expression of E. coli glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) in tomato increased free amino acid content 2–3×, with glutamate the primary beneficiary. The present study adopts this strategy with the Arabidopsis GDH1 (AtGDH1, At5g18170), which produces L-glutamate from 2-oxoglutarate + NH₄⁺ + NADH in the reverse of the deamination reaction. ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── CONSTRUCT DESIGN: GAD CRISPR KNOCKOUT Targets: CaGAD1 and CaGAD4, simultaneous dual-gene knockout. Cas9 promoter: LAP (leucine aminopeptidase) promoter, fruit-specific expression, avoids developmental glutamate decarboxylase activity in vegetative tissues. LAP is expressed in wounded and ripening Capsicum fruit (Fowler et al. 1992, Plant Physiol 99:439). Guide RNA sequences (SpCas9, protospacer + PAM): CaGAD1-g1: 5'-ATCGTACAGCTTGGCACCTA-3' (NGG: CGG) — targets exon 4 of CaGAD1 (PLP-binding domain) CaGAD1-g2: 5'-TGACCTGAAGCAATACGCTG-3' (NGG: AGG) — targets exon 5, generates ~100 bp deletion with g1 CaGAD4-g1: 5'-GCATAGCTCGTGACCAGATC-3' (NGG: TGG) — targets exon 2 of CaGAD4 (early coding) CaGAD4-g2: 5'-AATCGGCATCAGTGTACCGA-3' (NGG: CGG) — targets exon 3, generates ~85 bp deletion with g1 Doench 2016 on-target scores: CaGAD1-g1: 0.74; CaGAD1-g2: 0.68; CaGAD4-g1: 0.71; CaGAD4-g2: 0.66. CFD off-target scores (all predicted off-targets): <0.12; none in exonic regions. Expected loss-of-function: Frameshift + premature stop in both PLP-binding domain (GAD1) and early coding (GAD4). Confirmation by PCR (primers provided in supplementary CSV) + Sanger sequencing. ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── CONSTRUCT DESIGN: AtGDH1 OVEREXPRESSION Gene: AtGDH1 (At5g18170, Arabidopsi

summary: High-dimensional sparse recipe formulation in process industries involves nonlinear association of various covariates, bounded by sparsity constraints and multi-criteria tolerances. Traditional physics-based classical methods (such as Kubelka-Munk) fail to generate sparse candidate recipes properly due to their simplified assumptions and industrial process variations. This study proposes a hybrid physics-informed uncertainty-aware framework that is structured into three modules: (a) Module A, a multi-target forward quality model; (b) Module B, a sparse inverse reconstructor; and (c) Module C, a feasibility-constrained ranking layer. Then it has been validated in an industrial textile dyeing context with recipe-grouped cross-validation under multi-illuminant quality assessment comprising process and production information, target reflectance, K/S values, and spectral descriptors. Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB) with spectral-only features ($R_λ$, K/S) and Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBDT) with recipe-process features outperforms other configurations with out-of-Fold MAE of 0.1655 and 0.1523 in the forward quality model. For inverse reconstruction, a component-wise median blend achieved a recipe-vector MAE of 0.0295. Exploratory conditional treatment effect (CATE) suggests an observational association that alkali adjustment reduces error for red and pale shades (CATE = -0.196). This framework provides a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool that minimizes costly laboratory trials across industrial formulation domains.
title: A Physics-Informed Hybrid Forward-Inverse Machine Learning Framework for High-Dimensional Sparse Recipe Reconstruction

summary: Co-design methods optimize a robot's body and controller jointly and judge the result by one number, the task reward of the fully optimized pair. That number cannot separate morphologies whose competence depends on the controller to very different degrees. We evaluate a morphology by restricting its controller instead, recording the task competence it retains under an explicitly declared, low-complexity controller family, environment, task and search budget. On three EvoGym locomotion tasks, task reward explains only $39\%$, $33\%$ and $10\%$ of the variance in this quantity, and geometric descriptors do not predict it under run-grouped cross-validation. The measurement is reliable across optimizer restarts (ICC$(2,k) = 0.956$--$0.986$) but depends on the declared family: phasing the drive by actuator index instead of position ranks the same morphologies at Spearman $0.50$--$0.63$ and reverses reward-matched pairs. As a second search objective the axis improved competence at matched task reward in $3$ of $5$ paired runs, short of a pre-registered bar of $4$. Used after an ordinary reward-only search instead, to choose within its top task-reward band, it selected a different body in all $8$ runs offering a choice, at a cost of at most $0.10$ reward units, and in $6$ of $8$ that body also scored higher under a held-out family. Restricted-control competence is therefore a reportable property of a co-designed morphology, interpretable only with the controller family that defines it.
title: Beyond Task Reward: A Controller-Restriction Protocol for Evaluating Embodiment-Dependent Competence

summary: Brain metastases are the most common intracranial malignancy, occurring in roughly 30% of patients with primary solid tumors and carrying a median survival near 5.9 months. Automated segmentation is critical for treatment planning and volumetric monitoring, but metastases are frequently small, numerous, and heterogeneous in size within a single patient. We compare a plain nnU-Net baseline, a Residual Encoder Large (ResEncL) variant, region-based training, and a Primus transformer model for BraTS-METS 2026 Task 1, using patient-grouped cross-validation to prevent leakage from the longitudinal UCSD subset. Primus (label-based) is our strongest individual model by aggregate DSC/NSD, achieving 0.710/0.761 (ET), 0.742/0.785 (TC), 0.683/0.689 (WT), and 0.531/0.436 (RC). ResEncL trails Primus on aggregate DSC/NSD but achieves substantially higher lesion-wise F1 (e.g. ET: 0.452 vs. 0.052); a probability-averaging ensemble of the two only partially preserves ResEncL's F1 advantage (ET lesion-wise F1: 0.064). We further report three postprocessing and label-reconstruction pitfalls we believe generalize beyond this challenge. Code is available at https://github.com/mahdiislam79/BraTS_METS_2026.
title: Brain Metastases Segmentation for BraTS 2026 Task 1: A Multi-Architecture Comparison

summary: Spatially resolved stress proxies and rate-based seismicity models are increasingly combined for regional earthquake forecasting, yet formally testing their non-redundancy remains largely unaddressed. We present the Nested-Permutation Alarm for Dual-Parameter Earthquake Forecasting (ANADEF) pipeline, integrating a stress-sensitive Gutenberg--Richter $b$-value field, estimated via a penalized 2D B-spline inversion, with a stationary background rate ($μ$) from space--time ETAS stochastic declustering. Applied to the Zagros Fold--Thrust Belt using an 18-year catalog ($n=40{,}731$, $M_{\mathrm{N}}\geq1.5$, 2006--2024) under a two-stage protocol with non-overlapping training (2006--2014) and target (2015--2024) windows, the model achieves, for $M_w\geq5.0$ ($N=55$), a retrospective Area Skill Score $S=0.69$ (95\% CI: 0.64--0.73), reducing alarmed area from $τ\approx0.38$ ($μ$-only) to $τ\approx0.28$ while retaining hit rate $ν=92.7\%$; since thresholds are calibrated on the evaluation catalog, these are in-sample, not out-of-sample, estimates. A nested permutation procedure re-optimizing thresholds within each null realization tests whether $b$-value adds information beyond $μ$, absorbing the optimization bias. Significance is null-model dependent: cell-wise randomization yields $p=0.012$, while a conservative spatial-structure-preserving null gives weaker, non-significant evidence ($p=0.057$)---incremental stress information is suggestive but not unambiguously established. Calibrated thresholds were frozen and applied to updated 2015--2024 fields, generating an unvalidated, forward-looking spatial alarm template for 2025--2029. These results establish a reproducible, statistically transparent methodology for testing, rather than assuming, complementarity between stress-sensitive and rate-based predictors, offering a candidate operational template pending prospective validation.

Applied to the Zagros Fold--Thrust Belt using an 18-year catalog ($n=40{,}731$, $M_{\mathrm{N}}\geq1.5$, 2006--2024) under a two-stage protocol with non-overlapping training (2006--2014) and target (2015--2024) windows, the model achieves, for $M_w\geq5.0$ ($N=55$), a retrospective Area Skill Score $S=0.69$ (95\% CI: 0.64--0.73), reducing alarmed area from $τ\approx0.38$ ($μ$-only) to $τ\approx0.28$ while retaining hit rate $ν=92.7\%$; since thresholds are calibrated on the evaluation catalog, these are in-sample, not out-of-sample, estimates. A nested permutation procedure re-optimizing thresholds within each null realization tests whether $b$-value adds information beyond $μ$, absorbing the optimization bias. Significance is null-model dependent: cell-wise randomization yields $p=0.012$, while a conservative spatial-structure-preserving null gives weaker, non-significant evidence ($p=0.057$)---incremental stress information is suggestive but not unambiguously established. Calibrated thresholds were frozen and applied to updated 2015--2024 fields, generating an unvalidated, forward-looking spatial alarm template for 2025--2029. These results establish a reproducible, statistically transparent methodology for testing, rather than assuming, complementarity between stress-sensitive and rate-based predictors, offering a candidate operational template pending prospective validation.

summary: Performance claims in quantum technology are not properties of hardware alone. They are properties of a declared task, system boundary, normalization denominator, uncertainty or security convention, and comparator. We perform a cross-domain analysis spanning quantum computing, simulation, communication, sensing, clocks, randomness generation, and their enabling technologies. The analysis changes substantive conclusions in several representative cases. For the longest direct finite-key quantum key distribution case analyzed here, the same final key gives rates differing by a factor of $1.91$ when normalized by complete acquisition rather than transmission-active time. In Advanced LIGO, $6.1\,\mathrm{dB}$ peak quantum-noise reduction coexists with a $0.534$ coincident analysis-ready fraction, separating detector-level gain from delivered observing service. In quantum computation and photonic sampling, matching the observable, error tolerance, loss model, sample count, amortization, and classical hardware moves or reverses published crossover claims. Across domains, the recurring limits are correlated error, multiplicative interface loss, thermal and nonequilibrium occupation, calibration covariance, measurement efficiency, fabrication yield, and control latency. A quantum advantage is therefore established only for a fixed task and boundary when the accepted output outperforms the best documented alternative at matched accuracy, elapsed time, availability, and lifecycle cost. The resulting framework identifies the measurements required to convert component records into reproducible system capability. Credible progress is defined by reproduced logical workloads, prospectively validated simulations, repeater links outperforming direct transmission, long-duration calibrated sensors and clocks, integrated hardware with predictable yield and reliability.

summary: We present Attractor-Vascular Coupling Theory (AVCT), a theory-guided framework for deriving interpretable blood pressure (BP) predictors from photoplethysmography (PPG) attractor geometry. AVCT connects vascular dynamics, PPG observation, delay-coordinate reconstruction, and attractor descriptors within a unified framework for formulating testable hypotheses, without presupposing the physiological sufficiency of a particular low-dimensional feature set. We evaluate a LightGBM-based estimator using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) across two complementary experimental settings. Experiment 1 comprises 46 ICU/surgical subjects from BIDMC and VitalDB, with ECG, PPG, and repeated reference BP measurements. The calibrated full model achieves systolic/diastolic BP (SBP/DBP) mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 2.05/1.67 mmHg, compared with 2.02/1.63 mmHg for the PPG-attractor-only model. summary: Coal Mine Overburden Waste (CMOW) material in the coal mining industry possesses serious environmental risk through the leaching of hazardous and toxic heavy metals along with geotechnical constraints because of the low strength. Hence, the primary objective of the present study is to examine the efficacy of Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation (MICP) technique to immobilize the metal ions present in the CMOW and simultaneously to investigate the enhancement in the Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS). Leaching tests along with highly advanced Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) have been performed to examine the immobilization potential of MICP treated CMOW samples. ICP-MS analysis indicated that MICP treatment resulted in more than 90% immobilisation of several investigated metal ions, based on comparison of their initial concentrations in untreated CMOW obtained by direct digestion with their concentrations detected in the leachate following MICP treatment. However, the extent of immobilization was more pronounced in metals due to changes in the pH, controlling precipitation of calcite and thereby ionic exchange.   Further, UCS test of CMOW has achieved significant improvement in the average strength i.e., 437.76 kPa, 324.46 kPa and 141.83 kPa due to corresponding average precipitation of calcite is 7.46%, 6.06%, and 4.15% and thereby enhancement in particles bonding using bacterial strains (SP79, SP77 and SP78), respectively. Further, PFC(2D) based discrete element modelling was performed by calibrating particle-scale stiffness, friction, and parallel-bond strength parameters to reproduce the experimental stress–strain response of the MICP-treated CMOW samples, with UCS deviations of less than 4% for all three bacterial strains. The calibrated models further captured the development of bond failure and localized fracture patterns, which are consistent with the strain localization and shear-band evolution observed using Digital Image Correlation (DIC). This pronounces that the process is switched to localized brittle failure as cementation increased. In addition, FESEM examination has confirmed the presence of calcite between the particles, validating the results of XRD analysis. Finally, MICP technique is established to be used for heavy metal ions immobilization and improvement in strength of CMOW materials.
title: Metal Ions Immobilization and Strength Behaviour of Coal Mine Overburden Waste Materials Treated with Microbial Induced Calcite Precipitate Technique – Experimental and DEM Analyses

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. Data Site location information: Latitude: 39.836701  Longitude:  -84.838096 Local Eclipse Type: Total Solar Eclipse Eclipse Percent (%): 100 WAV files Time & Date Settings: Set with Automated AudioMoth Time Chime (More information on TimeStamp Setting below) Data Collector Start Time Notes: N/A Included Data: Audio files in WAV format  with the date and time in UTC within the file name: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS meaning YearMonthDay_HourMinuteSecond For example, 20240411_141600.WAV means that this audio file starts on April 11, 2024 at 14:16:00 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) CONFIG Text file:  Includes AudioMoth device setting information, such as sample rate in Hertz (Hz), gain, firmware, etc.  README.md:  Markdown formatted file with information about the recording and recording site. file_list.csv:  A machine and human file that gives the following information on each file in the record: File Name, File Type, Description, File Size in kilobytes, Name of Associated Data Dictionary with the file, calculated SHA-512 Hash of the file as a unique identifier to insure data integrity during transfer and compression. total_eclipse_data.csv:  A machine and human readable file that gives the following information about the site where the audio data recording was taken: ESID#, Latitude, Longitude, Eclipse_type, CoveragePercent, Eclipse Start UTC (1st contact), Totality Start UTC (2nd contact), Totality End UTC (3rd Contact), Eclipse End UTC (4th Contact), Max Eclipse Time UTC License.txt:  A human readable file that explains the terms and conditions under which the data can be used. summary: This software and selected-data release accompanies the manuscript “ Symmetry defects and state-dependent order reduction in Fourier Laplace–rotation splitting ” by Fei Xue and Tianqi Zhang. Version 2.0.0 substantially extends the previous scalar MATLAB release (v1.1.0, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23151617) to provide a unified reproducibility package for scalar and spinor Bose–Einstein condensate dynamics. The package includes: MATLAB implementations of three-dimensional rotational BEC solvers, including explicit Laplace–rotation integrators, merged compact splitting, and full-step forward–method-adjoint (FB) constructions, together with scalar and spinor model components. Python verification tools for the seven-factor (EEI7) and five-operator (EEI5) symmetry-defect certificates, selected spinor subflows, and independent numerical reference calculations. Numerical benchmarks and selected data , including a small-grid matrix-exponential reference test, accuracy-versus-work comparisons, and arbitrary-axis rotation experiments examining the dependence of defect visibility on spatial resolution. Reproducibility documentation , including execution instructions, validation records, file provenance, version comparisons, and SHA-256 checksums. The associated manuscript establishes rigorous fixed-grid symmetry-defect results, analyzes their state-dependent visibility, and develops an adjoint-based implementation that restores the designed temporal order under the stated assumptions. The software provides numerical verification and reproducible examples supporting this analysis. Scope and limitations: The small-grid reference benchmark and selected verification tests have been rerun for this release. Historical large-grid MATLAB production experiments have not been rerun, and some historical terminal-state arrays are not redistributed. The documentation distinguishes independently verified results, archived computations, and derived data. The Python certificate tests are numerical cross-checks rather than substitutes for the mathematical proofs. This release supersedes the scalar-only software distribution while preserving the earlier version in the Zenodo version history.
title: MATLAB reproducibility package for "Symmetry defects and state-dependent order reduction in Fourier Laplace–rotation splitting"

The numerical charts are synthetic hypotheses. Chinese materia medica inspires provenance, processing and compound questions, not a biological proof. Five different objects, five different vetoes F121 - Botanical Sheet-Mask Serum Active Stability at the Limit. Native measurement: stored mask-serum marker retention (%). Fair reference: equal-formula serum stored in an inert vessel, blank lyocell, matched nonwoven mask and light/dark paired packaging. Disqualifying rival: adsorption onto cellulose, packaging migration, altered extract recovery, optical co-elution or oxygen-driven degradation. F122 - Lyocell–Botanical Serum Adsorption at the Limit. Native measurement: identified botanical marker adsorbed on lyocell (mg/g). Fair reference: matched nonwoven material, no-sheet serum reservoir, same-area inert substrate and prewetted lyocell control. Disqualifying rival: surface liquid mistaken for bonded sorbate, unequal sheet density, incomplete desorption or retained marker counted as delivered. F123 - Botanical Mask Conformability and Liquid Distribution at the Limit. Native measurement: verified face-surface wet-contact area (cm2). Fair reference: shape-matched nonwoven mask, same-serum container exposure, equal-load flat phantom and reversed sheet orientation. Disqualifying rival: pressure shadows mistaken for contact, pixel threshold bias, droplet pooling in folds or high contact area with low local transfer. F124 - Botanical Mask Wear Time and Evaporation at the Limit. Native measurement: evaporation mass flux (g/m2/h). Fair reference: no-sheet serum film, humidity-matched nonwoven, impermeable occlusive reference and evaporation-free gravimetric blank. Disqualifying rival: short-term occlusion masquerades as barrier repair, variable wet area, edge leakage or ambient humidity drift. F125 - Botanical Nano-Sheet-Mask Sensitive-Skin Tolerability at the Limit. Native measurement: qualified reconstructed epidermis viability (%) and marker exposure (microg/cm2). Fair reference: same-contact-time matched serum alone, blank lyocell, nonwoven sheet with matched vehicle and qualified positive-irritant reference. Disqualifying rival: pigmented botanicals distort viability reagent, local occlusion hides evaporation, tissue necrosis mimics reduced flux or uncontrolled dose. F125 tests qualified RhE viability only with chemically verified exposure, matched vehicle and cell-free interference controls. None of the five outputs substitutes for another. summary: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent. However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Prior work established a lower bound of $Ω(d\log(1+T/d))$, leaving open whether the $d^{3/2}$ dependence in the upper bound is necessary. We resolve this question by proving a minimax lower bound of $Ω(d^{3/2}\log(1+T/d^{3/2}))$. To prove this result, we construct a family of hard instances in which the reward gap of each action is proportional to its squared distance from the optimal action. We establish a posterior Fisher information bound for adaptive quantum queries with quantum memory, relating the information acquired about the optimal direction to the regret incurred. summary: Many high-stakes AI failures trace to the training data rather than the model, yet teams still treat pre-training data validation as a checklist and rarely wire its signals to a go/no-go decision or to a governance framework. We study the detectability boundary of that validation: what a pre-training data-readiness gate catches, what it misses, and why a flagged source is often not blocked. We reuse a validation gate from a prior single-domain system and generalize it across three high-stakes domains (healthcare, finance, and government) on the real MIMIC-IV, SEC EDGAR, and CMS Open Payments datasets, injecting controlled defects across simulated sources. A composite readiness score detects 0.76 of degraded sources (95% CI [0.74, 0.76]) but withholds only 0.42; the 0.34 gap (95% CI [0.32, 0.35]) traces to a single averaging step, and we show it is fixable but privacy-sensitive. The grid is small by design (six sources per domain, two degraded, five seeds), so the intervals describe this controlled setting, not field variability. We map the privacy-utility curve of validating on differentially private summaries, prove a blind spot for symmetric label noise on balanced targets, and add a confident-learning label detector that runs on DP-noised summaries and keeps its recall down to epsilon = 0.1. We compare against Great Expectations and Deequ, measure how poorly thresholds port across domains, and map the gate to the NIST AI RMF MEASURE function. We report the negatives, among them a near-chance inter-rater reliability on fine-grained incident coding. What is new is the integration of production incidents, a private benchmarked gate, and a governance mapping, not any one of those parts.
title: Detection Is Not Action: The Detectability Boundary of Pre-training Data-Readiness Gating

summary: Acoustic holography in the megahertz range can impact applications from manufacturing and non-destructive testing to transcranial ultrasound. Designing lens topologies for complex holograms in the sub-megahertz to low-megahertz regime most relevant to transcranial therapy is difficult because wave propagation through an acoustically thick lens cannot be ignored. Here we show that the heterogeneous angular spectrum approach (HASA), which admits in-plane varying speed-of-sound maps and supports rapid differentiable optimization with the Adam optimizer, can generate three-dimensional lens topologies directly. summary: Underwater acoustic passive detection is essential to maritime surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Existing detection systems typically collapse multichannel array observations into a binary decision or a scalar confidence score, offering limited insight into the physical evidence that supports or contradicts a target declaration. This limitation is acute at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where isolated spectral peaks and transient beamforming responses are inherently ambiguous and physically verifiable targets are characterized by an ensemble of coupled reinforcing cues. Building on the unified from-signals-to-evidence framework introduced in the companion Part I, this paper instantiates the framework for passive target detection. A physics-aware multichannel acoustic encoder encodes the array observations into complementary acoustic evidence tokens through a direction-guided architecture that combines minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processing with time-frequency and fine-frequency representations. These tokens are combined with environmental priors and fed into a pretrained large language model (LLM) that evaluates target-present and noise-only hypotheses and generates a structured detection report detailing target presence, bearing, spectral-line locations, received SNR, range, and per-field confidence scores. A physics-parameterized data engine extended to realistic oceanic channels provides traceable supervision at both discrete-label and structured-description levels. Experiments under white-noise and mixed ocean-background conditions demonstrate reliable detection, accurate bearing estimation, and physically interpretable structured reports, validating the feasibility of evidence-grounded underwater acoustic detection.
title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part II: Passive Detection

summary: Routing-driven timely data collection in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) is crucial for marine environmental monitoring, disaster warning, and underwater resource exploration, etc. However, harsh underwater conditions, including high delays, limited bandwidth, and dynamic topologies, make efficient routing decisions challenging in UASNs. In this paper, we propose a smart interrupted routing scheme for UASNs to address dynamic underwater challenges. We first model underwater noise influences from real underwater routing features, e.g., turbulence and storms. We then propose a Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-based Interrupted Software-defined UASNs Reinforcement Learning (ISURL) framework, which ensures adaptive routing through dynamical failure handling (e.g., energy depletion of sensor nodes or link instability) and real-time interrupted recovery. Based on ISURL, we propose the MA-MAPPO algorithm, integrating multi-head attention mask mechanism with MAPPO to filter out infeasible actions and streamline training. Furthermore, to support interrupted data routing in UASNs, we introduce MA-MAPPO\_i, MA-MAPPO with interrupted policy, to enable smart interrupted routing decisions in UASNs. The evaluations demonstrate that our proposed routing scheme achieves exact underwater data routing decisions with faster convergence speed and lower routing delays than existing approaches.
title: Smart Interrupted Routing Based on Multi-head Attention Mask Mechanism-Driven MARL in Software-defined UASNs

summary: DjangoDefects is an inter-release defect prediction benchmark for Python, built from the full version history of the Django web framework. It covers 24 consecutive releases (1.0 to 5.2, September 2008 to April 2025). Construction. 5,585 closed, fixed Bug tickets from Django's Trac issue tracker were linked to 4,801 fix commits through Fixed #<ticket> references. Each fix was traced back to the commits that introduced the bug using SZZ Unleashed, with whitespace-insensitive blame and whitespace and comment filters, giving 6,306 bug records. Fixes that only add code, such as a missing check, change no existing line that blame could trace. Each one is attributed instead to the nearest code line above the insertion point. This adds 1,914 bug records, which label files and methods only. Releases are assigned by git ancestry rather than by date, which accounts for Django forking each stable branch months before the release tag. Buggy lines are located in each release snapshot by blame identity. summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) isolates a desired speaker from a multi-speaker mixture using cues that identify the target. Prior work has explored acoustic and textual cues, such as enrollment audio and different types of speaker descriptors, but typically relies on a single cue family. Moreover, most TSE systems adopt mask-prediction models, which are prone to audible artifacts and generalize poorly across acoustic conditions. To address these limitations, we propose PromptSep-Speaker, a generative TSE model based on latent diffusion that unifies four interchangeable cues: speaker temporal order, transcript, enrollment audio, and speaker caption. summary: Drum beats are often conceptualized and produced as arrangements of repeated single-drum sound events or one-shots. summary: Fertility has fallen across the developing world, but rarely at the same rate for every educational group, so a given fall in the total fertility rate can mask very different changes in who is bearing fewer children. This paper shows that the composition of such a decline, and not only its size, is a determinant of the long-run rate of population growth, and derives a statistic that measures the composition effect from standard survey data. In a dynamic model in which fertility differs by education and daughters inherit their mother's schooling imperfectly, the long-run growth rate weights each group's fertility by its stationary share times the reproductive value of its members; dividing this weight by the group's share of current births gives the long-run cost of a permanent decline in that group's fertility per unit of period fertility, a quantity that two Demographic and Health Surveys suffice to estimate. The archive contains 230 indexed scientific result tables with 18,522 recorded data rows, retained geometry and assignment evidence, small finite-element outputs, input and provenance records, and selected analysis and plotting scripts. It also includes 25 current figures, their captions and source-data maps, and 29 current publication display tables in CSV and cell/formula-record formats. The latter are separate from the 230 scientific result tables. Start with 00_START_HERE.txt . PUBLIC_DATA/SUPPLEMENTARY_DATA/DATA_INDEX_V41.csv indexes the scientific tables. CURRENT_FIGURES and CURRENT_TABLES identify the current displays; component-specific README files explain inputs, dependencies and reproduction steps. DATA_MANIFEST.csv provides file sizes and SHA-256 checksums. This release supports the documented data, algebraic, spectral, statistical and plotting reproductions. It is not a complete finite-element reproduction environment: native COMSOL models, a complete field/model archive, software licenses and private administrative records are not included. Recorded failed cases, qualification limits, negative results and historical component scopes are retained. No new scientific calculations were performed for this deposit. Contact: Wenli Zhu, zhuwenli@ucla.edu. ORCID: 0000-0002-2355-0422 .
title: Research data and code for Size–position correlations and stiffness reversals in cylinder composites

summary: Fertility has fallen across the developing world, but rarely at the same rate for every educational group, so a given fall in the total fertility rate can mask very different changes in who is bearing fewer children. This paper shows that the composition of such a decline, and not only its size, is a determinant of the long-run rate of population growth, and derives a statistic that measures the composition effect from standard survey data. In a dynamic model in which fertility differs by education and daughters inherit their mother's schooling imperfectly, the long-run growth rate weights each group's fertility by its stationary share times the reproductive value of its members; dividing this weight by the group's share of current births gives the long-run cost of a permanent decline in that group's fertility per unit of period fertility, a quantity that two Demographic and Health Surveys suffice to estimate. In Colombia between 2000 and 2015 this cost was 60 percent lower among women without completed secondary schooling, and the observed, education-biased decline implies long-run population growth 0.14 points per year higher than a uniform decline with the same effect on period fertility, with a 90 percent bootstrap interval of 0.06 to 0.23. The advantage emerges within two generations, holds at the 2015 composition, survives bounds for selective coresidence and a 288-specification curve, and is larger in Peru; census links between adult daughters and their mothers confirm it in Colombia, Peru, and, at ages 20 to 24, Kenya, though the Kenyan identified set turns negative at ages 25 to 29. A decline concentrated among women whose share of current births exceeds their share of the stable population is therefore inexpensive in long-run growth, which makes the composition of a fertility decline a margin distinct from its size and measurable before the decline has run its course. First version: December 2025. This version: November 2026. JEL classification: J11, J13, J24, J62, O15, O40.
title: Who Stops Having Children? Fertility Composition and Long-Run Growth

summary: # A Spectral Construction of Natural-Number Arithmetic [Archival DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22512592) ## Arithmetic with its construction history retained This paper constructs natural-number arithmetic from a correlation spectrum and then resolves its values into the expressions by which they are generated. Its central achievement is to connect three levels that are usually studied separately: arithmetic values, the histories of arithmetic operations, and an evolution acting on those histories. The resulting system retains both the familiar numerical laws and information that numerical evaluation alone removes. The source is minimal unbiased compositional change. The least-dimensional faithful irreducible real orthogonal carrier is a rotation plane. Independent composition, exact same-shape self-similarity and unit covariance determine square-root scaling and a Gaussian law. Local information and normalized total correlation give the characteristic local and global lengths. Preservation of constants selects Neumann closure within the stated separated nondegenerate homogeneous local boundary class. Spectral projections are ordered by their Gaussian response before an integer enumeration is introduced. Orientation selects the positive analytic modes. Pointwise modulation and circle-map composition define their addition and multiplication; modulation by the first positive mode defines successor. The paper proves the Peano recursion structure, unique prime factorization and canonical transport under scale and orientation changes. Winding degree certifies the resulting natural-number arithmetic. ## Resolving how a value is generated The next construction retains ordered, bracketed addition and multiplication expressions. Only the specified zero, unit and absorbing reductions are imposed at this level. Arithmetic evaluation identifies expressions with the same value, while each value has a finite expression fibre. This gives a precise space in which the construction of a number can itself be observed. The simplest example is six. Adding six unit leaves and multiplying an additive expression for three by an additive expression for two give the same root value and the same root energy. Their leaf counts are six and five, while their accumulated internal quadratic defects are thirty and thirty-one. In both cases leaf energy plus accumulated defect is thirty-six. The equality at the root coexists with a measurable difference in the construction. A recursive positive law gives equal weight to the admissible root channels and assembles their subhistories independently. This law differs from uniform counting of all complete expressions. Phase invariance determines a finite phase extension. Summing the resolved source over histories and phases recovers the original Gaussian mass of each mode exactly. Expression multiplicity therefore enriches the source without changing its original partition function. Weighted amplitude readout, probability pushforward and conditional expectation have distinct definitions. Exact variance and entropy identities separate the information in the root value from the information remaining within its fibre. The example of six has strictly positive conditional leaf-count variance, giving a concrete instance of information preserved by the resolved construction. ## A complete operator on generation histories The same source weights determine a parent-child assembly response. The paper constructs a nonnegative self-adjoint trace-class operator on the complete counting history space. Its trace tail has an explicit Gaussian bound independent of the number of expressions in each fibre. Finite root cutoffs converge in trace norm, and the full operator generates a contraction evolution with a dissipation identity. The decisive result is a nonzero transfer from an initially invisible history difference to a later value response. A difference supported on the six histories of four has zero initial value readout,

summary: Nature heedlessly dispatches the metabolic efforts of microscopic organisms. Conceptive fungibility—the assumption that any sexual mate is interchangeable and equal—is opposite to the constitution of macroscopic organisms. We let microscopic organisms encounter problems faced by macroscopic organisms, such as the Allee effect, inbreeding, and sterility. Classical oncology confronts cancers with cytotoxins and maximum cell killing, letting Darwinian selection and clone breeding kill the host, with evolution being a proximate cause of death in most cancer patients ( Enríquez -Navas et al., 2015). We respond by exploiting conceptive fungibility in mitotic cells, altering semi-dormant germline properties to be meiotic through gene delivery. We specify a general interceptive apparatus, the Induced Extinction Vortex (IEV), that exploits reproductive imperatives to drive localized tumoral populations toward extinction. We specify IEV in three sequential phases (sexualization, demographic skew, and a reversion sink), each with its own threshold conditions and failure criteria. The design is method-agnostic: no delivery vehicle, meiotic driver, or receptor set is required, and any method capable of instantiating the phases falls within the proposal. The instantiation criteria are the Circuit, Metabolic, and Resectability criteria, stated in advance as points at which the implementation can fail.  Every deterrence is backed by documented or modeled demographic effects in wild taxa, such as feminizing parasites, coercive tortoises, and bottlenecked mountain lions. Evolutionary oncology has validated the changing of an adaptive response into a lethal deterrence. To our knowledge, no study combines these effects and directs them toward a clade of cellular populations. The proposal hypothesizes that an engineered reproductive dependency could create tumor population vulnerabilities analogous to mate limitation and reproductive interference. Existing research supports the component principles, but there is no evidence of a combined circuitry.
title: A Revised Intraspecific Predation: IEV, an Induced Extinction Vortex

summary: The clinical biochemistry laboratories are vital for screening, diagnosis and selection of treatment and monitoring. These results are reliable as a result of reliable quality management carried out during pre-examination, examination and post-examination. Internal quality control (IQC) is used to track the day to day stability of analytical procedures and external quality assessment (EQA) is used to make an independent comparison of the laboratory's performance with assigned values or other laboratories. An unacceptable control result, however, does not, however, mean that the problem has been solved. The nonconformity must be investigated, the direct effects of the nonconformity must be controlled, the root cause (s) of the nonconformity must be identified, the corrective and preventive action (s) must be implemented and effectiveness verified through a structured corrective and preventive action (CAPA) framework. The principles of IQC and EQA in Clinical Biochemistry are reviewed and the contribution of the findings of the two to a CAPA system of Quality Management are assessed. It outlines typical nonconformities that will be found in an analysis, quality control statistical approaches, root cause analysis tools, corrective and preventive actions, documentation requirements and indicators of CAPA effectiveness. Special focus on quality management based on risk and the ISO 15189:2022 requirements. The review also points out that good CAPA go beyond incident reports closing and are evidenced by subsequent data on IQC, EQA, and process performance to show continued improvement. An integrated approach will decrease the chance of analytical failure, improve laboratory competence and promote patient safety.
title: Evaluation of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Framework for Internal and External Quality Control in a Clinical Biochemistry Laboratory

summary: Background: Emphysematous cystitis (EC) is a rare but potentially life-threatening urinary tract infection characterized by gas accumulation within the bladder wall and/or lumen, most commonly associated with gas-producing microorganisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, including empagliflozin, promote urinary glucose excretion, raising questions about a possible association with genitourinary infections. However, the relationship between empagliflozin use and EC remains uncertain, with evidence currently limited to published case reports. Aim: To review the reported cases of emphysematous cystitis (EC) associated with empagliflozin use and to summarize the demographics, clinical features, treatment modalities and outcomes. Methodology: A systematic review was conducted using the databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science from inception until October 2026. The review included published case reports and several patients who developed EC while taking empagliflozin. Patient characteristics, laboratory findings, radiographic findings, management strategies, and clinical outcomes were extracted and qualitatively evaluated. Results: We examined seven patient cases with ages ranging from 62 to 90 (median 76). Two patients received empagliflozin for heart failure, and five patients had type 2 diabetes. Hematuria, dysuria, frequent urination, and suprapubic discomfort were common symptoms that emerged between two weeks and eight months following treatment. Urinary retention, bladder outlet obstruction, chronic renal disease, advanced age, and recent catheterization were among the contributing variables. Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most frequently isolated microorganism, based on microbiological culture results. Computed tomography (CT) was the principal imaging modality used to confirm the diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis. Management generally included discontinuation of empagliflozin, antibiotic therapy, and bladder drainage or decompression when indicated. Five patients recovered, whereas two patients died. Conclusion: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis is a rare but serious condition mostly seen in elderly patients with multiple health issues and urinary tract abnormalities. Early detection and treatment are crucial to minimize risks. More research is needed to understand its causes and frequency.
title: Empagliflozin-associated emphysematous cystitis: a systematic review of published case reports

summary: Obesity is a growing public health issue in New Zealand, increasing the risk of chronic diseases and exacerbating health disparities. Mobile health (mHealth) initiatives, such as smartphone apps, have showed promise in improving weight management and physical exercise. The primary goal is to determine the efficacy of the FatSecret app in promoting weight loss and boosting physical activity among overweight and obese people in New Zealand. The secondary purpose is to investigate potential differences in intervention effectiveness based on ethnicity (European, Māori, Asian, and Pacific Islanders) and living place (urban or rural). A two-arm, parallel, randomized controlled trial design will be used. Adult volunteers (aged 18–65 years, BMI ≥25 kg/m²) from various ethnic groups and areas in New Zealand will be recruited and randomly assigned 1:1 to the intervention or control group, stratified by ethnicity and region. The intervention group will receive a 12-week weight management and physical activity program given via the FatSecret app, while the control group will not use the app and will continue with their usual lifestyle. The primary outcome is the change in body weight between baseline and 12 weeks. Secondary objectives include changes in body fat percentage, waist circumference, physical activity level measured using established methods, and health-related quality of life. This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the FatSecret app’s effectiveness in promoting weight loss and physical activity among New Zealand’s overweight and obese individuals. The study design allows for the evaluation of potential differences in intervention effectiveness across ethnic groups and residential locations, which will inform the creation of culturally appropriate and geographically targeted mHealth therapies for obesity control. summary: Modern AI assistants, agents, and decision-support systems increasingly rely on information beyond model parameters by retrieving documents, accessing memory, invoking tools, and combining external evidence. Retrieval-Augmented Generation is one prominent realization of this broader information-grounding paradigm. Yet external grounding does not by itself ensure trustworthiness. Systems can still fail under incomplete, noisy, conflicting, or misleading evidence, and these failures become harder to diagnose as retrieval, reasoning, memory, tool use, and generation interact. Existing evaluation frameworks measure important aspects of system quality, but do not necessarily ensure deliberate coverage of the conditions most likely to expose system vulnerabilities. We introduce PRISM as a methodology for systematic stress testing of retrieval-grounded AI through controlled synthetic data generation. Rather than treating evaluation data as a static benchmark, PRISM constructs and validates document and question-answer pairs designed to reproduce deployment-relevant failure conditions. Its 25 evaluation instruments are organized across ten diversity dimensions and eight thematic clusters, covering conditions such as fragmented or noisy evidence, lexical and semantic mismatch, unanswerable queries, and adversarial or epistemically unreliable content. Because these conditions are generated synthetically, they can reproduce relevant document and evidence characteristics without requiring access to proprietary or sensitive operational data. Stress conditions are also linked to concrete system choices to support targeted diagnosis. PRISM is expected to provide reproducible and traceable evaluation artifacts that help reveal vulnerabilities before deployment and distinguish failures originating from retrieval, evidence selection, generation, or abstention. Automated construction and validation are also intended to reduce the manual effort associated with human-curated evaluation sets while preserving the control, coverage, and consistency needed for systematic evaluation. More broadly, PRISM reframes evaluation as not only a measurement problem but also an experimental-design problem. By complementing existing metrics, human evaluation, observability, and post-deployment monitoring, it contributes toward more systematic pre-deployment assessment of increasingly agentic, retrieval-grounded AI systems.

summary: A negative and methodological result on Edward Elgar's Dorabella cipher (87 arc symbols, 14 July 1897). Thirty decipherment hypotheses were each tested against shuffled-symbol nulls and enciphered-English controls; all were ruled out or disfavoured. About 10% drawing slips reduce a standard substitution solver from 97% to about 57% accuracy on 87-letter controls, so earlier "not English" verdicts do not cover a carelessly drawn cipher; a slip-tolerant solver places Dorabella above all shuffles but below all English controls. Neighbouring arcs that are 180° flips of each other are strongly over-represented (27 of 86 against 12.6 expected, p ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁵). The cipher is not solved. AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) was used in transcription, decipherment, checking and drafting, under the author's direction; it is disclosed in the text. No archival images are reproduced.

In one sentence: for 1 < p < 2 this paper finds the exact Schatten-norm constant for sums of matrix moduli when there are at least as many matrices as the matrix size, gives a new general upper bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , and certifies in exact arithmetic that rank-one matrices do not give the answer to Lee’s two-matrix problem. The question. For numbers, |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|. A matrix A has a natural absolute value |A| = (A*A) 1/2 , but for matrices the size of a sum can exceed the size of the sum of the absolute values. Measuring size by the Schatten p-norm (p = 1 is the trace norm, p = 2 the Frobenius norm), one asks for the smallest constant c with ‖A 1 +…+A m ‖ p ≤ c ‖|A 1 |+…+|A m |‖ p . What was known. Eun-Young Lee (2010, 2012) asked for the best constant for two matrices. Lin and Zhang (2022) settled p = 2; Tang and Zhang extended the question to m matrices and conjectured a formula; Qiu (2026) proved it for p ≥ 2; below p = 2 the formula fails, by counterexamples of Zeng, Liu and Ratnavelu, of Pang and of Qiu, all built from rank-one matrices. The survey of Bourin and Zhang (2026) lists the range 1 < p < 2 as open. Results (1 < p < 2, n-by-n matrices). (1) When m ≥ n the best constant is an explicit one-variable maximum D p,n ; it depends only on the rank of the sum of the moduli, every equality case is classified, and for m < n the constant is strictly smaller. Consequently the best constant for rank-one summands is D p,min(m,n) in every dimension. (2) The best constant is log-convex in 1/p, so interpolating between p = 1 and p = 2 gives the dimension-free bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , better than the previous m (p−1)/(2p) for every m ≥ 2 (for two matrices at p = 3/2: 1.0648 instead of 1.1225, while the true value is at least 1.0364). (3) For two 3-by-3 matrices a computer-assisted proof in exact rational and interval arithmetic shows that the best rank-one value is beaten at nine exponents between 11/10 and 17/10. How. The sum is written as a product of two block matrices and Hölder’s inequality is applied; the problem reduces to comparing two Rényi entropies of the spectrum, whose extremal shape is one large eigenvalue and the rest equal. This extends T. Zhang’s Frobenius-norm argument; the matching examples are Pang’s, with a re-tuned parameter. Limits. The exact constant for two matrices of arbitrary size (Lee’s problem) for 1 < p < 2 remains open, as does the case m < n; the interpolation bound is not sharp; the certified excess over the rank-one value is tiny (about 10 −5 to 10 −7 ) and covers nine specific exponents, not an interval. summary: A law $F$ with mean $\mu$ is $n$-completely mixable if there are $n$ random variables with law $F$ whose sum is almost surely $n\mu$. Wang proved that such a law satisfies a family of inequalities between the norms of the positive and negative parts of $X-t$ and $X-s$, where $X\sim F$ and $s=(n\mu-t)/(n-1)$, for every threshold $t$ and every law-determined norm, and asked when these inequalities are also sufficient (Open Problem 4 in his 2015 survey). We show that for bounded $F$ the whole family is equivalent to the single convex-order condition $X-\mu\cx-(n-1)(X-\mu)$, and that the same holds for integrable $F$ if the norms are required to have the Fatou property. The inequalities do not imply $n$-complete mixability: for $n=3$ the analytic density $\frac1{10}+\frac{27}{10}(2x-1)^2$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies all of them and is not $3$-completely mixable, and for $n=3$ and $n=4$ there are counterexamples with densities bounded away from zero on $[0,1]$ and with $C^\infty$ densities, the one for $n=4$ not symmetric. A Bernoulli$(p)$ law satisfies the inequalities exactly when $1/n\le p\le1-1/n$, while it is $n$-completely mixable exactly when $np$ is an integer. For $n=2$ the inequalities are equivalent to symmetry, hence to $2$-complete mixability, for every integrable law. For $n=3$ the examples refine the symmetric non-mixable laws of Yin and Zhu, and the reduction explains why those laws satisfy the inequalities.
title: Law-determined norm inequalities do not imply complete mixability

Pick k of n given real numbers at random, without replacement, and add them. How concentrated can that random sum be? The paper answers three classical forms of this question exactly: how often the sum can be exactly zero, how small its entropy can be, and how rarely it can be nonnegative. Results. (1) Zero sums. If the numbers add up to zero and are not all zero, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum whenever k ≥ 5 and n ≥ 2k+1, and only the pattern (1, −1, 0, …, 0), up to scaling and reordering, attains this. This is the smallest support of an eigenfunction in the first nontrivial eigenspace of the Johnson graph, and proves Conjecture 1 of Mogilnykh, Vorob’ev and Valyuzhenich (2018), who had checked it by computer for n ≤ 600. A formula with all equality cases is given for every n and k, including the case (1, 1, −1, −1, 0) at n = 5, k = 2 that earlier classifications missed (Theorem 1.1). (2) Entropy. The minimum Rényi entropy of the sum is found for every finite order, answering a question of Ai, Kuželka and Pelekis (2026): one outlier is optimal except at half-sampling (n = 2k), where two outliers win above an explicit order α k (α 2 = 2, about 1.386k for large k). So the universal Bernoulli lower bound holds exactly for orders up to 2 (Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Corollary 1.4). (3) Tails. For two-valued populations, the probability that the sum is at least its mean is at least k/n whenever n ≥ 4k, with a single outlier the unique minimiser for n > 4k (Theorem 1.5); Ai and Pelekis (2026) had n ≥ 8k. The proof uses a 2026 lemma of Ai, Karagiannis, Kuželka and Pelekis. Consequently the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture (that two-valued populations are the worst case) would imply the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for all n ≥ 4k. summary: Supplementary note to arXiv:2611.08310 and arXiv:2610.19779. A fingerprint of coherent noise built from a stabilizer code is only as informative as the recovery gates that produce it, and every fixed choice of those gates is blind somewhere. This note isolates what can nevertheless be guaranteed, and states it as a worst-case floor rather than an average improvement. Two elementary facts about Fisher information make the guarantee exact. Because information matrices add, the identifiable set of a collection of designs is the union of theirs, so running several designs in parallel can never cost a direction that any member sees. Because the inverse of a sum is Loewner-dominated by the inverse of any summand, splitting a fixed shot budget over S designs can never cost more than sqrt(S) in standard deviation, that is, S in shots. The premium is therefore fixed in advance and independent of the working point, while the gain is not. Both statements are certified over the 64-design space of the three-qubit repetition code, under the 48- and 112-component fingerprints: the Loewner inequality is evaluated rather than assumed at every point tested, the worst case over 300 working points is 1.25 against the certified sqrt(2) = 1.4142, the bound is attained to five figures at one structured point, and at the worst points of the individual designs the parallel pair sits below the better single design by factors of 2.6 to 9.5. Two three-gate placements suffice; a third adds 3.5 to 11.5 per cent. The floor buys recoverability and worst-case precision, and it buys nothing else: it does not buy accuracy under common-mode calibration bias, and it does not repair a model degeneracy that no design can see. The comparison arm gives the same information, rendered as plain text, to a general-purpose language model (Claude Sonnet 5.5) with one fixed instruction. The test plan, its thresholds and its decision order were frozen, with a local SHA-256 hash, before any code, record or label existed. For each of two cohorts a separate model session generated 33 synthetic records, 12 valid and 21 with one injected defect, without seeing the rules, and labels were locked before either arm ran. In the first (in-sample) cohort the rules flagged 21 of 21 defective records and rejected 0 of 12 valid ones. The language model also flagged 21 of 21 but rejected 6 of 12 valid records, which disqualifies it under the plan. In the second (out-of-sample) cohort the rules again scored 21 of 21 with 0 of 12 rejected, and the language model scored 17 of 21 with 0 of 12. The gap of 4 is below the pre-registered margin of 5. The pre-registered verdict for both cohorts is therefore "compared, threshold not met", and the report makes no claim that the rules add detection. A reduced rule set (R1, R2 and R7 only) missed 12 of 21 defects in both cohorts and is refuted. No confidence intervals are reported, because the plan forbids them: the records are constructed counterexamples, not a sample from any population.   Deposit version: Working paper, version 1.2 (2026-11-12). summary: A hedge fund researcher needs to know whether a reported event contrast depends on the control used to judge it. This study compares downside-reversal, 52-week-high-breakout and reported-volume-event masks on 20 admitted, existing long-history equity series. summary: Single-valued neutrosophic set theory is an important soft computing approach for resolving uncertainty and imprecision in decision-making. Several models have been established under the framework of single-valued neutrosophic sets for decision-making purposes. Single-valued neutrosophic relations, their max-min-max composition and a score-based use of this composition in medical diagnosis already exist in the literature; this paper revisits the single-valued neutrosophic composite relation in the framework of composite relations under fuzzy-set extensions, describes its algebraic properties, and applies it to two new healthcare problems. In this work, this composite relation on single-valued neutrosophic sets is presented. The numerical illustrations of the composite relation are given, and some of its algebraic properties are proved (inverse, monotonicity, associativity and distributivity over union), while it is shown by counterexamples that the composition is neither commutative nor distributive over intersection. In addition, the applications of the single-valued neutrosophic composite relation to medical healthcare services are considered to illustrate its use. Two medical healthcare applications are considered involving prediction of maternal outcome for a pregnant woman and the diagnosis of some common ailments. The examples are illustrative and use data adapted from earlier studies; no clinical validation is claimed.
title: Single-Valued Neutrosophic Composite Relation and Its Application to Healthcare Services

summary: Emissions figures in ship weather routing rest on regulatory and market data that change with new legal acts and markets. Maintaining them by hand is slow and prone to plausible errors. This paper presents the Data Steward, an agent built on a large language model that maintains these data in EcoRouter, a workbench for ship weather routing. The agent changes a value that calculations use only through an approved proposal. Deterministic tools take over the tasks that the model performs unreliably, such as reading area boundaries from legal texts, and checks run as workflows of small steps with an outcome for every item. The contribution to artificial intelligence is the design of an agent that maintains regulatory reference data under human control, together with a method for evaluating such an agent. The engineering application is the maintenance of the regulatory data on which a ship-routing tool computes emissions and regulatory costs. In a controlled test with 40 errors injected into the data that a full check covers, the Steward corrected 36 to 38 in three runs, against 20 to 28 for the same model alone with web search. In three full checks of the live data, 96 to 99 % of judged items were correct. A person who took no part in building EcoRouter found 57 of the 59 approved values correct. The results show that a commercial language model can maintain regulatory reference data with few errors once the tasks it performs unreliably are moved into deterministic code. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Version 1. The records of the tests are published as a dataset: 10.5281/zenodo.24251511. Use of AI: during the preparation of this work the author used Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in order to correct the text, check its grammar, to create the tables and figures from the author's records, and to check the statements about EcoRouter against its source code. The same assistant also helped to run tests 1 and 3, to judge their results against the acts and publishers, to prepare the person's sheet for test 2 and to aggregate the results of the three tests. It did only the tasks that the author gave it, under the author's control. The author reviewed and edited the content as needed and takes full responsibility for it. Language models are also part of the research itself: Section 5 of the paper states which model the Data Steward ran on and which AI assistant judged its results.
title: A language-model data steward for emissions-regulation data in a weather-routing tool: design and controlled evaluation

summary: Data and code for the manuscript "Risk-Calibrated Gaze Compensation for Field-Sequential-Color Near-Eye Displays: A Certified Control Law with External Evidence" by Jingyang Li (School of Electronics and Information Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University, China). This deposit contains the analysis code, the result files behind every number reported in the manuscript, the figure sources and the executed forced-choice log. The external eye-tracking arm re-analyses the public SensCogAR dataset archived at Open Science Framework (https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/45tjp); that archive declares no explicit data licence, so the raw records are not redistributed here, while the derived per-participant windows and metrics are included in data/real_ar_gaze/. The nine display devices used in the external-evidence arms are described by published measurements, each cited with its DOI in the manuscript, and the extracted parameters are recorded in data/panel_response_identification/. The target display panel and the human observers of the perceptual arm were not measured, so no raw panel or eye-tracker record exists for them. summary: The records of the tests reported in the preprint "A language-model data steward for emissions-regulation data in a weather-routing tool: design and controlled evaluation" (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24250853). The Data Steward is an agent built on a large language model that keeps the emissions-regulation data of EcoRouter, a weather-routing tool, current. It proposes changes, and an administrator approves them. The files hold every message EcoRouter sent the agent and every answer, its proposals, the outcome of every item checked, and the judgement of each item and proposal against its act or publisher. - Test 1: three full checks of the live data, checks 1, 2 and 3. - Test 2: a person's check of the 59 values approved in test 1: the values, the instructions given to the person, the person's sheet, the key and the result. - Test 3: nine runs on a copy of the data with injected errors. A1 to A3 are the agent as built, B1 to B3 the same model alone with web search, and E1 to E3 a check of the EU ETS exemptions. Beside the runs: the answer key, the random draw of the errors with its seed, the changes that made the test copy, and the result of each run. - Severity: the rule that grades every wrong result as high, medium or small, the grade of each, and EcoRouter's value catalogue. E-mail addresses and names are replaced by codes. CONTENTS.md lists every file and the test it belongs to. The ZIP keeps the folder tree. These files are the output of the language-model agent evaluated in the paper, gpt-5.5 (version 2026-04-24) in Microsoft Foundry, and the judgements of its work, made by an AI assistant (Claude Opus 5.5) under the author's control, as Section 5 of the paper describes. They are research data on that agent. Some proposals carry area boundaries from Marine Regions: Flanders Marine Institute (2026), MarineRegions.org, licensed under CC BY. Some carry place positions from OpenStreetMap: © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright.
title: Records of the tests of a language-model data steward for emissions-regulation data in a weather-routing tool

summary: RideLab is a self-contained, browser-based platform for the design and teaching of active suspension control, for students, researchers, educators and engineers. It simulates a vehicle active suspension in real time and compares six controllers, PID, fuzzy logic, sliding mode, linear-quadratic regulator, model predictive control and a neural network, against a passive baseline on an ISO 8608 road, with live plots and a multi-indicator dashboard. An integrated adaptive AI tutor guides learners with missions, prediction questions and graded hints, and can be switched off for pure design work. The archive contains the toolbox, a Python reference engine, verification harnesses for the design tool and for the tutor, the road seeds and controller tunings, and the scripts that regenerate the published results and figures. How to use Option 1, use the toolbox: download RideLab.html and open it in any modern web browser (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Microsoft Edge). No installation or external dependencies are needed. Option 2, see the code and regenerate the results: download RideLab_v1.0.zip and unzip it. The toolbox is included as suspension_design_toolbox.html. To regenerate the results, follow README.md; the scripts need Python 3 with NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib, and the harnesses and timing script need Node.js. Generative AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) assisted in developing the software; the author verified all results against the reference engine. Access to the files is granted on request.
title: RideLab: a browser-based platform for the design and teaching of active suspension control

summary: This doctoral thesis, entitled Genomic Studies of Piscine Streptococci and Genome Assembly of Clariidae Catfishes (Siluriformes) for Aquaculture Enhancement, was prepared at the Faculty of Fisheries, Kasetsart University, Thailand, for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy (Fishery Science and Technology). The thesis integrates microbial comparative genomics, genome assembly, genome annotation, repeat and gene-family analysis, population genomics and chromosome evolution to develop genomic resources and analytical approaches relevant to aquaculture, fish health and genetic management. It comprises eight research chapters and a general discussion. Chapter 1 — Bighead catfish genome assembly. A chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved genome assembly of Clarias macrocephalus generated with PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore, Illumina and Hi-C sequencing. Chapter 2 — Streptococcus iniae comparative genomics and reverse vaccinology. The genome of strain SIKU01 and comparative analyses of 90 isolates used to prioritize candidate antigens. The candidates require experimental validation. Chapter 3 — F1 hybrid catfish genome annotation. A chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved assembly of the interspecific hybrid Clarias macrocephalus × Clarias gariepinus , with its protein-coding, non-coding, satellite and transposable-element annotation. Chapter 4 — Repetitive architecture of the two haplotypes. Tandem repeats, segmental duplications, gene-family clusters, the miR-430 array and the divergence of Gypsy and Helitron elements. Chapter 5 — Hatchery population genomics. Diversity, relatedness, family reconstruction, autozygosity, structural variation, polymorphic inversions and shared parents in a commercial C. gariepinus broodstock. Chapter 6 — Gene repertoire and divergence of the two parental haplotypes, on a phylogenomic framework of 17 catfish genomes. Chapter 7 — Composition of the 41 polymorphic inversions of C. gariepinus and deletion-based PCR markers for their arrangements. The markers were designed in silico and have not been tested in the laboratory. Chapter 8 — Fusion and fission between the karyotypes of the two species. Junctions are reported as intervals; no mechanism is resolved at any junction. Chapter 9 — General discussion and conclusion. Changes since the version of 2026-11-03: lists of tables and figures; Chapters 7 and 8 revised; five figures of the repeat analyses added to Chapters 3 and 4 (spacer types of the LG04 array, tandem repeats against chromosome ends, copy number by counting step, array structure of repeated loci, Gypsy and Helitron); new introductions of Chapters 6 and 7; Chapter 9 updated to the chapters. Several chapters are working versions of manuscripts in preparation. Institution: Kasetsart University, Faculty of Fisheries, Thailand. Degree: Doctor of Philosophy (Fishery Science and Technology). summary: Bench dataset of a small multirotor propulsion assembly (A2212 920 KV motor, 9450 propeller, SkyWalker 40 A ESC): five endurance runs at nominal 6, 8 and 9.5 A, represented by 87 intermittent 50-second captures sampled at 1 kHz (vibration, shunt-current and temperature channel voltages; 4.35 million samples per channel), plus 11 thrust curves (66 observations) comparing post-test configurations with a shared healthy reference. The package contains the original MAT files, value-identical raw-voltage CSV exports, run and capture metadata with session identifiers and quality flags, derived features, technical-validation outputs, and Python scripts that reproduce every table and figure of the associated data descriptor, including operating-condition controls, permutation tests and grouped-validation comparisons. Known limitations (unobserved gaps, unresolved current calibration, temperature-channel excursions, shared thrust reference and unverified physical failure endpoints) are documented in README.md and metadata/quality_flags.csv. Download the single ZIP file and start with README.md. Version 1.2.0 adds session identifiers, a current cross-check, operating-condition control analyses, a three-way split comparison, per-block spectra and a thrust-loss table.
title: UAV Propulsion Endurance Dataset: Vibration, Current, Temperature and Thrust Measurements of a Small Multirotor Propulsion System
