summary: The work looks at the Riemann hypothesis from the standpoint of the model “The Birth of Dimensions” (BD). The number arrow is understood as a projection of a process — the comparison of the standard-observer with its surroundings. Four reference quantities follow from the construction: 1 — the observer and the standard; 0 and ∞ — two infinities converging into one point; 1/2 — the level of lost phase, a line perpendicular to the arrow; 2 — the first distinction, the point of doubling. Together they define a sphere: the arrow is a tangent to the circle through the observer, the rotation goes about an axis, the spin-up force is applied at a point of the equator, and its trace on the arrow is 2. The main result is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD: if the original process is a sine, that is, a rotation; if everything tied to the observer is his likeness; if an instantaneous snapshot has no duplicates and balance sets the mirror, — then all zeros lie on the equator of the sphere, that is, on the line Re s = 1/2 (section 4). This is a proof within the model, not a mathematical proof. In mathematics the hypothesis remains open: of the nine links of the chain eight are known theorems, and the ninth — that the local rotations of all primes form one rotation — is equivalent to the hypothesis itself (section 5). Each step carries a status: [K] — a known mathematical fact, [H] — a hypothesis or interpretation of the author, [O] — an open question. The detailed exposition is placed in Appendices 1–11. They show that the logic of BD independently leads to what mathematicians obtained by abstract means: Riemann's mirror, the Euler product, the Gauss sum, Gram points, the Riemann–Siegel formula, the de Bruijn–Newman constant, Li's criterion, Weil positivity, the adelic approach of Tate and Connes, the Lee–Yang theorem and other results (section 6). For BD this is strong support: the model generates the same mathematics from its own principles. The outcome of the work: the two paths — through BD and through mathematics — run into one and the same limit at one place. In the model the answer is given by the postulate of closedness: there is no pumping of energy, and the amplitude of the standing waves is constant. In mathematics the same step is to prove that the amplitude of the Möbius sum has no power pumping: |M(x)| ≤ C_ ε · x^(1/2 + ε ) for every ε > 0; this is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (Titchmarsh, §14.25), and a stronger, energy form is equal work on the levels of the logarithmic arrow (Appendix 11). The postulate of BD and the Riemann hypothesis are two projections of one statement, and in this sense the paths are identical: neither gives an answer without its own condition. This is the limit of today's methods, not a proved impossibility. And whatever the outcome, the answer is the same: the falsity of the hypothesis is always detectable by a finite check, so either it will be proved, or it cannot be proved — and then it is true. The hypothesis rests on two sides of one standing wave: alternation of crest and trough cancels the sum of signs down to order √x, and equality of their amplitude gives positivity of the energy (Weil, Li); each is equivalent to the hypothesis (Appendix 7). The most direct indirect evidence of the connectedness of the system came from the check by turning the wheel: neighbouring levels separated by a square compensate each other like the crest and trough of one wave, and the accumulation does not grow (Appendix A5). Why a limit is a reason to change the picture of understanding, and what role philosophy plays here, is said in the preface. summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ and AUC to $0.852$. Its length-corrected variant no longer shows a significant bias towards stationary trajectories and short inter-message distances, but still favors candidates farther from the RF detection. A time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting remains ahead (precision $0.9013$, AUC $0.904$), so this single-detection, hand-designed PHMM formulation approaches but does not beat it.
title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion

summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.
title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations

summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.
title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple

summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.
title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers

summary: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.
title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners

summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.
title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval

summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $Λ$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address
title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?

summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.
title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions

summary: People's choices depend on both the payoffs of the available options and what they learn about those payoffs before deciding. This paper shows how choice data identify both unobserved payoff heterogeneity and the cost of information acquisition in a rational inattention discrete-choice model. I establish conditions for semiparametric point identification using exogenous payoff and information-cost shifters, without imposing parametric forms on the taste-shock distribution or on how the unit cost of information varies with observed characteristics. In the model with binary choice, I construct an unobserved choice threshold whose cumulative distribution function is the choice probability as a function of the payoff shifter. Moments of this threshold identify the payoff coefficients and the unit cost of information at each value of the information-cost shifter. A deconvolution argument then identifies the taste-shock distribution. I then extend identification to the model with multinomial choice. To estimate the model, I propose a sieve minimum-distance estimator based on observed market shares and establish its consistency. For inference, I construct confidence regions by test inversion because binding parameter constraints can make the estimator's limiting distribution nonnormal. In an application to Amazon Mechanical Turk, model counterfactuals show that lower unit costs of information raise the average task-taking probability and reduce wage elasticity.
title: Estimating a Rational Inattention Discrete Choice Model: A Semiparametric Approach

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.
title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection

summary: Although modern SAT solvers have made remarkable progress, they still exploit formula structure only to a limited extent. We present two techniques that make SAT solving more structure-aware and provide experimental results showing their promise. The first technique ``$\mathit{melts}$'' the formula by reducing interaction between its parts. This is achieved by adding new variables, using existential quantifiers, and applying a procedure called partial quantifier elimination. The second technique exploits the notion of a $\mathit{local}$ $\mathit{proof}$. The latter establishes that a formula is unsatisfiable by proving that certain literals of its clauses are redundant. We show that using local proofs makes SAT solving more formula-specific.
title: On Structure-Aware SAT Solving

summary: The work looks at the Riemann hypothesis from the standpoint of the model “The Birth of Dimensions” (BD). The number arrow is understood as a projection of a process — the comparison of the standard-observer with its surroundings. Four reference quantities follow from the construction: 1 — the observer and the standard; 0 and ∞ — two infinities converging into one point; 1/2 — the level of lost phase, a line perpendicular to the arrow; 2 — the first distinction, the point of doubling. Together they define a sphere: the arrow is a tangent to the circle through the observer, the rotation goes about an axis, the spin-up force is applied at a point of the equator, and its trace on the arrow is 2. The main result is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis within BD: if the original process is a sine, that is, a rotation; if everything tied to the observer is his likeness; if an instantaneous snapshot has no duplicates and balance sets the mirror, — then all zeros lie on the equator of the sphere, that is, on the line Re s = 1/2 (section 4). This is a proof within the model, not a mathematical proof. In mathematics the hypothesis remains open: of the nine links of the chain eight are known theorems, and the ninth — that the local rotations of all primes form one rotation — is equivalent to the hypothesis itself (section 5). Each step carries a status: [K] — a known mathematical fact, [H] — a hypothesis or interpretation of the author, [O] — an open question. The detailed exposition is placed in Appendices 1–11. They show that the logic of BD independently leads to what mathematicians obtained by abstract means: Riemann's mirror, the Euler product, the Gauss sum, Gram points, the Riemann–Siegel formula, the de Bruijn–Newman constant, Li's criterion, Weil positivity, the adelic approach of Tate and Connes, the Lee–Yang theorem and other results (section 6). For BD this is strong support: the model generates the same mathematics from its own principles. The outcome of the work: the two paths — through BD and through mathematics — run into one and the same limit at one place. In the model the answer is given by the postulate of closedness: there is no pumping of energy, and the amplitude of the standing waves is constant. In mathematics the same step is to prove that the amplitude of the Möbius sum has no power pumping: |M(x)| ≤ C_ ε · x^(1/2 + ε ) for every ε > 0; this is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (Titchmarsh, §14.25), and a stronger, energy form is equal work on the levels of the logarithmic arrow (Appendix 11). The postulate of BD and the Riemann hypothesis are two projections of one statement, and in this sense the paths are identical: neither gives an answer without its own condition. This is the limit of today's methods, not a proved impossibility. And whatever the outcome, the answer is the same: the falsity of the hypothesis is always detectable by a finite check, so either it will be proved, or it cannot be proved — and then it is true. The hypothesis rests on two sides of one standing wave: alternation of crest and trough cancels the sum of signs down to order √x, and equality of their amplitude gives positivity of the energy (Weil, Li); each is equivalent to the hypothesis (Appendix 7). The most direct indirect evidence of the connectedness of the system came from the check by turning the wheel: neighbouring levels separated by a square compensate each other like the crest and trough of one wave, and the accumulation does not grow (Appendix A5). Why a limit is a reason to change the picture of understanding, and what role philosophy plays here, is said in the preface. F182 | Botanical Seasonal Harvest and Active Variability at the Limit The harvest-season marker variance under repeated sampling flagship asks whether phenological stage, drying kinetics, marker synthesis and storage-linked chemical loss can be separated from weather shocks, soil moisture differences, harvest-time bias and HPLC injection drift. Its primary candidate endpoint is season-stratified marker coefficient of variation (percent). A rigorous design compares same species and site across a balanced harvest calendar with equal drying and assay delays and requires isotope-dilution calibrated marker concentration with retained time-stamped harvest vouchers. The decisive failure condition is that seasonal CV attribution disappears when repeated within-site harvests and independent instrument sequences are analyzed. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F183 | Botanical Extract Chemical Fingerprint Standardization at the Limit The inter-laboratory chromatographic fingerprint transfer flagship asks whether solvent-selective extraction, chromatographic peak coelution, retention-time drift and response normalization can be separated from solvent carryover, selective peak alignment and changed detector response rather than composition transfer. Its primary candidate endpoint is external chemical fingerprint transfer error (percent). The decisive failure condition is that fingerprint agreement collapses after switching laboratory, solvent lot or peak registration algorithm. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F184 | Botanical Raw-Material Adulteration and Contaminant Detection at the Limit The matrix-aware adulterant identification and contamination screens flagship asks whether target-ion suppression, botanical matrix interferents, adulterant recovery and confirmatory identification can be separated from matrix-driven response suppression, carryover and false positives from endogenous overlapping compounds. Its primary candidate endpoint is spiked adulterant method detection limit (mg/kg). A rigorous design compares blind low-level fortified matrices plus certified negative and positive reference materials and requires matrix-matched recovery, confirmatory second transition and independently blinded spike series. The decisive failure condition is that the declared detection limit fails its false-positive and recovery thresholds in an unselected botanical matrix. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F185 | Cross-Batch Botanical Nanoformulation Quality Consistency at the Limit The multi-lot critical-quality-attribute release and transport flagship asks whether raw material chemotype variability, shear sensitivity, droplet-size drift and noncompensatory CQA acceptance can be separated from post-hoc acceptance threshold adjustment, sensor drift and selection of only favorable manufacturing batches. A rigorous design compares origin-blinded external reference lots with locked species vouchers and acquisition protocol and requires voucher-backed taxon audit and orthogonal LC-MS marker panels tested on sealed external lots. The decisive failure condition is that the apparent geographic classifier fails when season and instrument batches are permuted on held-out provenance lots. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F182 | Botanical Seasonal Harvest and Active Variability at the Limit The harvest-season marker variance under repeated sampling flagship asks whether phenological stage, drying kinetics, marker synthesis and storage-linked chemical loss can be separated from weather shocks, soil moisture differences, harvest-time bias and HPLC injection drift. Its primary candidate endpoint is season-stratified marker coefficient of variation (percent). A rigorous design compares same species and site across a balanced harvest calendar with equal drying and assay delays and requires isotope-dilution calibrated marker concentration with retained time-stamped harvest vouchers. The decisive failure condition is that seasonal CV attribution disappears when repeated within-site harvests and independent instrument sequences are analyzed. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F183 | Botanical Extract Chemical Fingerprint Standardization at the Limit The inter-laboratory chromatographic fingerprint transfer flagship asks whether solvent-selective extraction, chromatographic peak coelution, retention-time drift and response normalization can be separated from solvent carryover, selective peak alignment and changed detector response rather than composition transfer. Its primary candidate endpoint is external chemical fingerprint transfer error (percent). A rigorous design compares sealed cross-laboratory extract exchange with predeclared peak matching and reference mixtures and requires orthogonal peak identity from LC-MS plus pooled QC injections and independent integration scripts. The decisive failure condition is that fingerprint agreement collapses after switching laboratory, solvent lot or peak registration algorithm. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F184 | Botanical Raw-Material Adulteration and Contaminant Detection at the Limit The matrix-aware adulterant identification and contamination screens flagship asks whether target-ion suppression, botanical matrix interferents, adulterant recovery and confirmatory identification can be separated from matrix-driven response suppression, carryover and false positives from endogenous overlapping compounds. Its primary candidate endpoint is spiked adulterant method detection limit (mg/kg). A rigorous design compares blind low-level fortified matrices plus certified negative and positive reference materials and requires matrix-matched recovery, confirmatory second transition and independently blinded spike series. The decisive failure condition is that the declared detection limit fails its false-positive and recovery thresholds in an unselected botanical matrix. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F185 | Cross-Batch Botanical Nanoformulation Quality Consistency at the Limit The multi-lot critical-quality-attribute release and transport flagship asks whether raw material chemotype variability, shear sensitivity, droplet-size drift and noncompensatory CQA acceptance can be separated from post-hoc acceptance threshold adjustment, sensor drift and selection of only favorable manufacturing batches. Its primary candidate endpoint is cross-batch critical quality attribute pass rate (percent). A rigorous design compares unselected supplier lots compared with frozen process windows and independent CQA release boundaries and requires orthogonal D90 and marker chemistry checks with timestamped batch deviation and release log. The decisive failure condition is that apparent consistency disappears when rejected and unselected lots enter the denominator or release bounds are frozen. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. Research position: The five flags are deliberately distinct. The historical attention to source description in Bencao Gangmu and Eastern relational thinking motivate the questions of harvest, provenance and preparation, while causal inference relies on current measurements, blind controls and independent reconstruction. The 3D plots in the research PDF are synthetic and explicitly reproducible; they are not experimental observations.

summary: City-scale data on population size and age structure are essential for urban planning, public service provision, and disaster risk assessment. However, existing population datasets for China are mainly available at national or administrative-unit scales, while data for individual cities remain limited. Here, we developed a dataset of population size, age structure, and population ageing for 342 major Chinese cities from 2000 to 2100. Historical urban population data were derived by aggregating age- and sex-specific population grids within urban built-up areas after calibration to census data using iterative proportional fitting. Taking 2020 as the baseline year, future populations were projected using the cohort-component method under five population scenarios based on the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), with projections provided annually from 2021 to 2025 and at five-year intervals from 2030 to 2100. Historical backcasting showed that the mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) for simulated total population and the population aged 65 years and older in 2020 were both below 10%, while the mean absolute error in the simulated share of the population aged 65 years and older was below 1 percentage point. The dataset also showed good agreement with existing population datasets, and its future projections were broadly consistent with existing population projection products in terms of regional ageing patterns. This dataset provides a basis for investigating urban population growth and shrinkage, population ageing, and regional demographic transitions in China, and can also support studies of urban disaster risk, public service demand, and sustainable urban development. Given China's rapid urbanization and continuing population ageing, the long-term demographic trajectories of its cities also provide useful evidence for understanding global urban demographic transitions and their social and environmental implications. This dataset contains age- and sex-specific population data for 342 Chinese cities, together with the principal R modules documenting the data-production workflow. The dataset includes historical population data for 2000, 2010, and 2020, a simulated population for 2020, and population projections under five SSP scenarios. The main historical and projected series use the fixed 2020 urban boundaries from the GHSL Urban Centre Database (GHS-UCDB R2024A). This keeps the geographic area consistent for comparisons over time. Urban expansion and contraction are outside the scope of the main series. The reporting unit is the urban built-up area within the specified boundary, distinct from the associated prefecture-level administrative area. In addition to the main series, the dataset provides historical reference estimates for 2000 and 2010, each covering the population within the GHS-UCDB urban boundaries for that year.
title: Population size, age structure, and ageing of Chinese cities from 2000 to 2100

summary: This replication package contains the lecture-level attendance data and Stata code underlying the study "Lecture Attendance Before and After the Emergence of Generative AI: Evidence from a Longitudinal Study". The dataset comprises 157 lecture observations from nine annual offerings of the same undergraduate business course at a Norwegian university between 2018 and 2026. The accompanying Stata code enables reproduction of the descriptive statistics, figure, regression analyses, and robustness checks reported in the manuscript. The package includes the analytical dataset in Stata and CSV formats, a replication do-file, and documentation describing the variables and replication procedures.
title: Replication Data and Code for: Lecture Attendance Before and After the Emergence of Generative AI: Evidence from a Longitudinal Study

summary: This record provides the companion experimental data, code, and execution environment for the manuscript “Input Reach versus Oracle Observation: A Systems Engineering Validation Protocol for AI-Reconstructed Components in Legacy System Replacement” by Kigon Park. The artifact includes the frozen experimental protocol and amendment log, library versions and license notices, input sets, reconstruction evidence and outputs, raw execution records, analysis code, re-execution instructions, and a separate Docker container image. The experiments comprise three complementary studies: an equal-budget comparison of input-generation policies on 24 frozen reconstructions; calibration of observation relations using 32 controlled perturbation operators across four APIs; and executable evaluation of 12 fresh reconstructions of cJSON and miniz components. Constructed control violations are distinguished from naturally occurring reconstruction errors. The deposit preserves the experimental release dated 29 October 2026. Some embedded documentation and manuscript-authoring files retain the earlier title, “Input and Observation Adequacy in AI Assisted Binary Reconstruction.” These authoring files correspond to the earlier manuscript rather than the revised MDPI layout. The frozen reconstruction outputs and supplied environment support re-execution of the reported evaluations. Exact reproduction of the model-generation step is limited because an immutable model snapshot and inference sampling seeds were unavailable. Please consult README.txt for the file inventory and re-execution instructions. Third-party components retain their original licenses and notices.
title: Companion Artifact for "Input Reach versus Oracle Observation: A Systems Engineering Validation Protocol for AI-Reconstructed Components in Legacy System Replacement"

summary: A considerable challenge in palaeoanthropology is the handling of fragmented and sensitive human remains, which provide an important source of information about the identity of humans in the past. Virtual reconstructions have facilitated the extraction of these information and can be applied in various fields. By using computed tomography and advanced computer software, the virtual reconstruction of a subadult Neolithic skull from Frankfurt am Main-Fechenheim, Germany, is presented in this study. In combination with a revised age estimation, the reconstruction provides new data for future comparative analyses of one of the oldest preserved human skeletons of Frankfurt city area.
title: A Virtual Cranial Reconstruction of the Oldest Human Remains of Frankfurt am Main-Fechenheim

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: the greedy row-selection rule built into every linear-algebra library, column-pivoted QR, can lose against the best possible choice by a factor of about exp(C√k), with an exact constant C, and never by the 2 k allowed by the textbook guarantee. Context. Many simulation and data methods keep only k of N coordinates of an N×k matrix Q with orthonormal columns (for example the interpolation points of the discrete empirical interpolation method, DEIM). The quality of a choice I is γ = ‖Q(I,:) −1 ‖ 2 , the factor by which interpolation from the chosen coordinates can be worse than the best approximation; some choice always has γ ≤ √(k(N−k+1)). The rule used in practice is column-pivoted QR (QRCP) on Q * , which repeatedly picks the coordinate least explained by those already chosen. Drmač and Gugercin (SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2016) proved a bound that grows like 2 k . Damle and Kressner asked whether QRCP meets the existence scale on orthonormal rows (Problem 4.3 of Amsel et al., arXiv:2602.05394). Chen, Liu, He and Dong (arXiv:2606.02484) gave the first answer, negative: their examples exceed every polynomial multiple of the existence scale, and their construction already gives growth of order exp(c√k) with a small c. Damle (arXiv:2607.13532) showed that the Bischof–Stewart rule meets the existence scale. Results. Let the coherence μ(Q) be the largest row energy divided by the average. (1) Theorem 2.3: if μ(Q) ≤ H, every legal QRCP selection, with any tie-breaking, has γ ≤ √(e(N−k+1)) exp(C(H)√k), with an explicit constant C(H): C(1) = 2 (equal row energies), C(2) ≈ 2.25, and C(H) 2 /log H → 1. This is the first bound below exponential in k for QRCP on orthonormal rows. (2) The constant is sharp: the worst case satisfies log G k (H) = (C(H)+o(1))√k, with real examples of fewer than 3k 3 rows built from a generalised Kahan matrix; for H > 1 their pivots are unique, and at H = 1 they use the smallest-label tie rule. (3) Corollary 2.6: since μ(Q) ≤ N/k, the bound holds for every input with C(N/k). (4) Theorem 2.7 and Corollary 2.8: without any coherence assumption the worst case is exp(Θ(√(k log(N/k)))) once N ≥ k 2+ε (and log N = o(k)), and exp((1+o(1))√(k log N)) when log N/log k → ∞. (5) Theorem 7.1: an a posteriori bound γ ≤ (√e/d k ) exp(√((k−1)L)) from the observed pivot range L, with an optimal coefficient. At k = 100 the new bound allows about 10 9 to 10 10 where the classical bound allowed about 10 30 ; it is smaller than the classical bound from k = 13 at H = 1. Limits. Exact arithmetic and worst cases only; typical inputs behave far better, and floating-point QRCP is not analysed. Sharpness is on the logarithmic scale: upper and lower bounds still differ by a factor polynomial in k, and the limits are approached slowly. The worst examples need N of order k 3 ; whether growth of order exp(c√k) occurs when N is a fixed multiple of k is open. Contents. Checks raise SystemExit and stay active under python -O. Assurance. Written proofs, with finite computational checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: five reviewer roles, an adver

summary: This dataset provides the numerical results supporting the manuscript entitled  A Topological Selected-Solve Approximation of Inverse Hodge Operators for Explicit DEC/FETD Maxwell Simulations , by A. S. Moura and W. G. Facco. The research investigates sparse approximations of the inverse electric Whitney–Hodge matrix using topologically defined sparsity patterns, with particular emphasis on the radius-three selected-solve approximation (G_{H,3}). The dataset contains 43 CSV files and eight PDF figures documenting the numerical experiments, including: Algebraic validation of topological sparsity patterns and approximation accuracy. Robustness under geometric mesh perturbations and material contrasts. Time-domain Maxwell simulations in two-dimensional perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) cavities. Modal and frequency-domain analyses. Scalability and computational-cost measurements. Comparisons between sparse selected-solve updates, diagonal approximations, and direct LU-based time stepping. CFL stability investigations and electromagnetic energy-drift diagnostics. The archive also includes supporting documentation and SHA-256 checksums for data integrity verification. Source code: https://github.com/alexmoura2024/selected-hodge-dec-fetd The accompanying Python scripts provide the algorithms and procedures required to reproduce the numerical experiments. Runtime measurements may vary with hardware, software versions, and computational environment. This dataset is released to support transparency, verification, and reproducibility in computational electromagnetics and numerical linear algebra.

The research investigates sparse approximations of the inverse electric Whitney–Hodge matrix using topologically defined sparsity patterns, with particular emphasis on the radius-three selected-solve approximation (G_{H,3}). The dataset contains 43 CSV files and eight PDF figures documenting the numerical experiments, including: Algebraic validation of topological sparsity patterns and approximation accuracy. Robustness under geometric mesh perturbations and material contrasts. Time-domain Maxwell simulations in two-dimensional perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) cavities. Modal and frequency-domain analyses. Scalability and computational-cost measurements. Comparisons between sparse selected-solve updates, diagonal approximations, and direct LU-based time stepping. CFL stability investigations and electromagnetic energy-drift diagnostics. The archive also includes supporting documentation and SHA-256 checksums for data integrity verification. Source code: https://github.com/alexmoura2024/selected-hodge-dec-fetd The accompanying Python scripts provide the algorithms and procedures required to reproduce the numerical experiments. Runtime measurements may vary with hardware, software versions, and computational environment. This dataset is released to support transparency, verification, and reproducibility in computational electromagnetics and numerical linear algebra.
title: Numerical Datasets for Topological Selected-Solve Approximation of Inverse Hodge Operators in Explicit DEC/FETD Maxwell Simulations
