summary: Multi-agent LLM systems are built by fixing a cast of roles and then designing how the cast coordinates. Which agents should make up the group for a given task is left to the designer, and the same cast is reused for every task. Financial trading makes the cost of that choice visible: stocks trade differently, and the trading styles suited to one need not suit another. We study task-conditioned persona selection, composing the group from the characteristics of the task it will face, and instantiate it with FinPanel, an LLM multi-agent trading system in which a recruiter selects a panel of named trader personas for each stock from a direction-blind statistical sketch of how the stock trades, each persona gives an independent daily call in its own style, and a manager commits the trade after reading the panel's arguments and their desk-kept, hierarchical track records. Because nothing is returned to the traders, the panel stays the panel that was selected, and it can trade a new stock from an empty record. On eight US stocks over the out-of-knowledge year 2025, against three prior LLM trading agents re-implemented in the same framework and against rule-based, predictive and reinforcement-learning baselines, the selected panel is ahead of a fixed panel of the same size and of the prior agents run as their papers prescribe, with a shallower drawdown than buy-and-hold on every stock; it keeps its performance with no warm-up and with no record at all, whereas the memory-augmented agents' returns swing with their warm-up; and neither more seats nor the manager's reading of the arguments substitutes for selecting the right ones. Who is in the group is a design decision to be made per task, before how the group coordinates.
title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents

summary: Tools for interpreting the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on LLMs themselves to both generate and evaluate explanations, creating a self-referential automated interpretation process with minimal human oversight. This automation raises significant reliability concerns, which are exacerbated by the absence of ground truth. In practice, it is difficult to validate explanations or to attribute interpretability failures to their source -- whether they originate from the tool's extracted representations or from the LLM used in the process. To address these challenges, we present DECODE, a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into the automated interpretation process. Our approach decomposes the diagnostic workflow into three progressive stages, isolating failure sources ranging from structural defects to explanation-level misalignments. Drawing inspiration from inter-coder consensus in qualitative analysis, we utilize consensus among independently generated explanations and their evaluation metrics as a proxy for reliability. To further scale human inspection, we employ a three-phase active seeding protocol that strategically recommends high-priority instances for manual review. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study on 16,384 Sparse Autoencoder features, showing that it can efficiently identify and attribute interpretability failures at scale.
title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process

summary: This record provides the reproducibility package for “Feature-Budget Trade-offs in Replay-Based Network Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Dataset Diagnostic Study”. It contains Python code, frozen 12-seed derived results, release figures, and supporting materials for a multi-dataset diagnostic study of feature-budget trade-offs in replay-based network intrusion detection. The archive does not redistribute NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, CTU-13, or any other third-party raw traffic data. Data provenance, access requirements, and reproduction boundaries are documented in README.md and DATA_ACCESS.md.
title: Reproducibility package for replay-based NIDS feature-budget experiments

summary: Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting the effects of multivariate dependence on the reliability of redundant systems.
title: Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark

summary: We present three multi-week, disc-integrated James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) campaigns monitoring HDO and SO$_2$ absorption in Venus' upper mesosphere at altitudes of approximately 80--110 km. Obtained in February 2022, July 2023, and August--September 2023, these observations provide dense temporal sampling and complementary observing geometries, enabling the disentanglement of short-term, long-term, and local solar time (LST) variability, which has been challenging in previous studies. We have four main findings. First, SO$_2$ in the upper mesosphere, being largely absent in February 2022 but present in both 2023 campaigns, may follow the same long-term trend observed at cloud tops. Second, long-term variability in H$_2$O is identified here for the first time and is interpreted as an anticorrelated response to the long-term change in SO$_2$, likely through H$_2$SO$_4$ formation. Third, H$_2$O is broadly stable within each campaign, although occasional short-term variability is present in the form of a depletion event. Finally, short-term variability is likely present for SO$_2$, but it does not dominate the overall behaviour. In the absence of strong long-term differences, the daily SO$_2$ abundance evolution is consistent with an asymmetric LST profile peaking near midnight, which is well reproduced by an independent model. These results are enabled by a dedicated reduction and retrieval pipeline that mitigates the strong standing-wave baseline structure in the spectra and quantifies systematic uncertainties, providing a methodological framework for future studies facing similar challenges.
title: JCMT--Venus: Daily Monitoring of HDO and SO$_2$ Absorption in Venus' Mesosphere

summary: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.
title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under 4 years the field has moved from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and to proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. This survey reviews 88 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. We follow a VLA through its life cycle, from model design to training and deployment, along seven axes. Model design covers (a) inputs and memory, what the model observes; (b) architecture, how its pipeline is built; (c) action output, how it produces motor commands; and (d) intermediate predictions, what else it predicts, from reasoning steps to future observations. Training covers (e) pretraining data, the mix of robot, web, human and simulated data, and (f) post-training, adaptation to the target robot. Deployment covers (g) real-time execution, keeping pace with the robot. We analyse 22 models on these axes and report their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge: (i) training data has broadened, from about 10,000 hours of teleoperated robot data ($π_0$) to 23,000 community-collected episodes (SmolVLA) and 20,000 hours of egocentric human video (GR00T N1.7); (ii) model sizes have split: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters, while a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs; and (iii) generalist VLAs are emerging that handle both manipulation and navigation, such as UniVLA and Qwen-VLA. We also compare VLAs with world-action models, which predict future observations as well as actions. We review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail when objects or the camera move slightly, and open up further research questions.
title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment

summary: When a sequential decision system falls short of an optimum, its score does not reveal which modifications would improve its decisions. DECODE is a benchmark for testing such modifications through controlled experiments on planning and available information. Its consumer-credit collections generator provides five partially observed environments that share known dynamics matrices and vary a memory parameter and process noise. The experiments change selected inputs or planning rules while keeping the rest of the solver fixed. Each comparison specifies the solver's state inputs, response inputs and planning horizon. On the deterministic base environment, which was selected for a large gap between six-month and one-month planning with the hidden state, extending planning from one to six months increases the scores of two gradient-boosted solvers by 15 to 17 percentage points of the exact optimum, computed with the hidden state and borrower traits. Even at this horizon, the best graded solver, whose repayment response is fitted on logs, remains 15.6 points below that optimum. In a specified intervention sequence, three changes to its state inputs and their evaluation during search lower its score by 6.3 points, and replacing its fitted repayment model with the true response, evaluated with hidden borrower traits, then raises it by 15.6, a net recovery of nine of those points. Because the intermediate effects are conditional on the repayment model and the order of the changes, they do not uniquely assign the gap to separate causes. Within these limits, DECODE makes hypotheses about solver performance testable through specified interventions under known dynamics and explicit information conditions.
title: DECODE: Decomposable Environments for COntrolled Sequential-Decision Evaluation

summary: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time. In medium Earth orbit (MEO)--low Earth orbit (LEO) networks, periodic reports leave CPU states stale or missing, making offloading sensitive to uncertain capacity and shared-destination congestion. We propose PUMA-Former, an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative offloading under incomplete information that balances completed work, service delay, and execution cost. A MEO coordinator maintains distinct-report memory and closes the loop between available evidence, capacity estimates, allocation commands, and execution feedback. Latent-delay attention weights plausible measurement-age hypotheses, and historical innovations refine CPU estimates around the latest received report. Queue-error-aware fusion incorporates auxiliary pressure while accounting for backlog uncertainty. The inferred resource moments condition a structured Transformer allocator for joint destination, partition, bandwidth, CPU, and power decisions. Bounded risk-aware calibration then adjusts workload splits to reflect uncertainty and shared destination load. In traffic-driven development evaluation, PUMA-Former increases admitted compute-work completion by 8.62%, reduces mean modeled service delay by 34.78%, and reduces mean episode-P95 delay by 71.08% relative to ATLA-adapt. It also improves completion and normalized energy over fixed-half round-robin offloading. Service gains over the learning baselines involve higher normalized energy.
title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information

summary: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. Here, we propose an alternative view, building on the principle that the correlations of a sequence reflect the structure of the process that generated it. We define the autocorrelation function of a layer as the average dot product between its activations at two context positions separated by a lag. Latent variables encoded persistently along the context create slowly decaying tails in the autocorrelation, and we find these tails to grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. In synthetic data with controlled hierarchical latent structure, this growth stems from the encoding of abstract latent variables, which govern long stretches of the input. Indeed, the persistence of latent codes predicts the qualitative structure of autocorrelations and accounts for most of the empirical measures. In real text, we take sparse-autoencoder features as proxies for latent variables, and find that their persistence correlates strongly with the magnitude of autocorrelations across datasets and LLMs. In particular, the persistence time increases with depth, as do autocorrelations, implying that deeper latent features persist for longer context spans. We complement this analysis by explicitly ablating the persistent sparse-autoencoder features and observing a consequent decrease in the autocorrelations.
title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations

summary: Training language models across low-bandwidth networks requires reducing synchronization overhead. Local optimization methods such as DiLoCo communicate only after several local steps, but outer gradient averaging and the outer update remain on the critical path. Existing computation-communication overlap methods avoid this stall through delayed or replica-local updates, which can degrade convergence or cause replicas to drift. We propose LACCO (Local Accumulation with Computation-Communication Overlap), a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global communication with local computation while applying globally aggregated updates shared by every replica, without introducing staleness in the outer update. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth non-convex objectives. Experiments on language-model pre-training with FineWeb show that LACCO consistently outperforms communication-overlapped baselines such as Eager and Delayed DiLoCo. These gains remain robust as model size scales up to 0.5B parameters and across a range of communication intervals and numbers of replicas up to 16 workers, while incurring only negligible-or fully overlappable-computational or memory overhead, which demonstrates the strength of LACCO.
title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap

summary: Scientific literature search can benefit from locally deployed LLM assistants, which reduce reliance on hosted model providers while giving research teams greater control over their data and infrastructure. This work investigates whether open-weight models can support web-assisted paper retrieval under practical computing constraints. We first characterize inference latency as the input context grows from 512 to 128k tokens on a Mac Studio and a server equipped with two NVIDIA A100 GPUs. We then evaluate eight models on the retrieval of 70 papers from seven scientific repositories, using queries that represent three levels of domain knowledge. The results show that retrieval success depends strongly on the selected model and the specificity of the query. And that A100 GPUs are generally faster than the Mac Studio, but its unified memory allows larger models that could not be loaded in the tested GPU configuration.
title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100

summary: Generative recommendation benefits from long interaction histories, but the cost of processing them directly grows with history length. We propose RecMem, a recurrent memory compression framework guided by three desiderata: space invariance, semantic fidelity, and lifelong evolvability. RecMem compresses historical segments into a fixed set of memory slots using a bifurcated encoder-decoder with shared lower layers and slot-wise forget-gated updates. Recommendation supervision trains the memory to preserve predictive information, while stream-consistency training aligns predictions from sequential and packed processing. By construction, the memory state and decoder context are independent of history length; under contraction and approximate semigroup consistency, we further derive a horizon-independent bound on the state discrepancy between these two processing orders. On MerRec, RecMem uses 16 memory slots and a 216-token decoder context, compared with 1,200 tokens for HSTU-1200, while retaining 87.9% of HSTU-1200's Recall@10 and 97.0% of its Recall@200. It outperforms PHSTU and the evaluated recent-only and retrieval baselines, and analyses of distant history show that archived interactions contribute predictive signal.
title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation

summary: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option. The four recipes differ in how an option is scored and how the scores become probabilities; one follows the expert gate of DeepSeek-V3. Trained on the same data as Qwen3-0.6B with the LLM-as-Jev recipe (67.6% test accuracy), the encoder reaches 69.7% to 72.1%. Scoring an option by "yes" minus "no" instead of "yes" alone gives the larger gain, from 69.7% to 71.3% on the test set and from 57.8% to 59.6% on external benchmarks (56.1% for the decoder). Sigmoid normalisation adds 0.8 test points; a square-root softplus adds none. One request at a time on an NVIDIA A100, the encoder takes 29 ms per decision against 68 ms, but uses more peak memory (2.8 against 2.2 GiB). An auxiliary head, trained on human-marked evidence and on labels selected with a reward adapted from SelfCite, predicts in the same pass the sentences annotated as support for the answer.
title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications

summary: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change. Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame, where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama) lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model. A controlled encoder x supervision study shows that the encoder decides what can be read and the supervision what is read: at a matched budget, counterfactual supervision adds 4.5 points on average and 38 on the speed questions of natural benchmarks. Code and models: https://github.com/kkt94/Llama-V-JEPA-LM.
title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations

summary: World models that support planning, control, and interpretable reasoning require latent representations that genuinely encode action. Yet the large-scale video data from which such models are learned overwhelmingly lack action annotations. Latent-action models infer action-like variables from observation sequences, enabling action-aware learning from unlabeled videos or trajectories. A fundamental concern, however, remains: a latent that improves future prediction may simply encode the current state, episode progress, task identity, or other predictive shortcuts. Existing evaluation practices---reconstruction loss, rollout fidelity, action recovery, or downstream performance---cannot isolate this distinction. We introduce the Latent Action Support Ratio (LASR), a dimensionless metric that measures, under offline evaluation on held-out data, whether a learned latent provides predictive support for action-related targets beyond the current state and non-action alternatives. LASR provides two complementary summaries: GeoLASR captures typical support, while WorstLASR identifies the weakest case. We instantiate the LASR benchmark with recorded actions and corresponding physical state changes as targets, episode-held-out splits, one predictor type for all comparisons, and positive and negative controls. Experiments on recorded robot manipulation data and a matched multi-task panel demonstrate that LASR detects known action information, rejects representative non-action shortcuts, and enables graded comparisons among imperfect latent representations. We further use LASR to train and audit a lightweight residual adapter, obtaining descriptively better point estimates whose uncertainty is assessed with paired comparisons. LASR thus provides a principled offline protocol for measuring action-related predictive support in world-model latents.
title: Beyond Prediction Gain: LASR as a Metric for Action-Grounded Latents in World Models

summary: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approximation (RAWATTA), a training-free method that runs attention in 8- bit precision and keeps 16-bit precision only in the layers where a worst-case calibration check requires it. Its fast set- ting, RAWATTA-Fast, also approximates attention in a few averaging and anchoring layers, while matching layers and the first image keep all their keys. On a 12 GB GPU at 50 im- ages, RAWATTA runs VGGT faster than the released code, mostly through our CUDA engine, and loses at most about one point of pose accuracy (AUC@3) on any dataset; RAWATTA-Fast is slightly faster and less accurate. Both fit 200 images, where the released code runs out of memory at 100.
title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation

summary: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that treats experience as a persistent state shared across successive language models. MIGRO follows a simple principle: preserve historical evidence exactly, organize it approximately, and decide what to retrieve only when the question is known. We call this asymmetric fidelity with deferred selectivity. A shared semantic index supports retrieval, while exact records retain observations and their historical relationships. Because models differ in vocabulary and tokenization, host-specific interfaces convert selected evidence into inputs the receiving model can use. Reversible encoding reduces archival storage while enabling exact recovery. The shared state and its access interfaces let successive hosts read and extend the accumulated experience. On matched LoCoMo states, MIGRO scores 7.3% higher and uses 99.3% less private memory than the strongest quality baseline. After handoff, continued writing retains 99.9% of full-history rebuilding quality by extending the inherited state. On million-token BEAM histories, MIGRO uses 57.5% less private storage on average than the most compact baseline. MIGRO combines high answer quality, continued memory growth across hosts, and low storage cost. Code is available at https://github.com/zOUMINGXI/MIGRO.
title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models

summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.
title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations

summary: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. In deployed agent systems, the same execution may be exposed through composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories, changing what execution evidence is directly observable to the verifier. It therefore remains unclear whether correct verifier judgments persist across such abstraction boundaries. We introduce Verification Transport, a reliability test that measures judgment stability under abstraction-induced changes in execution observability. We construct matched native, abstracted, and restored views of the same frozen executions while holding the task, realized trajectory, outcome, ground truth, evaluation criterion, and verifier fixed. Across four agent-evaluation benchmarks, seven verifier backbones, four verification protocols, and three abstraction boundaries, we find substantial transport failure, reaching about 31% under macro abstraction and delegation. Verification protocols exhibit distinct failure modes: direct verification more often produces incorrect verdicts, whereas evidence-grounded and deliberative protocols tend to abstain under limited observability. This suggests that lower transport failure rates do not necessarily imply greater reliability. Restoring the corresponding execution provenance recovers 85.5% of transport failures, while recovery is lower when provenance is lossy or unavailable. These results show that native-view accuracy alone is insufficient to characterize verifier reliability when execution evidence crosses abstraction boundaries.
title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation

summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.
title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations

summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.
title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.
title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection

summary: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.
title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support

summary: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon

summary: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Observation-to-observation models avoid this dependence, but most omit the recursive filtering cycle that lets DA systems carry a background state through sparse, irregular observations. We introduce WeatherDreamer, a world model that learns this cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems, without reanalysis. It infers a latent state from observations, carries it forward hour by hour with learned dynamics, corrects it each hour with new observations, and can predict what any of its observing systems would measure at any location. summary: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. The approach employs a general six-stage process with platform-specific adapters, utilizing either a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock to identify and read tensor allocations from video memory. We validate this acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, demonstrating that the recovered bytes are byte-exact and usable for downstream analysis. As a use case, we apply linear probes trained on standard framework activations to the recovered states, successfully distinguishing refusal from compliance with an AUROC of 0.88 on held-out prompts. This work establishes that live, observational access to intermediate hidden states is feasible on named inference platforms, providing a new source of evidence for examining the operational behavior of deployed AI systems.
title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States

summary: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation. However, translating this knowledge and research experience into model designs requires preserving source context and testing applicability under task-specific assumptions. In this paper, we propose NeoResearch, a literature- and experience-guided autonomous research framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) as researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models. Specifically, NeoResearch establishes an expert-inspired dual-loop research workflow, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization through experimental feedback. To enable knowledge-grounded discovery, the agent autonomously mines scientific literature from the Web, extracting modeling mechanisms, empirical evidence, and applicability conditions to formulate task-grounded, testable architecture hypotheses. Furthermore, a hierarchical experience memory links literature findings to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons, guiding architecture discovery and training optimization while supporting reuse across forecasting tasks. Experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and support dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. Our code is available.
title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery

summary: Machine learning systems specialize computation to the workload and hardware, but communication remains in generic libraries whose device code and transport decisions are not visible to high-level compilers. We present Obaleth, a compiler that makes GPU-initiated communication part of a kernel's intermediate representation, co-optimizes it alongside computation, and lowers it to specialized transport code. Obaleth plans completions around buffer lifetimes and optimizes memory ordering, synchronization, and batching across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On H100 GPUs, Obaleth sends small messages up to 3.3$\times$ faster, and on 256 GPUs runs all-to-all 1.25$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ faster than NVSHMEM and NCCL GIN, with much smaller memory and register use. In vLLM, it serves Qwen3-235B on 16 B200 GPUs and answers requests up to 1.29$\times$ faster than with DeepEP.
title: Compiling Specialized GPU-Initiated Networking

summary: Reproducibility Package — Version 1.1.0 This repository contains the complete computational reproducibility package for the study “Significance-Classification Instability Beyond p-Value Variability: A Monte Carlo Study of Effect Direction and Effect-Estimate Compatibility.” The study investigates statistical-significance classification instability across independent studies generated under the same population mechanism, jointly examining effect-direction agreement, differences in estimated effect magnitude, and direct between-estimate comparisons. Original Simulation Study (Version 1.0.0) The original study comprises 509 unique simulation scenarios, including 486 factorial scenarios and 25 directed transition-region scenarios, with two overlapping conditions. The factorial scenarios used 100,000 paired replications per scenario, while the directed scenarios used 250,000 paired replications. Statistical inference was based on two-sided Welch tests at a significance level of 0.05. The original reproducibility package includes R scripts, simulation functions, scenario definitions, random-number streams, aggregated simulation results, conditional analyses, tables, figures, metadata, and documentation required to reproduce the reported findings. Extensions Introduced in Version 1.1.0 Version 1.1.0 incorporates supplementary mathematical and computational analyses developed in response to the comments and methodological recommendations received during the peer-review process for the manuscript submitted to Mathematics (MDPI) . These extensions were designed to strengthen the methodological robustness, analytical interpretation, and reproducibility of the original findings, particularly regarding significance-classification discordance, effect-direction agreement, heteroscedasticity, statistical power, and direct comparisons between effect estimates. The additional materials are organized in the revision_mayor_2026 directory and include: Supplementary sensitivity analyses covering 24 simulation scenarios. Power-calibrated analyses covering 18 scenarios, targeting approximately 50% statistical power. Additional simulations involving Normal, Student's t, and Gamma distributions, unequal sample sizes, and different standard-deviation ratios. Conditional analyses of significance discordance, effect-direction agreement, and direct between-estimate rejection. Independent computational validation and cross-checks using R and Python. Supplementary numerical results, methodological validation reports, and file-integrity documentation. The supplementary analyses provide additional evidence concerning the robustness and interpretation of the original simulation findings. In particular, conditional rejection frequencies are distinguished from evidence of differences between underlying population effects, and failure to reject a direct between-estimate test is not interpreted as evidence of statistical equivalence. Reproducibility and Version History Version 1.0.0 remains preserved as originally published. Version 1.1.0 extends the computational reproducibility package without replacing or altering the original simulation results. The original and supplementary analyses are maintained separately to ensure transparency, computational traceability, and reproducibility. The accompanying README and CHANGELOG files document the repository structure, the modifications introduced in Version 1.1.0, and the procedures for reproducing the analyses. summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): polyhelper.ai/trends/markets , polyhelper.ai/trends/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24285333 . summary: R script and country-year analysis matrix for reconstructing the pooled DP2 index for the 27 EU Member States, 2015–2024. Put both files in the same directory and run Rscript DP2_EU27_reproduction_code.R from that directory. The script also produces calibration parameters and selected sensitivity summaries. The input matrix uses Eurostat indicators and includes the documented carry-forward for the missing France 2021 housing-cost value.
title: Replication code for multidimensional wellbeing convergence in the EU27, 2015–2024

summary: Task-based AI scenarios can map automation into productive capacity, factor shares, wages, and labor reallocation without uniquely determining current expenditure or realized activity when income shifts sharply across households and factors. This paper develops an empirically disciplined closure diagnostic for the 2030 scenarios in Korinek and others (2026). A corrected accounting decomposition shows that, in their Extreme scenario, aggregate labor income is almost unchanged relative to no AI even though cognitive labor income falls sharply, because gains to other workers nearly offset the loss. Using observed ranges for the transmission of persistent income shocks, cash-spending responses, recent corporate payout ratios, Federal Reserve ownership data, and household leverage benchmarks, I report deterministic rather than probabilistic sensitivity sets. The first-round current-consumption response relative to no AI is positive in the Modest scenario but not sign-identified in the Extreme scenario. Holding AI output fixed, however, the shift from labor to capital robustly lowers current consumption within the calibrated envelope. A minimal goods-market closure shows why investment, monetary policy, and external demand are necessary to translate either result into output. The central conclusion is therefore about identification: a task model can identify a production frontier without identifying the macroeconomic path used to reach it. The replication package (code, input tables, outputs, figures) reproduces all reported quantitative results: run python code/01_empirical_closure.py and python code/checks.py.
title: Closing the Loop: Distribution, Consumption, and Macroeconomic Closure under Transformative AI

summary: Toda táctica del manejo integrado de plagas y enfermedades (MIP) cuesta algo cada semana —mano de obra, producto, recorrido del lote— menos una: la que se decidió antes de sembrar. Este artículo examina la resistencia varietal como fundamento del sistema, con las magnitudes medidas en campo y sus condiciones impresas. En Yunnan, China, entre 1998 y 1999, las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes —material convencional, sin modificación transgénica— presentaron una severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor que en monocultivo, a escala de miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios, y los agricultores abandonaron el fungicida contra esa enfermedad (Zhu et al., 2000). Ese caso sostiene el titular: es resistencia disponible, sembrable y medida a escala de paisaje. El contraste opuesto lo aporta el banano frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4): en el ensayo australiano de cinco ciclos, la incidencia acumulada fue de 84 % en el testigo 'Williams' y de 66 % en 'Grand Nain', frente a 2 % en la línea QCAV-4 portadora del gen *MamRGA2* (Harding et al., 2025). Su estatuto es el contrario: QCAV-4 es un banano transgénico aprobado solo en Australia y no es sembrable hoy en Colombia; se cita como evidencia de cuánto puede valer una resistencia cuando existe, no como material disponible para el productor colombiano. Entre ambos extremos, el artículo recorre la durabilidad —que se mide en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva y depende del fondo del paisaje, no de la ficha del cultivar—, el material limpio como decisión separada de la genética, y el injerto como forma de trasplantar la resistencia en tomate. ## 2. Tres decisiones distintas bajo una misma palabra

En el lenguaje de finca
«buen material» mezcla tres cosas que la evidencia separa

porque cada una falla y se verifica de una manera distinta.

La primera decisión es **genética**: sembrar un genotipo que resiste o tolera al organismo dañino. Resistencia y tolerancia no son sinónimos: la resistencia reduce la infección o el desarrollo del patógeno —o la alimentación y reproducción de la plaga—
la tolerancia permite que el organismo esté presente pero limita el daño en el rendimiento. Un material tolerante puede verse enfermo y rendir bien
y uno con resistencia parcial puede verse limpio en un año de baja presión y colapsar en uno de alta. Importa también distinguir la resistencia de uno o pocos genes de efecto mayor —potente
pero expuesta a que una sola mutación del patógeno la vuelva inútil— de la cuantitativa
repartida en muchos genes de efecto menor
menos espectacular y más duradera. Antes de aceptar la palabra «resistente» hay que preguntar resistente a qué

durante cuántos ciclos y contra qué población del patógeno.

La segunda decisión es **sanitaria**: sembrar material limpio
libre —o tan libre como el sistema permite— de los patógenos que viajan dentro de la semilla
el tubérculo o la plántula. En cultivos de propagación vegetativa —yuca
batata— pesa tanto como la genética
porque el material de siembra es el vehículo principal de virus
bacterias y hongos sistémicos: un genotipo excelente con estacas infectadas es un programa condenado desde el primer día

como demuestra la sección 7.

La tercera decisión es **de arquitectura**: injertar la variedad productiva sobre un portainjerto que aporta la resistencia que la variedad no tiene
típicamente contra patógenos del suelo. El injerto no crea resistencia nueva
y su costo es operativo: vivero capaz

mano de obra entrenada y un portainjerto probado bajo condiciones locales. Las tres decisiones se compran y se verifican por separado.

## 3. Yunnan: la mezcla que llevó el titular

El ensayo de Yunnan sigue siendo la demostración más grande de que la composición genética del lote es una variable de manejo. Las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*

sin. *Pyricularia oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes presentaron una **severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor** que en monocultivo. El efecto no se quedó en parcelas: se mantuvo al escalar a miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios de Yunnan
y su consecuencia práctica fue que los agricultores abandonaron la aplicación de fungicida contra el añublo (Zhu et al.
2000). La fuente es primaria y leída con sus condiciones: es la magnitud mejor sostenida de este artículo

y por eso lleva el titular.

Tres precisiones gobiernan su lectura. La primera es la naturaleza del material: variedades convencionales
obtenidas por mejoramiento clásico y combinadas por diseño de siembra

nada en Yunnan exige aprobación transgénica ni espera regulatoria —la táctica estaba disponible en la misma temporada en que se midió—. La segunda es el mecanismo: la resistencia funcionó mejor repartida en mezcla que concentrada
porque la mezcla reduce a la vez la densidad de tejido susceptible y la velocidad de propagación entre plantas
la unidad de la táctica no fue el gen aislado sino la composición del lote. La tercera es económica: el ahorro no fue un porcentaje de una aplicación
y su comparación correcta es contra la suma de todas las temporadas en que la mezcla siga funcionando —lo que depende de la durabilidad

el tema de la sección 6—.

El caso enseña además qué significa que una resistencia sea «disponible»: que el material existe
que su uso es legal donde se siembra
que el productor puede obtenerlo y que su efecto fue medido en condiciones comparables. Yunnan cumple las cuatro
el banano cumple la última con la mayor magnitud de este artículo

para Colombia— las tres primeras.

## 4. La resistencia a escala de país: el contraste de la roya del café

Entre la parcela y el paisaje hay un punto intermedio: el país. En Colombia
la roya del café (*Hemileia vastatrix*) separa con nitidez los dos mundos de este artículo: **incidencia de 20 % o más en variedades susceptibles frente a 6 % o menos en resistentes**
con pérdidas de 30 a 80 % en las susceptibles cuando el manejo no compensa la susceptibilidad

y más de 84 % del área cafetera nacional sembrada ya con variedades resistentes. La clase de evidencia se imprime con la cifra: es una fuente institucional —la Federación Nacional de Cafeteros de Colombia y Cenicafé—
cuya fuerza es la escala de observación
se lee como balance nacional sostenido
no como comparación experimental entre parcelas

y se cita como magnitud de contexto dentro del tema de la resistencia.

El dato cumple dos funciones: confirma el orden de magnitud —decenas de puntos de incidencia y pérdidas de un tercio a cuatro quintos de la cosecha en el material equivocado— y advierte: la misma fuente reporta seis razas nuevas de roya y nueve variantes más virulentas recientes. La resistencia cafetera colombiana es un éxito en vigilancia permanente

no un problema archivado.

## 6. La durabilidad: hectáreas-año

no ficha de cultivar

Si el artículo terminara en la tabla anterior

el lector saldría con una regla simple y falsa: «siembre resistente y el problema queda resuelto». La evidencia obliga a examinar cómo y por qué la resistencia deja de funcionar.

La unidad honesta de la durabilidad no es el año calendario ni la frase «resistencia durable» de un catálogo: es la **hectárea-año de protección efectiva** —cada hectárea sembrada con el material
multiplicada por cada año en que la protección se mantiene bajo presión real—. Leída así
la durabilidad **no es una propiedad de la ficha del cultivar: depende del fondo del paisaje** —de cuánta superficie comparte el mismo genotipo
de cómo se mueve el inóculo entre fincas y regiones—. La mezcla de Yunnan es

una tecnología de durabilidad además de una de control: repartir la resistencia baja la severidad de la temporada y reduce la recompensa que el patógeno obtiene por adaptarse a cualquiera de los genotipos.

El primer mecanismo de quiebre es la **evolución del patógeno**: un genotipo resistente en grandes extensiones ejerce la selección más intensa posible

y sobreviven las variantes capaces de atacarlo. Las seis razas nuevas y las nueve variantes más virulentas de roya reportadas en Colombia son la respuesta esperable del hongo a décadas de resistencia desplegada. La consecuencia de manejo: toda resistencia se siembra junto con su plan de quiebre —diversidad de genotipos

vigilancia de la incidencia en el material «resistente» como alarma temprana y ruta de reemplazo pensada antes de necesitarla—.

El segundo mecanismo no requiere evolución alguna: **la tolerancia anunciada que nunca fue lo que el ensayo corto sugería**. El caso de advertencia permanente es la variante somaclonal GCTCV-218

desplegada en Filipinas como Cavendish tolerante a Foc TR4. Su estatuto de evidencia debe quedar impreso: las cifras favorables que circulan provienen de páginas comerciales y de literatura secundaria
sin fuente primaria abierta que las respalde en la búsqueda verificada del libro fuente
y por tanto no se imprimen aquí como magnitud. Lo que sí está verificado es lo contrario de la promesa: en el ensayo extendido de tres años discutido por Harding et al. (2025)
2025). Había mostrado resistencia moderada en planta madre y primer rebrote

la protección se desvaneció.

La regla de interpretación vale para todo el artículo: **una tolerancia medida en uno o dos ciclos es una compra de tiempo
y debe planearse como tal —monitoreo ciclo a ciclo
el lote tolerante como activo que se deprecia
y sin desmontar las demás capas del programa—. Quien siembra un tolerante sabiendo que compra tiempo decide legítimamente

quien lo siembra creyendo que compró inmunidad ha sido engañado por la propaganda.

El tercer límite no es quiebre sino **ausencia**: frente al rayado pardo de la yuca (CBSD)
la fuente primaria más reciente declara que no existe ninguna variedad con resistencia duradera (Casinga et al.
2025). Donde la genética no ofrece la herramienta
el programa se construye con las demás —material limpio
manejo del vector y roguing—: el hueco declarado orienta el esfuerzo

la resistencia imaginaria lo desperdicia.

## 7. Material limpio: la decisión que la resistencia no reemplaza

En los cultivos de propagación vegetativa
la pregunta «¿de dónde salió este material?» vale tanto como «¿qué genotipo es?»: los virus
las bacterias sistémicas y algunos hongos viajan dentro de la estaca

y el material de siembra es a la vez primera víctima y primer vehículo. La degeneración de la semilla vegetativa —la acumulación de infecciones cuando el productor resiembra su propio material— es el proceso que la estrategia integrada de salud de semilla busca interrumpir con tres componentes que no se sustituyen entre sí: resistencia varietal
manejo en finca y reemplazo estratégico de los lotes (Thomas-Sharma et al.
derrotada por la estaca.** El ensayo de Kabare
en Kivu del Sur (República Democrática del Congo)
sembró dos variedades resistentes al mosaico —'Nabana' (MM 96/4653) y 'Sawasawa' (MM 96/3920)— con estacas sanas y con estacas infectadas por los virus del rayado pardo. Con estacas infectadas
el rendimiento de raíz fresca cayó **44 % a los 9 meses y 86 % a los 12 meses en 'Nabana'
frente a las mismas variedades con estacas sanas
mientras el material sano rindió 5 % más a los 12 meses que a los 9
2025). La resistencia al mosaico era real en ambas parcelas
porque el problema venía dentro de la estaca y era otra enfermedad —una frente a la cual
no existe resistencia duradera: en ese patosistema el material limpio es

casi toda la estrategia disponible—.

**Papa: la selección positiva como tecnología sin laboratorio.** Donde no hay semilla certificada al alcance
la herramienta verificada es marcar en el ciclo anterior las plantas sanas y vigorosas y cosechar de ellas —y solo de ellas— la semilla siguiente. En Uganda
a lo largo de tres generaciones
la selección positiva redujo la incidencia de virus (PVY
PLRV y otros) generación tras generación frente a la selección habitual y la aleatoria
porque al PLRV la literatura le atribuye reducciones de rendimiento de hasta 90 % (*Potato Research*
el análisis por ELISA dio la fotografía complementaria: en los lotes de selección positiva no se detectaron PVY
mientras en los de selección aleatoria se detectaron PVS en 78 %
PLRV en 16 % y PVM en 9 % de los tubérculos (Okeyo et al.
2018). La selección positiva no esteriliza un lote infectado

es frenar la degeneración y ganar ciclos de semilla aceptable.

El criterio práctico es uno solo: **«limpio» y «resistente» se compran por separado y se verifican por separado** —con certificación formal donde existe

renovación periódica y la disciplina de no sembrar jamás material de un lote con síntomas sistémicos visibles—.

## 9. Verificar antes de comprar: el interrogatorio del material

Entre la evidencia y la finca hay un mostrador: el del proveedor de semilla

el vivero o el vecino que vende estacas. La mayoría de las decisiones malas de material se toman aceptando en ese mostrador palabras sin precisiones. El interrogatorio que sigue las convierte en preguntas aplicables a cualquier oferta de material «resistente»
exactamente?** La respuesta aceptable nombra el organismo y

es un adjetivo publicitario. Segunda: **¿medido dónde y contra qué testigo?** Una incidencia de 5 % no significa nada sin el testigo susceptible en el mismo ensayo: el dato de TR4 es interpretable porque 'Grand Nain' y 'Williams' marcaron 66 % y 84 % en el mismo campo y los mismos ciclos (Harding et al.
2025). Tercera: **¿durante cuántos ciclos?** Es la pregunta que desarma el caso 'Formosana': en perennes
una resistencia sin al menos tres ciclos bajo presión real es una hipótesis. Cuarta: **¿qué pasa cuando se quiebre?** Genotipos alternos
lo inválido no es el material sino la dependencia exclusiva de él. Y quinta
para material de origen biotecnológico: **¿su uso está aprobado donde yo siembro?** —la pregunta que separa a QCAV-4

de cualquier cultivar convencional—.

Para el material limpio se verifica la procedencia
no el genotipo: ¿de qué lote madre salió —en selección positiva bien hecha
de plantas marcadas como sanas el ciclo anterior—?

¿el lote madre tenía síntomas? —un lote cosechado en un campo con síntomas sistémicos no se «mejora» eligiendo los órganos de mejor aspecto: el ensayo keniano encontró PVS en 78 % de los tubérculos de selección aleatoria (Okeyo et al.
la verificación es del proceso: portainjerto con nombre y respaldo local —'Hawaii7996' y 'Padma F1' en Benín
2024)— y un vivero capaz de mostrar su disciplina sanitaria: sin desinfección

el vivero se convierte en distribuidor del patógeno que el injerto pretendía evitar.

## 10. Conclusiones: la regla de la primera línea

La primera decisión fitosanitaria del programa es el material
antes de sembrar: (1) el genotipo —resistente o tolerante al problema dominante del lote
(2) el estado sanitario —limpio por certificación o por selección positiva verificada—
y (3) la arquitectura —injerto sobre portainjerto demostrado donde un patógeno del suelo limita el cultivo y existe vivero capaz—. Si alguna falla
el programa se rediseña alrededor de ese límite antes de sembrar

no después.

Las magnitudes quedan con sus condiciones y su estatuto. Yunnan —94 % menos severidad
miles de hectáreas en 1998–1999— es evidencia primaria de una táctica convencional y ejecutable. La roya del café —20 % o más frente a 6 % o menos

con fuente institucional— confirma el orden de magnitud y la obligación de vigilar. El TR4 —84 % en 'Williams' y 66 % en 'Grand Nain' frente a 2 % en QCAV-4— mide el techo de una resistencia y delimita la vía transgénica hoy no disponible en Colombia: QCAV-4 está aprobado solo en Australia. Y la durabilidad no se lee en la ficha del cultivar sino en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva sobre el fondo del paisaje.

Tres huecos delimitan la regla: no existe variedad de yuca con resistencia duradera al rayado pardo
las cifras favorables de los somaclonales tipo 'Formosana' carecen de verificación en fuente primaria abierta —solo está verificado su colapso en ensayo largo—
y la rentabilidad del injerto para el pequeño productor no está medida en serie abierta. Los huecos no debilitan la regla: la delimitan
que es lo que distingue una regla de decisión de un eslogan. Sembrar resistente sigue siendo la única táctica que trabaja gratis toda la temporada —siempre que lo sembrado sea

limpio y sembrable donde se siembra—.

title: Sembrar resistente es la única táctica que trabaja gratis toda la temporada: 94 % menos severidad del añublo en el arroz de Yunnan

summary: Toda táctica del manejo integrado de plagas y enfermedades (MIP) cuesta algo cada semana —mano de obra, producto, recorrido del lote— menos una: la que se decidió antes de sembrar. Este artículo examina la resistencia varietal como fundamento del sistema, con las magnitudes medidas en campo y sus condiciones impresas. En Yunnan, China, entre 1998 y 1999, las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes —material convencional, sin modificación transgénica— presentaron una severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor que en monocultivo, a escala de miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios, y los agricultores abandonaron el fungicida contra esa enfermedad (Zhu et al., 2000). Ese caso sostiene el titular: es resistencia disponible, sembrable y medida a escala de paisaje. El contraste opuesto lo aporta el banano frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4): en el ensayo australiano de cinco ciclos, la incidencia acumulada fue de 84 % en el testigo 'Williams' y de 66 % en 'Grand Nain', frente a 2 % en la línea QCAV-4 portadora del gen *MamRGA2* (Harding et al., 2025). Su estatuto es el contrario: QCAV-4 es un banano transgénico aprobado solo en Australia y no es sembrable hoy en Colombia; se cita como evidencia de cuánto puede valer una resistencia cuando existe, no como material disponible para el productor colombiano. Entre ambos extremos, el artículo recorre la durabilidad —que se mide en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva y depende del fondo del paisaje, no de la ficha del cultivar—, el material limpio como decisión separada de la genética, y el injerto como forma de trasplantar la resistencia en tomate. La resistencia es la primera línea porque es la única decisión irreversible dentro del ciclo, y por eso mismo es la que más verificación exige antes de comprar. **Palabras clave:** resistencia varietal; mezclas de cultivares; añublo del arroz; *Magnaporthe oryzae*; Foc TR4; QCAV-4; durabilidad de la resistencia; material limpio; manejo integrado de plagas ## 1. Ninguna aplicación posterior devuelve lo que se perdió por sembrar susceptible en un suelo con historia del patógeno. Esa anterioridad le da una propiedad que ninguna otra táctica tiene en el mismo grado: trabaja gratis toda la temporada, sin recorrido ni aplicación, desde la emergencia hasta la cosecha. Y comparte una segunda propiedad, menos amable: es irreversible dentro del ciclo. Si el monitoreo falla, se corrige la semana siguiente; si el material sembrado era el equivocado, el error dura lo que dura el cultivo —en perennes, años—. ## 2. Tres decisiones distintas bajo una misma palabra

En el lenguaje de finca
«buen material» mezcla tres cosas que la evidencia separa

porque cada una falla y se verifica de una manera distinta.

La primera decisión es **genética**: sembrar un genotipo que resiste o tolera al organismo dañino. Resistencia y tolerancia no son sinónimos: la resistencia reduce la infección o el desarrollo del patógeno —o la alimentación y reproducción de la plaga—
la tolerancia permite que el organismo esté presente pero limita el daño en el rendimiento. Un material tolerante puede verse enfermo y rendir bien
y uno con resistencia parcial puede verse limpio en un año de baja presión y colapsar en uno de alta. Importa también distinguir la resistencia de uno o pocos genes de efecto mayor —potente
pero expuesta a que una sola mutación del patógeno la vuelva inútil— de la cuantitativa
repartida en muchos genes de efecto menor
menos espectacular y más duradera. Antes de aceptar la palabra «resistente» hay que preguntar resistente a qué

durante cuántos ciclos y contra qué población del patógeno.

La segunda decisión es **sanitaria**: sembrar material limpio
libre —o tan libre como el sistema permite— de los patógenos que viajan dentro de la semilla
el tubérculo o la plántula. En cultivos de propagación vegetativa —yuca
batata— pesa tanto como la genética
porque el material de siembra es el vehículo principal de virus
bacterias y hongos sistémicos: un genotipo excelente con estacas infectadas es un programa condenado desde el primer día

como demuestra la sección 7.

La tercera decisión es **de arquitectura**: injertar la variedad productiva sobre un portainjerto que aporta la resistencia que la variedad no tiene
típicamente contra patógenos del suelo. El injerto no crea resistencia nueva
y su costo es operativo: vivero capaz

mano de obra entrenada y un portainjerto probado bajo condiciones locales. Las tres decisiones se compran y se verifican por separado.

## 3. Yunnan: la mezcla que llevó el titular

El ensayo de Yunnan sigue siendo la demostración más grande de que la composición genética del lote es una variable de manejo. Las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*

sin. *Pyricularia oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes presentaron una **severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor** que en monocultivo. El efecto no se quedó en parcelas: se mantuvo al escalar a miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios de Yunnan
y su consecuencia práctica fue que los agricultores abandonaron la aplicación de fungicida contra el añublo (Zhu et al.
2000). La fuente es primaria y leída con sus condiciones: es la magnitud mejor sostenida de este artículo

y por eso lleva el titular.

Tres precisiones gobiernan su lectura. La primera es la naturaleza del material: variedades convencionales
obtenidas por mejoramiento clásico y combinadas por diseño de siembra

nada en Yunnan exige aprobación transgénica ni espera regulatoria —la táctica estaba disponible en la misma temporada en que se midió—. La segunda es el mecanismo: la resistencia funcionó mejor repartida en mezcla que concentrada
porque la mezcla reduce a la vez la densidad de tejido susceptible y la velocidad de propagación entre plantas
la unidad de la táctica no fue el gen aislado sino la composición del lote. La tercera es económica: el ahorro no fue un porcentaje de una aplicación
y su comparación correcta es contra la suma de todas las temporadas en que la mezcla siga funcionando —lo que depende de la durabilidad

el tema de la sección 6—.

El caso enseña además qué significa que una resistencia sea «disponible»: que el material existe
que su uso es legal donde se siembra
que el productor puede obtenerlo y que su efecto fue medido en condiciones comparables. Yunnan cumple las cuatro
el banano cumple la última con la mayor magnitud de este artículo

## 4. La resistencia a escala de país: el contraste de la roya del café

Entre la parcela y el paisaje hay un punto intermedio: el país. En Colombia
la roya del café (*Hemileia vastatrix*) separa con nitidez los dos mundos de este artículo: **incidencia de 20 % o más en variedades susceptibles frente a 6 % o menos en resistentes**
con pérdidas de 30 a 80 % en las susceptibles cuando el manejo no compensa la susceptibilidad

y más de 84 % del área cafetera nacional sembrada ya con variedades resistentes. La clase de evidencia se imprime con la cifra: es una fuente institucional —la Federación Nacional de Cafeteros de Colombia y Cenicafé—
cuya fuerza es la escala de observación
se lee como balance nacional sostenido
no como comparación experimental entre parcelas

y se cita como magnitud de contexto dentro del tema de la resistencia.

El dato cumple dos funciones: confirma el orden de magnitud —decenas de puntos de incidencia y pérdidas de un tercio a cuatro quintos de la cosecha en el material equivocado— y advierte: la misma fuente reporta seis razas nuevas de roya y nueve variantes más virulentas recientes. La resistencia cafetera colombiana es un éxito en vigilancia permanente

no un problema archivado.
