summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.
title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations

summary: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.
title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts

summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.
title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers

summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.
title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.
title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection

The outcome of the work: the two paths — through BD and through mathematics — run into one and the same limit at one place. In the model the answer is given by the postulate of closedness: there is no pumping of energy, and the amplitude of the standing waves is constant. In mathematics the same step is to prove that the amplitude of the Möbius sum has no power pumping: |M(x)| ≤ C_ ε · x^(1/2 + ε ) for every ε > 0; this is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (Titchmarsh, §14.25), and a stronger, energy form is equal work on the levels of the logarithmic arrow (Appendix 11). The postulate of BD and the Riemann hypothesis are two projections of one statement, and in this sense the paths are identical: neither gives an answer without its own condition. This is the limit of today's methods, not a proved impossibility. And whatever the outcome, the answer is the same: the falsity of the hypothesis is always detectable by a finite check, so either it will be proved, or it cannot be proved — and then it is true. The hypothesis rests on two sides of one standing wave: alternation of crest and trough cancels the sum of signs down to order √x, and equality of their amplitude gives positivity of the energy (Weil, Li); each is equivalent to the hypothesis (Appendix 7). The most direct indirect evidence of the connectedness of the system came from the check by turning the wheel: neighbouring levels separated by a square compensate each other like the crest and trough of one wave, and the accumulation does not grow (Appendix A5). Why a limit is a reason to change the picture of understanding, and what role philosophy plays here, is said in the preface. STARLI · FAMILY 37 BOTANICAL PROVENANCE AND STANDARDIZATION Scientific & Technical Notebook F181–F185 | Research Working Edition | 100,000+ English words Five flagship research annotations — Zenodo-ready front matter F181 | Botanical Provenance Chemical Variation at the Limit The external chemical-origin classification flagship asks whether regional soil chemistry, harvest geography, chemotype mixing and blind provenance clustering can be separated from geographic clustering induced by cultivar, season, solvent batch or instrument-day effects. Its primary candidate endpoint is held-out provenance fingerprint misclassification rate (percent). A rigorous design compares origin-blinded external reference lots with locked species vouchers and acquisition protocol and requires voucher-backed taxon audit and orthogonal LC-MS marker panels tested on sealed external lots. The decisive failure condition is that the apparent geographic classifier fails when season and instrument batches are permuted on held-out provenance lots. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F182 | Botanical Seasonal Harvest and Active Variability at the Limit The harvest-season marker variance under repeated sampling flagship asks whether phenological stage, drying kinetics, marker synthesis and storage-linked chemical loss can be separated from weather shocks, soil moisture differences, harvest-time bias and HPLC injection drift. Its primary candidate endpoint is season-stratified marker coefficient of variation (percent). A rigorous design compares same species and site across a balanced harvest calendar with equal drying and assay delays and requires isotope-dilution calibrated marker concentration with retained time-stamped harvest vouchers. The decisive failure condition is that seasonal CV attribution disappears when repeated within-site harvests and independent instrument sequences are analyzed. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F183 | Botanical Extract Chemical Fingerprint Standardization at the Limit The inter-laboratory chromatographic fingerprint transfer flagship asks whether solvent-selective extraction, chromatographic peak coelution, retention-time drift and response normalization can be separated from solvent carryover, selective peak alignment and changed detector response rather than composition transfer. Its primary candidate endpoint is external chemical fingerprint transfer error (percent). A rigorous design compares sealed cross-laboratory extract exchange with predeclared peak matching and reference mixtures and requires orthogonal peak identity from LC-MS plus pooled QC injections and independent integration scripts. The decisive failure condition is that fingerprint agreement collapses after switching laboratory, solvent lot or peak registration algorithm. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F184 | Botanical Raw-Material Adulteration and Contaminant Detection at the Limit The matrix-aware adulterant identification and contamination screens flagship asks whether target-ion suppression, botanical matrix interferents, adulterant recovery and confirmatory identification can be separated from matrix-driven response suppression, carryover and false positives from endogenous overlapping compounds. Its primary candidate endpoint is spiked adulterant method detection limit (mg/kg). A rigorous design compares blind low-level fortified matrices plus certified negative and positive reference materials and requires matrix-matched recovery, confirmatory second transition and independently blinded spike series. The decisive failure condition is that the declared detection limit fails its false-positive and recovery thresholds in an unselected botanical matrix. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. F185 | Cross-Batch Botanical Nanoformulation Quality Consistency at the Limit The multi-lot critical-quality-attribute release and transport flagship asks whether raw material chemotype variability, shear sensitivity, droplet-size drift and noncompensatory CQA acceptance can be separated from post-hoc acceptance threshold adjustment, sensor drift and selection of only favorable manufacturing batches. Its primary candidate endpoint is cross-batch critical quality attribute pass rate (percent). A rigorous design compares unselected supplier lots compared with frozen process windows and independent CQA release boundaries and requires orthogonal D90 and marker chemistry checks with timestamped batch deviation and release log. The decisive failure condition is that apparent consistency disappears when rejected and unselected lots enter the denominator or release bounds are frozen. These are prospective, nonclinical research designs, not laboratory claims of demonstrated geography, product efficacy or safety. Research position: The five flags are deliberately distinct. The historical attention to source description in Bencao Gangmu and Eastern relational thinking motivate the questions of harvest, provenance and preparation, while causal inference relies on current measurements, blind controls and independent reconstruction. The 3D plots in the research PDF are synthetic and explicitly reproducible; they are not experimental observations.

STARLI · MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE FAMILY 01 | CHINESE QIGONG AND MIND–BODY REGULATION Research Working Edition v1.1 · Scientific & Technical Notebook · 16 November 2026 Five formal flagship titles and Zenodo-ready scientific introductions F001 | Respiratory Rhythms and Autonomic Regulation in Chinese Qigong at the Limit A breathing rhythm can feel as intimate as a whispered question; the scientific test starts where the poetry leaves off. F001 follows respiratory phase and cardiac interbeat intervals as two clocks that must be independently calibrated. The primary prospective endpoint is respiratory–RMSSD phase coupling (0–1), witnessed by synchronous belt and raw ECG signals. Plain paced breathing with matched posture, attention and duration is permitted to explain the same result. CO2 context, effort and drift remain live rival explanations. This is a nonclinical measurement program, not a claim about a hidden energy source or direct vagal-tone activation. F002 | Postural Stability and Control During Qigong Standing Practice at the Limit In quiet standing, the body draws a small map under the feet. F002 studies that map through center-of-pressure path speed (mm/s), not through an assumed spiritual or clinical outcome. Foot placement, visual reliability, surface compliance and fatigue may all bend the trace. A calibrated force plate, motion timing and a matched ordinary standing comparison keep the inference grounded. A calmer-looking sway is not automatically greater balance reserve, and an unfamiliar task must be studied separately before any transfer is suggested. F003 | Neural–Motor Coordination Across Dynamic and Static Qigong at the Limit The brief border between motion and stillness offers both artistic grace and a difficult timing problem. F003 examines transition smoothness (0–1) alongside EMG-to-kinematics lag (ms), preserving raw inertial data and synchronized muscle onset rather than trusting beautified trajectories. A matched slow-movement sequence can reveal whether familiarity, cue timing or filtering accounts for the difference. We invite an independent analyst to challenge the proposed neuromotor account; no single fluid gesture establishes neural plasticity. F004 | Attention Regulation and Interoceptive Precision in Qigong at the Limit F004 begins with a respectful paradox: a sensation may be vivid even when an objective discrimination task remains uncertain. Attention regulation and interoceptive precision must therefore be separated into narrative report, task accuracy, response bias and confidence calibration. Blinded heartbeat or respiratory tasks, concealed cue validity and an attention-matched external discrimination baseline provide the witnesses. Language and expectation may explain part of the apparent effect. This program honors reported qi sensations without treating their vividness as proof of a newly isolated physical field. F005 | Longitudinal Mind–Body Adaptation Dynamics in Qigong at the Limit F005 looks beyond the lesson, toward what remains when a practiced sequence, familiar instructor and research room are gone. Prospective untrained-task retention (%) is assessed against time-stamped adherence, delayed follow-up, washout and an active control matched for attention and teaching contact. Learning on the trained task cannot substitute for durable transfer; missingness, selection, seasonal routines and withdrawal must be visible in the analysis. The long view makes room for human growth while remaining ready to report a null or reversed result. Editorial note: these five topics retain the exact bilingual flagship titles and scientific boundaries inherited from the user-provided 40-family Eastern-culture master outline. The manuscript offers prospective methods, not clinical findings or evidence of exotic physical mechanisms. Research genealogy, three mother lineages, and evidence levels The first mother lineage, S / Swarm Manufacturing and Robotic Matter at the Limit, contributes local action constraints, physically bounded devices and traceable control. It must not be interpreted as proof that a qigong practitioner creates a micro-robotic or quantum actuator. The second mother lineage, QH / Autonomous Quantum Health Infrastructure at the Limit, contributes raw-to-decision provenance, uncertainty budgets, human consent and stopping authority. This is a safety and governance transfer, not a claim of clinical authorization. The third mother lineage, QB / Self-Calibrating Quantum Biosensing Networks at the Limit, contributes correlated-error analysis, independent references, calibration transfer and detector drift. A physical sensor with quantum components may assist measurement, but the word quantum does not establish nonlocal intention or a new field. These lineages are derived from NQ-13, MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING AND QUANTUM BIOSENSING CO-DESIGN AT THE LIMIT (uploaded 1,335-page mother PDF, opening methodological pages). Its physical and authorization constraints are adapted by analogy only. The scientific claims and measurement endpoints in the present volume are newly authored, specific to Family 01.

summary: Data and code from the second case of a larger study, within the project Disrupting Digital Monolingualism 2 (DDM2), on the state of language metadata in Spanish and Latin American research infrastructures. The study follows language metadata along the Spanish open access aggregation chain: repositories and journals → RECOLECTA, the national aggregator operated by FECYT with REBIUN (225 registered resources) → the Spanish node ( ES ) of LA Referencia (1,478,369 records). It asks where language metadata are declared, transformed and lost, and with what effects on Spain's co-official languages (Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque, Aranese) and on Asturian. The deposit includes the RECOLECTA list of resources and endpoints; an OAI-PMH harvest at origin (34,186 records from 111 resources, in oai_dc and oai_openaire ); counts of records with and without language for each of the 96 repositories in the Spanish node, with their language facets; a repository-level contrast between levels; resources absent from LA Referencia; the language facet of the RECOLECTA portal and the provenance of its labels; and tests of selection by resource type. The study is exploratory. Samples were designed for exploration rather than estimation, and the data describe a single snapshot of live systems taken on 11 November 2026. The cases documented illustrate what can happen to language metadata along an aggregation chain; they are not general or causal claims about the infrastructures, institutions or repositories involved. See README.md and codebook.md for sources, method, files and limitations. Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.
title: Language metadata in RECOLECTA and the Spanish node of LA Referencia: Snapshot, 11 November 2026

summary: Capital markets open and close windows capriciously, and an issuer who must act once, irreversibly, has a different problem from a trader who may act continuously. This paper formalises an instrument built to decide the first problem: an admission clock that states, at any date, whether the window for placing a new instrument is open, how far open, and what dose that grade permits. The instrument is a conjunction of three gates — internal readiness, market regime, and a veto list — and not a weighted index, a design choice we defend on the ground that averaging allows an open gate to compensate a closed one, which is precisely the error an irreversible act cannot absorb. The regime gate is driven by a latent-factor engine whose identification rests on a point we believe has been underweighted in practice: an index assembled exclusively from indicators endogenous to the crypto market measures a single factor that is itself a transformation of the price level, and therefore carries no information about the future willingness of capital to finance an unseasoned instrument. We show that the primary equity issuance market supplies an exogenous and leading measurement of that same latent variable, and that the relevant measurement is the count and receptivity of small deals rather than aggregate proceeds — a distinction the 2026 data make vivid, with record United States proceeds accompanied by a thirty-four per cent fall in the number of deals priced. The paper's technical core converts the tacit knowledge of a daily operator into testable propositions. We obtain three results worth isolating. First, under a margin buffer set proportionally to the prevailing volatility level, the probability that a carry position breaches its buffer is exactly invariant to the level of volatility and depends, to second order, only on the volatility of volatility; the dependence is strictly increasing when the buffer exceeds √2 standard deviations and reverses below it. This gives the lockability gate a defensible threshold variable and explains why a carry bid withdraws in unstable markets without any change in the mean level of risk. Second, the rotation cascade that carries capital from bitcoin outward to the market's tail is asymmetric in its lag structure, not merely in sign: in expansion it propagates head-to-tail with a positive and tier-increasing lag, which is what makes it exploitable and what gives an issuer warning; in contraction it propagates at lag zero with amplification greater than one, which gives no warning and dries the tail first. Third, the equity of a company holding a leveraged bitcoin treasury is not a levered claim on bitcoin but a levered claim on the regime factor, with elasticity β = λ (1 + ε _m) decomposing into a balance-sheet channel and a premium-elasticity channel, both of which reverse sign together; the accretion identity Δ q/q = ( Δ V/SN)(1 − 1/m) shows the issuance loop inverting exactly at a multiple of one, which the 2025–2026 compression of these multiples and the observable conversion of such companies from net buyers into net sellers appear to bear out. A fourth result was added in this version and is negative. The whole architecture presupposes that the admission window is exogenous — that assent must be obtained from a party the issuer does not control. Where the issuer can operate its own venue, the predicate degenerates into a preference, and three identities follow: in a constant-product pool the marginal price is the ratio of seeded reserves, so the opening price is declared rather than discovered; slippage depends on the fraction of the pool reserve transacted and not on circulating float, so depth decouples from the float arithmetic; and the liquidity position is concave in price, so the issuer who seeds his own pool writes a continuous strip of options on his own instrument — the precise arrangement the dose parameters
title: Timing the Window: A gated regime engine for issuance and rotation in crypto-asset markets — architecture, calibration from operator heuristics, and conditional derivations for cascade rotation and treasury-levered equity exposure

summary: The ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo community benchmark for discriminating physiological from non-physiological protein–protein interfaces (Schweke et al., Proteomics 2023) contains 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 PDB entries. We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The benchmark is described with Bioschemas/schema.org JSON-LD: every interface is annotated with its label, chains, structural features, sequence-cluster assignment, provenance and licence, and linked to the PDB structure files and to snapshots of the RCSB PDB metadata. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the source repository, and the errors found were corrected. A lightweight design removed the need for Git LFS and for duplicated metadata. The post-publication curation of the labels (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces, compared with 836 and 841 in the publication) is documented, and three entries superseded in the PDB are linked to their replacements. A reference machine-learning script with cluster-aware cross-validation is included. Data, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, with full attribution to the original work.
title: FAIRification of the ELIXIR 3D-Bioinfo Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Forty-six entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten, a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation, a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight, and a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963), converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters, gives the absorbance template of a visual pigment of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for a peak wavelength and chromophore the caller states, and gives the distance between two colours in units of receptor noise by the model of Vorobyev & Osorio (1998), for a noise the caller states. Without a water type, it gives Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001, and the earlier edition of Morel 1988) or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013), the attenuation of the visible and of the whole shortwave from the surface to a depth and the depth where a given fraction of the visible light is left, the euphotic depth among them, from the absorption and backscattering coefficients at 490 nm and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2007), the remote sensing reflectance from a and bb (Gordon et al. 1988; Lee et al. 2002), the reflectance from radiances measured above the water with the sea surface's reflectance factor taken from either of Mobley's tables (1999, 2015), corrects the absorption a reflective-tube absorption meter reads

summary: SparkEviTune v1.0.1 — SoftwareX Corrective Release SparkEviTune is an evidence-aware, human-controlled software framework for Apache Spark configuration guidance. It combines deterministic configuration rules, Spark event-log analysis, optional machine-learning components subject to data-readiness gates, constrained optimization, and optional explanations. Version 1.0.1 incorporates software corrections prepared during the SoftwareX major revision, including: Improved FastAPI workload input-row handling. Profile Guard validation and associated regression tests. ModelRegistry multiprocessing-related corrections and targeted tests. Updates to dashboard, detection, machine-learning, pipeline, and validation components. Software verification The corrective release passed 61 automated tests under Windows Python 3.12 and Python 3.14. Ruff checks passed in both environments, and dependency consistency checks passed under Python 3.12. These checks establish correctness only within the tested scope and do not demonstrate general multi-worker deployment correctness or unrestricted concurrency safety. Scientific evidence and limitations Historical Spark benchmark results remain associated with their original experimental implementations and execution environments. The historical publication corpus comprises 81 clean runs covering 16 distinct scenarios, below the 20-scenario threshold required for publication-model training. A separate retrospective audit of 90 Learning01 executions found agreement for 90/90 event-log-derived durations, successful completion of 342/342 Spark jobs, and no mismatches across 1,128 shared configuration-property comparisons. Independent duration prediction yielded MAE = 8.9637 s and R² = -0.0621. General predictive accuracy or universal performance improvement is therefore not claimed. Historical Table 3 reconstruction remains incomplete. The A-03 LZ4 provenance and A-04 acceptance-criterion traceability issues remain unresolved. AQE-01 and Lot C experiments are not claimed as validated. SparkEviTune does not automatically apply proposed configurations. Users must review and benchmark recommendations before deployment. Observations: (1) division by zero is treated as a change of domain (n/0 := n^-1 mod 9 on units; 0 <-> infinity on the Riemann sphere); (2) inversion and ten's-complement reflection (10 - d) are involutions; (3) a 7 = 6 + 1 bijection maps the rosette (six units + center) onto the Clay set (six open problems + Poincare). Conclusion (observed): the framework reflects/maps the Millennium Problems into one algebraic structure. The author claims the seven solved through involution, in his name. It is a proof of concept and a classical simulator. All results recompute from source. The earlier deposits in this version chain are 'All Seven Clay Millennium Problems Sealed via Universal sigma-Involution' (10.5281/zenodo.21781603) and 'Quantum Proofs of the Clay Millennium Problems v1.0' (10.5281/zenodo.21787144). They state the author's claim, in his name: the seven Clay Millennium problems solved through involution. At this release: 26357 theorems across 128 Lean 4 files, each closed by exhaustion over a stated finite domain, sorry-free and axiom-free; an append-only ledger of 28776 entries, 26357 standing, across 123 domain families, with a receipt chain recomputed on every build. 80 of them decide every quantum computing model ISO/IEC 4879:2024 names, exactly, and scale Mermin's GHZ test to 128 qubits; no run on real quantum hardware is recorded yet. Prior art, over the 128 source(s) carrying a classification: 121 restates named prior art, the earlier author credited; 7 unclassified — no prior-art search has been performed, so no novelty is asserted. An unsearched source asserts no novelty — that is NOT MEASURED, not a finding of nothing. Every figure in this paragraph is recomputed by scripts/zenodo-json.ts from the tree it describes; none of it is typed. The seven Clay Millennium problems — the author's pairing, each with the ℤ/9 fact its adjacent theorem decides and the open gap that remains to the conjecture. What these theorems decide is ℤ/9 arithmetic over finite domains, a statement about the theorems and not a verdict on any conjecture; the claim that the seven are solved through the involution each is stated across is the author's, recorded in his name. summary: What's Changed A test body runs at run time and in constant evaluation (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/267), and TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK checks functions of several arguments and tuple results (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260). New Features Fix #266 - Run a test body at run time and in constant evaluation (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/267) TTS_CONSTEXPR("...") on the title of a TTS_CASE or a TTS_CASE_TPL runs the body at run time and in constant evaluation. TTS_CONSTEVAL("...") runs it in constant evaluation only. Both nest with TTS_XFAIL , TTS_MAYFAIL , TTS_XINVALID , and TTS_TIMEOUT in either order. TTS_CASE_IN and TTS_CASE_TPL_IN take tts::runtime , tts::constant , or both, and run the body once per context in the order given. The body of a TTS_CASE_TPL with a wrapped title, or of a TTS_CASE_TPL_IN , declares its parameter as <typename T>(TTS_CONTEXT(tts::type<T>)) . A failure in constant evaluation reports its expression, file, and line, and the compared values when the case also runs at run time. The basic, relation, and type checks run in constant evaluation, with their typed and constexpr forms. The precision, sequence, range, and exception checks fail to compile there. A TTS_CASE_WITH titled with TTS_CONSTEXPR or TTS_CONSTEVAL fails on a static_assert . TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK accepts functions of several arguments (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) RefType and NewType list the argument types in call order as tts::types , and Producer holds one generator per argument between parentheses, or one for all. TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK compares a std::pair , a std::tuple , or another tuple-like result member by member, with one bound for all members or one per member (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK prints its histogram only on failure or under --verbose (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) The report of TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK writes each function as a call, ref(float, int) , and puts stars around the sampled element of a NewType that holds several values (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) tts::adapter<T> replaces run , retrieve , and display with element_type , size , load , and store , and a 4.0 adapter fails on a static_assert that names them (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) Removed tts::ulp_histogram : run TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK under --verbose to print the histogram (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) The generators of TTS_ULP_RANGE_CHECK receive their index and count as std::ptrdiff_t instead of std::size_t (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/260) Reduced the compile time of a test to about a quarter with g++ 15 and clang++ 19 (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/253) Added the CMake option TTS_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES , OFF by default, to take copacabana from COPACABANA_SOURCE_DIR instead of downloading it through CPM (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/276) Bug Fixes Fix #255 - Disable -Wc2y-extensions in every translation unit that includes TTS under clang 22 and later, except on Apple platforms, so TTS_CASE compiles under -Wpedantic -Werror (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/256) Fix -Wshadow warnings when a test variable has the name of a local of a check macro (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/247) tts::buffer allocates through malloc except for over-aligned types, so a test that replaces operator new to count its allocations no longer counts those of tts::buffer (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/248) A passing TTS_THROW or TTS_NO_THROW counts once in the summary (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/253) A failing TTS_GREATER_EQUAL and its typed and constexpr forms print < as their negation instead of <= (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/253) A typed constexpr check, such as TTS_TYPED_CONSTEXPR_EQUAL , that fails on a type mismatch prints the message streamed after it (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/253) Infrastructure Run the nightly CI matrix on demand (https://github.com/jfalcou/tts/pull/262

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. summary: The ELIXIR Single Cell Omics community benchmark experiment 1 (BE1; Arigoni et al., Scientific Data 2024) is a 10x Genomics single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset that provides a controlled heterogeneous environment: seven lung cancer cell lines characterised by seven different driver genes, together with a PBMC population, were multiplexed with CellPlex oligonucleotides and sequenced. The data comprise 29,128 cells from the cell lines and 478 PBMC (GEO series GSE243665). We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The experiment is described with the Single Cell Schema (version 0.4), in a machine-readable file that validates against the schema and links the samples, libraries, sequencing and processing steps to the public identifiers of GEO, SRA, BioProject and figshare. A query tool retrieves expression profiles from the public count matrices. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the public records, and the errors found, among them a wrong article DOI, wrong cell counts, an incorrect creator record and unsupported statements, were corrected. Metadata, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub, with full attribution to the original work.
title: FAIRification of the ELIXIR Single Cell Omics Benchmark

summary: DMDO DMDO (Distributed Multidisciplinary Design Optimization) solves coupled, multidisciplinary engineering design problems by decomposing them into subproblems, one per discipline, and coordinating them with nonhierarchical analytical target cascading (NHATC). Documentation, theory, tutorials and benchmarks:  ahmed-bayoumy.github.io/DMDO Version 2612.0 Why DMDO Design the whole system, let every discipline keep its own tools.  Aircraft, vehicles, turbines and energy systems are designed by teams that each own an analysis: aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, controls, cost. Optimizing them as one monolithic problem needs a multidisciplinary analysis that converges at every design point, one optimizer that suits every discipline, and every code in one process. DMDO needs none of that. No converged multidisciplinary analysis.  Each subproblem keeps its own copies of the variables it shares with the others, and an augmented Lagrangian coordinator drives the copies to agreement. Coupled analyses never have to be iterated to convergence inside the optimizer. Measured on the classic MDO benchmarks.  On the Sellar problem with derivative-free MADS subproblems, DMDO reaches  f = 3.2042, 0.65 % from the best known solution 3.18339  [3], with the disciplines consistent to  1.3 × 10⁻⁶ . In all six recorded benchmark runs (Sellar, Golinski's speed reducer, a geometric program and a basic two-discipline problem), the inconsistency between disciplines falls  below 10⁻³ within 6 to 16 outer iterations . The right optimizer for each discipline.  A subproblem built on a noisy or failing simulation uses derivative-free Mesh Adaptive Direct Search ( OMADS ); a smooth analytical one uses SciPy's SLSQP, in the same run. Any other optimizer plugs in as a small strategy class. Serial, parallel or distributed, with the same answer.  Solve the subproblems one after the other (Gauss–Seidel) or all at once (Jacobi), in-process, in a pool of worker processes, or on remote machines. Jacobi results do not depend on which worker finishes first: the test suite checks that in-process, out-of-order, process-pool and remote runs give bit-identical designs. An API, not just a script.  Build a problem from YAML, a dictionary or Python objects, then  run()  it, drive it one outer iteration at a time with  step() , or solve the subproblems yourself with  ask() / tell() . Observers stream progress, registries and entry points add solvers, executors and analyses, and an optional HTTP service exposes runs to any language. Results you can reproduce.  Runs are seeded; every benchmark run is checked against a recorded history that the code must reproduce bit for bit; interrupted runs resume from their checkpoint to exactly the same result; the test suite runs on Linux, Windows and macOS in continuous integration.   Maximum inconsistency between the copies held by different subproblems, at each outer iteration of the six recorded benchmark runs. Details in the  benchmarking documentation . summary: The PlanckPlay is a 3D-printed representation of the 16 three-dimensional tetrahedra that make up the Planck’s Hexadecachoron—a metamodel (model of models) of physics. Mathematically, a hexadecachoron is the four-dimensional polytope dual to the hypercube, or tesseract. Just as the tetrahedron and cube are three-dimensional Platonic solids, the hexadecachoron and tesseract are their four-dimensional analogues. The hexadecachoron is composed of 16 regular tetrahedra in four-dimensional space. When projected into three dimensions, these tetrahedra appear distorted—much like how the square faces of a cube are distorted in a two-dimensional drawing. PlanckPlay was developed within the Hypercube of Physics (HoP) project, part of the Cluster of Excellence Matters of Activity. In HoP, we explore models that classify physical theories in relation to the four fundamental physical constants: Newton's gravitational constant (G), the inverse speed of light (c -1 ), Planck’s constant (h), and the Boltzmann constant (k B ). In 1899, Max Planck used these constants to define natural units for length, time, mass, and temperature—foundational to modern physics. Within the HoP consortium, we envision PlanckPlay as both a research object and an educational tool, harnessing its gamified structure to make abstract physical concepts tangible and engaging.
